   499→def _sorted_clusters_by_queue_pos(
   500→    clusters: dict, queue_order: list[str],
   501→) -> tuple[list[tuple[str, dict]], dict[str, int]]:
   502→    """Sort clusters by (priority, earliest queue position).
   503→
   504→    Clusters with explicit priority sort first (ascending), then unset-priority
   505→    clusters sort by queue position.
   506→
   507→    Returns (sorted_cluster_pairs, min_pos_cache) where min_pos_cache maps
   508→    cluster name to its earliest queue position (999_999 if no members queued).
   509→    """
   510→    pos_map = {fid: i for i, fid in enumerate(queue_order)}
   511→
   512→    def _min_pos(cluster_data: dict) -> int:
   513→        positions = [pos_map[fid] for fid in cluster_data.get("issue_ids", []) if fid in pos_map]
   514→        return min(positions) if positions else 999_999
   515→
   516→    min_pos_cache = {name: _min_pos(c) for name, c in clusters.items()}
   517→    sorted_clusters = sorted(
   518→        clusters.items(),
   519→        key=lambda kv: (kv[1].get("priority", 999), min_pos_cache[kv[0]]),
   520→    )
   521→    return sorted_clusters, min_pos_cache
   522→
   523→
   524→def _print_cluster_list_verbose(
   525→    sorted_clusters: list[tuple[str, dict]],
   526→    min_pos_cache: dict[str, int],
   527→    active: str | None,
   528→) -> None:
   529→    """Print the verbose table view of the cluster list."""
   530→    name_width = max(20, min(35, max(len(n) for n, _ in sorted_clusters)))
   531→    total = len(sorted_clusters)
   532→    has_dep = any(c.get("dependency_order") is not None for _, c in sorted_clusters)
   533→    print(colorize(f"  Clusters ({total} total, sorted by priority/queue position):", "bold"))
   534→    print()
   535→    dep_header = f"  {'Dep':>3}" if has_dep else ""
   536→    header = f"  {'#pos':<5}  {'Pri':>3}{dep_header}  {'Name':<{name_width}}  {'Items':>5}  {'Steps':>5}  {'Type':<6}  Description"
   537→    dep_sep = f"  {'─'*3}" if has_dep else ""
   538→    sep = f"  {'─'*4}  {'─'*3}{dep_sep}  {'─'*name_width}  {'─'*5}  {'─'*5}  {'─'*6}  {'─'*40}"
   539→    print(colorize(header, "dim"))
   540→    print(colorize(sep, "dim"))
   541→    for name, cluster in sorted_clusters:
   542→        min_p = min_pos_cache[name]
   543→        pos_str = f"#{min_p}" if min_p < 999_999 else "—"
   544→        priority = cluster.get("priority")
   545→        pri_str = str(priority) if priority is not None else "—"
   546→        dep_order = cluster.get("dependency_order")
   547→        dep_str = f"  {dep_order:>3}" if has_dep and dep_order is not None else ("  {:>3}".format("—") if has_dep else "")
   548→        member_count = len(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   549→        steps = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
   550→        steps_str = str(len(steps)) if steps else "—"
   551→        type_str = "auto" if cluster.get("auto") else "manual"
   552→        desc = cluster.get("description") or ""
   553→        if not desc and min_p == 999_999 and not member_count:
   554→            desc = "(no queue position — no members)"
   555→        desc_truncated = (desc[:39] + "…") if len(desc) > 40 else desc
   556→        name_display = (name[:name_width - 1] + "…") if len(name) > name_width else name
   557→        focused = " *" if name == active else ""
   558→        print(f"  {pos_str:>5}  {pri_str:>3}{dep_str}  {name_display:<{name_width}}  {member_count:>5}  {steps_str:>5}  {type_str:<6}  {desc_truncated}{focused}")
   559→    print()
   560→

   562→def _cmd_cluster_list(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   563→    plan = load_plan()
   564→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   565→    active = plan.get("active_cluster")
   566→    verbose: bool = getattr(args, "verbose", False)
   567→    missing_steps: bool = getattr(args, "missing_steps", False)
   568→
   569→    if not clusters:
   570→        print("  No clusters defined.")
   571→        return
   572→
   573→    queue_order: list[str] = plan.get("queue_order", [])
   574→    sorted_clusters, min_pos_cache = _sorted_clusters_by_queue_pos(clusters, queue_order)
   575→
   576→    if missing_steps:
   577→        from desloppify.app.commands.plan.triage.stage_helpers import _unenriched_clusters
   578→        gaps = _unenriched_clusters(plan)
   579→        if not gaps:
   580→            print(colorize("  All clusters have action steps.", "green"))
   581→            return
   582→        print(colorize(f"  {len(gaps)} cluster(s) need action steps:", "bold"))
   583→        for name, missing in gaps:
   584→            print(colorize(f"    {name}: missing {', '.join(missing)}", "yellow"))
   585→        print()
   586→        print(colorize("  Fix with:", "dim"))
   587→        print(colorize('    desloppify plan cluster update <name> --description "..." --steps "step1" "step2"', "dim"))
   588→        print(colorize('    desloppify plan cluster update <name> --add-step "step title" --detail "sub-details"', "dim"))
   589→        return
   590→
   591→    if verbose:
   592→        _print_cluster_list_verbose(sorted_clusters, min_pos_cache, active)
   593→        return
   594→
   595→    print(colorize("  Clusters (ordered by priority/queue position):", "bold"))
   596→    for name, cluster in sorted_clusters:
   597→        min_p = min_pos_cache[name]
   598→        pos_str = f"#{min_p}" if min_p < 999_999 else "—"
   599→        priority = cluster.get("priority")
   600→        pri_tag = f" [P{priority}]" if priority is not None else ""
   601→        member_count = len(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   602→        desc = cluster.get("description") or ""
   603→        marker = " (focused)" if name == active else ""
   604→        desc_str = f" — {desc}" if desc else ""
   605→        auto_tag = " [auto]" if cluster.get("auto") else ""
   606→        print(f"    {pos_str:>5} {pri_tag} {name}: {member_count} items{auto_tag}{desc_str}{marker}")
   607→

   609→def _cmd_cluster_update(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   610→    """Update cluster description, steps, and/or priority."""
   611→    cluster_name: str = getattr(args, "cluster_name", "")
   612→    description: str | None = getattr(args, "description", None)
   613→    steps: list[str] | None = getattr(args, "steps", None)
   614→    steps_file: str | None = getattr(args, "steps_file", None)
   615→    add_step: str | None = getattr(args, "add_step", None)
   616→    detail: str | None = getattr(args, "detail", None)
   617→    update_step: int | None = getattr(args, "update_step", None)
   618→    remove_step: int | None = getattr(args, "remove_step", None)
   619→    done_step: int | None = getattr(args, "done_step", None)
   620→    undone_step: int | None = getattr(args, "undone_step", None)
   621→    priority: int | None = getattr(args, "priority", None)
   622→    effort: str | None = getattr(args, "effort", None)
   623→    depends_on: list[str] | None = getattr(args, "depends_on", None)
   624→    issue_refs: list[str] | None = getattr(args, "issue_refs", None)
   625→
   626→    has_update = any(x is not None for x in [
   627→        description, steps, steps_file, add_step, update_step,
   628→        remove_step, done_step, undone_step, priority, effort,
   629→        depends_on, issue_refs,
   630→    ])
   631→    if not has_update:
   632→        print(colorize("  Nothing to update. Use --description, --steps, --steps-file, --add-step, --priority, etc.", "yellow"))
   633→        return
   634→
   635→    with plan_lock():
   636→        _cmd_cluster_update_locked(args, cluster_name=cluster_name,
   637→            description=description, steps=steps, steps_file=steps_file,
   638→            add_step=add_step, detail=detail, update_step=update_step,
   639→            remove_step=remove_step, done_step=done_step,
   640→            undone_step=undone_step, priority=priority, effort=effort,
   641→            depends_on=depends_on, issue_refs=issue_refs)
   642→
   643→
   644→def _cmd_cluster_update_locked(
   645→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   646→    *,
   647→    cluster_name: str,
   648→    description: str | None,
   649→    steps: list[str] | None,
   650→    steps_file: str | None,
   651→    add_step: str | None,
   652→    detail: str | None,
   653→    update_step: int | None,
   654→    remove_step: int | None,
   655→    done_step: int | None,
   656→    undone_step: int | None,
   657→    priority: int | None,
   658→    effort: str | None,
   659→    depends_on: list[str] | None,
   660→    issue_refs: list[str] | None,
   661→) -> None:
   662→    """Inner body of cluster update, called under plan_lock."""
   663→    plan = load_plan()
   664→    cluster = plan.get("clusters", {}).get(cluster_name)
   665→    if cluster is None:
   666→        print(colorize(f"  Cluster {cluster_name!r} does not exist.", "red"))
   667→        return
   668→
   669→    if description is not None:
   670→        cluster["description"] = description
   671→
   672→    if priority is not None:
   673→        cluster["priority"] = priority
   674→        print(colorize(f"  Priority set to {priority}.", "dim"))
   675→
   676→    if depends_on is not None:
   677→        all_clusters = set(plan.get("clusters", {}).keys())
   678→        bad = [n for n in depends_on if n not in all_clusters]
   679→        if bad:
   680→            print(colorize(f"  Unknown cluster(s): {', '.join(bad)}", "red"))
   681→            return
   682→        cluster["depends_on_clusters"] = depends_on
   683→        print(colorize(f"  Dependencies set: {', '.join(depends_on)}", "dim"))
   684→
   685→    # Steps replacement: --steps-file takes precedence over --steps
   686→    if steps_file is not None:
   687→        path = Path(steps_file)
   688→        if not path.is_file():
   689→            print(colorize(f"  Steps file not found: {steps_file}", "red"))
   690→            return
   691→        parsed = parse_steps_file(path.read_text())
   692→        cluster["action_steps"] = parsed
   693→        print(colorize(f"  Loaded {len(parsed)} step(s) from {steps_file}.", "dim"))
   694→    elif steps is not None:
   695→        # Legacy flat strings → wrap as ActionStep dicts
   696→        cluster["action_steps"] = [normalize_step(s) for s in steps]
   697→        print(colorize(f"  Stored {len(steps)} action step(s).", "dim"))
   698→
   699→    # Incremental step operations
   700→    current_steps: list = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
   701→
   702→    MAX_STEP_TITLE = 150
   703→
   704→    if add_step is not None:
   705→        new_step: dict = {"title": add_step}
   706→        if detail is not None:
   707→            new_step["detail"] = detail
   708→        if effort is not None:
   709→            new_step["effort"] = effort
   710→        if issue_refs is not None:
   711→            new_step["issue_refs"] = issue_refs
   712→        if len(add_step) > MAX_STEP_TITLE:
   713→            print(colorize(
   714→                f"  Warning: step title is {len(add_step)} chars (recommended max {MAX_STEP_TITLE}).",
   715→                "yellow",
   716→            ))
   717→            print(colorize("  Move implementation detail to --detail instead.", "dim"))
   718→        current_steps.append(new_step)
   719→        cluster["action_steps"] = current_steps
   720→        print(colorize(f"  Added step {len(current_steps)}: {add_step}", "dim"))
   721→
   722→    if update_step is not None:
   723→        idx = update_step - 1
   724→        if idx < 0 or idx >= len(current_steps):
   725→            print(colorize(f"  Step {update_step} out of range (1-{len(current_steps)}).", "red"))
   726→            return
   727→        old = current_steps[idx]
   728→        if isinstance(old, str):
   729→            old = {"title": old}
   730→        if add_step is None:
   731→            # When --update-step is used without --add-step, keep title, update detail only
   732→            if detail is not None:
   733→                old["detail"] = detail
   734→        else:
   735→            old["title"] = add_step
   736→            if detail is not None:
   737→                old["detail"] = detail
   738→            if len(add_step) > MAX_STEP_TITLE:
   739→                print(colorize(
   740→                    f"  Warning: step title is {len(add_step)} chars (recommended max {MAX_STEP_TITLE}).",
   741→                    "yellow",
   742→                ))
   743→                print(colorize("  Move implementation detail to --detail instead.", "dim"))
   744→        if effort is not None:
   745→            old["effort"] = effort
   746→        if issue_refs is not None:
   747→            old["issue_refs"] = issue_refs
   748→        current_steps[idx] = old
   749→        cluster["action_steps"] = current_steps
   750→        print(colorize(f"  Updated step {update_step}.", "dim"))
   751→
   752→    if remove_step is not None:
   753→        idx = remove_step - 1
   754→        if idx < 0 or idx >= len(current_steps):
   755→            print(colorize(f"  Step {remove_step} out of range (1-{len(current_steps)}).", "red"))
   756→            return
   757→        removed = current_steps.pop(idx)
   758→        cluster["action_steps"] = current_steps
   759→        title = step_summary(removed)
   760→        print(colorize(f"  Removed step {remove_step}: {title}", "dim"))
   761→
   762→    if done_step is not None:
   763→        idx = done_step - 1
   764→        if idx < 0 or idx >= len(current_steps):
   765→            print(colorize(f"  Step {done_step} out of range (1-{len(current_steps)}).", "red"))
   766→            return
   767→        step = current_steps[idx]
   768→        if isinstance(step, str):
   769→            step = {"title": step}
   770→            current_steps[idx] = step
   771→        step["done"] = True
   772→        cluster["action_steps"] = current_steps
   773→        print(colorize(f"  Marked step {done_step} as done: {step.get('title', '')}", "dim"))
   774→
   775→    if undone_step is not None:
   776→        idx = undone_step - 1
   777→        if idx < 0 or idx >= len(current_steps):
   778→            print(colorize(f"  Step {undone_step} out of range (1-{len(current_steps)}).", "red"))
   779→            return
   780→        step = current_steps[idx]
   781→        if isinstance(step, str):
   782→            step = {"title": step}
   783→            current_steps[idx] = step
   784→        step["done"] = False
   785→        cluster["action_steps"] = current_steps
   786→        print(colorize(f"  Marked step {undone_step} as not done: {step.get('title', '')}", "dim"))
   787→
   788→    # Show resulting steps after any mutation
   789→    final_steps = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
   790→    if final_steps and any(x is not None for x in [steps, steps_file, add_step, update_step, remove_step, done_step, undone_step]):
   791→        print()
   792→        print(colorize(f"  Current steps ({len(final_steps)}):", "dim"))
   793→        for i, s in enumerate(final_steps, 1):
   794→            _print_step(i, s)
   795→
   796→    cluster["user_modified"] = True
   797→    cluster["updated_at"] = utc_now()
   798→    append_log_entry(
   799→        plan, "cluster_update", cluster_name=cluster_name, actor="user",
   800→        detail={"description": description},
   801→    )
   802→    save_plan(plan)
   803→    print(colorize(f"  Updated cluster: {cluster_name}", "green"))
   804→
   805→
   806→def _cmd_cluster_export(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   807→    """Export cluster steps to stdout in text or YAML format."""
   808→    cluster_name: str = getattr(args, "cluster_name", "")
   809→    export_format: str = getattr(args, "export_format", "text")
   810→
   811→    plan = load_plan()
   812→    cluster = plan.get("clusters", {}).get(cluster_name)
   813→    if cluster is None:
   814→        print(colorize(f"  Cluster {cluster_name!r} does not exist.", "red"))
   815→        return
   816→
   817→    steps = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
   818→    if not steps:
   819→        print(colorize("  No steps to export.", "yellow"))
   820→        return
   821→
   822→    if export_format == "yaml":
   823→        import yaml  # noqa: PLC0415
   824→        data = {
   825→            "clusters": [{
   826→                "name": cluster_name,
   827→                "description": cluster.get("description") or "",
   828→                **({"priority": cluster["priority"]} if "priority" in cluster else {}),
   829→                "steps": [
   830→                    normalize_step(s) for s in steps
   831→                ],
   832→            }]
   833→        }
   834→        print(yaml.dump(data, default_flow_style=False, sort_keys=False))
   835→    else:
   836→        print(format_steps(steps))
   837→
   838→
   839→def _cmd_cluster_import(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   840→    """Bulk create/update clusters from a YAML file."""
   841→    file_path: str = getattr(args, "file", "")
   842→    dry_run: bool = getattr(args, "dry_run", False)
   843→
   844→    path = Path(file_path)
   845→    if not path.is_file():
   846→        print(colorize(f"  File not found: {file_path}", "red"))
   847→        return
   848→
   849→    import yaml  # noqa: PLC0415
   850→    data = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text())
   851→    if not isinstance(data, dict) or "clusters" not in data:
   852→        print(colorize("  Invalid YAML: expected top-level 'clusters' key.", "red"))
   853→        return
   854→
   855→    entries = data["clusters"]
   856→    if not isinstance(entries, list):
   857→        print(colorize("  Invalid YAML: 'clusters' must be a list.", "red"))
   858→        return
   859→
   860→    plan = load_plan()
   861→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   862→    created = 0
   863→    updated = 0
   864→
   865→    for entry in entries:
   866→        if not isinstance(entry, dict) or "name" not in entry:
   867→            print(colorize(f"  Skipping entry without 'name': {entry!r}", "yellow"))
   868→            continue
   869→        name = entry["name"]
   870→        is_new = name not in clusters
   871→
   872→        if dry_run:
   873→            action = "CREATE" if is_new else "UPDATE"
   874→            step_count = len(entry.get("steps", []))
   875→            print(colorize(f"  [{action}] {name}: {step_count} step(s)", "cyan"))
   876→            continue
   877→
   878→        if is_new:
   879→            try:
   880→                cluster = create_cluster(plan, name, entry.get("description"))
   881→            except ValueError as ex:
   882→                print(colorize(f"  {ex}", "red"))
   883→                continue
   884→            created += 1
   885→        else:
   886→            cluster = clusters[name]
   887→            updated += 1
   888→
   889→        if "description" in entry:
   890→            cluster["description"] = entry["description"]
   891→        if "priority" in entry:
   892→            cluster["priority"] = entry["priority"]
   893→        if "steps" in entry:
   894→            imported_steps = []
   895→            for s in entry["steps"]:
   896→                if isinstance(s, str):
   897→                    imported_steps.append({"title": s})
   898→                elif isinstance(s, dict):
   899→                    step: dict = {"title": s.get("title", "")}
   900→                    if "detail" in s:
   901→                        step["detail"] = s["detail"]
   902→                    if "refs" in s:
   903→                        step["issue_refs"] = s["refs"]
   904→                    elif "issue_refs" in s:
   905→                        step["issue_refs"] = s["issue_refs"]
   906→                    imported_steps.append(step)
   907→            cluster["action_steps"] = imported_steps
   908→        cluster["user_modified"] = True
   909→        cluster["updated_at"] = utc_now()
   910→
   911→    if dry_run:
   912→        print(colorize("  (dry run — no changes saved)", "dim"))
   913→        return
   914→
   915→    save_plan(plan)
   916→    print(colorize(f"  Import complete: {created} created, {updated} updated.", "green"))
   917→
   918→
   919→def _cmd_cluster_merge(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   920→    """Merge source cluster into target cluster."""
   921→    source: str = getattr(args, "source", "")
   922→    target: str = getattr(args, "target", "")
   923→
   924→    plan = load_plan()
   925→    try:
   926→        added, source_ids = merge_clusters(plan, source, target)
   927→    except ValueError as ex:
   928→        print(colorize(f"  {ex}", "red"))
   929→        return
   930→
   931→    append_log_entry(
   932→        plan, "cluster_merge", issue_ids=source_ids,
   933→        cluster_name=target, actor="user",
   934→        detail={"source": source, "added": added},
   935→    )
   936→    save_plan(plan)
   937→    print(colorize(
   938→        f"  Merged cluster {source!r} into {target!r}: "
   939→        f"{added} issue(s) added, {len(source_ids)} total moved. Source deleted.",
   940→        "green",
   941→    ))
   942→
   943→
   944→def cmd_cluster_dispatch(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   945→    """Route cluster subcommands."""
   946→    cluster_action = getattr(args, "cluster_action", None)
   947→    dispatch = {
   948→        "create": _cmd_cluster_create,
   949→        "add": _cmd_cluster_add,
   950→        "remove": _cmd_cluster_remove,
   951→        "delete": _cmd_cluster_delete,
   952→        "reorder": _cmd_cluster_reorder,
   953→        "show": _cmd_cluster_show,
   954→        "list": _cmd_cluster_list,
   955→        "update": _cmd_cluster_update,
   956→        "merge": _cmd_cluster_merge,
   957→        "export": _cmd_cluster_export,
   958→        "import": _cmd_cluster_import,
   959→    }
   960→    handler = dispatch.get(cluster_action)
   961→    if handler is None:
   962→        _cmd_cluster_list(args)

     6→def parse_dimensions(args: object) -> set[str] | None:
     7→    """Parse ``--dimensions`` from *args* into a set, or ``None`` if absent."""

1→"""Shared helpers for scan command orchestration."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import logging
     6→from pathlib import Path
     7→
     8→from desloppify import languages as lang_api
     9→from desloppify import state as state_mod
    10→from desloppify.base.discovery.source import (
    11→    DEFAULT_EXCLUSIONS,
    12→    read_file_text,
    13→)
    14→from desloppify.base.discovery.file_paths import count_lines

    17→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

    19→
    20→def audit_excluded_dirs(
    21→    exclusions: tuple[str, ...],
    22→    scanned_files: list[str],
    23→    project_root: Path,
    24→) -> list[dict]:
    25→    """Check if any --exclude directory has zero references from scanned code.
    26→
    27→    Returns issues for directories that appear stale (no file references them).
    28→    """
    29→    if not exclusions:
    30→        return []
    31→
    32→    candidate_dirs = [
    33→        ex_dir
    34→        for ex_dir in exclusions
    35→        if ex_dir not in DEFAULT_EXCLUSIONS and (project_root / ex_dir).is_dir()
    36→    ]
    37→    if not candidate_dirs:
    38→        return []
    39→
    40→    # Read each scanned file once and mark any exclusions observed in content.
    41→    unresolved = set(candidate_dirs)
    42→    for filepath in scanned_files:
    43→        if not unresolved:
    44→            break
    45→        abs_path = (
    46→            filepath if Path(filepath).is_absolute() else str(project_root / filepath)
    47→        )
    48→        content = read_file_text(abs_path)
    49→        if content is None:
    50→            logger.debug(
    51→                "Skipping unreadable file %s while auditing exclusions", filepath
    52→            )
    53→            continue
    54→
    55→        matched = {ex_dir for ex_dir in unresolved if ex_dir in content}
    56→        if matched:
    57→            unresolved.difference_update(matched)
    58→
    59→    stale_issues = []
    60→    for ex_dir in candidate_dirs:
    61→        if ex_dir not in unresolved:
    62→            continue
    63→        stale_issues.append(
    64→            state_mod.make_issue(
    65→                "stale_exclude",
    66→                ex_dir,
    67→                ex_dir,
    68→                tier=4,
    69→                confidence="low",
    70→                summary=(
    71→                    f"Excluded directory '{ex_dir}' has 0 references from scanned code — "
    72→                    "may be stale"
    73→                ),
    74→                detail={"directory": ex_dir, "references": 0},
    75→            )
    76→        )
    77→    return stale_issues
    78→

    80→def collect_codebase_metrics(lang, path: Path) -> dict | None:
    81→    """Collect LOC/file/directory counts for the configured language."""
    82→    if not lang or not lang.file_finder:
    83→        return None
    84→    files = lang.file_finder(path)
    85→    total_loc = 0
    86→    dirs = set()
    87→    for filepath in files:
    88→        try:
    89→            total_loc += count_lines(Path(filepath))
    90→            dirs.add(str(Path(filepath).parent))
    91→        except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
    92→            logger.debug(
    93→                "Skipping unreadable file %s while collecting scan metrics: %s",
    94→                filepath,
    95→                exc,
    96→            )
    97→    return {
    98→        "total_files": len(files),
    99→        "total_loc": total_loc,
   100→        "total_directories": len(dirs),
   101→    }

   104→def resolve_scan_profile(profile: str | None, lang) -> str:
   105→    """Resolve effective scan profile from CLI and language defaults."""
   106→    if profile in {"objective", "full", "ci"}:
   107→        return profile
   108→    default_profile = getattr(lang, "default_scan_profile", "full") if lang else "full"
   109→    if default_profile in {"objective", "full", "ci"}:
   110→        return default_profile
   111→    return "full"
   112→

   114→def effective_include_slow(include_slow: bool, profile: str) -> bool:
   115→    """Determine whether slow phases should run for this profile."""
   116→    return include_slow and profile != "ci"

   127→    """Warn when user explicitly selected a language but scan found zero files."""
   128→    explicit_lang = getattr(args, "lang", None)

   158→def format_delta(value: float, prev: float | None) -> tuple[str, str]:
   159→    """Return (delta_str, color) for a score change."""
   160→    delta = value - prev if prev is not None else 0
   161→    delta_str = f" ({'+' if delta > 0 else ''}{delta:.1f})" if delta != 0 else ""
   162→    color = "green" if delta > 0 else ("red" if delta < 0 else "dim")
   163→    return delta_str, color
   164→
   165→

     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from desloppify import state as state_mod

    10→def coerce_int(value: object, *, default: int) -> int:
    11→    """Best-effort int coercion for config values."""
    12→    if isinstance(value, bool):
    13→        return default
    14→    if isinstance(value, int):
    15→        return value
    16→    if isinstance(value, float):
    17→        return int(value)
    18→    if isinstance(value, str):
    19→        text = value.strip()
    20→        if text:
    21→            try:
    22→                return int(text)
    23→            except ValueError:
    24→                return default
    25→    return default
    26→
    27→
    28→def coerce_float(value: object, *, default: float) -> float:
    29→    """Best-effort float coercion for scan metadata payloads."""
    30→    if isinstance(value, bool):
    31→        return default
    32→    if isinstance(value, int | float):
    33→        return float(value)
    34→    if isinstance(value, str):
    35→        text = value.strip()
    36→        if text:
    37→            try:
    38→                return float(text)
    39→            except ValueError:
    40→                return default
    41→    return default
    42→
    43→
    44→def _coerce_text(value: object) -> str:
    45→    return str(value or "").strip()
    46→
    47→
    48→def _coverage_payload_dict(raw: object) -> dict | None:
    49→    if raw is None:
    50→        return None
    51→    if hasattr(raw, "__dataclass_fields__"):
    52→        return {
    53→            key: getattr(raw, key)
    54→            for key in getattr(raw, "__dataclass_fields__", {})
    55→            if hasattr(raw, key)
    56→        }
    57→    if isinstance(raw, dict):
    58→        return dict(raw)
    59→    return None
    60→
    61→
    62→def normalize_coverage_warning(raw: object) -> DetectorCoverageRecord | None:
    63→    """Normalize runtime coverage payloads to a stable typed shape."""
    64→    payload = _coverage_payload_dict(raw)
    65→    if payload is None:
    66→        return None
    67→
    68→    detector = _coerce_text(payload.get("detector"))
    69→    if not detector:
    70→        return None
    71→
    72→    status = _coerce_text(payload.get("status", "full")).lower() or "full"
    73→    confidence = coerce_float(payload.get("confidence"), default=1.0)
    74→    summary = _coerce_text(payload.get("summary"))
    75→    impact = _coerce_text(payload.get("impact"))
    76→    remediation = _coerce_text(payload.get("remediation"))
    77→    tool = _coerce_text(payload.get("tool"))
    78→    reason = _coerce_text(payload.get("reason"))
    79→
    80→    return {
    81→        "detector": detector,
    82→        "status": "reduced" if status == "reduced" or confidence < 1.0 else "full",
    83→        "confidence": max(0.0, min(1.0, confidence)),
    84→        "summary": summary,
    85→        "impact": impact,
    86→        "remediation": remediation,
    87→        "tool": tool,
    88→        "reason": reason,
    89→    }
    90→
    91→
    92→def seed_runtime_coverage_warnings(lang: LangRun | None) -> list[DetectorCoverageRecord]:
    93→    """Collect preflight scan-coverage warnings and seed runtime coverage state."""
    94→    if lang is None:
    95→        return []
    96→
    97→    warnings: list[DetectorCoverageRecord] = []
    98→    raw_entries = lang.scan_coverage_prerequisites()
    99→    for raw in raw_entries:
   100→        normalized = normalize_coverage_warning(raw)
   101→        if normalized is None:
   102→            continue
   103→        detector = str(normalized.get("detector", "")).strip()
   104→        if detector:
   105→            lang.detector_coverage[detector] = dict(normalized)
   106→        if normalized.get("status") == "reduced":
   107→            warnings.append(dict(normalized))
   108→    lang.coverage_warnings = warnings
   109→    return warnings
   110→
   111→
   112→def persist_scan_coverage(
   113→    state: state_mod.StateModel,
   114→    lang: LangRun | None,
   115→) -> None:
   116→    """Persist detector coverage confidence for the active language scan."""
   117→    if lang is None:
   118→        return
   119→
   120→    detectors: dict[str, DetectorCoverageRecord] = {}
   121→    for detector, payload in lang.detector_coverage.items():
   122→        normalized = normalize_coverage_warning(payload)
   123→        if normalized is None:
   124→            continue
   125→        detectors[str(detector)] = normalized
   126→
   127→    warnings: list[DetectorCoverageRecord] = []
   128→    for warning in lang.coverage_warnings:
   129→        normalized_warning = normalize_coverage_warning(warning)
   130→        if normalized_warning is not None and normalized_warning.get("status") == "reduced":
   131→            warnings.append(normalized_warning)
   132→
   133→    reduced_entries = [
   134→        payload
   135→        for payload in detectors.values()
   136→        if payload.get("status") == "reduced"
   137→    ]
   138→    if reduced_entries:
   139→        confidence = min(
   140→            coerce_float(entry.get("confidence"), default=1.0)
   141→            for entry in reduced_entries
   142→        )
   143→        status = "reduced"
   144→    else:
   145→        confidence = 1.0
   146→        status = "full"
   147→
   148→    state.setdefault("scan_coverage", {})[lang.name] = {
   149→        "status": status,
   150→        "confidence": round(max(0.0, min(1.0, confidence)), 2),
   151→        "detectors": detectors,
   152→        "warnings": warnings,
   153→        "updated_at": state_mod.utc_now(),
   154→    }
   155→

   160→    "normalize_coverage_warning",
   161→    "persist_scan_coverage",
   162→    "seed_runtime_coverage_warnings",
   163→]

    24→def _cmd_commit_log_status(plan: dict) -> None:
    25→    """Show full commit-log status: uncommitted, committed, git context."""
    26→    git = detect_git_context()
    27→    summary = commit_tracking_summary(plan)
    28→
    29→    print(colorize("  Commit Tracking Status", "bold"))
    30→    print(colorize("  " + "─" * 40, "dim"))
    31→
    32→    if git.available:
    33→        print(f"  Branch:  {git.branch or '(detached)'}")
    34→        print(f"  HEAD:    {git.head_sha or '?'}")
    35→        if git.has_uncommitted:
    36→            print(colorize("  Working tree has uncommitted changes", "yellow"))
    37→    else:
    38→        print(colorize("  Git: not available", "dim"))
    39→
    40→    config = load_config()
    41→    pr = config.get("commit_pr", 0)
    42→    if pr:
    43→        print(f"  PR:      #{pr}")
    44→
    45→    uncommitted = get_uncommitted_issues(plan)
    46→    print(f"\n  Uncommitted:  {summary['uncommitted']} issue(s)")
    47→    for fid in uncommitted[:10]:
    48→        print(f"    {fid}")
    49→    if len(uncommitted) > 10:
    50→        print(f"    ... and {len(uncommitted) - 10} more")
    51→
    52→    commit_log = plan.get("commit_log", [])
    53→    committed_count = sum(len(r.get("issue_ids", [])) for r in commit_log)
    54→    print(f"  Committed:    {committed_count} issue(s) in {len(commit_log)} commit(s)")
    55→
    56→    if not uncommitted and not commit_log:
    57→        print(colorize("\n  No commit tracking data yet.", "dim"))
    58→        print(colorize("  Resolve issues with `desloppify resolve` or `desloppify plan resolve` to start.", "dim"))
    59→
    60→
    61→def _cmd_commit_log_record(args: argparse.Namespace, plan: dict) -> None:
    62→    """Record a commit: capture HEAD, move uncommitted → committed, update PR."""
    63→    sha = getattr(args, "sha", None)
    64→    branch = getattr(args, "branch", None)
    65→    note = getattr(args, "note", None)
    66→    only_patterns: list[str] | None = getattr(args, "only", None)
    67→
    68→    # Auto-detect from git if not overridden
    69→    if not sha or not branch:
    70→        git = detect_git_context()
    71→        if git.available:
    72→            sha = sha or git.head_sha
    73→            branch = branch or git.branch
    74→        elif not sha:
    75→            print(colorize("  Cannot detect HEAD. Use --sha to specify.", "red"))
    76→            return
    77→
    78→    # Determine which issues to record
    79→    uncommitted = get_uncommitted_issues(plan)
    80→    if not uncommitted:
    81→        print(colorize("  No uncommitted issues to record.", "yellow"))
    82→        return
    83→
    84→    if only_patterns:
    85→        issue_ids = filter_issue_ids_by_pattern(uncommitted, only_patterns)
    86→        if not issue_ids:
    87→            print(colorize("  No uncommitted issues match --only patterns.", "yellow"))
    88→            return
    89→    else:
    90→        issue_ids = None  # record all
    91→
    92→    record = record_commit(
    93→        plan,
    94→        sha=sha,
    95→        branch=branch,
    96→        issue_ids=issue_ids,
    97→        note=note,
    98→    )
    99→    append_log_entry(
   100→        plan,
   101→        "commit_record",
   102→        issue_ids=record["issue_ids"],
   103→        actor="user",
   104→        note=note,
   105→        detail={"sha": sha, "branch": branch},
   106→    )
   107→    save_plan(plan)
   108→
   109→    recorded = len(record["issue_ids"])
   110→    print(colorize(f"  Recorded commit {sha} with {recorded} issue(s).", "green"))
   111→    if note:
   112→        print(colorize(f"  Note: {note}", "dim"))
   113→
   114→    # Update PR if configured
   115→    config = load_config()
   116→    pr_number = config.get("commit_pr", 0)
   117→    if pr_number:
   118→        try:
   119→            state = state_mod.load_state()
   120→            body = generate_pr_body(plan, state)
   121→            ok = update_pr_body(pr_number, body)
   122→            if ok:
   123→                print(colorize(f"  PR #{pr_number} description updated.", "green"))
   124→            else:
   125→                print(colorize(f"  Could not update PR #{pr_number} (gh may not be available).", "yellow"))
   126→        except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError) as exc:
   127→            print(

   129→                file=sys.stderr,
   130→            )

   133→def _cmd_commit_log_history(args: argparse.Namespace, plan: dict) -> None:
   134→    """Show commit records."""
   135→    top = getattr(args, "top", 10)
   136→    commit_log = plan.get("commit_log", [])
   137→
   138→    if not commit_log:

   142→    print(colorize("  Commit History", "bold"))
   143→    print(colorize("  " + "─" * 40, "dim"))
   144→
   145→    shown = commit_log[-top:] if top else commit_log
   146→    for record in reversed(shown):
   147→        sha = record.get("sha", "?")[:7]
   148→        branch = record.get("branch", "")
   149→        issue_ids = record.get("issue_ids", [])
   150→        note = record.get("note", "")

   152→
   153→        header = f"  {sha}"
   154→        if branch:
   155→            header += f" ({branch})"
   156→        header += f" — {len(issue_ids)} issue(s)"
   157→        if recorded_at:
   158→            header += f"  [{recorded_at[:16]}]"
   159→        print(header)
   160→        if note:
   161→            print(colorize(f"    Note: {note}", "dim"))
   162→        for fid in issue_ids[:5]:
   163→            print(f"    - {fid}")
   164→        if len(issue_ids) > 5:
   165→            print(f"    ... and {len(issue_ids) - 5} more")
   166→
   167→
   168→def _cmd_commit_log_pr(plan: dict) -> None:
   169→    """Print PR body markdown to stdout (dry run)."""
   170→    try:
   171→        state = state_mod.load_state()
   172→    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError):
   173→        state = {"issues": {}}
   174→
   175→    body = generate_pr_body(plan, state)
   176→    print(body)
   177→
   178→
   179→_COMMIT_LOG_HANDLERS = {
   180→    "record": _cmd_commit_log_record,
   181→    "history": _cmd_commit_log_history,
   182→    "pr": lambda _args, plan: _cmd_commit_log_pr(plan),
   183→}
   184→
   185→
   186→def cmd_commit_log_dispatch(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   187→    """Route commit-log subcommands."""
   188→    config = load_config()
   189→    if not config.get("commit_tracking_enabled", True):
   190→        print(colorize("  Commit tracking is disabled. Enable with: desloppify config set commit_tracking_enabled true", "yellow"))
   191→        return
   192→
   193→    plan = load_plan()
   194→    action = getattr(args, "commit_log_action", None)
   195→    handler = _COMMIT_LOG_HANDLERS.get(action)
   196→    if handler is None:
   197→        _cmd_commit_log_status(plan)
   198→        return
   199→    handler(args, plan)
   200→
   201→
   202→__all__ = ["cmd_commit_log_dispatch"]
   203→

    22→def detail_dict(item: WorkQueueItem | dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    23→    """Return issue detail as a dict; tolerate legacy/non-dict payloads."""
    24→    detail = item.get("detail")
    25→    return detail if isinstance(detail, dict) else {}
    26→
    27→
    28→def status_matches(item_status: str, status_filter: str) -> bool:
    29→    return status_filter == "all" or item_status == status_filter
    30→
    31→
    32→def is_subjective_issue(item: WorkQueueItem | dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    33→    detector = item.get("detector")
    34→    if detector in {"subjective_assessment"}:
    35→        return True
    36→    if detector == "holistic_review":
    37→        return True
    38→    return False
    39→
    40→
    41→def is_review_issue(item: WorkQueueItem | dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    42→    return item.get("detector") == "review"
    43→
    44→
    45→def is_subjective_queue_item(item: WorkQueueItem | dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    46→    """True for subjective work items, including collapsed subjective clusters."""
    47→    if item.get("kind") == "subjective_dimension":
    48→        return True
    49→    if item.get("kind") == "cluster":
    50→        members = item.get("members", [])
    51→        return bool(members) and all(
    52→            m.get("kind") == "subjective_dimension" for m in members
    53→        )
    54→    return False
    55→
    56→
    57→def review_issue_weight(item: WorkQueueItem | dict[str, Any]) -> float:
    58→    """Return review issue weight aligned with issues list ordering."""
    59→    confidence = str(item.get("confidence", "low")).lower()
    60→    weight_by_confidence = {
    61→        "high": 1.0,
    62→        "medium": 0.7,
    63→        "low": 0.3,
    64→    }
    65→    weight = weight_by_confidence.get(confidence, 0.3)
    66→    if detail_dict(item).get("holistic"):
    67→        weight *= 10.0
    68→    return float(weight)
    69→
    70→
    71→def scope_matches(item: WorkQueueItem | dict[str, Any], scope: str | None) -> bool:
    72→    """Apply show-style pattern matching against a queue item."""
    73→    if not scope:
    74→        return True
    75→
    76→    item_id = item.get("id", "")
    77→    detector = item.get("detector", "")
    78→    filepath = item.get("file", "")
    79→    summary = item.get("summary", "")
    80→    dimension = detail_dict(item).get("dimension_name", "")
    81→    kind = item.get("kind", "")
    82→
    83→    if "*" in scope:
    84→        return any(
    85→            fnmatch(candidate, scope)
    86→            for candidate in (item_id, filepath, detector, dimension, summary)
    87→        )
    88→
    89→    if "::" in scope:
    90→        return item_id.startswith(scope)
    91→
    92→    lowered = scope.lower()

    94→        return (
    95→            lowered in item_id.lower()
    96→            or lowered in dimension.lower()
    97→            or lowered in summary.lower()
    98→        )
    99→
   100→    # Hash suffix: 8+ hex chars matches the tail segment of a issue ID.
   101→    if len(lowered) >= 8 and re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]+", lowered):
   102→        return item_id.lower().endswith("::" + lowered)
   103→
   104→    return (
   105→        detector == scope
   106→        or filepath == scope
   107→        or filepath.startswith(scope.rstrip("/") + "/")
   108→    )

   110→
   111→def workflow_stage_name(item: WorkQueueItem | dict[str, Any]) -> str:
   112→    """Resolve the triage stage name from an item, with fallbacks."""
   113→    stage_name = str(item.get("stage_name", "")).strip()
   114→    if stage_name:
   115→        return stage_name
   116→
   117→    stage_name = str(detail_dict(item).get("stage", "")).strip()
   118→    if stage_name:
   119→        return stage_name
   120→
   121→    item_id = str(item.get("id", "")).strip()
   122→    if item_id.startswith("triage::"):
   123→        return item_id.split("::", 1)[1]
   124→    return ""
   125→
   126→
   127→def slugify(text: str) -> str:
   128→    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9_]+", "_", text.lower()).strip("_")
   129→
   130→
   131→def supported_fixers_for_item(
   132→    state: StateModel, item: WorkQueueItem
   133→) -> set[str] | None:
   134→    """Return supported fixers for an item's language when known."""
   135→    lang = str(item.get("lang", "") or "").strip()
   136→    if not lang:
   137→        return None
   138→
   139→    caps_obj = state.get("lang_capabilities")
   140→    if not isinstance(caps_obj, dict):
   141→        return None
   142→    lang_caps_obj = caps_obj.get(lang)
   143→    if not isinstance(lang_caps_obj, dict):
   144→        return None
   145→
   146→    fixers = lang_caps_obj.get("fixers")
   147→    if not isinstance(fixers, list):
   148→        return None
   149→    return {fixer for fixer in fixers if isinstance(fixer, str)}
   150→
   151→
   152→def primary_command_for_issue(
   153→    item: WorkQueueItem, *, supported_fixers: set[str] | None = None
   154→) -> str:
   155→    detector = item.get("detector", "")
   156→    meta = DETECTORS.get(detector)
   157→    if meta and meta.action_type == "auto_fix" and meta.fixers:
   158→        available_fixers = [
   159→            fixer
   160→            for fixer in meta.fixers
   161→            if supported_fixers is not None and fixer in supported_fixers
   162→        ]
   163→        if available_fixers:
   164→            return f"desloppify autofix {available_fixers[0]} --dry-run"
   165→    if detector == "subjective_review":
   166→        from desloppify.intelligence.integrity import (
   167→            is_holistic_subjective_issue,  # cycle-break: helpers.py ↔ integrity.py
   168→        )
   169→
   170→        if is_holistic_subjective_issue(item):
   171→            return "desloppify review --prepare"
   172→        return "desloppify show subjective"
   173→    return f'desloppify plan resolve "{item.get("id", "")}" --note "<what you did>" --confirm'

1→"""Runtime compatibility governance matrix and helper predicates.
     2→
     3→This module is the single source of truth for import-boundary policy:
     4→- public runtime modules (stable entry surfaces),
     5→- deprecated compatibility modules (removal candidates),
     6→- private modules (internal implementation details).
     7→"""
     8→
     9→from __future__ import annotations
    10→
    11→from collections.abc import Iterable
    12→
    13→# Public package roots intended for runtime imports across the codebase.
    14→PUBLIC_RUNTIME_ROOTS: tuple[str, ...] = (
    15→    "desloppify.app",
    16→    "desloppify.base",
    17→    "desloppify.engine",
    18→    "desloppify.intelligence",
    19→    "desloppify.languages",
    20→)
    21→
    22→# Compatibility shims removed from runtime usage; these must not be reintroduced.
    23→SOFT_DEPRECATED_MODULES: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
    24→    {
    25→        "desloppify.utils",
    26→        "desloppify.file_discovery",
    27→        "desloppify.base.output_api",
    28→        "desloppify.base.output_contract",
    29→        "desloppify.base.text.text_api",
    30→        "desloppify.base.discovery.api",
    31→        "desloppify.base.discovery.path_io",
    32→    }
    33→)
    34→
    35→SOFT_DEPRECATED_SHORT_IMPORTS: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
    36→    {
    37→        "utils",
    38→        "file_discovery",
    39→    }
    40→)
    41→
    42→# Private internals: only code under these roots may import them directly.
    43→PRIVATE_MODULE_PREFIXES: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    44→PRIVATE_ALLOWED_IMPORTER_PREFIXES: tuple[str, ...] = ("desloppify.base",)
    45→
    46→
    47→def is_soft_deprecated_module(module: str) -> bool:
    48→    """Return True when module is a soft-deprecated compatibility surface."""
    49→    return module in SOFT_DEPRECATED_MODULES
    50→
    51→
    52→def is_private_module(module: str) -> bool:
    53→    """Return True when module path belongs to a private internal namespace."""
    54→    normalized = module.strip()
    55→    if not normalized:
    56→        return False
    57→    for prefix in PRIVATE_MODULE_PREFIXES:
    58→        if normalized == prefix or normalized.startswith(f"{prefix}."):
    59→            return True
    60→    return False
    61→
    62→
    63→def importer_can_access_private(importer_module: str) -> bool:
    64→    """Return True when importer module is allowed to reference private APIs."""
    65→    normalized = importer_module.strip()
    66→    if not normalized:
    67→        return False
    68→    for prefix in PRIVATE_ALLOWED_IMPORTER_PREFIXES:
    69→        if normalized == prefix or normalized.startswith(f"{prefix}."):
    70→            return True
    71→    return False
    72→
    73→
    74→def iter_soft_deprecated_module_paths() -> Iterable[str]:
    75→    """Yield python-module relative paths for deprecated compatibility modules."""
    76→    for module in sorted(SOFT_DEPRECATED_MODULES):
    77→        parts = module.split(".")
    78→        yield "/".join(parts) + ".py"
    79→
    80→
    81→__all__ = [
    82→    "PRIVATE_ALLOWED_IMPORTER_PREFIXES",
    83→    "PRIVATE_MODULE_PREFIXES",
    84→    "PUBLIC_RUNTIME_ROOTS",
    85→    "SOFT_DEPRECATED_MODULES",
    86→    "SOFT_DEPRECATED_SHORT_IMPORTS",
    87→    "importer_can_access_private",
    88→    "is_private_module",
    89→    "is_soft_deprecated_module",
    90→    "iter_soft_deprecated_module_paths",
    91→]
    92→

   170→# Skip / unskip
   171→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   172→
   173→
   174→def _validate_skip_requirements(
   175→    *,
   176→    kind: str,
   177→    attestation: str | None,
   178→    note: str | None,
   179→) -> bool:
   180→    if not skip_kind_requires_attestation(kind):
   181→        return True
   182→    if not validate_attestation(attestation):
   183→        show_attestation_requirement(
   184→            "Permanent skip" if kind == "permanent" else "False positive",
   185→            attestation,
   186→            ATTEST_EXAMPLE,
   187→        )
   188→        return False
   189→    if skip_kind_requires_note(kind) and not note:
   190→        print(
   191→            colorize("  --permanent requires --note to explain the decision.", "yellow"),
   192→            file=sys.stderr,
   193→        )
   194→        return False
   195→    return True
   196→
   197→
   198→def _apply_state_skip_resolution(
   199→    *,
   200→    kind: str,
   201→    state_file: Path | None,
   202→    issue_ids: list[str],
   203→    note: str | None,
   204→    attestation: str | None,
   205→) -> dict | None:
   206→    status = skip_kind_state_status(kind)
   207→    if status is None:
   208→        return None
   209→    state_data = state_mod.load_state(state_file)
   210→    for fid in issue_ids:
   211→        state_mod.resolve_issues(
   212→            state_data,
   213→            fid,
   214→            status,
   215→            note or "",
   216→            attestation=attestation,
   217→        )
   218→    return state_data
   219→
   220→
   221→def cmd_plan_skip(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   222→    """Skip issues — unified command for temporary/permanent/false-positive."""
   223→    runtime = command_runtime(args)
   224→    state = runtime.state
   225→    if not require_completed_scan(state):
   226→        return
   227→
   228→    patterns: list[str] = getattr(args, "patterns", [])
   229→    reason: str | None = getattr(args, "reason", None)
   230→    review_after: int | None = getattr(args, "review_after", None)
   231→    permanent: bool = getattr(args, "permanent", False)
   232→    false_positive: bool = getattr(args, "false_positive", False)
   233→    note: str | None = getattr(args, "note", None)
   234→    attestation: str | None = getattr(args, "attest", None)
   235→
   236→    kind = skip_kind_from_flags(permanent=permanent, false_positive=false_positive)
   237→    if not _validate_skip_requirements(
   238→        kind=kind,
   239→        attestation=attestation,
   240→        note=note,
   241→    ):
   242→        return
   243→
   244→    state_file = runtime.state_path
   245→    plan_file = _plan_file_for_state(state_file)
   246→    plan = load_plan(plan_file)
   247→    issue_ids = resolve_ids_from_patterns(state, patterns, plan=plan)
   248→    if not issue_ids:
   249→        print(colorize("  No matching issues found.", "yellow"))
   250→        return
   251→
   252→    # Bulk skip guard — prevent agents from draining the queue in one shot
   253→    if len(issue_ids) > _BULK_SKIP_THRESHOLD:
   254→        print(colorize(
   255→            f"  Bulk skip: {len(issue_ids)} items will be removed from the active queue.",
   256→            "yellow",
   257→        ), file=sys.stderr)
   258→        if not getattr(args, "confirm", False):
   259→            raise CommandError(
   260→                f"Skipping {len(issue_ids)} items requires --confirm. "
   261→                "Review the items first, or skip individually."
   262→            )
   263→
   264→    # For permanent/false_positive: delegate to state layer for score impact
   265→    state_data = _apply_state_skip_resolution(
   266→        kind=kind,
   267→        state_file=state_file,
   268→        issue_ids=issue_ids,
   269→        note=note,
   270→        attestation=attestation,
   271→    )
   272→
   273→    scan_count = state.get("scan_count", 0)
   274→    count = skip_items(
   275→        plan,
   276→        issue_ids,
   277→        kind=kind,
   278→        reason=reason,
   279→        note=note,
   280→        attestation=attestation,
   281→        review_after=review_after,
   282→        scan_count=scan_count,
   283→    )
   284→
   285→    # Log the skip action
   286→    append_log_entry(
   287→        plan,
   288→        "skip",
   289→        issue_ids=issue_ids,
   290→        actor="user",
   291→        note=note,
   292→        detail={"kind": kind, "reason": reason},
   293→    )
   294→    if state_data is not None:
   295→        _save_plan_state_transactional(
   296→            plan=plan,
   297→            plan_path=plan_file,
   298→            state_data=state_data,
   299→            state_path_value=state_file,
   300→        )
   301→    else:
   302→        save_plan(plan, plan_file)
   303→
   304→    print(colorize(f"  {SKIP_KIND_LABELS[kind]} {count} item(s).", "green"))
   305→    if review_after:
   306→        print(colorize(f"  Will re-surface after {review_after} scan(s).", "dim"))
   307→    print_user_message(
   308→        "Hey — if skipping was the right call, just continue with"
   309→        " what you were doing. If you think a broader re-triage is"
   310→        " needed, use `desloppify plan triage`. Run `desloppify"
   311→        " plan --help` to see all available plan tools. Otherwise"
   312→        " no need to reply, just keep going."
   313→    )
   314→
   315→
   316→def cmd_plan_unskip(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   317→    """Unskip issues — bring back to queue."""
   318→    runtime = command_runtime(args)
   319→    state = runtime.state
   320→    if not require_completed_scan(state):
   321→        return
   322→
   323→    patterns: list[str] = getattr(args, "patterns", [])
   324→
   325→    state_file = runtime.state_path
   326→    plan_file = _plan_file_for_state(state_file)
   327→    plan = load_plan(plan_file)
   328→    # For unskip we need to match against all statuses (skipped items may be wontfix/fp)
   329→    issue_ids = resolve_ids_from_patterns(state, patterns, plan=plan, status_filter="all")
   330→    if not issue_ids:
   331→        print(colorize("  No matching issues found.", "yellow"))
   332→        return
   333→
   334→    include_protected = bool(getattr(args, "force", False))
   335→    count, need_reopen, protected_kept = unskip_items(
   336→        plan, issue_ids, include_protected=include_protected,
   337→    )
   338→    unskipped_ids = [fid for fid in issue_ids if fid not in protected_kept]
   339→    append_log_entry(
   340→        plan, "unskip", issue_ids=unskipped_ids, actor="user",
   341→        detail={"need_reopen": need_reopen},
   342→    )
   343→
   344→    # Reopen permanent/false_positive items in state
   345→    reopened: list[str] = []
   346→    if need_reopen:
   347→        state_data = state_mod.load_state(state_file)
   348→        for fid in need_reopen:
   349→            reopened.extend(state_mod.resolve_issues(state_data, fid, "open"))
   350→        _save_plan_state_transactional(
   351→            plan=plan,
   352→            plan_path=plan_file,
   353→            state_data=state_data,
   354→            state_path_value=state_file,
   355→        )
   356→        print(colorize(f"  Reopened {len(reopened)} issue(s) in state.", "dim"))
   357→    else:
   358→        save_plan(plan, plan_file)
   359→
   360→    print(colorize(f"  Unskipped {count} item(s) — back in queue.", "green"))
   361→    if protected_kept:
   362→        print(colorize(
   363→            f"  Kept {len(protected_kept)} protected skip(s) "
   364→            f"(permanent/false_positive with notes). Use --force to override.",
   365→            "yellow",
   366→        ))
   367→
   368→
   369→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   370→# Reopen
   371→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   372→
   373→def cmd_plan_reopen(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   374→    """Reopen resolved issues from plan context."""
   375→    patterns: list[str] = getattr(args, "patterns", [])
   376→
   377→    raw_state_path = state_path(args)
   378→    state_file = raw_state_path if isinstance(raw_state_path, Path) else Path(raw_state_path) if raw_state_path else None
   379→    state_data = state_mod.load_state(state_file)
   380→    plan_file = _plan_file_for_state(state_file)
   381→
   382→    reopened: list[str] = []
   383→    for pattern in patterns:
   384→        reopened.extend(
   385→            state_mod.resolve_issues(state_data, pattern, "open")
   386→        )
   387→
   388→    if not reopened:
   389→        print(colorize("  No resolved issues matching: " + " ".join(patterns), "yellow"))
   390→        return
   391→
   392→    # Remove from skipped if present, and ensure all reopened IDs are in queue
   393→    plan = load_plan(plan_file)
   394→
   395→    # Remove from commit tracking uncommitted list
   396→    purge_uncommitted_ids(plan, reopened)
   397→
   398→    skipped = plan.get("skipped", {})
   399→    count = 0
   400→    order = set(plan.get("queue_order", []))
   401→    for fid in reopened:
   402→        if fid in skipped:
   403→            skipped.pop(fid)
   404→            count += 1
   405→        if fid not in order:
   406→            plan["queue_order"].append(fid)
   407→            order.add(fid)
   408→            count += 1
   409→    append_log_entry(
   410→        plan, "reopen", issue_ids=reopened, actor="user",
   411→    )
   412→    _save_plan_state_transactional(
   413→        plan=plan,
   414→        plan_path=plan_file,
   415→        state_data=state_data,
   416→        state_path_value=state_file,
   417→    )
   418→
   419→    print(colorize(f"  Reopened {len(reopened)} issue(s).", "green"))
   420→    if count:
   421→        print(colorize("  Plan updated: items moved back to queue.", "dim"))
   422→
   423→
   424→_CLUSTER_INDIVIDUAL_THRESHOLD = 10
   425→
   426→
   427→def _check_cluster_guard(patterns: list[str], plan: dict, state: dict) -> bool:
   428→    """Return True if blocked by cluster guard, False if OK to proceed."""
   429→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   430→    issues = state.get("issues", {})
   431→    for pattern in patterns:
   432→        if pattern in clusters:
   433→            cluster = clusters[pattern]
   434→            # Filter to alive issues only — stale IDs should not count
   435→            ids = [
   436→                fid for fid in cluster.get("issue_ids", [])
   437→                if fid in issues and issues[fid].get("status") == "open"
   438→            ]
   439→            if len(ids) == 0:
   440→                print(colorize(
   441→                    f"\n  Cluster '{pattern}' is empty — add items before marking it done.\n",
   442→                    "yellow",
   443→                ))
   444→                print(colorize(
   445→                    f"  Use: desloppify plan cluster add {pattern} <issue-id>",
   446→                    "dim",
   447→                ))
   448→                return True  # blocked
   449→            if len(ids) <= _CLUSTER_INDIVIDUAL_THRESHOLD:
   450→                _print_cluster_guard(pattern, ids, state)
   451→                return True  # blocked
   452→    return False  # OK
   453→
   454→
   455→def _print_cluster_guard(cluster_name: str, issue_ids: list[str], state: dict) -> None:
   456→    issues = state.get("issues", {})
   457→    print(colorize(
   458→        f"\n  Cluster '{cluster_name}' has {len(issue_ids)} item(s) — mark them done individually first:\n",
   459→        "yellow",
   460→    ))
   461→    for fid in issue_ids:
   462→        f = issues.get(fid, {})
   463→        summary = f.get("summary", "(no summary)")[:80]
   464→        detector = f.get("detector", "?")
   465→        print(f"    {fid}  [{detector}]  {summary}")
   466→    print(colorize(
   467→        "\n  Use: desloppify resolve <id> --status fixed --note '...' --attest '...'",
   468→        "dim",
   469→    ))
   470→    print(colorize(
   471→        "  Or mark each resolved: desloppify plan resolve <id> --note '...' --confirm\n",
   472→        "dim",
   473→    ))
   474→
   475→
   476→def _is_synthetic_id(fid: str) -> bool:
   477→    """Return True if the ID is a synthetic workflow/triage item, not a real issue."""
   478→    return fid.startswith("triage::") or fid.startswith("workflow::") or fid.startswith("subjective::")
   479→
   480→
   481→def _resolve_synthetic_ids(patterns: list[str]) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:
   482→    """Separate synthetic IDs from real issue patterns.
   483→
   484→    Returns (synthetic_ids, remaining_patterns).
   485→    """
   486→    synthetic = [p for p in patterns if _is_synthetic_id(p)]
   487→    remaining = [p for p in patterns if not _is_synthetic_id(p)]
   488→    return synthetic, remaining
   489→
   490→
   491→def _blocked_triage_stages(plan: dict) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
   492→    """Return ``{stage_id: [blocked_by_ids]}`` for triage stages that can't run yet.
   493→
   494→    Uses the dependency graph and confirmed-stage metadata directly —
   495→    no state needed, no queue item construction.
   496→    """
   497→    order_set = set(plan.get("queue_order", []))
   498→    present = order_set & TRIAGE_IDS
   499→    if not present:
   500→        return {}
   501→
   502→    confirmed = set(plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {}).get("triage_stages", {}).keys())
   503→    stage_names = ("observe", "reflect", "organize", "enrich", "sense-check", "commit")
   504→
   505→    blocked: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
   506→    for sid, name in zip(TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS, stage_names, strict=False):
   507→        if sid not in present or name in confirmed:
   508→            continue
   509→        deps = TRIAGE_STAGE_DEPENDENCIES.get(name, set())
   510→        unmet = sorted(
   511→            f"triage::{dep}" for dep in deps
   512→            if f"triage::{dep}" in present and dep not in confirmed
   513→        )
   514→        if unmet:
   515→            blocked[sid] = unmet
   516→    return blocked
   517→
   518→
   519→def cmd_plan_resolve(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   520→    """Mark issues as fixed — delegates to cmd_resolve for rich UX."""
   521→    patterns: list[str] = getattr(args, "patterns", [])
   522→    attestation: str | None = getattr(args, "attest", None)
   523→    note: str | None = getattr(args, "note", None)
   524→
   525→    # --confirm: auto-generate attestation from --note
   526→    if getattr(args, "confirm", False):
   527→        if not note:
   528→            print(colorize("  --confirm requires --note to describe what you did.", "red"))
   529→            return
   530→        attestation = f"I have actually {note} and I am not gaming the score."
   531→        args.attest = attestation
   532→
   533→    # Handle synthetic IDs (triage::*, workflow::*, subjective::*) directly
   534→    synthetic_ids, real_patterns = _resolve_synthetic_ids(patterns)
   535→    if synthetic_ids:
   536→        plan = load_plan()
   537→        # Validate triage dependency chain
   538→        blocked_map = _blocked_triage_stages(plan)
   539→        for sid in synthetic_ids:
   540→            if sid in blocked_map:
   541→                deps = ", ".join(b.replace("triage::", "") for b in blocked_map[sid])
   542→                print(colorize(f"  Cannot resolve {sid} — blocked by: {deps}", "red"))
   543→                print(colorize("  Complete those stages first, or use --force-resolve to override.", "dim"))
   544→                if not getattr(args, "force_resolve", False):
   545→                    return
   546→
   547→        # Gate workflow items behind triage completion
   548→        GATED_WORKFLOW_IDS = {WORKFLOW_SCORE_CHECKPOINT_ID, WORKFLOW_CREATE_PLAN_ID}
   549→        gated_ids = [sid for sid in synthetic_ids if sid in GATED_WORKFLOW_IDS]
   550→        if gated_ids:
   551→            force = getattr(args, "force_resolve", False)
   552→            meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   553→            # Triage is complete if last_completed_at is set (stages archive on --complete)
   554→            triage_ever_completed = bool(meta.get("last_completed_at"))
   555→            if triage_ever_completed:
   556→                # --complete archives stages and sets last_completed_at → all 4 done
   557→                missing: set[str] = set()
   558→            else:
   559→                confirmed_stages = set(meta.get("triage_stages", {}).keys())
   560→                required_stages = {"observe", "reflect", "organize", "enrich", "commit"}
   561→                missing = required_stages - confirmed_stages
   562→
   563→            if missing and not force:
   564→                # Auto-inject triage stages if not already in queue
   565→                if not has_triage_in_queue(plan):
   566→                    inject_triage_stages(plan)
   567→                    meta.setdefault("triage_stages", {})
   568→                    plan["epic_triage_meta"] = meta
   569→                    save_plan(plan)
   570→
   571→                # Print targeted error based on which stage is next
   572→                stage_order = ["observe", "reflect", "organize", "enrich", "commit"]
   573→                next_stage = next((s for s in stage_order if s in missing), "observe")
   574→
   575→                for wid in gated_ids:
   576→                    print(colorize(f"  Cannot resolve {wid} — triage not complete.", "red"))
   577→                print()
   578→
   579→                if next_stage == "observe":
   580→                    print(colorize("  You must analyze the findings before resolving this.", "yellow"))
   581→                    print(colorize("  Start by examining themes, root causes, and contradictions:", "dim"))
   582→                    print(colorize('    desloppify plan triage --stage observe --report "..."', "dim"))
   583→                    print()
   584→                    print(colorize("  The report must be 100+ chars describing what you found.", "dim"))
   585→                elif next_stage == "reflect":
   586→                    print(colorize("  Observe is done. Now compare against previously completed work:", "yellow"))
   587→                    print(colorize('    desloppify plan triage --stage reflect --report "..."', "dim"))
   588→                    print()
   589→                    print(colorize("  The report must mention recurring dimensions if any exist.", "dim"))
   590→                elif next_stage == "organize":
   591→                    print(colorize("  Reflect is done. Now create clusters and prioritize:", "yellow"))
   592→                    print(colorize('    desloppify plan cluster create <name> --description "..."', "dim"))
   593→                    print(colorize("    desloppify plan cluster add <name> <issue-patterns>", "dim"))
   594→                    print(colorize('    desloppify plan cluster update <name> --steps "step1" "step2"', "dim"))
   595→                    print(colorize('    desloppify plan triage --stage organize --report "..."', "dim"))
   596→                    print()
   597→                    print(colorize("  All manual clusters must have descriptions and action_steps.", "dim"))
   598→                elif next_stage == "enrich":
   599→                    print(colorize("  Organize is done. Now enrich steps with detail and issue refs:", "yellow"))
   600→                    print(colorize('    desloppify plan cluster update <name> --update-step N --detail "sub-details"', "dim"))
   601→                    print(colorize('    desloppify plan triage --stage enrich --report "..."', "dim"))
   602→                elif next_stage == "commit":
   603→                    print(colorize("  Enrich is done. Finalize the execution plan:", "yellow"))
   604→                    print(colorize('    desloppify plan triage --complete --strategy "..."', "dim"))
   605→
   606→                print()
   607→                print(colorize(f"  Remaining stages: {', '.join(sorted(missing))}", "dim"))
   608→                print(colorize(
   609→                    "  To skip triage: --force-resolve --note 'reason for skipping triage'",
   610→                    "dim",
   611→                ))
   612→
   613→                # Log the blocked attempt
   614→                append_log_entry(
   615→                    plan, "workflow_blocked",
   616→                    issue_ids=gated_ids, actor="user",
   617→                    note=note,
   618→                    detail={"missing_stages": sorted(missing), "next_stage": next_stage},
   619→                )
   620→                save_plan(plan)
   621→                return
   622→
   623→            if missing and force:
   624→                # Force-resolve: require substantial note, log prominently
   625→                if not note or len(note.strip()) < 50:
   626→                    print(colorize(
   627→                        f"  --force-resolve still requires --note (min 50 chars) explaining "
   628→                        f"why you're skipping triage.",
   629→                        "red",
   630→                    ))
   631→                    return
   632→                print(colorize(
   633→                    "  WARNING: Skipping triage requirement — this is logged.",
   634→                    "yellow",
   635→                ))
   636→                append_log_entry(
   637→                    plan, "workflow_force_skip",
   638→                    issue_ids=gated_ids, actor="user",
   639→                    note=note,
   640→                    detail={"forced": True, "missing_stages": sorted(missing)},
   641→                )
   642→                save_plan(plan)
   643→                # Fall through to scan gate / purge_ids below
   644→
   645→        # Gate workflow items behind scan completion
   646→        if gated_ids:
   647→            scan_count_at_start = plan.get("scan_count_at_plan_start")
   648→            if scan_count_at_start is not None:
   649→                resolved_state_path = state_path(args)
   650→                state_data = state_mod.load_state(resolved_state_path)
   651→                current_scan_count = int(state_data.get("scan_count", 0) or 0)
   652→                scan_ran = current_scan_count > scan_count_at_start
   653→                scan_skipped = plan.get("scan_gate_skipped", False)
   654→
   655→                if not scan_ran and not scan_skipped and not force:
   656→                    for wid in gated_ids:
   657→                        print(colorize(
   658→                            f"  Cannot resolve {wid} — no scan has run this cycle.",
   659→                            "red",
   660→                        ))
   661→                    print()
   662→                    print(colorize(
   663→                        "  You must run a scan before resolving workflow items:",
   664→                        "yellow",
   665→                    ))
   666→                    print(colorize("    desloppify scan", "dim"))
   667→                    print()
   668→                    print(colorize(
   669→                        f"  Scans at cycle start: {scan_count_at_start}  "
   670→                        f"Current: {current_scan_count}",
   671→                        "dim",
   672→                    ))
   673→                    print(colorize(
   674→                        "  To skip scan requirement: desloppify plan scan-gate --skip "
   675→                        '--note "reason for skipping scan"',
   676→                        "dim",
   677→                    ))
   678→                    print(colorize(
   679→                        "  Or use: --force-resolve --note 'reason for skipping'",
   680→                        "dim",
   681→                    ))
   682→
   683→                    append_log_entry(
   684→                        plan, "scan_gate_blocked",
   685→                        issue_ids=gated_ids, actor="user",
   686→                        note=note,
   687→                        detail={
   688→                            "scan_count_at_start": scan_count_at_start,
   689→                            "current_scan_count": current_scan_count,
   690→                        },
   691→                    )
   692→                    save_plan(plan)
   693→                    return
   694→
   695→        purge_ids(plan, synthetic_ids)
   696→        # Auto-complete steps whose issue_refs are all resolved
   697→        step_messages = auto_complete_steps(plan)
   698→        for msg in step_messages:
   699→            print(colorize(msg, "green"))
   700→        append_log_entry(
   701→            plan, "done", issue_ids=synthetic_ids, actor="user", note=note,
   702→        )
   703→        save_plan(plan)
   704→        for sid in synthetic_ids:
   705→            print(colorize(f"  Resolved: {sid}", "green"))
   706→        if not real_patterns:
   707→            return
   708→        # Continue with remaining real patterns
   709→        patterns = real_patterns
   710→        args.patterns = patterns
   711→
   712→    # Validate note length
   713→    if not validate_note_length(note):
   714→        show_note_length_requirement(note)
   715→        return
   716→
   717→    # Pre-validate attestation before delegating (avoids stale hint in resolve)
   718→    if not validate_attestation(attestation):
   719→        show_attestation_requirement("Plan resolve", attestation, ATTEST_EXAMPLE)
   720→        return
   721→
   722→    # Cluster completion guard: block bulk-completing small clusters
   723→    try:
   724→        runtime = command_runtime(args)
   725→        state = runtime.state
   726→        plan = load_plan()
   727→        if _check_cluster_guard(patterns, plan, state):
   728→            return
   729→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS:
   730→        plan = None
   731→
   732→    # Log the done action (best-effort)
   733→    try:
   734→        if plan is None:
   735→            plan = load_plan()
   736→        clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   737→        cluster_name = None
   738→        for p in patterns:
   739→            if p in clusters:
   740→                cluster_name = p
   741→                break
   742→        append_log_entry(
   743→            plan,
   744→            "done",
   745→            issue_ids=patterns,
   746→            cluster_name=cluster_name,
   747→            actor="user",
   748→            note=note,
   749→        )
   750→        save_plan(plan)
   751→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS as exc:
   752→        log_best_effort_failure(logger, "append plan resolve log entry", exc)
   753→        print(colorize(f"  Note: unable to append plan resolve log entry ({exc}).", "dim"))
   754→
   755→    # Build a Namespace that cmd_resolve expects
   756→    resolve_args = argparse.Namespace(

   758→        patterns=patterns,
   759→        note=note,
   760→        attest=attestation,
   761→        confirm_batch_wontfix=False,
   762→        force_resolve=bool(getattr(args, "force_resolve", False)),
   763→        state=getattr(args, "state", None),
   764→        lang=getattr(args, "lang", None),
   765→        path=getattr(args, "path", None),
   766→        exclude=getattr(args, "exclude", None),
   767→    )
   768→
   769→    cmd_resolve(resolve_args)

   772→def cmd_plan_focus(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   773→    """Set or clear the active cluster focus."""
   774→    clear_flag = getattr(args, "clear", False)
   775→    cluster_name: str | None = getattr(args, "cluster_name", None)
   776→
   777→    plan = load_plan()
   778→    if clear_flag:
   779→        prev = plan.get("active_cluster")
   780→        clear_focus(plan)
   781→        append_log_entry(

   785→        save_plan(plan)

   787→        return
   788→
   789→    if not cluster_name:
   790→        active = plan.get("active_cluster")
   791→        if active:

   797→    try:

   802→    append_log_entry(

   806→    save_plan(plan)
