   172→def _confirm_reflect(
   173→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   174→    plan: dict,
   175→    stages: dict,
   176→    attestation: str | None,
   177→    *,
   178→    services: TriageServices | None = None,
   179→) -> None:
   180→    """Show reflect summary and record confirmation if attestation is valid."""
   181→    resolved_services = services or default_triage_services()
   182→    if "reflect" not in stages:
   183→        print(colorize("  Cannot confirm: reflect stage not recorded.", "red"))
   184→        print(colorize('  Run: desloppify plan triage --stage reflect --report "..."', "dim"))
   185→        return
   186→    if stages["reflect"].get("confirmed_at"):
   187→        print(colorize("  Reflect stage already confirmed.", "green"))
   188→        return
   189→
   190→    runtime = resolved_services.command_runtime(args)
   191→    si = resolved_services.collect_triage_input(plan, runtime.state)
   192→    ref = stages["reflect"]
   193→
   194→    print(colorize("  Stage: REFLECT — Form strategy & present to user", "bold"))
   195→    print(colorize("  " + "─" * 50, "dim"))
   196→
   197→    # Recurring dimensions
   198→    recurring = resolved_services.detect_recurring_patterns(
   199→        si.open_issues,
   200→        si.resolved_issues,
   201→    )
   202→    if recurring:
   203→        print(f"  Your strategy identified {len(recurring)} recurring dimension(s):")
   204→        for dim, info in sorted(recurring.items()):
   205→            resolved_count = len(info["resolved"])
   206→            open_count = len(info["open"])
   207→            label = "potential loop" if open_count >= resolved_count else "root cause unaddressed"
   208→            print(f"    {dim}: {resolved_count} resolved, {open_count} still open — {label}")
   209→    else:
   210→        print("  No recurring patterns detected.")
   211→
   212→    # Strategy briefing excerpt
   213→    report = ref.get("report", "")
   214→    if report:
   215→        print()
   216→        print(colorize("  ┌─ Your strategy briefing ───────────────────────┐", "cyan"))
   217→        for line in report.strip().splitlines()[:8]:
   218→            print(colorize(f"  │ {line}", "cyan"))
   219→        if len(report.strip().splitlines()) > 8:
   220→            print(colorize("  │ ...", "cyan"))
   221→        print(colorize("  └" + "─" * 51 + "┘", "cyan"))
   222→
   223→    # Collect data references for validation — include observe-stage dimensions
   224→    _by_dim, observe_dims = observe_dimension_breakdown(si)
   225→    reflect_dims = sorted(set((list(recurring.keys()) if recurring else []) + observe_dims))
   226→    reflect_clusters = [n for n in plan.get("clusters", {}) if not plan["clusters"][n].get("auto")]
   227→
   228→    if not attestation or len(attestation.strip()) < _MIN_ATTESTATION_LEN:
   229→        if attestation:
   230→            print(colorize(
   231→                f"\n  Attestation too short ({len(attestation.strip())} chars, min {_MIN_ATTESTATION_LEN}).",
   232→                "red",
   233→            ))
   234→        print(colorize("\n  If satisfied, confirm:", "dim"))
   235→        print(colorize('    desloppify plan triage --confirm reflect --attestation "My strategy accounts for..."', "dim"))
   236→        print(colorize("  If not, refine your strategy before organizing.", "dim"))
   237→        return
   238→
   239→    # Validate attestation references actual data
   240→    validation_err = _validate_attestation(
   241→        attestation.strip(), "reflect",
   242→        dimensions=reflect_dims, cluster_names=reflect_clusters,
   243→    )
   244→    if validation_err:
   245→        print(colorize(f"\n  {validation_err}", "red"))
   246→        return
   247→
   248→    stages["reflect"]["confirmed_at"] = utc_now()
   249→    stages["reflect"]["confirmed_text"] = attestation.strip()
   250→    purge_triage_stage(plan, "reflect")
   251→    resolved_services.save_plan(plan)
   252→    resolved_services.append_log_entry(
   253→        plan,
   254→        "triage_confirm_reflect",
   255→        actor="user",
   256→        detail={"attestation": attestation.strip()},
   257→    )
   258→    resolved_services.save_plan(plan)
   259→    print(colorize(f'  ✓ Reflect confirmed: "{attestation.strip()}"', "green"))
   260→    print_user_message(
   261→        "Hey — reflect is confirmed. Now create clusters, enrich"
   262→        " them with action steps, then run `desloppify plan triage"
   263→        " --stage organize --report \"...\"`. No need to reply,"
   264→        " just keep going."
   265→    )

   267→def _confirm_organize(
   268→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   269→    plan: dict,
   270→    stages: dict,
   271→    attestation: str | None,
   272→    *,
   273→    services: TriageServices | None = None,
   274→) -> None:
   275→    """Show full plan summary and record confirmation if attestation is valid."""
   276→    resolved_services = services or default_triage_services()
   277→    if "organize" not in stages:
   278→        print(colorize("  Cannot confirm: organize stage not recorded.", "red"))
   279→        print(colorize('  Run: desloppify plan triage --stage organize --report "..."', "dim"))
   280→        return
   281→    if stages["organize"].get("confirmed_at"):
   282→        print(colorize("  Organize stage already confirmed.", "green"))
   283→        return
   284→
   285→    runtime = resolved_services.command_runtime(args)
   286→    state = runtime.state
   287→
   288→    print(colorize("  Stage: ORGANIZE — Defer contradictions, cluster, & prioritize", "bold"))
   289→    print(colorize("  " + "─" * 63, "dim"))
   290→
   291→    # Activity since reflect
   292→    reflect_ts = stages.get("reflect", {}).get("timestamp", "")
   293→    if reflect_ts:
   294→        activity = count_log_activity_since(plan, reflect_ts)
   295→        if activity:
   296→            print("  Since reflect, you have:")
   297→            for action, count in sorted(activity.items()):
   298→                print(f"    {action}: {count}")
   299→        else:
   300→            print("  No logged plan operations since reflect.")
   301→
   302→    # Show full plan
   303→    print(colorize("\n  Plan:", "bold"))
   304→    show_plan_summary(plan, state)
   305→
   306→    organize_clusters = [n for n in plan.get("clusters", {}) if not plan["clusters"][n].get("auto")]
   307→
   308→    # Re-validate enrichment at confirm time
   309→    from .stage_helpers import _unclustered_review_issues, _unenriched_clusters
   310→
   311→    gaps = _unenriched_clusters(plan)
   312→    if gaps:
   313→        print(colorize(f"\n  Cannot confirm: {len(gaps)} cluster(s) still need enrichment.", "red"))
   314→        for name, missing in gaps:
   315→            print(colorize(f"    {name}: missing {', '.join(missing)}", "yellow"))
   316→        print(colorize("  Small clusters (<5 issues) need at least 1 action step per issue.", "dim"))
   317→        print(
   318→            colorize(
   319→                '  Fix: desloppify plan cluster update <name> --steps "step1" "step2"',
   320→                "dim",
   321→            )
   322→        )
   323→        return
   324→
   325→    unclustered = _unclustered_review_issues(plan, state)
   326→    if unclustered:
   327→        print(colorize(f"\n  Cannot confirm: {len(unclustered)} review issue(s) have no action plan.", "red"))
   328→        for fid in unclustered[:5]:
   329→            short = fid.rsplit("::", 2)[-2] if "::" in fid else fid
   330→            print(colorize(f"    {short}", "yellow"))
   331→        if len(unclustered) > 5:
   332→            print(colorize(f"    ... and {len(unclustered) - 5} more", "yellow"))
   333→        print(colorize("  Add each to a cluster or wontfix it before confirming.", "dim"))
   334→        return
   335→
   336→    # Advisory: directory scatter warning (theme-grouping instead of area-grouping)
   337→    from ._stage_validation import (
   338→        _cluster_file_overlaps,
   339→        _clusters_with_directory_scatter,
   340→        _clusters_with_high_step_ratio,
   341→    )
   342→    scattered = _clusters_with_directory_scatter(plan)
   343→    if scattered:
   344→        print(colorize(f"\n  Warning: {len(scattered)} cluster(s) span many unrelated directories:", "yellow"))
   345→        for name, dir_count, sample_dirs in scattered:
   346→            print(colorize(f"    {name}: {dir_count} directories — likely grouped by theme, not area", "yellow"))
   347→            for d in sample_dirs[:3]:
   348→                print(colorize(f"      {d}", "dim"))
   349→        print(colorize("  Consider splitting into area-focused clusters (same files in same PR).", "dim"))
   350→
   351→    # Advisory: high step-to-issue ratio (1:1 mapping instead of consolidation)
   352→    high_ratio = _clusters_with_high_step_ratio(plan)
   353→    if high_ratio:
   354→        print(colorize(f"\n  Warning: {len(high_ratio)} cluster(s) have step count ≥ issue count:", "yellow"))
   355→        for name, steps, issues, ratio in high_ratio:
   356→            print(colorize(f"    {name}: {steps} steps for {issues} issues ({ratio:.1f}x)", "yellow"))
   357→        print(colorize("  Steps should consolidate changes to the same file. 1:1 means each issue is its own step.", "dim"))
   358→
   359→    # Advisory: cross-cluster file overlap warning with specific suggestions
   360→    overlaps = _cluster_file_overlaps(plan)
   361→    if overlaps:
   362→        clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   363→        print(colorize(f"\n  Note: {len(overlaps)} cluster pair(s) reference the same files:", "yellow"))
   364→        for a, b, files in overlaps[:5]:
   365→            print(colorize(f"    {a} ↔ {b}: {len(files)} shared file(s)", "yellow"))
   366→        # Suggest specific --depends-on for pairs that don't already have a dependency
   367→        needs_dep = []
   368→        for a, b, files in overlaps:
   369→            a_deps = set(clusters.get(a, {}).get("depends_on_clusters", []))
   370→            b_deps = set(clusters.get(b, {}).get("depends_on_clusters", []))
   371→            if b not in a_deps and a not in b_deps:
   372→                needs_dep.append((a, b, files))
   373→        if needs_dep:
   374→            print(colorize("  These pairs have no dependency relationship — add one to prevent merge conflicts:", "dim"))
   375→            for a, b, _files in needs_dep[:5]:
   376→                print(colorize(f"    desloppify plan cluster update {b} --depends-on {a}", "dim"))
   377→                print(colorize(f"    # or: desloppify plan cluster update {a} --depends-on {b}", "dim"))
   378→
   379→    # Advisory: dependency self-references
   380→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   381→    for cname, c in clusters.items():
   382→        deps = c.get("depends_on_clusters", [])
   383→        if cname in deps:
   384→            print(colorize(f"  Warning: {cname} depends on itself.", "yellow"))
   385→
   386→    # Advisory: clusters with steps but no issues (may need cleanup)
   387→    orphaned = [
   388→        (n, len(c.get("action_steps", [])))
   389→        for n, c in clusters.items()
   390→        if not c.get("auto") and not c.get("issue_ids") and c.get("action_steps")
   391→    ]
   392→    if orphaned:
   393→        print(colorize(f"\n  Note: {len(orphaned)} cluster(s) have steps but no issues:", "yellow"))
   394→        for name, step_count in orphaned:
   395→            print(colorize(f"    {name}: {step_count} steps, 0 issues", "yellow"))
   396→        print(colorize("  These may need issues added, or may be leftover from resolved work.", "dim"))
   397→
   398→    if not attestation or len(attestation.strip()) < _MIN_ATTESTATION_LEN:
   399→        if attestation:
   400→            print(colorize(
   401→                f"\n  Attestation too short ({len(attestation.strip())} chars, min {_MIN_ATTESTATION_LEN}).",
   402→                "red",
   403→            ))
   404→        print(colorize("\n  If satisfied, confirm:", "dim"))
   405→        print(colorize('    desloppify plan triage --confirm organize --attestation "This plan is correct..."', "dim"))
   406→        print(colorize("  If not, adjust clusters, priorities, or queue order before completing.", "dim"))
   407→        return
   408→
   409→    # Validate attestation references actual data
   410→    validation_err = _validate_attestation(
   411→        attestation.strip(), "organize", cluster_names=organize_clusters,
   412→    )
   413→    if validation_err:
   414→        print(colorize(f"\n  {validation_err}", "red"))
   415→        return
   416→
   417→    organized, total, _ = triage_coverage(
   418→        plan, open_review_ids=open_review_ids_from_state(state),
   419→    )
   420→    stages["organize"]["confirmed_at"] = utc_now()
   421→    stages["organize"]["confirmed_text"] = attestation.strip()
   422→    purge_triage_stage(plan, "organize")
   423→    resolved_services.save_plan(plan)
   424→    resolved_services.append_log_entry(
   425→        plan,
   426→        "triage_confirm_organize",
   427→        actor="user",
   428→        detail={
   429→            "attestation": attestation.strip(),
   430→            "coverage": f"{organized}/{total}",
   431→        },
   432→    )
   433→    resolved_services.save_plan(plan)
   434→    print(colorize(f'  ✓ Organize confirmed: "{attestation.strip()}"', "green"))
   435→    print_user_message(
   436→        "Hey — organize is confirmed. Next: enrich your steps"
   437→        " with detail and issue_refs so they're executor-ready."
   438→        " Run `desloppify plan triage --stage enrich --report \"...\"`."
   439→        " You can still reorganize (add/remove clusters, reorder)"
   440→        " during the enrich stage."
   441→    )

   443→def _confirm_enrich(
   444→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   445→    plan: dict,
   446→    stages: dict,
   447→    attestation: str | None,
   448→    *,
   449→    services: TriageServices | None = None,
   450→) -> None:
   451→    """Show enrich summary and record confirmation if attestation is valid."""
   452→    resolved_services = services or default_triage_services()
   453→    if "enrich" not in stages:
   454→        print(colorize("  Cannot confirm: enrich stage not recorded.", "red"))
   455→        print(colorize('  Run: desloppify plan triage --stage enrich --report "..."', "dim"))
   456→        return
   457→    if stages["enrich"].get("confirmed_at"):
   458→        print(colorize("  Enrich stage already confirmed.", "green"))
   459→        return
   460→
   461→    from ._stage_validation import (
   462→        _shallow_steps,
   463→        _steps_missing_issue_refs,
   464→        _steps_referencing_skipped_issues,
   465→        _steps_with_bad_paths,
   466→        _steps_with_vague_detail,
   467→        _steps_without_effort,
   468→    )
   469→
   470→    print(colorize("  Stage: ENRICH — Make steps executor-ready (detail, refs)", "bold"))
   471→    print(colorize("  " + "─" * 54, "dim"))
   472→
   473→    shallow = _shallow_steps(plan)
   474→    if shallow:
   475→        total_bare = sum(n for _, n, _ in shallow)
   476→        print(colorize(f"  Cannot confirm: {total_bare} step(s) still lack detail or issue_refs.", "red"))
   477→        for name, bare, total in shallow[:5]:
   478→            print(colorize(f"    {name}: {bare}/{total} steps", "yellow"))
   479→        print()
   480→        print(colorize("  Every step needs --detail (sub-points) or --issue-refs (for auto-completion).", "dim"))
   481→        print(colorize("  Fix:", "dim"))
   482→        print(colorize('    desloppify plan cluster update <name> --update-step N --detail "sub-details"', "dim"))
   483→        return
   484→    else:
   485→        print(colorize("  All steps have detail or issue_refs.", "green"))
   486→
   487→    # Block on bad file paths at confirm time
   488→    from desloppify.base.discovery.paths import get_project_root
   489→    bad_paths = _steps_with_bad_paths(plan, get_project_root())
   490→    if bad_paths:
   491→        total_bad = sum(len(bp) for _, _, bp in bad_paths)
   492→        print(colorize(f"\n  Cannot confirm: {total_bad} file path(s) in step details don't exist on disk.", "red"))
   493→        for name, step_num, paths in bad_paths:
   494→            for p in paths:
   495→                print(colorize(f"    {name} step {step_num}: {p}", "yellow"))
   496→        print(colorize("  Fix paths with: desloppify plan cluster update <name> --update-step N --detail '...'", "dim"))
   497→        return
   498→
   499→    # Block on missing effort tags (was advisory, now blocking)
   500→    untagged = _steps_without_effort(plan)
   501→    if untagged:
   502→        total_missing = sum(n for _, n, _ in untagged)
   503→        print(colorize(f"\n  Cannot confirm: {total_missing} step(s) have no effort tag.", "red"))
   504→        for name, missing, total in untagged[:5]:
   505→            print(colorize(f"    {name}: {missing}/{total} steps missing effort", "yellow"))
   506→        print(colorize("  Every step needs --effort (trivial/small/medium/large).", "dim"))
   507→        print(colorize("  Fix: desloppify plan cluster update <name> --update-step N --effort small", "dim"))
   508→        return
   509→
   510→    # Block on missing issue_refs (traceability)
   511→    no_refs = _steps_missing_issue_refs(plan)
   512→    if no_refs:
   513→        total_missing = sum(n for _, n, _ in no_refs)
   514→        print(colorize(f"\n  Cannot confirm: {total_missing} step(s) have no issue_refs.", "red"))
   515→        for name, missing, total in no_refs[:5]:
   516→            print(colorize(f"    {name}: {missing}/{total} steps missing refs", "yellow"))
   517→        print(colorize("  Every step needs --issue-refs linking it to the review issue(s) it addresses.", "dim"))
   518→        print(colorize("  Fix: desloppify plan cluster update <name> --update-step N --issue-refs <hash1> <hash2>", "dim"))
   519→        return
   520→
   521→    # Block on vague detail (too short, no file paths)
   522→    vague = _steps_with_vague_detail(plan, get_project_root())
   523→    if vague:
   524→        print(colorize(f"\n  Cannot confirm: {len(vague)} step(s) have vague detail (< 80 chars, no file paths).", "red"))
   525→        for name, step_num, title in vague[:5]:
   526→            print(colorize(f"    {name} step {step_num}: {title}", "yellow"))
   527→        print(colorize("  Executor-ready means: someone with zero context knows which file to open and what to change.", "dim"))
   528→        print(colorize("  Add file paths and specific instructions to each step's --detail.", "dim"))
   529→        return
   530→
   531→    # Warn on steps referencing skipped/wontfixed issues
   532→    stale_refs = _steps_referencing_skipped_issues(plan)
   533→    if stale_refs:
   534→        total_stale = sum(len(ids) for _, _, ids in stale_refs)
   535→        print(colorize(f"\n  Warning: {total_stale} step issue_ref(s) point to skipped/wontfixed issues.", "yellow"))
   536→        for name, step_num, ids in stale_refs[:5]:
   537→            print(colorize(f"    {name} step {step_num}: {', '.join(ids[:3])}", "yellow"))
   538→        print(colorize("  Consider removing stale refs or removing the step if it's no longer needed.", "dim"))
   539→
   540→    enrich_clusters = [n for n in plan.get("clusters", {}) if not plan["clusters"][n].get("auto")]
   541→
   542→    if not attestation or len(attestation.strip()) < _MIN_ATTESTATION_LEN:
   543→        if attestation:
   544→            print(colorize(
   545→                f"\n  Attestation too short ({len(attestation.strip())} chars, min {_MIN_ATTESTATION_LEN}).",
   546→                "red",
   547→            ))
   548→        print(colorize("\n  If satisfied, confirm:", "dim"))
   549→        print(colorize('    desloppify plan triage --confirm enrich --attestation "Steps are executor-ready..."', "dim"))
   550→        return
   551→
   552→    validation_err = _validate_attestation(
   553→        attestation.strip(), "enrich", cluster_names=enrich_clusters,
   554→    )
   555→    if validation_err:
   556→        print(colorize(f"\n  {validation_err}", "red"))
   557→        return
   558→
   559→    stages["enrich"]["confirmed_at"] = utc_now()
   560→    stages["enrich"]["confirmed_text"] = attestation.strip()
   561→    purge_triage_stage(plan, "enrich")
   562→    resolved_services.save_plan(plan)
   563→    resolved_services.append_log_entry(
   564→        plan,
   565→        "triage_confirm_enrich",
   566→        actor="user",
   567→        detail={"attestation": attestation.strip()},
   568→    )
   569→    resolved_services.save_plan(plan)
   570→    print(colorize(f'  ✓ Enrich confirmed: "{attestation.strip()}"', "green"))
   571→    print_user_message(
   572→        "Hey — enrich is confirmed. Run `desloppify plan triage"
   573→        " --stage sense-check --report \"...\"` to verify step"
   574→        " accuracy and cross-cluster dependencies."
   575→    )

   578→def _confirm_sense_check(
   579→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   580→    plan: dict,
   581→    stages: dict,
   582→    attestation: str | None,
   583→    *,
   584→    services: TriageServices | None = None,
   585→) -> None:
   586→    """Show sense-check summary and record confirmation if attestation is valid."""
   587→    resolved_services = services or default_triage_services()
   588→    if "sense-check" not in stages:
   589→        print(colorize("  Cannot confirm: sense-check stage not recorded.", "red"))
   590→        print(colorize('  Run: desloppify plan triage --stage sense-check --report "..."', "dim"))
   591→        return
   592→    if stages["sense-check"].get("confirmed_at"):
   593→        print(colorize("  Sense-check stage already confirmed.", "green"))
   594→        return
   595→
   596→    # Re-run all enrich-level validations
   597→    from ._stage_validation import (
   598→        _shallow_steps,
   599→        _steps_missing_issue_refs,
   600→        _steps_with_bad_paths,
   601→        _steps_with_vague_detail,
   602→        _steps_without_effort,
   603→    )
   604→    from desloppify.base.discovery.paths import get_project_root
   605→
   606→    print(colorize("  Stage: SENSE-CHECK — Verify accuracy & cross-cluster deps", "bold"))
   607→    print(colorize("  " + "─" * 57, "dim"))
   608→
   609→    repo_root = get_project_root()
   610→
   611→    shallow = _shallow_steps(plan)
   612→    if shallow:
   613→        total_bare = sum(n for _, n, _ in shallow)
   614→        print(colorize(f"  Cannot confirm: {total_bare} step(s) still lack detail or issue_refs.", "red"))
   615→        for name, bare, total in shallow[:5]:
   616→            print(colorize(f"    {name}: {bare}/{total} steps", "yellow"))
   617→        return
   618→
   619→    bad_paths = _steps_with_bad_paths(plan, repo_root)
   620→    if bad_paths:
   621→        total_bad = sum(len(bp) for _, _, bp in bad_paths)
   622→        print(colorize(f"\n  Cannot confirm: {total_bad} file path(s) in step details don't exist on disk.", "red"))
   623→        for name, step_num, paths in bad_paths:
   624→            for p in paths:
   625→                print(colorize(f"    {name} step {step_num}: {p}", "yellow"))
   626→        return
   627→
   628→    untagged = _steps_without_effort(plan)
   629→    if untagged:
   630→        total_missing = sum(n for _, n, _ in untagged)
   631→        print(colorize(f"\n  Cannot confirm: {total_missing} step(s) have no effort tag.", "red"))
   632→        return
   633→
   634→    no_refs = _steps_missing_issue_refs(plan)
   635→    if no_refs:
   636→        total_missing = sum(n for _, n, _ in no_refs)
   637→        print(colorize(f"\n  Cannot confirm: {total_missing} step(s) have no issue_refs.", "red"))
   638→        return
   639→
   640→    vague = _steps_with_vague_detail(plan, repo_root)
   641→    if vague:
   642→        print(colorize(f"\n  Cannot confirm: {len(vague)} step(s) have vague detail.", "red"))
   643→        return
   644→
   645→    print(colorize("  All enrich-level checks pass.", "green"))
   646→
   647→    sense_check_clusters = [n for n in plan.get("clusters", {}) if not plan["clusters"][n].get("auto")]
   648→
   649→    if not attestation or len(attestation.strip()) < _MIN_ATTESTATION_LEN:
   650→        if attestation:

   653→                "red",

   656→        print(colorize('    desloppify plan triage --confirm sense-check --attestation "Content and structure verified..."', "dim"))
   657→        return
   658→
   659→    validation_err = _validate_attestation(

   664→        return
   665→
   666→    stages["sense-check"]["confirmed_at"] = utc_now()

   676→    resolved_services.save_plan(plan)
   677→    print(colorize(f'  ✓ Sense-check confirmed: "{attestation.strip()}"', "green"))
   678→    print_user_message(

   680→        " --complete --strategy \"...\"` to finish triage."
   681→    )

   683→
   684→def _cmd_confirm_stage(
   685→    args: argparse.Namespace,

   707→

    37→
    38→def _suggest_close_matches(state: dict, plan: dict | None, patterns: list[str]) -> None:
    39→    """Print fuzzy match suggestions for patterns that resolved to zero issues."""
    40→    all_ids: list[str] = list(state.get("issues", {}).keys())
    41→    if plan is not None:
    42→        seen_ids: set[str] = set(all_ids)
    43→        for fid in plan.get("queue_order", []):
    44→            if fid not in seen_ids:
    45→                seen_ids.add(fid)
    46→                all_ids.append(fid)
    47→        for cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).values():
    48→            for fid in cluster.get("issue_ids", []):
    49→                if fid not in seen_ids:
    50→                    seen_ids.add(fid)
    51→                    all_ids.append(fid)
    52→
    53→    for pattern in patterns:
    54→        segments = pattern.split("::")
    55→        last_seg = segments[-1]
    56→        suggestions: list[str] = []
    57→
    58→        if _HEX8_RE.match(last_seg):
    59→            suggestions = [fid for fid in all_ids if fid.endswith(f"::{last_seg}") or fid == last_seg]
    60→            if suggestions:
    61→                print(colorize(f"  No match for: {pattern!r}", "yellow"))
    62→                print(colorize("  Did you mean:", "dim"))
    63→                for m in suggestions[:3]:
    64→                    print(colorize(f"    {m}", "dim"))
    65→                print(colorize(f"  Tip: match by hash suffix alone: {last_seg}", "dim"))
    66→            continue
    67→
    68→        # Try last segment and second-to-last as descriptive name slugs
    69→        slug = segments[-2] if len(segments) >= 2 else ""
    70→        for fid in all_ids:
    71→            if f"::{last_seg}::" in fid or fid.endswith(f"::{last_seg}"):
    72→                suggestions.append(fid)
    73→            elif slug and (f"::{slug}::" in fid or fid.endswith(f"::{slug}")):
    74→                suggestions.append(fid)
    75→        if suggestions:
    76→            print(colorize(f"  No match for: {pattern!r}", "yellow"))
    77→            print(colorize("  Did you mean:", "dim"))
    78→            for m in suggestions[:3]:
    79→                print(colorize(f"    {m}", "dim"))

1→"""Multi-line smell detection utilities (brace-tracked).
     2→
     3→Shared utilities: string-aware scanning, brace tracking, comment stripping,
     4→and line-state classification. All detector functions live in _smell_detectors.py.
     5→"""
     6→
     7→from __future__ import annotations
     8→
     9→from typing import NamedTuple
    10→
    11→from desloppify.base.text_utils import strip_c_style_comments
    12→from desloppify.languages.typescript.syntax.scanner import scan_code
    13→
    14→__all__ = [
    15→    "_FileContext",
    16→    "_build_ts_line_state",
    17→    "_code_text",
    18→    "_content_line_info",
    19→    "_extract_block_body",
    20→    "_find_block_end",
    21→    "_scan_template_content",
    22→    "_strip_ts_comments",
    23→    "_track_brace_body",
    24→    "_ts_match_is_in_string",
    25→    "scan_code",
    26→]
    27→
    28→
    29→class _FileContext(NamedTuple):
    30→    """Per-file data bundle passed to all smell detectors."""
    31→
    32→    filepath: str
    33→    content: str
    34→    lines: list[str]
    35→    line_state: dict[int, str]
    36→
    37→
    38→def _strip_ts_comments(text: str) -> str:
    39→    """Strip // and /* */ comments while preserving strings.
    40→
    41→    Delegates to the shared implementation in utils.py.
    42→    """
    43→    return strip_c_style_comments(text)
    44→
    45→
    46→def _ts_match_is_in_string(line: str, match_start: int) -> bool:
    47→    """Check if a match position falls inside a string literal or comment on a single line.
    48→
    49→    Mirrors Python's _match_is_in_string but for TS syntax (', ", `, //).
    50→    """
    51→    i = 0
    52→    in_str = None
    53→
    54→    while i < len(line):
    55→        if i == match_start:
    56→            return in_str is not None
    57→
    58→        ch = line[i]
    59→
    60→        # Escape sequences inside strings
    61→        if in_str and ch == "\\" and i + 1 < len(line):
    62→            i += 2
    63→            continue
    64→
    65→        if in_str:
    66→            if ch == in_str:
    67→                in_str = None
    68→            i += 1
    69→            continue
    70→
    71→        # Line comment — everything after is non-code
    72→        if ch == "/" and i + 1 < len(line) and line[i + 1] == "/":
    73→            return match_start > i
    74→
    75→        if ch in ("'", '"', "`"):
    76→            in_str = ch
    77→            i += 1
    78→            continue
    79→
    80→        i += 1
    81→
    82→    return False
    83→
    84→
    85→def _track_brace_body(
    86→    lines: list[str], start_line: int, *, max_scan: int = 2000
    87→) -> int | None:
    88→    """Find the closing brace that matches the first opening brace from start_line.
    89→
    90→    Tracks brace depth with string-literal awareness (', ", `).
    91→    Returns the line index of the closing brace, or None if not found.
    92→    """
    93→    depth = 0
    94→    found_open = False
    95→    for line_idx in range(start_line, min(start_line + max_scan, len(lines))):
    96→        for _, ch, in_string in scan_code(lines[line_idx]):
    97→            if in_string:
    98→                continue
    99→            if ch == "{":
   100→                depth += 1
   101→                found_open = True
   102→            elif ch == "}":
   103→                depth -= 1
   104→                if found_open and depth == 0:
   105→                    return line_idx
   106→    return None
   107→
   108→
   109→def _find_block_end(content: str, brace_start: int, max_scan: int = 5000) -> int | None:
   110→    """Find the closing brace position in a content string starting from an opening brace.
   111→
   112→    Uses scan_code for string-literal awareness. Returns the index of the
   113→    matching ``}`` or None.
   114→    """
   115→    depth = 0
   116→    for ci, ch, in_s in scan_code(
   117→        content, brace_start, min(brace_start + max_scan, len(content))
   118→    ):
   119→        if in_s:
   120→            continue
   121→        if ch == "{":
   122→            depth += 1
   123→        elif ch == "}":
   124→            depth -= 1
   125→            if depth == 0:
   126→                return ci
   127→    return None
   128→
   129→
   130→def _extract_block_body(
   131→    content: str, brace_start: int, max_scan: int = 5000
   132→) -> str | None:
   133→    """Return the text between ``{`` at *brace_start* and its matching ``}``.
   134→
   135→    Delegates to :func:`_find_block_end` for brace tracking.
   136→    Returns ``None`` when the closing brace is not found.
   137→    """
   138→    end = _find_block_end(content, brace_start, max_scan)
   139→    if end is None:
   140→        return None
   141→    return content[brace_start + 1 : end]
   142→
   143→
   144→def _content_line_info(content: str, pos: int) -> tuple[int, str]:
   145→    """Return ``(1-based line number, stripped snippet[:100])`` for a position in *content*."""
   146→    line_no = content[:pos].count("\n") + 1
   147→    line_start = content.rfind("\n", 0, pos) + 1
   148→    line_end = content.find("\n", pos)
   149→    if line_end == -1:
   150→        line_end = len(content)
   151→    return line_no, content[line_start:line_end].strip()[:100]
   152→
   153→
   154→def _code_text(text: str) -> str:
   155→    """Blank string literals and ``//`` comments to spaces, preserving positions.
   156→
   157→    Built on :func:`scan_code` with added line-comment detection.
   158→    """
   159→    out = list(text)
   160→    in_line_comment = False
   161→    prev_code_idx = -2
   162→    prev_code_ch = ""
   163→    for i, ch, in_s in scan_code(text):
   164→        if ch == "\n":
   165→            in_line_comment = False
   166→            prev_code_ch = ""
   167→            continue
   168→        if in_line_comment:
   169→            out[i] = " "
   170→            continue
   171→        if in_s:
   172→            out[i] = " "
   173→            continue
   174→        if ch == "/" and prev_code_ch == "/" and prev_code_idx == i - 1:
   175→            out[prev_code_idx] = " "
   176→            out[i] = " "
   177→            in_line_comment = True
   178→            prev_code_ch = ""
   179→            continue
   180→        prev_code_idx = i
   181→        prev_code_ch = ch
   182→    return "".join(out)
   183→
   184→
   185→def _scan_template_content(
   186→    line: str, start: int, brace_depth: int = 0
   187→) -> tuple[int, bool, int]:
   188→    """Scan template literal content from *start* in *line*.
   189→
   190→    Returns ``(end_pos, found_close, brace_depth)`` where *found_close* is True
   191→    if a closing backtick was found and *end_pos* is the position after it.
   192→    """
   193→    j = start
   194→    while j < len(line):
   195→        ch = line[j]
   196→        if ch == "\\" and j + 1 < len(line):
   197→            j += 2
   198→            continue
   199→        if ch == "$" and j + 1 < len(line) and line[j + 1] == "{":
   200→            brace_depth += 1
   201→            j += 2
   202→            continue
   203→        if ch == "}" and brace_depth > 0:
   204→            brace_depth -= 1
   205→            j += 1
   206→            continue
   207→        if ch == "`" and brace_depth == 0:
   208→            return (j + 1, True, brace_depth)
   209→        j += 1
   210→    return (j, False, brace_depth)
   211→
   212→
   213→def _scan_code_line(line: str) -> tuple[bool, bool, int]:
   214→    """Scan a normal code line for block comment or template literal start.
   215→
   216→    Returns ``(entered_block_comment, entered_template, template_brace_depth)``.
   217→    """
   218→    j = 0
   219→    in_str = None
   220→    while j < len(line):
   221→        ch = line[j]
   222→
   223→        # Skip escape sequences
   224→        if in_str and ch == "\\" and j + 1 < len(line):
   225→            j += 2
   226→            continue
   227→
   228→        # String tracking
   229→        if in_str:
   230→            if ch == in_str:
   231→                in_str = None
   232→            j += 1
   233→            continue
   234→
   235→        # Line comment — rest is not code
   236→        if ch == "/" and j + 1 < len(line) and line[j + 1] == "/":
   237→            break
   238→
   239→        # Block comment start
   240→        if ch == "/" and j + 1 < len(line) and line[j + 1] == "*":
   241→            # Check if it closes on same line
   242→            close = line.find("*/", j + 2)
   243→            if close != -1:
   244→                j = close + 2
   245→                continue
   246→            return (True, False, 0)
   247→
   248→        # Template literal start
   249→        if ch == "`":
   250→            end_pos, found_close, depth = _scan_template_content(line, j + 1)
   251→            if found_close:
   252→                j = end_pos
   253→                continue
   254→            return (False, True, depth)
   255→
   256→        if ch in ("'", '"'):
   257→            in_str = ch
   258→            j += 1
   259→            continue
   260→
   261→        j += 1
   262→
   263→    return (False, False, 0)
   264→
   265→
   266→def _build_ts_line_state(lines: list[str]) -> dict[int, str]:
   267→    """Build a map of line numbers that are inside block comments or template literals.
   268→
   269→    Returns {0-indexed line: reason} where reason is "block_comment" or "template_literal".
   270→    Lines not in the map are normal code lines suitable for regex checks.
   271→
   272→    Tracks:
   273→    - Block comment state (opened by /*, closed by */)
   274→    - Template literal state (opened by backtick, closed by backtick,
   275→      with ${} nesting awareness)
   276→    """
   277→    state: dict[int, str] = {}
   278→    in_block_comment = False
   279→    in_template = False
   280→    template_brace_depth = 0
   281→
   282→    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
   283→        if in_block_comment:
   284→            state[i] = "block_comment"
   285→            if "*/" in line:
   286→                in_block_comment = False
   287→            continue
   288→
   289→        if in_template:
   290→            state[i] = "template_literal"
   291→            _, found_close, template_brace_depth = _scan_template_content(
   292→                line, 0, template_brace_depth
   293→            )
   294→            if found_close:
   295→                in_template = False
   296→            continue
   297→
   298→        in_block_comment, in_template, depth = _scan_code_line(line)
   299→        if in_template:
   300→            template_brace_depth = depth
   301→
   302→    return state
   303→

    74→        "high_level_elegance",
    75→        "mid_level_elegance",
    76→        "low_level_elegance",
    77→    }
    78→)
    79→
    80→_LEGACY_WEIGHT_BY_DIMENSION: dict[str, float] = {}
    81→for _dimension_key, _display_name in _LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES.items():
    82→    _weight = _LEGACY_SUBJECTIVE_WEIGHTS_BY_DISPLAY.get(
    83→        " ".join(_display_name.strip().lower().split())
    84→    )
    85→    if _weight is not None:
    86→        _LEGACY_WEIGHT_BY_DIMENSION[_dimension_key] = _weight
    87→
    88→
    89→def _normalize_dimension_name(name: str) -> str:
    90→    return "_".join(str(name).strip().lower().replace("-", "_").split())
    91→
    92→
    93→def _title_display_name(dimension_key: str) -> str:
    94→    return dimension_key.replace("_", " ").title()
    95→
    96→
    97→def _normalize_lang_name(lang_name: str | None) -> str | None:
    98→    if not isinstance(lang_name, str):
    99→        return None
   100→    cleaned = lang_name.strip().lower()
   101→    return cleaned or None
   102→
   103→
   104→def _merge_prompt_display_and_weights(
   105→    payload: dict[str, object],
   106→    *,
   107→    prompt_meta: dict[str, object],
   108→    override_existing: bool,
   109→) -> None:
   110→    if "display_name" in prompt_meta and (
   111→        override_existing or "display_name" not in payload
   112→    ):
   113→        payload["display_name"] = prompt_meta["display_name"]
   114→    if "weight" in prompt_meta and (override_existing or "weight" not in payload):
   115→        payload["weight"] = prompt_meta["weight"]
   116→    if "reset_on_scan" in prompt_meta and (
   117→        override_existing or "reset_on_scan" not in payload
   118→    ):
   119→        payload["reset_on_scan"] = prompt_meta["reset_on_scan"]
   120→
   121→
   122→def _merge_enabled_by_default_flag(
   123→    payload: dict[str, object],
   124→    *,
   125→    prompt_meta: dict[str, object],
   126→    override_existing: bool,
   127→    default_enabled: bool,
   128→) -> None:
   129→    if default_enabled:
   130→        payload["enabled_by_default"] = True
   131→    if "enabled_by_default" not in prompt_meta:
   132→        return
   133→    prompt_enabled = bool(prompt_meta["enabled_by_default"])
   134→    if override_existing:
   135→        payload["enabled_by_default"] = prompt_enabled
   136→        return
   137→    payload["enabled_by_default"] = bool(
   138→        payload.get("enabled_by_default", False) or prompt_enabled
   139→    )
   140→
   141→
   142→def _normalized_default_dimensions(dimensions: list[str]) -> set[str]:
   143→    return {
   144→        _normalize_dimension_name(dim)
   145→        for dim in dimensions
   146→        if isinstance(dim, str) and dim.strip()
   147→    }
   148→
   149→
   150→def _merge_dimension_meta(
   151→    target: dict[str, dict[str, object]],
   152→    *,
   153→    dimensions: list[str],
   154→    prompts: dict[str, dict[str, object]],
   155→    override_existing: bool = False,
   156→) -> None:
   157→    defaults = _normalized_default_dimensions(dimensions)
   158→
   159→    for raw_dim, entry in prompts.items():
   160→        dim = _normalize_dimension_name(raw_dim)
   161→        if not dim:
   162→            continue
   163→
   164→        payload = target.setdefault(dim, {})
   165→        prompt_meta = extract_prompt_meta(entry)
   166→        _merge_prompt_display_and_weights(
   167→            payload,
   168→            prompt_meta=prompt_meta,
   169→            override_existing=override_existing,
   170→        )
   171→        _merge_enabled_by_default_flag(
   172→            payload,
   173→            prompt_meta=prompt_meta,
   174→            override_existing=override_existing,
   175→            default_enabled=dim in defaults,
   176→        )
   177→
   178→
   179→def _default_available_languages() -> list[str]:
   180→    try:
   181→        return list(_available_langs())
   182→    except (ImportError, ValueError, TypeError, RuntimeError):
   183→        return []
   184→
   185→
   186→def _default_load_dimensions_payload() -> tuple[
   187→    list[str], dict[str, dict[str, object]], str
   188→]:
   189→    return _load_dimensions()
   190→
   191→
   192→def _default_load_dimensions_payload_for_lang(
   193→    lang_name: str,
   194→) -> tuple[list[str], dict[str, dict[str, object]], str]:
   195→    return _load_dimensions_for_lang(lang_name)
   196→
   197→
   198→class _SubjectiveProviderState:
   199→    def __init__(self) -> None:
   200→        self.available_languages_provider: Callable[[], list[str]] = (
   201→            _default_available_languages
   202→        )
   203→        self.load_dimensions_payload_provider: Callable[
   204→            [], tuple[list[str], dict[str, dict[str, object]], str]
   205→        ] = _default_load_dimensions_payload
   206→        self.load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider: Callable[
   207→            [str], tuple[list[str], dict[str, dict[str, object]], str]
   208→        ] = _default_load_dimensions_payload_for_lang
   209→
   210→
   211→_PROVIDER_STATE = _SubjectiveProviderState()
   212→
   213→
   214→def _available_languages() -> list[str]:
   215→    return _PROVIDER_STATE.available_languages_provider()
   216→
   217→
   218→def _load_dimensions_payload() -> tuple[list[str], dict[str, dict[str, object]], str]:
   219→    return _PROVIDER_STATE.load_dimensions_payload_provider()
   220→
   221→
   222→def _load_dimensions_payload_for_lang(
   223→    lang_name: str,
   224→) -> tuple[list[str], dict[str, dict[str, object]], str]:
   225→    return _PROVIDER_STATE.load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider(lang_name)
   226→
   227→
   228→def _clear_subjective_dimension_caches() -> None:
   229→    default_dimension_keys.cache_clear()
   230→    default_dimension_keys_for_lang.cache_clear()
   231→    load_subjective_dimension_metadata.cache_clear()
   232→    load_subjective_dimension_metadata_for_lang.cache_clear()
   233→
   234→
   235→def configure_subjective_dimension_providers(
   236→    *,
   237→    available_languages_provider: Callable[[], list[str]] | None = None,
   238→    load_dimensions_payload_provider: Callable[
   239→        [], tuple[list[str], dict[str, dict[str, object]], str]
   240→    ]
   241→    | None = None,
   242→    load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider: Callable[
   243→        [str], tuple[list[str], dict[str, dict[str, object]], str]
   244→    ]
   245→    | None = None,
   246→) -> None:
   247→    """Configure metadata providers for subjective-dimension lookups."""
   248→    state = _PROVIDER_STATE
   249→
   250→    changed = False
   251→    if (
   252→        available_languages_provider is not None
   253→        and available_languages_provider is not state.available_languages_provider
   254→    ):
   255→        state.available_languages_provider = available_languages_provider
   256→        changed = True
   257→    if (
   258→        load_dimensions_payload_provider is not None
   259→        and load_dimensions_payload_provider
   260→        is not state.load_dimensions_payload_provider
   261→    ):
   262→        state.load_dimensions_payload_provider = load_dimensions_payload_provider
   263→        changed = True
   264→    if (
   265→        load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider is not None
   266→        and load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider
   267→        is not state.load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider
   268→    ):
   269→        state.load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider = (
   270→            load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider
   271→        )
   272→        changed = True
   273→
   274→    if changed:
   275→        _clear_subjective_dimension_caches()
   276→
   277→
   278→def reset_subjective_dimension_providers() -> None:
   279→    """Reset metadata providers to built-in defaults."""
   280→    configure_subjective_dimension_providers(
   281→        available_languages_provider=_default_available_languages,
   282→        load_dimensions_payload_provider=_default_load_dimensions_payload,
   283→        load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider=_default_load_dimensions_payload_for_lang,
   284→    )
   285→
   286→
   287→def _normalize_dimension_list(values: list[str]) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   288→    normalized: list[str] = []
   289→    for raw in values:
   290→        if not isinstance(raw, str):
   291→            continue
   292→        dim = _normalize_dimension_name(raw)
   293→        if not dim or dim in normalized:
   294→            continue
   295→        normalized.append(dim)
   296→    return tuple(normalized)
   297→
   298→
   299→@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
   300→def default_dimension_keys() -> tuple[str, ...]:
   301→    """Return canonical default subjective dimension keys."""
   302→    try:
   303→        dims, _, _ = _load_dimensions_payload()
   304→    except (ImportError, ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
   305→        logger.debug("Failed to load default subjective dimensions: %s", exc)
   306→        return tuple(_LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES.keys())
   307→    return _normalize_dimension_list(dims)
   308→
   309→
   310→@lru_cache(maxsize=16)
   311→def default_dimension_keys_for_lang(lang_name: str | None) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   312→    """Return default subjective dimension keys for a specific language."""
   313→    normalized = _normalize_lang_name(lang_name)
   314→    if normalized is None:
   315→        return default_dimension_keys()
   316→    try:
   317→        dims, _, _ = _load_dimensions_payload_for_lang(normalized)
   318→    except (ImportError, ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
   319→        logger.debug(
   320→            "Failed to load subjective dimensions for lang %s: %s",
   321→            normalized,
   322→            exc,
   323→        )
   324→        return default_dimension_keys()
   325→    return _normalize_dimension_list(dims)
   326→
   327→
   328→def _build_subjective_dimension_metadata(
   329→    *,
   330→    lang_name: str | None,
   331→) -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
   332→    out: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
   333→
   334→    try:
   335→        shared_defaults, shared_prompts, _ = _load_dimensions_payload()
   336→    except (ImportError, ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
   337→        logger.debug("Failed to load shared subjective dimension payload: %s", exc)
   338→        shared_defaults, shared_prompts = [], {}
   339→    _merge_dimension_meta(out, dimensions=shared_defaults, prompts=shared_prompts)
   340→
   341→    langs = (
   342→        [lang_name]
   343→        if isinstance(lang_name, str) and lang_name.strip()
   344→        else _available_languages()
   345→    )
   346→    for name in langs:
   347→        try:
   348→            lang_defaults, lang_prompts, _ = _load_dimensions_payload_for_lang(name)
   349→            _merge_dimension_meta(
   350→                out,
   351→                dimensions=lang_defaults,
   352→                prompts=lang_prompts,
   353→                override_existing=bool(lang_name),
   354→            )
   355→        except (ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
   356→            logger.debug("Failed to load dimensions for lang %s: %s", name, exc)
   357→            continue
   358→
   359→    for dim, payload in out.items():
   360→        payload.setdefault(
   361→            "display_name",
   362→            _LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES.get(dim, _title_display_name(dim)),
   363→        )
   364→        payload.setdefault("weight", _LEGACY_WEIGHT_BY_DIMENSION.get(dim, 1.0))
   365→        payload.setdefault("enabled_by_default", False)
   366→        if dim in _LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES:
   367→            payload.setdefault("reset_on_scan", dim in _LEGACY_RESET_ON_SCAN_DIMENSIONS)
   368→        else:
   369→            payload.setdefault("reset_on_scan", True)
   370→
   371→    # Preserve legacy dimensions even if a payload temporarily drops one.
   372→    for dim, display in _LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES.items():
   373→        payload = out.setdefault(dim, {})
   374→        payload.setdefault("display_name", display)
   375→        payload.setdefault("weight", _LEGACY_WEIGHT_BY_DIMENSION.get(dim, 1.0))
   376→        payload.setdefault("enabled_by_default", True)
   377→        payload.setdefault("reset_on_scan", dim in _LEGACY_RESET_ON_SCAN_DIMENSIONS)
   378→
   379→    return out
   380→
   381→
   382→@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
   383→def load_subjective_dimension_metadata() -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
   384→    """Return merged metadata across all known dimensions/languages."""
   385→    return _build_subjective_dimension_metadata(lang_name=None)
   386→
   387→
   388→@lru_cache(maxsize=16)
   389→def load_subjective_dimension_metadata_for_lang(
   390→    lang_name: str | None,
   391→) -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
   392→    """Return merged metadata for one language (with language overrides)."""
   393→    normalized = _normalize_lang_name(lang_name)
   394→    return _build_subjective_dimension_metadata(lang_name=normalized)
   395→
   396→
   397→def _metadata_registry(lang_name: str | None) -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
   398→    normalized = _normalize_lang_name(lang_name)
   399→    if normalized is None:
   400→        return load_subjective_dimension_metadata()
   401→    return load_subjective_dimension_metadata_for_lang(normalized)
   402→
   403→
   404→def get_dimension_metadata(
   405→    dimension_name: str, *, lang_name: str | None = None
   406→) -> dict[str, object]:
   407→    """Return metadata for one dimension key (with sane defaults)."""
   408→    dim = _normalize_dimension_name(dimension_name)
   409→    all_meta = _metadata_registry(lang_name)
   410→    payload = dict(all_meta.get(dim, {}))
   411→
   412→    payload.setdefault("display_name", _title_display_name(dim))
   413→    payload.setdefault("weight", 1.0)
   414→    payload.setdefault("enabled_by_default", False)
   415→    payload.setdefault("reset_on_scan", True)
   416→    return payload
   417→
   418→
   419→def dimension_display_name(dimension_name: str, *, lang_name: str | None = None) -> str:
   420→    meta = get_dimension_metadata(dimension_name, lang_name=lang_name)
   421→    return str(meta.get("display_name", _title_display_name(dimension_name)))
   422→
   423→
   424→def dimension_weight(dimension_name: str, *, lang_name: str | None = None) -> float:
   425→    meta = get_dimension_metadata(dimension_name, lang_name=lang_name)
   426→    raw = meta.get("weight", 1.0)
   427→    if is_numeric(raw):
   428→        return max(0.0, float(raw))
   429→    return 1.0
   430→
   431→
   432→def default_display_names_map(*, lang_name: str | None = None) -> dict[str, str]:
   433→    """Display-name map for default subjective dimensions."""
   434→    out: dict[str, str] = {}
   435→    for dim, payload in _metadata_registry(lang_name).items():
   436→        if not bool(payload.get("enabled_by_default", False)):
   437→            continue
   438→        out[dim] = str(payload.get("display_name", _title_display_name(dim)))
   439→    return out
   440→
   441→
   442→def resettable_default_dimensions(*, lang_name: str | None = None) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   443→    """Default subjective dimensions that should be reset by scan reset."""
   444→    out = []
   445→    for dim, payload in _metadata_registry(lang_name).items():
   446→        if not bool(payload.get("enabled_by_default", False)):
   447→            continue
   448→        if not bool(payload.get("reset_on_scan", True)):
   449→            continue
   450→        out.append(dim)
   451→    return tuple(sorted(set(out)))
   452→
   453→
   454→__all__ = [
   455→    "DISPLAY_NAMES",
   456→    "configure_subjective_dimension_providers",
   457→    "default_dimension_keys",
   458→    "default_dimension_keys_for_lang",
   459→    "default_display_names_map",
   460→    "dimension_display_name",
   461→    "dimension_weight",
   462→    "get_dimension_metadata",
   463→    "load_subjective_dimension_metadata",
   464→    "load_subjective_dimension_metadata_for_lang",
   465→    "reset_subjective_dimension_providers",
   466→    "resettable_default_dimensions",
   467→]

    43→def module_patterns(content: str) -> list[str]:
    44→    """Extract module-level dependency specs for review context."""
    45→    return [match.group(1) for match in _IMPORT_EXPORT_RE.finditer(content)]
    46→
    47→
    48→def api_surface(file_contents: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    49→    """Build minimal API-surface summary from parsed Dart files."""
    50→    public_types: set[str] = set()
    51→    public_functions: set[str] = set()
    52→    for content in file_contents.values():
    53→        for match in _TYPE_RE.finditer(content):
    54→            name = match.group(1)
    55→            if not name.startswith("_"):
    56→                public_types.add(name)
    57→        for match in _FUNCTION_RE.finditer(content):
    58→            name = match.group(1)
    59→            if not name.startswith("_"):
    60→                public_functions.add(name)
    61→
    62→    return {
    63→        "public_types": sorted(public_types),
    64→        "public_functions": sorted(public_functions),
    65→    }
    66→

1→"""Zone classification system — deterministic file intent classification.
     2→
     3→Classifies files into zones (production, test, config, generated, script, vendor)
     4→based on path patterns. Zone metadata flows through issues, scoring, and the LLM.
     5→"""
     6→
     7→from __future__ import annotations
     8→
     9→import logging
    10→import os
    11→from dataclasses import dataclass, field
    12→from enum import Enum
    13→
    14→from desloppify.base.output.fallbacks import log_best_effort_failure
    15→from desloppify.engine.policy.zones_data import (
    16→    CONFIG_SKIP_DETECTORS,
    17→    SCRIPT_SKIP_DETECTORS,
    18→    SKIP_ALL_DETECTORS,
    19→    TEST_SKIP_DETECTORS,
    20→)
    21→
    22→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    23→
    24→
    25→class Zone(str, Enum):
    26→    """File intent zone — determines scoring and detection policy."""
    27→
    28→    PRODUCTION = "production"
    29→    TEST = "test"
    30→    CONFIG = "config"
    31→    GENERATED = "generated"
    32→    SCRIPT = "script"
    33→    VENDOR = "vendor"
    34→
    35→
    36→# Zones excluded from the health score
    37→EXCLUDED_ZONES = {Zone.TEST, Zone.CONFIG, Zone.GENERATED, Zone.VENDOR}
    38→
    39→# String values for quick lookup in scoring (issues store zone as string)
    40→EXCLUDED_ZONE_VALUES = {z.value for z in EXCLUDED_ZONES}
    41→
    42→
    43→@dataclass
    44→class ZoneRule:
    45→    """A classification rule: zone + list of path patterns.
    46→
    47→    Patterns are matched against relative file paths. First matching rule wins.
    48→    Pattern types (auto-detected from shape):
    49→      - "/dir/"   → substring match on full path (directory marker)
    50→      - ".ext"    → basename ends-with (suffix/extension, e.g. ".d.ts", ".test.")
    51→      - "prefix_" → basename starts-with (trailing underscore)
    52→      - "name.py" → basename exact match (has extension, no /)
    53→      - fallback  → substring on full path
    54→    """
    55→
    56→    zone: Zone
    57→    patterns: list[str]
    58→
    59→
    60→def _match_pattern(rel_path: str, pattern: str) -> bool:
    61→    """Match a zone pattern against a relative file path.
    62→
    63→    See ZoneRule docstring for pattern type conventions.
    64→    """
    65→    basename = os.path.basename(rel_path)
    66→
    67→    # Directory pattern: "/dir/" → substring on padded path
    68→    if pattern.startswith("/") and pattern.endswith("/"):
    69→        return pattern in ("/" + rel_path + "/")
    70→
    71→    # Suffix/extension pattern: starts with "." → contains on basename
    72→    if pattern.startswith("."):
    73→        return pattern in basename
    74→
    75→    # Prefix pattern: ends with "_" → basename starts-with
    76→    if pattern.endswith("_"):
    77→        return basename.startswith(pattern)
    78→
    79→    # Suffix pattern: starts with "_" → basename ends-with (_test.py, _pb2.py)
    80→    if pattern.startswith("_"):
    81→        return basename.endswith(pattern)
    82→
    83→    # Exact basename: has a proper file extension (1-5 chars after last dot),
    84→    # no "/" → exact basename match (config.py, setup.py, conftest.py)
    85→    if "/" not in pattern and "." in pattern:
    86→        ext = pattern.rsplit(".", 1)[-1]
    87→        if ext and len(ext) <= 5 and ext.isalnum():
    88→            return basename == pattern
    89→
    90→    # Fallback: substring on full path (vite.config, tsconfig, eslint, etc.)
    91→    return pattern in rel_path
    92→
    93→
    94→# ── Common zone rules (shared across languages) ──────────
    95→
    96→COMMON_ZONE_RULES = [
    97→    ZoneRule(Zone.VENDOR, ["/vendor/", "/third_party/", "/vendored/"]),
    98→    ZoneRule(Zone.GENERATED, ["/generated/", "/__generated__/"]),
    99→    ZoneRule(Zone.TEST, ["/tests/", "/test/", "/fixtures/"]),
   100→    ZoneRule(Zone.SCRIPT, ["/scripts/", "/bin/"]),
   101→]
   102→
   103→
   104→def classify_file(
   105→    rel_path: str, rules: list[ZoneRule], overrides: dict[str, str] | None = None
   106→) -> Zone:
   107→    """Classify a file by its relative path. Overrides take priority."""
   108→    if overrides:
   109→        override = overrides.get(rel_path)
   110→        if override:
   111→            try:
   112→                return Zone(override)
   113→            except ValueError as exc:
   114→                log_best_effort_failure(
   115→                    logger, f"parse zone override for {rel_path}", exc
   116→                )
   117→    for rule in rules:
   118→        for pattern in rule.patterns:
   119→            if _match_pattern(rel_path, pattern):
   120→                return rule.zone
   121→    return Zone.PRODUCTION
   122→
   123→
   124→class FileZoneMap:
   125→    """Cached zone classification for a set of files.
   126→
   127→    Built once per scan from file list + zone rules.
   128→    """
   129→
   130→    def __init__(
   131→        self,
   132→        files: list[str],
   133→        rules: list[ZoneRule],
   134→        rel_fn=None,
   135→        overrides: dict[str, str] | None = None,
   136→    ):
   137→        """Build a zone map from files, ordered rules, and optional overrides."""
   138→        self._map: dict[str, Zone] = {}
   139→        self._overrides = overrides
   140→        for f in files:
   141→            rp = rel_fn(f) if rel_fn else f
   142→            self._map[f] = classify_file(rp, rules, overrides)
   143→
   144→    def get(self, path: str) -> Zone:
   145→        """Get zone for a file path. Returns PRODUCTION if not classified."""
   146→        return self._map.get(path, Zone.PRODUCTION)
   147→
   148→    def exclude(self, files: list[str], *zones: Zone) -> list[str]:
   149→        """Return files NOT in the given zones."""
   150→        zone_set = set(zones)
   151→        return [f for f in files if self._map.get(f, Zone.PRODUCTION) not in zone_set]
   152→
   153→    def include_only(self, files: list[str], *zones: Zone) -> list[str]:
   154→        """Return files that ARE in the given zones."""
   155→        zone_set = set(zones)
   156→        return [f for f in files if self._map.get(f, Zone.PRODUCTION) in zone_set]
   157→
   158→    def counts(self) -> dict[str, int]:
   159→        """Return file count per zone."""
   160→        counts: dict[str, int] = {}
   161→        for zone in self._map.values():
   162→            counts[zone.value] = counts.get(zone.value, 0) + 1
   163→        return counts
   164→
   165→    def production_count(self) -> int:
   166→        """Count files classified as production."""
   167→        return len(self._map) - self.non_production_count()
   168→
   169→    def non_production_count(self) -> int:
   170→        """Count files in excluded zones (test/config/generated/vendor)."""
   171→        return sum(1 for z in self._map.values() if z in EXCLUDED_ZONES)
   172→
   173→    def all_files(self) -> list[str]:
   174→        """Return all classified file paths."""
   175→        return list(self._map.keys())
   176→
   177→    def items(self) -> list[tuple[str, Zone]]:
   178→        """Return all (path, zone) pairs."""
   179→        return list(self._map.items())
   180→
   181→
   182→# ── Zone detection policies ────────────────────────────────
   183→
   184→
   185→@dataclass
   186→class ZonePolicy:
   187→    """Per-zone detection policy.
   188→
   189→    skip_detectors: detectors to skip entirely for this zone.
   190→    downgrade_detectors: detectors whose confidence is downgraded to "low".
   191→    exclude_from_score: whether issues in this zone are excluded from scoring.
   192→    """
   193→
   194→    skip_detectors: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
   195→    downgrade_detectors: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
   196→    exclude_from_score: bool = False
   197→
   198→
   199→ZONE_POLICIES: dict[Zone, ZonePolicy] = {
   200→    Zone.PRODUCTION: ZonePolicy(),
   201→    Zone.TEST: ZonePolicy(
   202→        skip_detectors=TEST_SKIP_DETECTORS,
   203→        downgrade_detectors={"smells", "structural"},
   204→        exclude_from_score=True,
   205→    ),
   206→    Zone.CONFIG: ZonePolicy(
   207→        skip_detectors=CONFIG_SKIP_DETECTORS,
   208→        exclude_from_score=True,
   209→    ),
   210→    Zone.GENERATED: ZonePolicy(
   211→        skip_detectors=SKIP_ALL_DETECTORS,
   212→        exclude_from_score=True,
   213→    ),
   214→    Zone.VENDOR: ZonePolicy(
   215→        skip_detectors=SKIP_ALL_DETECTORS,
   216→        exclude_from_score=True,
   217→    ),
   218→    Zone.SCRIPT: ZonePolicy(
   219→        skip_detectors=SCRIPT_SKIP_DETECTORS,
   220→        downgrade_detectors={"structural"},
   221→    ),
   222→}
   223→
   224→
   225→# ── Helpers for phase runners ─────────────────────────────
   226→
   227→
   228→def adjust_potential(zone_map, total: int) -> int:
   229→    """Subtract non-production files from a potential count.
   230→
   231→    Uses the zone map's own file list — no need to pass files separately.
   232→    No-op if zone_map is None.
   233→    """
   234→    if zone_map is None:
   235→        return total
   236→    return max(total - zone_map.non_production_count(), 0)
   237→
   238→
   239→def should_skip_issue(zone_map, filepath: str, detector: str) -> bool:
   240→    """Check if a issue should be skipped based on zone policy.
   241→
   242→    Returns True if the file's zone policy says to skip this detector.
   243→    """
   244→    if zone_map is None:
   245→        return False
   246→    zone = zone_map.get(filepath)
   247→    policy = ZONE_POLICIES.get(zone)
   248→    return policy is not None and detector in policy.skip_detectors
   249→
   250→
   251→def filter_entries(
   252→    zone_map, entries: list[dict], detector: str, file_key: str = "file"
   253→) -> list[dict]:
   254→    """Filter detector entries by zone policy. No-op if zone_map is None.
   255→
   256→    If file_key points to a list (e.g. cycle entries with "files"), checks
   257→    the first element.
   258→    """
   259→    if zone_map is None:
   260→        return entries
   261→
   262→    def _get_path(entry):
   263→        val = entry[file_key]
   264→        return val[0] if isinstance(val, list) else val
   265→
   266→    return [
   267→        e for e in entries if not should_skip_issue(zone_map, _get_path(e), detector)
   268→    ]
   269→

    11→    "For each batch: start from listed seed files, then explore likely hotspots/unreviewed neighbors; evaluate the batch's dimensions (batches are independent — parallelize)",
    12→    "Cross-reference issues with the sibling_behavior and convention data",
    13→    "IMPORTANT: issues must be defects only — never positive observations. High scores capture quality; issues capture problems.",
    14→    "Write ALL issues to issues.json — do NOT fix code before importing. Import creates tracked state entries that let desloppify correlate fixes to issues.",
    15→    "Codex: desloppify review --run-batches --runner codex --parallel --scan-after-import",
    16→    "Claude / other agent: desloppify review --run-batches --dry-run → launch one subagent per prompt file (all in parallel) → desloppify review --import-run <run-dir> --scan-after-import",
    17→    "Cloud/external: run `desloppify review --external-start --external-runner claude`, follow the session template, then run the printed `--external-submit` command",
    18→    "Fallback path: `desloppify review --import issues.json` (issues only). Use manual override only for emergency/provisional imports.",
    19→    "AFTER importing: run `desloppify show review --status open` to see the work queue, then fix each issue in code and `desloppify plan resolve <id>`",
    20→]
    21→
    22→
    23→def append_full_sweep_batch(
    24→    *,
    25→    batches: list[dict[str, Any]],
    26→    dims: list[str],
    27→    all_files: list[str],
    28→    lang: Any,
    29→    max_files: int | None = None,
    30→) -> None:
    31→    """Append an optional cross-cutting full-codebase batch."""
    32→    if not dims:
    33→        return
    34→    all_rel_files: list[str] = []
    35→    for filepath in all_files:
    36→        if lang.zone_map is not None:
    37→            zone = lang.zone_map.get(filepath)
    38→            if zone.value in ("test", "generated", "vendor"):
    39→                continue
    40→        all_rel_files.append(rel(filepath))
    41→        if isinstance(max_files, int) and max_files > 0 and len(all_rel_files) >= max_files:
    42→            break
    43→    if not all_rel_files:
    44→        return
    45→    batches.append(
    46→        {
    47→            "name": "Full Codebase Sweep",
    48→            "dimensions": list(dims),
    49→            "files_to_read": all_rel_files,
    50→            "why": "thorough default: evaluate cross-cutting quality across all production files",
    51→        }
    52→    )
    53→

    10→def _require_triage_pending(plan: dict, *, action: str) -> bool:

    12→    order = set(plan.get("queue_order", []))
    13→    if order & TRIAGE_IDS:

    18→
    19→def _validate_stage_report(
    20→    report: str | None,
    21→    *,
    22→    stage: str,
    23→    min_chars: int,
    24→    missing_guidance: list[str] | None = None,
    25→    short_guidance: list[str] | None = None,
    26→) -> str | None:
    27→    """Validate staged report presence/length and print consistent guidance."""
    28→    if not report:
    29→        print(colorize(f"  --report is required for --stage {stage}.", "red"))
    30→        for line in missing_guidance or []:
    31→            print(colorize(f"  {line}", "dim"))
    32→        return None
    33→    cleaned = report.strip()

    38→                "red",
    39→            )
    40→        )
    41→        for line in short_guidance or []:
    42→            print(colorize(f"  {line}", "dim"))
    43→        return None
    44→    return cleaned
    45→

    47→def _triage_coverage(plan: dict) -> tuple[int, int, dict]:
    48→    """Return (organized, total, clusters) for triage progress."""
    49→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
    50→    all_cluster_ids: set[str] = set()
    51→    for cluster in clusters.values():
    52→        all_cluster_ids.update(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
    53→    queue_ids = [issue_id for issue_id in plan.get("queue_order", []) if issue_id not in TRIAGE_IDS]
    54→    organized = sum(1 for issue_id in queue_ids if issue_id in all_cluster_ids)
    55→    return organized, len(queue_ids), clusters

    58→def _unenriched_clusters(plan: dict) -> list[tuple[str, list[str]]]:
    59→    """Return clusters with issues that are missing required enrichment.
    60→
    61→    Requirements:
    62→    - Every cluster needs a description and at least one action_step.
    63→    - Small clusters (< 5 issues) need at least 1 action step per issue,
    64→      so each item has a concrete plan. Large clusters (>= 5) just need
    65→      steps overall (cluster-level plan is sufficient).
    66→    """
    67→    gaps: list[tuple[str, list[str]]] = []
    68→    for name, cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items():
    69→        if not cluster.get("issue_ids"):
    70→            continue
    71→        if cluster.get("auto"):
    72→            continue
    73→        missing: list[str] = []
    74→        if not cluster.get("description"):
    75→            missing.append("description")
    76→        steps = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
    77→        issue_count = len(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
    78→        if not steps:
    79→            missing.append("action_steps")
    80→        elif issue_count < 5 and len(steps) < issue_count:
    81→            missing.append(
    82→                f"action_steps (have {len(steps)}, need >= {issue_count} for small cluster)"
    83→            )
    84→        if missing:
    85→            gaps.append((name, missing))
    86→    return gaps

    92→    When *state* is provided, uses open review/concerns issues from state
    93→    (the canonical source). Falls back to scanning queue_order for backwards

    97→    clustered_ids: set[str] = set()
    98→    for cluster in clusters.values():
    99→        if not cluster.get("auto"):
   100→            clustered_ids.update(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   101→
   102→    if state is not None:
   103→        review_ids = [
   104→            fid for fid, f in state.get("issues", {}).items()
   105→            if f.get("status") == "open" and f.get("detector") in _REVIEW_DETECTORS
   106→        ]
   107→    else:

    25→@dataclass(frozen=True)

    40→def _validate_resolve_inputs(args: argparse.Namespace, attestation: str | None) -> None:
    41→    if args.status == "wontfix" and not args.note:
    42→        raise CommandError(
    43→            "Wontfix items become technical debt. Add --note to record your reasoning for future review."
    44→        )
    45→    if args.status == "open":
    46→        return
    47→    if not validate_attestation(attestation):
    48→        show_attestation_requirement(
    49→            "Manual resolve",

    51→            ATTEST_EXAMPLE,
    52→        )
    53→        raise CommandError("Manual resolve requires a valid attestation.")
    54→

    56→def _previous_score_snapshot(state: dict) -> state_mod.ScoreSnapshot:
    57→    """Load a score snapshot for comparison after resolve operations."""
    58→    return state_mod.score_snapshot(state)
    59→
    60→
    61→def _preview_resolve_count(state: dict, patterns: list[str]) -> int:
    62→    """Count unique open issues matching the provided patterns."""
    63→    matched_ids: set[str] = set()
    64→    for pattern in patterns:
    65→        for issue in state_mod.match_issues(state, pattern, status_filter="open"):
    66→            issue_id = issue.get("id")
    67→            if issue_id:
    68→                matched_ids.add(issue_id)
    69→    return len(matched_ids)

    71→
    72→def _estimate_wontfix_strict_delta(
    73→    state: dict,
    74→    args: argparse.Namespace,
    75→    *,
    76→    attestation: str | None,
    77→    resolve_all_patterns_fn,
    78→) -> float:
    79→    """Estimate strict score drop if this resolve command is applied as wontfix."""
    80→    before = state_mod.score_snapshot(state).strict
    81→    if before is None:
    82→        return 0.0
    83→
    84→    preview_state = copy.deepcopy(state)
    85→    resolve_all_patterns_fn(preview_state, args, attestation=attestation)
    86→    after = state_mod.score_snapshot(preview_state).strict
    87→    if after is None:
    88→        return 0.0
    89→    return max(0.0, before - after)
    90→
    91→
    92→def _enforce_batch_wontfix_confirmation(
    93→    state: dict,
    94→    args: argparse.Namespace,
    95→    *,
    96→    attestation: str | None,
    97→    resolve_all_patterns_fn,
    98→) -> None:
    99→    if args.status != "wontfix":
   100→        return
   101→
   102→    preview_count = _preview_resolve_count(state, args.patterns)
   103→    if preview_count <= 10:
   104→        return
   105→    if getattr(args, "confirm_batch_wontfix", False):
   106→        return
   107→
   108→    strict_delta = _estimate_wontfix_strict_delta(
   109→        state,

   112→        resolve_all_patterns_fn=resolve_all_patterns_fn,
   113→    )
   114→    _emit_warning(f"Large wontfix batch detected ({preview_count} issues).")
   115→    if strict_delta > 0:
   116→        _emit_warning(f"Estimated strict-score debt added now: {strict_delta:.1f} points.")
   117→    raise CommandError(
   118→        "Re-run with --confirm-batch-wontfix if this debt is intentional."
   119→    )

Findings illustrate and support your score \u2014 they are the \"here is what I saw\" behind your judgment.\n\nGLOBAL ANCHORS \u2014 what each score range means:\n- 100: exemplary. A developer working here would find this quality reliably strong with no material issues.\n- 90: strong.    238→def _shallow_steps(plan: dict) -> list[tuple[str, int, int]]:
   239→    """Return (cluster_name, bare_count, total_count) for clusters with steps lacking detail."""
   240→    results: list[tuple[str, int, int]] = []
   241→    for name, cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items():
   242→        if cluster.get("auto") or not cluster.get("issue_ids"):
   243→            continue
   244→        steps = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
   245→        if not steps:
   246→            continue
   247→        bare = sum(
   248→            1 for s in steps
   249→            if isinstance(s, dict) and not s.get("detail") and not s.get("issue_refs")
   250→        )
   251→        if bare > 0:
   252→            results.append((name, bare, len(steps)))
   253→    return results
