    30→_UNSCORED_NAME = "auto/initial-review"
    31→_UNDER_TARGET_KEY = "subjective::under-target"
    32→_UNDER_TARGET_NAME = "auto/under-target-review"
    33→_MIN_UNSCORED_CLUSTER_SIZE = 1
    34→
    35→
    36→def _manual_member_ids(clusters: dict) -> set[str]:
    37→    """Collect all issue IDs belonging to manual (non-auto) clusters."""
    38→    ids: set[str] = set()
    39→    for cluster in clusters.values():
    40→        if not cluster.get("auto"):
    41→            ids.update(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
    42→    return ids
    43→
    44→
    45→def _group_clusterable_issues(
    46→    issues: dict,
    47→    *,
    48→    manual_member_ids: set[str],
    49→) -> tuple[dict[str, list[str]], dict[str, dict]]:
    50→    """Group open, non-suppressed, non-manual issues by detector/subtype key.
    51→
    52→    Returns (groups_by_key, issue_data) where groups_by_key maps grouping keys
    53→    to lists of issue IDs, filtered to clusters >= _MIN_CLUSTER_SIZE.
    54→    """
    55→    groups: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
    56→    issue_data: dict[str, dict] = {}
    57→    for fid, issue in issues.items():
    58→        if issue.get("status") != "open":
    59→            continue
    60→        if issue.get("suppressed"):
    61→            continue
    62→        if fid in manual_member_ids:
    63→            continue
    64→
    65→        detector = issue.get("detector", "")
    66→        meta = DETECTORS.get(detector)
    67→        key = _grouping_key(issue, meta)
    68→        if key is None:
    69→            continue
    70→
    71→        groups[key].append(fid)
    72→        issue_data[fid] = issue
    73→
    74→    groups = {k: v for k, v in groups.items() if len(v) >= _MIN_CLUSTER_SIZE}
    75→    return groups, issue_data
    76→
    77→
    78→def _sync_user_modified_cluster_members(
    79→    plan: dict,
    80→    *,
    81→    clusters: dict,
    82→    existing_name: str,
    83→    member_ids: list[str],
    84→    now: str,
    85→) -> int:
    86→    """Sync member IDs for a user-modified cluster, returns count of changes."""
    87→    cluster = clusters[existing_name]
    88→    changes = 0
    89→    existing_ids = set(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
    90→    new_ids = [fid for fid in member_ids if fid not in existing_ids]
    91→    if new_ids:
    92→        cluster["issue_ids"].extend(new_ids)
    93→        cluster["updated_at"] = now
    94→        changes = 1
    95→    overrides = plan.get("overrides", {})
    96→    for fid in member_ids:
    97→        if fid not in overrides:
    98→            overrides[fid] = {"issue_id": fid, "created_at": now}
    99→        overrides[fid]["cluster"] = existing_name
   100→        overrides[fid]["updated_at"] = now
   101→    return changes
   102→
   103→
   104→def _subjective_state_sets(
   105→    state: StateModel,
   106→    *,
   107→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility | None,
   108→    target_strict: float,
   109→) -> tuple[set, set, set]:
   110→    """Return (stale_ids, under_target_ids, unscored_ids) for subjective cluster logic."""
   111→    if policy is not None:
   112→        unscored_ids = policy.unscored_ids
   113→        stale_ids = policy.stale_ids
   114→        under_target_ids = policy.under_target_ids
   115→    else:
   116→        unscored_ids = current_unscored_ids(state)
   117→        stale_ids = _current_stale_ids(state)
   118→        under_target_ids = current_under_target_ids(state, target_strict=target_strict)
   119→    return stale_ids, under_target_ids, unscored_ids
   120→
   121→
   122→def _has_objective_backlog(
   123→    issues: dict,
   124→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility | None,
   125→) -> bool:
   126→    """Check if objective backlog exists (open non-subjective issues)."""
   127→    if policy is not None:
   128→        return policy.has_objective_backlog
   129→    return any(
   130→        f.get("status") == "open"
   131→        and f.get("detector") not in NON_OBJECTIVE_DETECTORS
   132→        and not f.get("suppressed")
   133→        for f in issues.values()
   134→    )
   135→
   136→
   137→def _sync_auto_cluster(
   138→    plan: dict,
   139→    clusters: dict,
   140→    existing_by_key: dict[str, str],
   141→    *,
   142→    cluster_key: str,
   143→    cluster_name: str,
   144→    member_ids: list[str],
   145→    description: str,
   146→    action: str,
   147→    now: str,
   148→    optional: bool = False,
   149→) -> int:
   150→    """Create or update an auto-cluster and sync its override entries."""
   151→    changes = 0
   152→    existing_name = existing_by_key.get(cluster_key)
   153→    if existing_name and existing_name in clusters:
   154→        cluster = clusters[existing_name]
   155→        old_ids = set(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   156→        new_ids_set = set(member_ids)
   157→        if (
   158→            old_ids != new_ids_set
   159→            or cluster.get("description") != description
   160→            or cluster.get("action") != action
   161→        ):
   162→            cluster["issue_ids"] = list(member_ids)
   163→            cluster["description"] = description
   164→            cluster["action"] = action
   165→            cluster["updated_at"] = now
   166→            changes = 1
   167→    else:
   168→        new_cluster = {
   169→            "name": cluster_name,
   170→            "description": description,
   171→            "issue_ids": list(member_ids),
   172→            "created_at": now,
   173→            "updated_at": now,
   174→            "auto": True,
   175→            "cluster_key": cluster_key,
   176→            "action": action,
   177→            "user_modified": False,
   178→        }
   179→        if optional:
   180→            new_cluster["optional"] = True
   181→        clusters[cluster_name] = new_cluster
   182→        existing_by_key[cluster_key] = cluster_name
   183→        changes = 1
   184→
   185→    overrides = plan.get("overrides", {})
   186→    current_name = existing_by_key.get(cluster_key, cluster_name)
   187→    for fid in member_ids:
   188→        if fid not in overrides:
   189→            overrides[fid] = {"issue_id": fid, "created_at": now}
   190→        overrides[fid]["cluster"] = current_name
   191→        overrides[fid]["updated_at"] = now
   192→
   193→    return changes
   194→
   195→
   196→def sync_issue_clusters(
   197→    plan: dict,
   198→    issues: dict,
   199→    clusters: dict,
   200→    existing_by_key: dict[str, str],
   201→    active_auto_keys: set[str],
   202→    now: str,
   203→) -> int:
   204→    """Group open issues by detector/subtype and sync auto-clusters."""
   205→    changes = 0
   206→
   207→    groups, issue_data = _group_clusterable_issues(
   208→        issues, manual_member_ids=_manual_member_ids(clusters)
   209→    )
   210→
   211→    for key, member_ids in groups.items():
   212→        active_auto_keys.add(key)
   213→        cluster_name = _cluster_name_from_key(key)
   214→
   215→        rep = issue_data.get(member_ids[0], {})
   216→        detector = rep.get("detector", "")
   217→        meta = DETECTORS.get(detector)
   218→        members = [issue_data[fid] for fid in member_ids if fid in issue_data]
   219→
   220→        key_parts = key.split("::")
   221→        subtype = key_parts[2] if len(key_parts) >= 3 else None
   222→
   223→        description = _generate_description(cluster_name, members, meta, subtype)
   224→        action = _generate_action(meta, subtype)
   225→
   226→        existing_name = existing_by_key.get(key)
   227→        if existing_name and existing_name in clusters:
   228→            cluster = clusters[existing_name]
   229→            if cluster.get("user_modified"):
   230→                changes += _sync_user_modified_cluster_members(
   231→                    plan,
   232→                    clusters=clusters,
   233→                    existing_name=existing_name,
   234→                    member_ids=member_ids,
   235→                    now=now,
   236→                )
   237→                continue
   238→
   239→        if cluster_name in clusters and clusters[cluster_name].get("cluster_key") != key:
   240→            cluster_name = f"{cluster_name}-{len(member_ids)}"
   241→
   242→        changes += _sync_auto_cluster(
   243→            plan,
   244→            clusters,
   245→            existing_by_key,
   246→            cluster_key=key,
   247→            cluster_name=cluster_name,
   248→            member_ids=member_ids,
   249→            description=description,
   250→            action=action,
   251→            now=now,
   252→        )
   253→
   254→    return changes
   255→
   256→
   257→def sync_subjective_clusters(
   258→    plan: dict,
   259→    state: StateModel,
   260→    issues: dict,
   261→    clusters: dict,
   262→    existing_by_key: dict[str, str],
   263→    active_auto_keys: set[str],
   264→    now: str,
   265→    *,
   266→    target_strict: float,
   267→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility | None = None,
   268→    cycle_just_completed: bool = False,
   269→) -> int:
   270→    """Sync unscored, stale, and under-target subjective dimension clusters."""
   271→    changes = 0
   272→
   273→    all_subjective_ids = sorted(
   274→        fid for fid in plan.get("queue_order", [])
   275→        if fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX)
   276→    )
   277→
   278→    stale_state_ids, under_target_ids, unscored_state_ids = _subjective_state_sets(
   279→        state, policy=policy, target_strict=target_strict
   280→    )
   281→
   282→    unscored_queue_ids = sorted(
   283→        fid for fid in all_subjective_ids if fid in unscored_state_ids
   284→    )
   285→    stale_queue_ids = sorted(
   286→        fid for fid in all_subjective_ids
   287→        if fid in stale_state_ids and fid not in unscored_state_ids
   288→    )
   289→
   290→    if len(unscored_queue_ids) >= _MIN_UNSCORED_CLUSTER_SIZE:
   291→        active_auto_keys.add(_UNSCORED_KEY)
   292→        cli_keys = [fid.removeprefix(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX) for fid in unscored_queue_ids]
   293→        description = (
   294→            f"Initial review of {len(unscored_queue_ids)} unscored subjective dimensions"
   295→        )
   296→        action = f"desloppify review --prepare --dimensions {','.join(cli_keys)}"
   297→        changes += _sync_auto_cluster(
   298→            plan,
   299→            clusters,
   300→            existing_by_key,
   301→            cluster_key=_UNSCORED_KEY,
   302→            cluster_name=_UNSCORED_NAME,
   303→            member_ids=unscored_queue_ids,
   304→            description=description,
   305→            action=action,
   306→            now=now,
   307→        )
   308→
   309→    if len(stale_queue_ids) >= _MIN_CLUSTER_SIZE:
   310→        active_auto_keys.add(_STALE_KEY)
   311→        cli_keys = [fid.removeprefix(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX) for fid in stale_queue_ids]
   312→        description = f"Re-review {len(stale_queue_ids)} stale subjective dimensions"
   313→        action = "desloppify review --prepare --dimensions " + ",".join(cli_keys)
   314→        changes += _sync_auto_cluster(
   315→            plan,
   316→            clusters,
   317→            existing_by_key,
   318→            cluster_key=_STALE_KEY,
   319→            cluster_name=_STALE_NAME,
   320→            member_ids=stale_queue_ids,
   321→            description=description,
   322→            action=action,
   323→            now=now,
   324→        )
   325→
   326→    under_target_queue_ids = sorted(under_target_ids)
   327→
   328→    prev_ut_cluster = clusters.get(_UNDER_TARGET_NAME, {})
   329→    prev_ut_ids = set(prev_ut_cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   330→    order = plan.get("queue_order", [])
   331→    ut_prune = [
   332→        fid for fid in prev_ut_ids
   333→        if fid not in under_target_ids
   334→        and fid not in stale_state_ids
   335→        and fid not in unscored_state_ids
   336→        and fid in order
   337→    ]
   338→    for fid in ut_prune:
   339→        order.remove(fid)
   340→        changes += 1
   341→
   342→    has_objective_items = _has_objective_backlog(issues, policy)
   343→
   344→    if not has_objective_items and len(under_target_queue_ids) >= _MIN_CLUSTER_SIZE:
   345→        active_auto_keys.add(_UNDER_TARGET_KEY)
   346→        cli_keys = [fid.removeprefix(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX) for fid in under_target_queue_ids]
   347→        description = (
   348→            f"Consider re-reviewing {len(under_target_queue_ids)} "
   349→            f"dimensions under target score"
   350→        )
   351→        action = "desloppify review --prepare --dimensions " + ",".join(cli_keys)
   352→        changes += _sync_auto_cluster(
   353→            plan,
   354→            clusters,
   355→            existing_by_key,
   356→            [REDACTED],
   357→            cluster_name=_UNDER_TARGET_NAME,
   358→            member_ids=under_target_queue_ids,
   359→            description=description,
   360→            action=action,
   361→            now=now,
   362→            optional=True,
   363→        )
   364→
   365→        existing_order = set(order)
   366→        for fid in under_target_queue_ids:
   367→            if fid not in existing_order:
   368→                order.append(fid)
   369→
   370→    if has_objective_items and not cycle_just_completed:
   371→        objective_evict = [
   372→            fid for fid in order
   373→            if fid in under_target_ids
   374→        ]
   375→        for fid in objective_evict:
   376→            order.remove(fid)
   377→            changes += 1
   378→
   379→    return changes
   380→
   381→
   382→def prune_stale_clusters(
   383→    plan: dict,
   384→    issues: dict,
   385→    clusters: dict,
   386→    active_auto_keys: set[str],
   387→    now: str,
   388→) -> int:
   389→    """Delete auto-clusters that no longer have matching groups."""
   390→    changes = 0
   391→    for name in list(clusters.keys()):
   392→        cluster = clusters[name]
   393→        if not cluster.get("auto"):
   394→            continue
   395→        ck = cluster.get("cluster_key", "")
   396→        if ck in active_auto_keys:
   397→            continue
   398→        if cluster.get("user_modified"):
   399→            alive = [
   400→                fid for fid in cluster.get("issue_ids", [])
   401→                if fid in issues and issues[fid].get("status") == "open"
   402→            ]
   403→            if alive:
   404→                if len(alive) != len(cluster.get("issue_ids", [])):
   405→                    cluster["issue_ids"] = alive
   406→                    cluster["updated_at"] = now
   407→                    changes += 1
   408→                continue
   409→        del clusters[name]
   410→        for fid in cluster.get("issue_ids", []):
   411→            override = plan.get("overrides", {}).get(fid)
   412→            if override and override.get("cluster") == name:
   413→                override["cluster"] = None
   414→                override["updated_at"] = now
   415→        if plan.get("active_cluster") == name:
   416→            plan["active_cluster"] = None
   417→        changes += 1
   418→    return changes
   419→
   420→
   421→__all__ = ["prune_stale_clusters", "sync_issue_clusters", "sync_subjective_clusters"]
   422→

a developer making a cross-module change must understand surprising implicit contracts.\n- low_level_elegance:\n  100 = function and class internals are concise, precise, and proportionate.\n  90 = mostly clean craft with isolated rough edges.\n  80 = a developer regularly encounters local complexity \u2014 deep nesting, over-extraction, defensive sprawl \u2014 that makes individual functions harder to follow than they should be.\n  60 = local implementation quality routinely impedes understanding; 1→"""Queue-order enforcement helpers for resolve command flows."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import logging
     6→
     7→from desloppify.base.exception_sets import PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS
     8→from desloppify.base.output.terminal import colorize
     9→from desloppify.engine._work_queue.context import queue_context
    10→from desloppify.engine._work_queue.core import (
    11→    QueueBuildOptions,
    12→    build_work_queue,
    13→)
    14→from desloppify.engine._work_queue.plan_order import collapse_clusters
    15→from desloppify.engine.plan import has_living_plan, load_plan
    16→
    17→_logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    18→
    19→
    20→def _front_item_ids(front_item: dict) -> tuple[str, set[str]]:
    21→    front_id = front_item["id"]
    22→    front_ids = {front_id}
    23→    if front_item.get("kind") != "cluster":
    24→        return front_id, front_ids
    25→    for member in front_item.get("members", []):
    26→        front_ids.add(member["id"])
    27→    return front_id, front_ids
    28→
    29→
    30→def _resolve_target_ids(patterns: list[str], clusters: dict) -> set[str]:
    31→    resolved_ids: set[str] = set()
    32→    for pattern in patterns:
    33→        if pattern in clusters:
    34→            resolved_ids.update(clusters[pattern].get("issue_ids", []))
    35→            resolved_ids.add(pattern)
    36→            continue
    37→        resolved_ids.add(pattern)
    38→    return resolved_ids
    39→
    40→
    41→def _filter_open_or_cluster_targets(
    42→    resolved_ids: set[str],
    43→    *,
    44→    clusters: dict,
    45→    issues: dict,
    46→) -> set[str]:
    47→    return {
    48→        issue_id
    49→        for issue_id in resolved_ids
    50→        if issue_id in clusters
    51→        or (issue_id in issues and issues[issue_id].get("status") == "open")
    52→    }
    53→
    54→
    55→def _prune_front_covered_clusters(
    56→    out_of_order: set[str],
    57→    *,
    58→    clusters: dict,
    59→    issues: dict,
    60→    front_ids: set[str],
    61→) -> None:
    62→    for cluster_id in list(out_of_order):
    63→        if cluster_id not in clusters:
    64→            continue
    65→        alive_members = {
    66→            issue_id
    67→            for issue_id in clusters[cluster_id].get("issue_ids", [])
    68→            if issue_id in issues and issues[issue_id].get("status") == "open"
    69→        }
    70→        if alive_members and alive_members <= front_ids:
    71→            out_of_order.discard(cluster_id)
    72→
    73→
    74→def _print_queue_order_violation(front_id: str, out_of_order: set[str]) -> None:
    75→    print(colorize("\n  Queue order violation: these items are not next in the plan queue:\n", "yellow"))
    76→    for issue_id in sorted(out_of_order):
    77→        print(f"    {issue_id}")
    78→    print(colorize(f"\n  The current next item is: {front_id}", "dim"))
    79→    print(colorize("  Items must be resolved in plan order. If you need to reprioritize:", "dim"))
    80→    print(colorize("    desloppify plan reorder <pattern> top            # move to front", "dim"))
    81→    print(colorize("    desloppify plan skip <pattern> --reason '...'    # skip for now", "dim"))
    82→    print(colorize("    desloppify next                                  # see what's next\n", "dim"))
    83→
    84→
    85→def _check_queue_order_guard(
    86→    state: dict,
    87→    patterns: list[str],
    88→    status: str,
    89→) -> bool:
    90→    """Warn and block if resolving items not at the front of the plan queue."""
    91→    if status != "fixed":
    92→        return False
    93→    try:
    94→        if not has_living_plan():
    95→            return False
    96→        plan = load_plan()
    97→        queue_order = plan.get("queue_order", [])
    98→        if not queue_order:
    99→            return False
   100→
   101→        ctx = queue_context(state, plan=plan)
   102→        result = build_work_queue(
   103→            state,
   104→            options=QueueBuildOptions(
   105→                count=None,
   106→                include_subjective=True,
   107→                context=ctx,
   108→            ),
   109→        )
   110→        items = result["items"]
   111→        if not plan.get("active_cluster"):
   112→            items = collapse_clusters(items, plan)
   113→        if not items:
   114→            return False
   115→
   116→        clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   117→        issues = state.get("issues", {})
   118→        resolved_ids = _resolve_target_ids(patterns, clusters)
   119→        resolved_ids = _filter_open_or_cluster_targets(
   120→            resolved_ids,
   121→            clusters=clusters,
   122→            issues=issues,
   123→        )
   124→        if not resolved_ids:
   125→            return False
   126→
   127→        # Collect IDs from the first N queue positions where N is the
   128→        # number of items being resolved.  This allows batch-resolving
   129→        # a contiguous prefix (e.g. the first 9 items in one command).
   130→        prefix_depth = max(len(resolved_ids), 1)
   131→        front_ids: set[str] = set()
   132→        front_id = items[0]["id"]
   133→        for item in items[:prefix_depth]:
   134→            _, item_ids = _front_item_ids(item)
   135→            front_ids.update(item_ids)
   136→
   137→        out_of_order = resolved_ids - front_ids
   138→        _prune_front_covered_clusters(
   139→            out_of_order,
   140→            clusters=clusters,
   141→            issues=issues,
   142→            front_ids=front_ids,
   143→        )
   144→        if not out_of_order:
   145→            return False
   146→
   147→        _print_queue_order_violation(front_id, out_of_order)
   148→        return True
   149→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS:
   150→        _logger.debug("queue order guard skipped", exc_info=True)
   151→        return False
   152→
   153→
   154→__all__ = ["_check_queue_order_guard"]
   155→

    68→def print_progress(plan: dict, open_issues: dict) -> None:
    69→    """Show cluster state and unclustered issues."""
    70→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
    71→    # Only show clusters that actually have issues (hide empty/stale ones)
    72→    active_clusters = {
    73→        name: c for name, c in clusters.items()
    74→        if c.get("issue_ids")
    75→    }
    76→    if active_clusters:
    77→        print(colorize("\n  Current clusters:", "cyan"))
    78→        for name, cluster in active_clusters.items():
    79→            count = len(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
    80→            desc = cluster.get("description") or ""
    81→            steps = cluster.get("action_steps", [])
    82→            auto = cluster.get("auto", False)
    83→            tags: list[str] = []
    84→            if auto:
    85→                tags.append("auto")
    86→            if desc:
    87→                tags.append("desc")
    88→            else:
    89→                tags.append("no desc")
    90→            if steps:
    91→                tags.append(f"{len(steps)} steps")
    92→            else:
    93→                if not auto:
    94→                    tags.append("no steps")
    95→            tag_str = f" [{', '.join(tags)}]"
    96→            desc_str = f" \u2014 {desc}" if desc else ""
    97→            print(f"    {name}: {count} items{tag_str}{desc_str}")
    98→
    99→    all_clustered: set[str] = set()
   100→    for c in clusters.values():
   101→        all_clustered.update(c.get("issue_ids", []))
   102→    unclustered = [fid for fid in open_issues if fid not in all_clustered]
   103→    if unclustered:
   104→        print(colorize(f"\n  {len(unclustered)} issues not yet in a cluster:", "yellow"))
   105→        for fid in unclustered[:10]:
   106→            f = open_issues[fid]
   107→            dim = (f.get("detail", {}) or {}).get("dimension", "") if isinstance(f.get("detail"), dict) else ""
   108→            short = short_issue_id(fid)
   109→            print(f"    [{short}] [{dim}] {f.get('summary', '')}")
   110→        if len(unclustered) > 10:
   111→            print(colorize(f"    ... and {len(unclustered) - 10} more", "dim"))
   112→    elif open_issues:
   113→        organized, total, _ = triage_coverage(plan, open_review_ids=set(open_issues.keys()))
   114→        print(colorize(f"\n  All {organized}/{total} issues are in clusters.", "green"))

   203→def print_reflect_dashboard(
   204→    si: object,
   205→    plan: dict,

   208→) -> None:
   209→    """Show completed clusters, resolved issues, and recurring patterns."""

   212→    completed = getattr(si, "completed_clusters", [])
   213→    resolved = getattr(si, "resolved_issues", {})
   214→    open_issues = getattr(si, "open_issues", {})
   215→
   216→    if completed:

   219→            name = c.get("name", "?")

   221→            thesis = c.get("thesis", "")
   222→            print(f"    {name}: {count} issues")

   249→            print(colorize(

   347→    elif "enrich" not in stages:

   352→        else:

   362→def _print_prior_stage_reports(stages: dict) -> None:
   363→    """Print prior stage reports (observe/reflect) as context for current action."""

   365→        obs_report = stages["observe"].get("report", "")

   382→def _print_issues_by_dimension(open_issues: dict) -> None:
   383→    """Print issues grouped by dimension with suggestions to surface contradictions."""
   384→    by_dim: dict[str, list[tuple[str, dict]]] = defaultdict(list)
   385→    for fid, f in open_issues.items():
   386→        detail = f.get("detail", {}) if isinstance(f.get("detail"), dict) else {}
   387→        dim = detail.get("dimension", "unknown")
   388→        by_dim[dim].append((fid, f))
   389→
   390→    print(colorize("\n  Review issues by dimension:", "cyan"))
   391→    print(colorize("  (Look for contradictions: issues in the same dimension that", "dim"))
   392→    print(colorize("  recommend opposite changes. These must be resolved before clustering.)", "dim"))
   393→    max_per_dim = 5
   394→    for dim in sorted(by_dim, key=lambda d: (-len(by_dim[d]), d)):
   395→        items = by_dim[dim]
   396→        print(colorize(f"\n    {dim} ({len(items)}):", "bold"))
   397→        for fid, f in items[:max_per_dim]:
   398→            summary = f.get("summary", "")
   399→            short = short_issue_id(fid)
   400→            detail = f.get("detail", {}) if isinstance(f.get("detail"), dict) else {}
   401→            suggestion = (detail.get("suggestion") or "")[:120]
   402→            print(f"      [{short}] {summary}")
   403→            if suggestion:
   404→                print(colorize(f"        \u2192 {suggestion}", "dim"))
   405→        if len(items) > max_per_dim:
   406→            print(colorize(f"      ... and {len(items) - max_per_dim} more", "dim"))
   407→    print(colorize("\n  Use hash in commands: desloppify plan skip <hash>  |  desloppify show <hash>", "dim"))

   410→def cmd_triage_dashboard(
   411→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   412→    *,
   413→    services: TriageServices | None = None,
   414→) -> None:
   415→    """Default view: show issues, stage progress, and next command."""
   416→    resolved_services = services or default_triage_services()
   417→    runtime = resolved_services.command_runtime(args)
   418→    state = runtime.state
   419→    plan = resolved_services.load_plan()
   420→    si = resolved_services.collect_triage_input(plan, state)
   421→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   422→    stages = meta.get("triage_stages", {})
   423→
   424→    _print_dashboard_header(si, stages, meta, plan)
   425→    _print_action_guidance(stages, meta, si, plan)
   426→    _print_prior_stage_reports(stages)
   427→    _print_issues_by_dimension(si.open_issues)
   428→
   429→    # Show reflect dashboard when observe done, reflect not done
   430→    if "observe" in stages and "reflect" not in stages:
   431→        print_reflect_dashboard(si, plan, services=resolved_services)
   432→
   433→    # Show current cluster progress
   434→    print_progress(plan, si.open_issues)

   436→def show_plan_summary(plan: dict, state: dict) -> None:
   437→    """Print a compact plan rendering: clusters + queue order + coverage."""
   438→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   439→    active = {
   440→        n: c for n, c in clusters.items()
   441→        if c.get("issue_ids") and not c.get("auto")
   442→    }
   443→    issues = state.get("issues", {})
   444→
   445→    if active:
   446→        print(colorize(f"\n  Clusters ({len(active)}):", "bold"))
   447→        for name, cluster in active.items():
   448→            count = len(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   449→            steps = len(cluster.get("action_steps", []))
   450→            desc = (cluster.get("description") or "")[:60]
   451→            print(f"    {name}: {count} items, {steps} steps — {desc}")
   452→
   453→    queue_order = [
   454→        fid for fid in plan.get("queue_order", [])
   455→        if not fid.startswith("triage::") and not fid.startswith("workflow::")
   456→    ]
   457→    if queue_order:
   458→        show = min(15, len(queue_order))
   459→        print(colorize(f"\n  Queue order (first {show} of {len(queue_order)}):", "bold"))
   460→        for i, fid in enumerate(queue_order[:show]):
   461→            f = issues.get(fid, {})
   462→            summary = (f.get("summary") or fid)[:60]
   463→            detector = f.get("detector", "?")
   464→            cn = find_cluster_for(fid, active)
   465→            print(f"    {i+1}. [{detector}] {summary}{f' ({cn})' if cn else ''}")
   466→
   467→    organized, total, _ = triage_coverage(
   468→        plan, open_review_ids=open_review_ids_from_state(state),
   469→    )
   470→    pct = int(organized / total * 100) if total else 0
   471→    print(colorize(f"\n  Coverage: {organized}/{total} in clusters ({pct}%)", "bold"))
   472→

    49→@dataclass(frozen=True)
    50→class QueueBuildOptions:
    51→    """Configuration for queue construction.
    52→
    53→    ``scan_path`` defaults to reading from ``state["scan_path"]`` so callers
    54→    don't need to thread it manually.  Pass an explicit ``str`` or ``None``
    55→    to override (``None`` disables scope filtering).
    56→    """
    57→
    58→    # Output control
    59→    count: int | None = 1
    60→    explain: bool = False
    61→
    62→    # Scope filtering
    63→    scan_path: str | None | object = _SCAN_PATH_FROM_STATE
    64→    scope: str | None = None
    65→    status: str = "open"
    66→    chronic: bool = False
    67→
    68→    # Subjective gating
    69→    include_subjective: bool = True
    70→    subjective_threshold: float = 100.0
    71→
    72→    # Plan integration
    73→    plan: dict | None = None
    74→    include_skipped: bool = False
    75→    cluster: str | None = None
    76→
    77→    # Pre-computed context (overrides plan)
    78→    context: QueueContext | None = None
    79→

    81→class WorkQueueResult(TypedDict):
    82→    """Typed shape of the dict returned by :func:`build_work_queue`."""
    83→
    84→    items: list[WorkQueueItem]
    85→    total: int
    86→    grouped: dict[str, list[WorkQueueItem]]
    87→    new_ids: set[str]
    88→
    89→
    90→def build_work_queue(
    91→    state: StateModel,
    92→    *,
    93→    options: QueueBuildOptions | None = None,
    94→) -> WorkQueueResult:
    95→    """Build a ranked work queue from state issues.
    96→
    97→    Pipeline:
    98→    1. Gather    — issue items, subjective dimensions, workflow stages
    99→    2. Score     — estimate impact from dimension headroom
   100→    3. Presort   — stamp plan positions, separate skipped items
   101→    4. Lifecycle — filter endgame-only items when objective work remains
   102→    5. Sort      — rank by impact/confidence, apply plan order
   103→    6. Limit     — truncate to count, optionally add explain metadata
   104→    """
   105→    opts = options or QueueBuildOptions()
   106→    plan, scan_path, status, threshold = _resolve_inputs(opts, state)
   107→
   108→    # 1. Gather
   109→    items = build_issue_items(
   110→        state, scan_path=scan_path, status_filter=status,
   111→        scope=opts.scope, chronic=opts.chronic,
   112→    )
   113→    items += _gather_subjective_items(state, opts, threshold)
   114→    items += _gather_workflow_items(state, plan, status)
   115→
   116→    # 2. Score
   117→    enrich_with_impact(items, state.get("dimension_scores", {}))
   118→
   119→    # 3. Plan-aware ordering (part 1: separate skipped items)
   120→    new_ids, skipped = _plan_presort(items, state, plan)
   121→
   122→    # 4. Lifecycle filter — endgame-only items filtered when objective work remains
   123→    items = _apply_lifecycle_filter(items)
   124→
   125→    # 5. Sort & plan post-processing
   126→    items.sort(key=item_sort_key)
   127→    _plan_postsort(items, skipped, plan, opts)
   128→
   129→    # 6. Finalize
   130→    if not items:
   131→        items += _empty_queue_fallback(plan)
   132→    total = len(items)
   133→    if opts.count is not None and opts.count > 0:
   134→        items = items[:opts.count]
   135→    if opts.explain:
   136→        for item in items:
   137→            item["explain"] = item_explain(item)
   138→
   139→    return {
   140→        "items": items,
   141→        "total": total,
   142→        "grouped": group_queue_items(items, "item"),
   143→        "new_ids": new_ids,
   144→    }
   145→
   146→
   147→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   148→# Pipeline helpers (private to this module)
   149→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   150→
   151→
   152→def _resolve_inputs(
   153→    opts: QueueBuildOptions, state: StateModel,
   154→) -> tuple[dict | None, str | None, str, float]:
   155→    """Resolve plan, scan_path, status, and subjective threshold from options."""
   156→    ctx = opts.context
   157→    plan = ctx.plan if ctx is not None else opts.plan
   158→
   159→    scan_path: str | None = (
   160→        state.get("scan_path")
   161→        if opts.scan_path is _SCAN_PATH_FROM_STATE
   162→        else opts.scan_path  # type: ignore[assignment]
   163→    )
   164→
   165→    status = opts.status
   166→    if status not in ALL_STATUSES:
   167→        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported status filter: {status}")
   168→
   169→    try:
   170→        threshold = float(opts.subjective_threshold)
   171→    except (TypeError, ValueError):
   172→        threshold = 100.0
   173→    threshold = max(0.0, min(100.0, threshold))
   174→
   175→    return plan, scan_path, status, threshold
   176→
   177→
   178→def _gather_subjective_items(
   179→    state: StateModel,
   180→    opts: QueueBuildOptions,
   181→    threshold: float,
   182→) -> list[WorkQueueItem]:
   183→    """Build subjective dimension candidates.
   184→
   185→    Lifecycle filtering (endgame gating) happens in _apply_lifecycle_filter,
   186→    not here. This function only handles configuration and scope.
   187→    """
   188→    if not opts.include_subjective:
   189→        return []
   190→    if opts.status not in {"open", "all"}:
   191→        return []
   192→    if opts.chronic:
   193→        return []
   194→
   195→    candidates = build_subjective_items(
   196→        state, state.get("issues", {}), threshold=threshold,
   197→    )
   198→    return [item for item in candidates if scope_matches(item, opts.scope)]
   199→
   200→
   201→def _gather_workflow_items(
   202→    state: StateModel, plan: dict | None, status: str,
   203→) -> list[WorkQueueItem]:
   204→    """Inject triage stages, checkpoints, and create-plan when plan is active."""
   205→    if not plan or status not in {"open", "all"}:
   206→        return []
   207→
   208→    items: list[WorkQueueItem] = list(build_triage_stage_items(plan, state))
   209→    for builder in (
   210→        build_score_checkpoint_item,
   211→        build_import_scores_item,
   212→        build_communicate_score_item,
   213→    ):
   214→        item = builder(plan, state)
   215→        if item is not None:
   216→            items.append(item)
   217→    plan_item = build_create_plan_item(plan)
   218→    if plan_item is not None:
   219→        items.append(plan_item)
   220→    return items
   221→
   222→
   223→
   224→def _plan_presort(
   225→    items: list[WorkQueueItem], state: StateModel, plan: dict | None,
   226→) -> tuple[set[str], list[WorkQueueItem]]:
   227→    """Enrich plan metadata and stamp sort keys before sorting.
   228→
   229→    Returns ``(new_ids, skipped)`` — skipped items are removed from
   230→    ``items`` in place and returned separately for post-sort re-append.
   231→    """
   232→    if not plan:
   233→        return set(), []
   234→
   235→    new_ids = _new_item_ids(state)
   236→    enrich_plan_metadata(items, plan)
   237→    stamp_plan_sort_keys(items, plan, new_ids)
   238→    remaining, skipped = separate_skipped(items, plan)
   239→    items[:] = remaining
   240→    return new_ids, skipped
   241→
   242→
   243→def _plan_postsort(
   244→    items: list[WorkQueueItem],
   245→    skipped: list[WorkQueueItem],
   246→    plan: dict | None,
   247→    opts: QueueBuildOptions,
   248→) -> None:
   249→    """Re-append skipped items, stamp positions, filter to cluster focus."""
   250→    if not plan:
   251→        return
   252→
   253→    if opts.include_skipped:
   254→        items.extend(skipped)
   255→    stamp_positions(items, plan)
   256→    focused = filter_cluster_focus(items, plan, opts.cluster)
   257→    items[:] = focused
   258→
   259→
   260→def _has_objective_items(items: list[WorkQueueItem]) -> bool:
   261→    """True if any objective mechanical work items remain in the queue."""
   262→    return any(
   263→        i.get("kind") == "issue"
   264→        and i.get("detector", "") not in NON_OBJECTIVE_DETECTORS
   265→        for i in items
   266→    )
   267→
   268→
   269→def _has_initial_reviews(items: list[WorkQueueItem]) -> bool:
   270→    """True if any unassessed subjective dimensions need initial review."""
   271→    return any(
   272→        i.get("kind") == "subjective_dimension"
   273→        and i.get("initial_review")
   274→        for i in items
   275→    )
   276→
   277→
   278→def _is_endgame_only(item: WorkQueueItem) -> bool:
   279→    """True if this item should only appear when the objective queue is drained."""
   280→    return (
   281→        item.get("kind") == "subjective_dimension"
   282→        and not item.get("initial_review")
   283→    )
   284→
   285→
   286→def _has_triage_stages(items: list[WorkQueueItem]) -> bool:
   287→    """True if any pending triage stage items are in the queue."""
   288→    return any(
   289→        i.get("kind") == "workflow_stage"
   290→        and str(i.get("id", "")).startswith("triage::")
   291→        for i in items
   292→    )
   293→
   294→
   295→def _apply_lifecycle_filter(items: list[WorkQueueItem]) -> list[WorkQueueItem]:
   296→    """Enforce lifecycle visibility rules.
   297→
   298→    The queue enforces a phase order: scan → initial review → triage → objective work.
   299→
   300→    1. **Initial reviews pending** → only show initial-review subjective items.
   301→       The user must complete first-time reviews before working objective items.
   302→    2. **Triage in progress** → only show triage stages and workflow items.
   303→       Cluster work items aren't ready until triage completes (enrich adds
   304→       the detail that makes steps actionable).
   305→    3. **Objective work remains** → show objective items, hide endgame-only
   306→       subjective reassessments (stale re-reviews).
   307→    4. **Objective drained** → everything visible (endgame).
   308→    """
   309→    if _has_initial_reviews(items):
   310→        # Phase 1: only initial reviews visible — triage and workflow
   311→        # items stay hidden until initial reviews are complete.
   312→        return [
   313→            i for i in items
   314→            if i.get("kind") == "subjective_dimension" and i.get("initial_review")
   315→        ]
   316→    if _has_triage_stages(items):
   317→        # Phase 2: triage in progress — only triage stages and workflow items visible.
   318→        # Cluster work items aren't ready until enrich completes.
   319→        return [
   320→            i for i in items
   321→            if i.get("kind") in ("workflow_stage", "workflow_action")
   322→        ]
   323→    if not _has_objective_items(items):
   324→        return items  # endgame: everything visible
   325→    return [i for i in items if not _is_endgame_only(i)]
   326→
   327→
   328→def _empty_queue_fallback(plan: dict | None) -> list[WorkQueueItem]:
   329→    """Return a 'run scan' nudge when an active plan cycle has cleared."""
   330→    if not plan:
   331→        return []
   332→    plan_scores = plan.get("plan_start_scores", {})
   333→    if plan_scores.get("strict") is None:
   334→        return []
   335→    return [{

1→"""Shared issue-merge primitives.
     2→
     3→Both ``app/commands/review/merge.py`` (post-import CLI) and
     4→``app/commands/review/batch_core.py`` (batch accumulation) need the same
     5→dedup-and-merge mechanics.  Extracting them here prevents drift.
     6→"""
     7→
     8→from __future__ import annotations
     9→
    10→from collections.abc import Sequence
    11→
    12→
    13→def normalize_word_set(text: str) -> set[str]:
    14→    """Tokenize *text* into lowercase words >= 3 chars."""
    15→    words = "".join(ch.lower() if ch.isalnum() else " " for ch in text).split()
    16→    return {word for word in words if len(word) >= 3}
    17→
    18→
    19→def merge_list_fields(
    20→    target: dict, source: dict, fields: Sequence[str]
    21→) -> None:
    22→    """Deduplicated merge of list *fields* from *source* into *target*."""
    23→    for field in fields:
    24→        merged: list[str] = []
    25→        seen: set[str] = set()
    26→        for src in (target.get(field), source.get(field)):
    27→            if not isinstance(src, list):
    28→                continue
    29→            for item in src:
    30→                value = str(item).strip()
    31→                if not value or value in seen:
    32→                    continue
    33→                seen.add(value)
    34→                merged.append(value)
    35→        if merged:
    36→            target[field] = merged
    37→
    38→
    39→def pick_longer_text(target: dict, source: dict, field: str) -> None:
    40→    """Keep the longer text value for a string *field*."""
    41→    target_text = str(target.get(field, "")).strip()
    42→    source_text = str(source.get(field, "")).strip()
    43→    if len(source_text) > len(target_text):
    44→        target[field] = source_text
    45→
    46→
    47→def track_merged_from(target: dict, source_id: str) -> None:
    48→    """Append *source_id* to ``target['merged_from']`` if not already present."""
    49→    merged_from = target.get("merged_from")
    50→    if not isinstance(merged_from, list):
    51→        merged_from = []
    52→    if source_id and source_id not in merged_from:
    53→        merged_from.append(source_id)
    54→    if merged_from:
    55→        target["merged_from"] = merged_from
    56→

   138→def _parse_and_validate_import(
   139→    import_file: str,
   140→    *,
   141→    config: ImportLoadConfig | None = None,
   142→    lang_name: str | None = None,
   143→    allow_partial: bool = False,
   144→    trusted_assessment_source: bool = False,
   145→    trusted_assessment_label: str | None = None,
   146→    attested_external: bool = False,
   147→    manual_override: bool = False,
   148→    manual_attest: str | None = None,
   149→) -> tuple[ReviewImportPayload | None, list[str]]:
   150→    """Parse and validate a review import file (pure function).
   151→
   152→    Returns ``(data, errors)`` where *data* is the normalized payload on
   153→    success, or ``None`` when errors prevent import.
   154→    """
   155→    options = config or ImportLoadConfig(
   156→        lang_name=lang_name,
   157→        allow_partial=allow_partial,
   158→        trusted_assessment_source=trusted_assessment_source,
   159→        trusted_assessment_label=trusted_assessment_label,
   160→        attested_external=attested_external,
   161→        manual_override=manual_override,
   162→        manual_attest=manual_attest,
   163→    )
   164→    issues_path = Path(import_file)
   165→    if not issues_path.exists():
   166→        return None, [f"file not found: {import_file}"]
   167→    try:
   168→        issues_data = json.loads(issues_path.read_text())
   169→    except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError) as exc:
   170→        return None, [f"error reading issues: {exc}"]
   171→
   172→    if isinstance(issues_data, list):
   173→        issues_data = {"issues": issues_data}
   174→
   175→    if not isinstance(issues_data, dict):
   176→        return None, ["issues file must contain a JSON array or object"]
   177→
   178→    if "issues" not in issues_data:
   179→        return None, ["issues object must contain a 'issues' key"]
   180→    normalized_issues_data, shape_errors = _normalize_import_payload_shape(
   181→        issues_data
   182→    )
   183→    if shape_errors:
   184→        return None, shape_errors
   185→    if normalized_issues_data is None:
   186→        raise ValueError(
   187→            "normalized import payload missing after successful shape validation"
   188→        )
   189→
   190→    override_enabled, override_attest = resolve_override_context(
   191→        manual_override=options.manual_override,
   192→        manual_attest=options.manual_attest,
   193→    )
   194→    if options.attested_external and override_enabled:
   195→        return None, [
   196→            "--attested-external cannot be combined with --manual-override"
   197→        ]
   198→    if options.attested_external and options.allow_partial:
   199→        return None, [
   200→            "--attested-external cannot be combined with --allow-partial; "
   201→            "attested score imports require fully valid issues payloads"
   202→        ]
   203→    if override_enabled and options.allow_partial:
   204→        return None, [
   205→            "--manual-override cannot be combined with --allow-partial; "
   206→            "manual score imports require fully valid issues payloads"
   207→        ]
   208→    issues_data, policy_errors = apply_assessment_import_policy(
   209→        normalized_issues_data,
   210→        import_file=import_file,
   211→        attested_external=options.attested_external,
   212→        attested_attest=override_attest,
   213→        manual_override=override_enabled,
   214→        manual_attest=override_attest,
   215→        trusted_assessment_source=options.trusted_assessment_source,
   216→        trusted_assessment_label=options.trusted_assessment_label,
   217→    )
   218→    if policy_errors:
   219→        return None, policy_errors
   220→    if issues_data is None:
   221→        raise ValueError(
   222→            "assessment import policy returned no payload without reporting errors"
   223→        )
   224→
   225→    missing_feedback, missing_low_score_issues = _validate_assessment_feedback(
   226→        issues_data
   227→    )
   228→    if missing_low_score_issues:
   229→        if override_enabled:
   230→            if not isinstance(override_attest, str) or not override_attest.strip():
   231→                return None, ["--manual-override requires --attest"]
   232→            return issues_data, []
   233→        return None, [
   234→            f"assessments below {LOW_SCORE_ISSUE_THRESHOLD:.1f} must include at "
   235→            "least one issue for that same dimension with a concrete suggestion. "
   236→            f"Missing: {', '.join(missing_low_score_issues)}"
   237→        ]
   238→
   239→    if missing_feedback:
   240→        if override_enabled:
   241→            if not isinstance(override_attest, str) or not override_attest.strip():
   242→                return None, ["--manual-override requires --attest"]
   243→            return issues_data, []
   244→        return None, [
   245→            f"assessments below {ASSESSMENT_FEEDBACK_THRESHOLD:.1f} must include explicit feedback "
   246→            "(issue with same dimension and non-empty suggestion, or "
   247→            "dimension_notes evidence for that dimension). "
   248→            f"Missing: {', '.join(missing_feedback)}"
   249→        ]
   250→
   251→    schema_errors = _validate_holistic_issues_schema(
   252→        issues_data,
   253→        lang_name=options.lang_name,
   254→    )
   255→    if schema_errors and not options.allow_partial:
   256→        visible_errors = schema_errors[:10]
   257→        remaining = len(schema_errors) - len(visible_errors)
   258→        errors = [
   259→            "issues schema validation failed for holistic import. "
   260→            "Fix payload or rerun with --allow-partial to continue."
   261→        ]
   262→        errors.extend(visible_errors)
   263→        if remaining > 0:
   264→            errors.append(f"... {remaining} additional schema error(s) omitted")
   265→        return None, errors
   266→
   267→    return issues_data, []

   273→    config: ImportLoadConfig | None = None,

   310→def print_assessment_policy_notice(
   311→    policy,

   338→        print(

    37→        payload: AssessmentProvenanceStatus = {

    30→def register_lang(name: str) -> Callable[[T], T]:
    31→    """Decorator to register a language config class.
    32→
    33→    Validates structure, instantiates the class, validates the contract,
    34→    and stores the *instance* in the registry.
    35→    """
    36→
    37→    def decorator(cls: T) -> T:
    38→        module = inspect.getmodule(cls)
    39→        if module and hasattr(module, "__file__"):
    40→            validate_lang_structure(Path(module.__file__).parent, name)
    41→        if isinstance(cls, type) and issubclass(cls, LangConfig):
    42→            cfg = make_lang_config(name, cls)  # instantiate + validate
    43→            registry_state.register(name, cfg)  # store instance
    44→        else:
    45→            registry_state.register(name, cls)  # test doubles
    46→        return cls
    47→
    48→    return decorator
    49→
    50→
    51→def register_generic_lang(name: str, cfg: LangConfig) -> None:
    52→    """Register a pre-built language plugin instance (no package structure required)."""
    53→    validate_lang_contract(name, cfg)
    54→    registry_state.register(name, cfg)
    55→
    56→
    57→def reload_lang_plugins() -> list[str]:
    58→    """Force plugin rediscovery and return refreshed language names."""
    59→    discovery.load_all(force_reload=True)
    60→    return sorted(registry_state.all_keys())

    26→    if isinstance(value, int | float):
    27→        return float(value)
    28→    if isinstance(value, str):
    29→        try:
    30→            return float(value)
    31→        except ValueError:
    32→            return None
    33→    return None
    34→
    35→
    36→def _structural_growth_details(
    37→    snapshot: dict[str, Any],
    38→    current: dict[str, Any],
    39→) -> dict[str, dict[str, float]]:
    40→    """Return structural drift details for wontfix issues."""
    41→    snapshot_detail = (
    42→        snapshot.get("detail", {}) if isinstance(snapshot.get("detail"), dict) else {}
    43→    )
    44→    current_detail = (
    45→        current.get("detail", {}) if isinstance(current.get("detail"), dict) else {}
    46→    )
    47→    drift: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = {}
    48→
    49→    old_complexity = _to_float(snapshot_detail.get("complexity_score"))
    50→    new_complexity = _to_float(current_detail.get("complexity_score"))
    51→    if (
    52→        old_complexity is not None
    53→        and new_complexity is not None
    54→        and new_complexity >= old_complexity + _STRUCTURAL_COMPLEXITY_GROWTH_THRESHOLD
    55→    ):
    56→        drift["complexity_score"] = {"from": old_complexity, "to": new_complexity}
    57→
    58→    old_loc = _to_float(snapshot_detail.get("loc"))
    59→    new_loc = _to_float(current_detail.get("loc"))
    60→    if (
    61→        old_loc is not None
    62→        and new_loc is not None
    63→        and new_loc >= old_loc + _STRUCTURAL_LOC_GROWTH_THRESHOLD
    64→    ):
    65→        drift["loc"] = {"from": old_loc, "to": new_loc}
    66→
    67→    return drift
    68→
    69→
    70→def _wontfix_staleness_reasons(
    71→    previous: dict[str, Any],
    72→    current: dict[str, Any],
    73→    *,
    74→    since_scan: int,
    75→    decay_scans: int,
    76→) -> tuple[list[str], dict[str, dict[str, float]]]:
    77→    """Determine why a wontfix issue is stale and compute structural drift."""
    78→    reasons: list[str] = []
    79→    if decay_scans > 0 and since_scan >= decay_scans:
    80→        reasons.append("scan_decay")
    81→
    82→    drift: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = {}
    83→    if previous.get("detector") == "structural":
    84→        snapshot = previous.get("wontfix_snapshot")
    85→        if isinstance(snapshot, dict):
    86→            drift = _structural_growth_details(snapshot, current)
    87→            if drift:
    88→                reasons.append("severity_drift")
    89→
    90→    return reasons, drift
    91→
    92→
    93→def _format_drift_summary(drift: dict[str, dict[str, float]]) -> str:
    94→    """Format structural drift metrics into a human-readable suffix."""
    95→    parts = []
    96→    if "complexity_score" in drift:
    97→        comp = drift["complexity_score"]
    98→        parts.append(f"complexity {comp['from']:.0f}->{comp['to']:.0f}")
    99→    if "loc" in drift:
   100→        loc = drift["loc"]
   101→        parts.append(f"loc {loc['from']:.0f}->{loc['to']:.0f}")
   102→    return f"; drift: {', '.join(parts)}" if parts else ""
   103→
   104→
   105→def _build_stale_wontfix_issue(
   106→    issue_id: str,
   107→    previous: dict[str, Any],
   108→    *,
   109→    reasons: list[str],
   110→    drift: dict[str, dict[str, float]],
   111→    since_scan: int,
   112→) -> dict[str, Any]:
   113→    """Construct a stale_wontfix issue from staleness metadata."""
   114→    tier = 4 if "severity_drift" in reasons else 3
   115→    confidence = "high" if "severity_drift" in reasons else "medium"
   116→    reason_text = " + ".join(reasons)
   117→    summary = (
   118→        f"Stale wontfix ({reason_text}): re-triage `{issue_id}` "
   119→        f"(last reviewed {since_scan} scans ago)"
   120→    )
   121→    summary += _format_drift_summary(drift)
   122→
   123→    return state_mod.make_issue(
   124→        "stale_wontfix",
   125→        previous.get("file", ""),
   126→        issue_id,
   127→        tier=tier,
   128→        confidence=confidence,
   129→        summary=summary,
   130→        detail={
   131→            "subtype": "stale_wontfix",
   132→            "original_issue_id": issue_id,
   133→            "original_detector": previous.get("detector"),
   134→            "reasons": reasons,
   135→            "scans_since_wontfix": since_scan,
   136→            "drift": drift,
   137→        },
   138→    )
   139→
   140→
   141→def augment_with_stale_wontfix_issues(
   142→    issues: list[dict[str, Any]],
   143→    *,
   144→    state: state_mod.StateModel,
   145→    scan_path: Path,
   146→    project_root: Path,
   147→    decay_scans: int,
   148→) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], int]:
   149→    """Append re-triage issues for stale or worsening wontfix debt."""
   150→    existing = state.get("issues", {})
   151→    if not isinstance(existing, dict):
   152→        return issues, 0
   153→
   154→    current_by_id = {
   155→        issue.get("id"): issue
   156→        for issue in issues
   157→        if issue.get("id")
   158→    }
   159→    augmented = list(issues)
   160→    monitored = 0
   161→
   162→    for issue_id, previous in existing.items():
   163→        if not isinstance(previous, dict):
   164→            continue
   165→        if previous.get("status") != "wontfix":
   166→            continue
   167→        if issue_id not in current_by_id:
   168→            continue
   169→        if not _in_scan_scope(
   170→            str(previous.get("file", "")),
   171→            scan_path,
   172→            project_root=project_root,
   173→        ):
   174→            continue
   175→
   176→        monitored += 1
   177→        scan_count = int(state.get("scan_count", 0) or 0)
   178→        since_scan = scan_count - int(previous.get("wontfix_scan_count", scan_count) or 0)
   179→        since_scan = max(since_scan, 0)
   180→
   181→        reasons, drift = _wontfix_staleness_reasons(
   182→            previous,
   183→            current_by_id[issue_id],
   184→            since_scan=since_scan,
   185→            decay_scans=decay_scans,
   186→        )
   187→        if not reasons:
   188→            continue
   189→
   190→        augmented.append(
   191→            _build_stale_wontfix_issue(
   192→                issue_id,
   193→                previous,
   194→                reasons=reasons,
   195→                drift=drift,
   196→                since_scan=since_scan,
   197→            )
   198→        )
   199→
   200→    return augmented, monitored
   201→
   202→
   203→__all__ = ["augment_with_stale_wontfix_issues"]
   204→

    20→def audit_excluded_dirs(
    21→    exclusions: tuple[str, ...],
    22→    scanned_files: list[str],
    23→    project_root: Path,
    24→) -> list[dict]:
    25→    """Check if any --exclude directory has zero references from scanned code.
    26→
    27→    Returns issues for directories that appear stale (no file references them).
    28→    """
    29→    if not exclusions:
    30→        return []
    31→
    32→    candidate_dirs = [
    33→        ex_dir
    34→        for ex_dir in exclusions
    35→        if ex_dir not in DEFAULT_EXCLUSIONS and (project_root / ex_dir).is_dir()
    36→    ]
    37→    if not candidate_dirs:
    38→        return []
    39→
    40→    # Read each scanned file once and mark any exclusions observed in content.
    41→    unresolved = set(candidate_dirs)
    42→    for filepath in scanned_files:
    43→        if not unresolved:
    44→            break
    45→        abs_path = (
    46→            filepath if Path(filepath).is_absolute() else str(project_root / filepath)
    47→        )
    48→        content = read_file_text(abs_path)
    49→        if content is None:
    50→            logger.debug(
    51→                "Skipping unreadable file %s while auditing exclusions", filepath
    52→            )
    53→            continue
    54→
    55→        matched = {ex_dir for ex_dir in unresolved if ex_dir in content}
    56→        if matched:
    57→            unresolved.difference_update(matched)
    58→
    59→    stale_issues = []
    60→    for ex_dir in candidate_dirs:
    61→        if ex_dir not in unresolved:
    62→            continue
    63→        stale_issues.append(
    64→            state_mod.make_issue(
    65→                "stale_exclude",
    66→                ex_dir,
    67→                ex_dir,
    68→                tier=4,
    69→                confidence="low",
    70→                summary=(
    71→                    f"Excluded directory '{ex_dir}' has 0 references from scanned code — "
    72→                    "may be stale"
    73→                ),
    74→                detail={"directory": ex_dir, "references": 0},
    75→            )
    76→        )
    77→    return stale_issues

    80→def collect_codebase_metrics(lang, path: Path) -> dict | None:
    81→    """Collect LOC/file/directory counts for the configured language."""
    82→    if not lang or not lang.file_finder:
    83→        return None
    84→    files = lang.file_finder(path)
    85→    total_loc = 0
    86→    dirs = set()
    87→    for filepath in files:
    88→        try:
    89→            total_loc += count_lines(Path(filepath))
    90→            dirs.add(str(Path(filepath).parent))
    91→        except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
    92→            logger.debug(
    93→                "Skipping unreadable file %s while collecting scan metrics: %s",
    94→                filepath,
    95→                exc,
    96→            )
    97→    return {
    98→        "total_files": len(files),
    99→        "total_loc": total_loc,
   100→        "total_directories": len(dirs),
   101→    }
   102→

   104→def resolve_scan_profile(profile: str | None, lang) -> str:
   105→    """Resolve effective scan profile from CLI and language defaults."""
   106→    if profile in {"objective", "full", "ci"}:
   107→        return profile
   108→    default_profile = getattr(lang, "default_scan_profile", "full") if lang else "full"
   109→    if default_profile in {"objective", "full", "ci"}:
   110→        return default_profile
   111→    return "full"
   112→
   113→
   114→def effective_include_slow(include_slow: bool, profile: str) -> bool:
   115→    """Determine whether slow phases should run for this profile."""
   116→    return include_slow and profile != "ci"
   117→
   118→
   119→def _format_hidden_by_detector(hidden_by_detector: dict[str, int]) -> str:
   120→    """Format hidden issues counts for terminal output."""
   121→    return ", ".join(f"{det}: +{count}" for det, count in hidden_by_detector.items())
   122→
   123→
   124→def warn_explicit_lang_with_no_files(
   125→    args, lang, path: Path, metrics: dict | None
   126→) -> None:
   127→    """Warn when user explicitly selected a language but scan found zero files."""
   128→    explicit_lang = getattr(args, "lang", None)
   129→    if not explicit_lang or not lang or not metrics:
   130→        return
   131→    if metrics.get("total_files", 0) > 0:
   132→        return
   133→
   134→    suggestion = " Omit `--lang` to auto-detect."
   135→    root = path if path.is_dir() else path.parent
   136→    try:
   137→        detected = lang_api.auto_detect_lang(root)
   138→    except ValueError as exc:
   139→        detected = None
   140→        logger.debug(
   141→            "Auto-detect failed while warning for explicit lang on %s: %s", root, exc
   142→        )
   143→    else:
   144→        if detected and detected != lang.name:
   145→            suggestion = (
   146→                f" Detected `{detected}` for this path — use `--lang {detected}` "
   147→                "or omit `--lang`."
   148→            )
   149→
   150→    print(
   151→        colorize(
   152→            f"  ⚠ No {lang.name} source files found under `{path}`.{suggestion}",
   153→            "yellow",
   154→        )
   155→    )
   156→
   157→
   158→def format_delta(value: float, prev: float | None) -> tuple[str, str]:
   159→    """Return (delta_str, color) for a score change."""
   160→    delta = value - prev if prev is not None else 0
   161→    delta_str = f" ({'+' if delta > 0 else ''}{delta:.1f})" if delta != 0 else ""
   162→    color = "green" if delta > 0 else ("red" if delta < 0 else "dim")
   163→    return delta_str, color
   164→

   138→def _parse_and_validate_import(
   139→    import_file: str,

   149→) -> tuple[ReviewImportPayload | None, list[str]]:
   150→    """Parse and validate a review import file (pure function).
   151→
   152→    Returns ``(data, errors)`` where *data* is the normalized payload on
   153→    success, or ``None`` when errors prevent import.

   158→        trusted_assessment_source=trusted_assessment_source,
   159→        trusted_assessment_label=trusted_assessment_label,

   163→    )

   176→        return None, ["issues file must contain a JSON array or object"]

   238→
   239→    if missing_feedback:
   240→        if override_enabled:
   241→            if not isinstance(override_attest, str) or not override_attest.strip():
   242→                return None, ["--manual-override requires --attest"]
   243→            return issues_data, []
   244→        return None, [
   245→            f"assessments below {ASSESSMENT_FEEDBACK_THRESHOLD:.1f} must include explicit feedback "
   246→            "(issue with same dimension and non-empty suggestion, or "
   247→            "dimension_notes evidence for that dimension). "
   248→            f"Missing: {', '.join(missing_feedback)}"
   249→        ]
   250→
   251→    schema_errors = _validate_holistic_issues_schema(
   252→        issues_data,
   253→        lang_name=options.lang_name,
   254→    )
   255→    if schema_errors and not options.allow_partial:
   256→        visible_errors = schema_errors[:10]
   257→        remaining = len(schema_errors) - len(visible_errors)
   258→        errors = [
   259→            "issues schema validation failed for holistic import. "
   260→            "Fix payload or rerun with --allow-partial to continue."
   261→        ]
   262→        errors.extend(visible_errors)
   263→        if remaining > 0:
   264→            errors.append(f"... {remaining} additional schema error(s) omitted")
   265→        return None, errors
   266→
   267→    return issues_data, []
   268→
   269→
   270→def load_import_issues_data(
   271→    import_file: str,
   272→    *,
   273→    config: ImportLoadConfig | None = None,
   274→    colorize_fn=None,
   275→    lang_name: str | None = None,
   276→    allow_partial: bool = False,
   277→    trusted_assessment_source: bool = False,
   278→    trusted_assessment_label: str | None = None,
   279→    attested_external: bool = False,
   280→    manual_override: bool = False,
   281→    manual_attest: str | None = None,
   282→) -> ReviewImportPayload:
   283→    """Load and normalize review import payload to object format.
   284→
   285→    Raises ``ImportPayloadLoadError`` when validation fails.
   286→    """
   287→    _ = colorize_fn
   288→    options = config or ImportLoadConfig(
   289→        lang_name=lang_name,
   290→        allow_partial=allow_partial,
   291→        trusted_assessment_source=trusted_assessment_source,
   292→        trusted_assessment_label=trusted_assessment_label,
   293→        attested_external=attested_external,
   294→        manual_override=manual_override,
   295→        manual_attest=manual_attest,
   296→    )
   297→    data, errors = _parse_and_validate_import(
   298→        import_file,
   299→        config=options,
   300→    )
   301→    if errors:
   302→        raise ImportPayloadLoadError(errors)
   303→    if data is None:
   304→        raise ValueError(
   305→            "import payload missing after parse completed without validation errors"
   306→        )
   307→    return data
   308→

1→"""Planning helpers for move command operations."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import os
     6→from dataclasses import dataclass
     7→from pathlib import Path
     8→
     9→Replacement = tuple[str, str]
    10→ReplacementList = list[Replacement]
    11→ReplacementMap = dict[str, ReplacementList]
    12→
    13→
    14→def dedup_replacements(replacements: ReplacementList) -> ReplacementList:
    15→    """Deduplicate replacement tuples while preserving order."""
    16→    seen: set[Replacement] = set()
    17→    result: ReplacementList = []
    18→    for pair in replacements:
    19→        if pair not in seen:
    20→            seen.add(pair)
    21→            result.append(pair)
    22→    return result
    23→
    24→
    25→def resolve_dest(source: str, dest_raw: str, resolve_path_fn) -> str:
    26→    """Resolve destination path, keeping source filename if dest is a directory."""
    27→    dest_path = Path(dest_raw)
    28→    if dest_path.is_dir() or dest_raw.endswith("/"):
    29→        dest_path = dest_path / Path(source).name
    30→    return resolve_path_fn(str(dest_path))
    31→
    32→
    33→def compute_replacements(
    34→    move_mod,
    35→    source_abs: str,
    36→    dest_abs: str,
    37→    graph: dict,
    38→) -> tuple[ReplacementMap, ReplacementList]:
    39→    """Compute importer/self replacements via language move module."""
    40→    return (
    41→        move_mod.find_replacements(source_abs, dest_abs, graph),
    42→        move_mod.find_self_replacements(source_abs, dest_abs, graph),
    43→    )
    44→
    45→
    46→def collect_source_files(source_path: Path, extensions: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    47→    """Collect files under a directory for the target language extensions."""
    48→    source_files: list[Path] = []
    49→    for ext in extensions:
    50→        source_files.extend(source_path.rglob(f"*{ext}"))
    51→    return sorted(
    52→        str(filepath.resolve()) for filepath in source_files if filepath.is_file()
    53→    )
    54→
    55→
    56→def _merge_unique_changes(
    57→    target: ReplacementMap,
    58→    filepath: str,
    59→    replacements: ReplacementList,
    60→) -> None:
    61→    """Merge replacement tuples into ``target`` without duplicating entries."""
    62→    if not replacements:
    63→        return
    64→    if filepath in target:
    65→        existing = set(target[filepath])
    66→        target[filepath].extend(repl for repl in replacements if repl not in existing)
    67→        return
    68→    target[filepath] = list(replacements)
    69→
    70→
    71→@dataclass
    72→class DirectoryMovePlan:
    73→    """Planned directory move operations and grouped replacement sets."""
    74→
    75→    file_moves: list[tuple[str, str]]
    76→    external_changes: ReplacementMap
    77→    intra_package_changes: ReplacementMap
    78→    self_changes: ReplacementMap
    79→
    80→
    81→def build_directory_move_plan(
    82→    source_abs: str,
    83→    source_path: Path,
    84→    dest_abs: str,
    85→    source_files: list[str],
    86→    move_mod,
    87→    graph: dict,
    88→) -> DirectoryMovePlan:
    89→    """Build file move mapping and import replacement groups for directory moves."""
    90→    file_moves: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    91→    for src_file in source_files:
    92→        rel_in_dir = Path(src_file).relative_to(source_path)
    93→        dst_file = str(Path(dest_abs) / rel_in_dir)
    94→        file_moves.append((src_file, dst_file))
    95→
    96→    moving_files = {src for src, _ in file_moves}
    97→
    98→    all_importer_changes: ReplacementMap = {}
    99→    intra_pkg_changes: ReplacementMap = {}
   100→    all_self_changes: ReplacementMap = {}
   101→
   102→    intra_filter = getattr(
   103→        move_mod,
   104→        "filter_intra_package_importer_changes",
   105→        lambda _source, replacements, _moving: replacements,
   106→    )
   107→    self_filter = getattr(
   108→        move_mod,
   109→        "filter_directory_self_changes",
   110→        lambda _source, replacements, _moving: replacements,
   111→    )
   112→
   113→    for src_file, dst_file in file_moves:
   114→        importer_changes, self_changes = compute_replacements(
   115→            move_mod, src_file, dst_file, graph
   116→        )
   117→
   118→        for filepath, replacements in importer_changes.items():
   119→            if filepath in moving_files:
   120→                filtered = intra_filter(src_file, replacements, moving_files)
   121→                _merge_unique_changes(intra_pkg_changes, filepath, filtered)
   122→            else:
   123→                _merge_unique_changes(all_importer_changes, filepath, replacements)
   124→
   125→        if self_changes:
   126→            filtered_self = self_filter(src_file, self_changes, moving_files)
   127→            if filtered_self:
   128→                all_self_changes[src_file] = filtered_self
   129→
   130→    source_prefix = source_abs + os.sep
   131→    external_changes = {
   132→        filepath: replacements
   133→        for filepath, replacements in all_importer_changes.items()
   134→        if not filepath.startswith(source_prefix)
   135→    }
   136→
   137→    return DirectoryMovePlan(
   138→        file_moves=file_moves,
   139→        external_changes=external_changes,
   140→        intra_package_changes=intra_pkg_changes,
   141→        self_changes=all_self_changes,
   142→    )
   143→
   144→
   145→def build_internal_directory_changes(plan: DirectoryMovePlan) -> ReplacementMap:
   146→    """Return replacement map for moved files themselves after directory rename."""
   147→    all_internal_changes: ReplacementMap = {}
   148→    for src_file, changes in plan.self_changes.items():
   149→        all_internal_changes.setdefault(src_file, []).extend(changes)
   150→    for src_file, changes in plan.intra_package_changes.items():
   151→        all_internal_changes.setdefault(src_file, []).extend(changes)
   152→    return all_internal_changes
   153→
   154→
   155→def summarize_directory_plan(plan: DirectoryMovePlan) -> tuple[int, int]:
   156→    """Return (total_changed_files, total_replacement_count) for directory plan."""
   157→    total_changes = (
   158→        len(plan.external_changes)
   159→        + len(plan.intra_package_changes)
   160→        + len(plan.self_changes)
   161→    )
   162→    total_replacements = (
   163→        sum(len(v) for v in plan.external_changes.values())
   164→        + sum(len(v) for v in plan.intra_package_changes.values())
   165→        + sum(len(v) for v in plan.self_changes.values())
   166→    )
   167→    return total_changes, total_replacements
   168→
   169→
   170→__all__ = [
   171→    "DirectoryMovePlan",
   172→    "build_directory_move_plan",
   173→    "build_internal_directory_changes",
   174→    "collect_source_files",
   175→    "compute_replacements",
   176→    "dedup_replacements",
   177→    "resolve_dest",
   178→    "summarize_directory_plan",
   179→]
   180→

    23→def has_triage_in_queue(plan: dict) -> bool:
    24→    """Check if any triage stage ID is in the queue."""
    25→    order = set(plan.get("queue_order", []))
    26→    return bool(order & TRIAGE_IDS)

    28→def inject_triage_stages(plan: dict) -> None:
    29→    """Inject all 4 triage stage IDs into the queue (fresh start)."""
    30→    order: list[str] = plan.setdefault("queue_order", [])
    31→    existing = set(order)
    32→    for sid in TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS:
    33→        if sid not in existing:
    34→            order.insert(0 if sid == TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS[0] else len(order), sid)
    35→    # Re-insert in correct order at front
    36→    for sid in reversed(TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS):
    37→        if sid in order:
    38→            order.remove(sid)
    39→    insert_at = 0
    40→    for sid in TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS:
    41→        order.insert(insert_at, sid)
    42→        insert_at += 1

    49→def cascade_clear_later_confirmations(stages: dict, from_stage: str) -> list[str]:
    50→    """Clear confirmed_at/confirmed_text on stages AFTER *from_stage*. Returns cleared names."""
    51→    try:
    52→        idx = _STAGE_ORDER.index(from_stage)
    53→    except ValueError:
    54→        return []
    55→    cleared: list[str] = []
    56→    for later in _STAGE_ORDER[idx + 1:]:
    57→        if later in stages and stages[later].get("confirmed_at"):
    58→            stages[later].pop("confirmed_at", None)
    59→            stages[later].pop("confirmed_text", None)
    60→            cleared.append(later)
    61→    return cleared
    62→
    63→def print_cascade_clear_feedback(cleared: list[str], stages: dict) -> None:
    64→    """Print yellow cascade-clear message with next-step guidance."""
    65→    if not cleared:
    66→        return
    67→    print(colorize(f"  Cleared confirmations on: {', '.join(cleared)}", "yellow"))
    68→    next_unconfirmed = next(
    69→        (s for s in _STAGE_ORDER if s in stages and not stages[s].get("confirmed_at")),
    70→        None,
    71→    )
    72→    if next_unconfirmed:
    73→        print(colorize(
    74→            f"  Re-confirm with: desloppify plan triage --confirm {next_unconfirmed}",
    75→            "dim",
    76→        ))

    78→def observe_dimension_breakdown(si) -> tuple[dict[str, int], list[str]]:
    79→    """Count issues per dimension from a TriageInput. Returns (by_dim, sorted_dim_names)."""
    80→    by_dim: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)
    81→    for _fid, f in si.open_issues.items():
    82→        detail = f.get("detail", {}) if isinstance(f.get("detail"), dict) else {}
    83→        dim = detail.get("dimension", "unknown")
    84→        by_dim[dim] += 1
    85→    dim_names = sorted(by_dim, key=lambda d: (-by_dim[d], d))
    86→    return dict(by_dim), dim_names
    87→
    88→def group_issues_into_observe_batches(
    89→    si,
    90→    max_batches: int = 5,
    91→) -> list[tuple[list[str], dict[str, dict]]]:
    92→    """Group issues by dimension into batches for parallel observe.
    93→
    94→    Returns list of (dimension_names, issues_subset) tuples.
    95→    Single batch if only one dimension exists.
    96→    """
    97→    by_dim, dim_names = observe_dimension_breakdown(si)
    98→
    99→    if len(dim_names) <= 1:
   100→        return [(dim_names, dict(si.open_issues))]
   101→
   102→    # Distribute dimensions into balanced batches by issue count
   103→    num_batches = min(max_batches, len(dim_names))
   104→    batch_dims: list[list[str]] = [[] for _ in range(num_batches)]
   105→    batch_counts: list[int] = [0] * num_batches
   106→
   107→    # Greedy: assign each dimension (largest first) to the lightest batch
   108→    for dim in dim_names:
   109→        lightest = min(range(num_batches), key=lambda i: batch_counts[i])
   110→        batch_dims[lightest].append(dim)
   111→        batch_counts[lightest] += by_dim[dim]
   112→
   113→    # Build issue subsets per batch
   114→    # Pre-index issues by dimension
   115→    dim_to_issues: dict[str, dict[str, dict]] = defaultdict(dict)
   116→    for fid, f in si.open_issues.items():
   117→        detail = f.get("detail", {}) if isinstance(f.get("detail"), dict) else {}
   118→        dim = detail.get("dimension", "unknown")
   119→        dim_to_issues[dim][fid] = f
   120→
   121→    result: list[tuple[list[str], dict[str, dict]]] = []
   122→    for dims in batch_dims:
   123→        if not dims:
   124→            continue
   125→        subset: dict[str, dict] = {}
   126→        for dim in dims:
   127→            subset.update(dim_to_issues.get(dim, {}))
   128→        if subset:
   129→            result.append((dims, subset))
   130→
   131→    return result
