   104→def resolve_scan_profile(profile: str | None, lang) -> str:
   105→    """Resolve effective scan profile from CLI and language defaults."""
   106→    if profile in {"objective", "full", "ci"}:
   107→        return profile
   108→    default_profile = getattr(lang, "default_scan_profile", "full") if lang else "full"
   109→    if default_profile in {"objective", "full", "ci"}:
   110→        return default_profile
   111→    return "full"
   112→
   113→
   114→def effective_include_slow(include_slow: bool, profile: str) -> bool:
   115→    """Determine whether slow phases should run for this profile."""
   116→    return include_slow and profile != "ci"

   119→def _format_hidden_by_detector(hidden_by_detector: dict[str, int]) -> str:
   120→    """Format hidden issues counts for terminal output."""
   121→    return ", ".join(f"{det}: +{count}" for det, count in hidden_by_detector.items())

   124→def warn_explicit_lang_with_no_files(
   125→    args, lang, path: Path, metrics: dict | None
   126→) -> None:
   127→    """Warn when user explicitly selected a language but scan found zero files."""
   128→    explicit_lang = getattr(args, "lang", None)
   129→    if not explicit_lang or not lang or not metrics:
   130→        return
   131→    if metrics.get("total_files", 0) > 0:
   132→        return
   133→
   134→    suggestion = " Omit `--lang` to auto-detect."
   135→    root = path if path.is_dir() else path.parent
   136→    try:
   137→        detected = lang_api.auto_detect_lang(root)
   138→    except ValueError as exc:
   139→        detected = None
   140→        logger.debug(
   141→            "Auto-detect failed while warning for explicit lang on %s: %s", root, exc
   142→        )
   143→    else:
   144→        if detected and detected != lang.name:
   145→            suggestion = (
   146→                f" Detected `{detected}` for this path — use `--lang {detected}` "
   147→                "or omit `--lang`."
   148→            )
   149→
   150→    print(
   151→        colorize(
   152→            f"  ⚠ No {lang.name} source files found under `{path}`.{suggestion}",
   153→            "yellow",
   154→        )
   155→    )
   156→
   157→
   158→def format_delta(value: float, prev: float | None) -> tuple[str, str]:
   159→    """Return (delta_str, color) for a score change."""
   160→    delta = value - prev if prev is not None else 0
   161→    delta_str = f" ({'+' if delta > 0 else ''}{delta:.1f})" if delta != 0 else ""
   162→    color = "green" if delta > 0 else ("red" if delta < 0 else "dim")
   163→    return delta_str, color
   164→

   187→    extract_fn = make_ts_extractor(ts_spec, file_finder)
   188→    if ts_spec.import_query and ts_spec.resolve_import:
   189→        dep_graph_fn = make_ts_dep_builder(ts_spec, file_finder)
   190→    return file_finder, extract_fn, dep_graph_fn, has_treesitter, ts_spec
   191→
   192→
   193→def _build_generic_phases(
   194→    *,
   195→    tool_specs: list[dict[str, Any]],
   196→    ts_spec: Any,
   197→    has_treesitter: bool,
   198→    extract_fn,
   199→    dep_graph_fn,
   200→) -> list[DetectorPhase]:
   201→    from desloppify.languages._framework.base.phase_builders import (
   202→        detector_phase_security,
   203→        detector_phase_test_coverage,
   204→        shared_subjective_duplicates_tail,
   205→    )
   206→
   207→    phases = [
   208→        make_tool_phase(tool["label"], tool["cmd"], tool["fmt"], tool["id"], tool["tier"])
   209→        for tool in tool_specs
   210→    ]
   211→    phases.append(_make_structural_phase(ts_spec if has_treesitter else None))
   212→
   213→    if has_treesitter and ts_spec is not None:
   214→        from desloppify.languages._framework.treesitter.phases import (
   215→            make_ast_smells_phase,
   216→            make_cohesion_phase,
   217→            make_unused_imports_phase,
   218→        )
   219→
   220→        phases.append(make_ast_smells_phase(ts_spec))
   221→        phases.append(make_cohesion_phase(ts_spec))
   222→        if ts_spec.import_query:
   223→            phases.append(make_unused_imports_phase(ts_spec))
   224→
   225→    if extract_fn is not noop_extract_functions:
   226→        from desloppify.languages._framework.base.phase_builders import detector_phase_signature
   227→
   228→        phases.append(detector_phase_signature())
   229→
   230→    phases.append(detector_phase_security())
   231→    if dep_graph_fn is not empty_dep_graph:
   232→        phases.append(_make_coupling_phase(dep_graph_fn))
   233→        phases.append(detector_phase_test_coverage())
   234→
   235→    phases.extend(shared_subjective_duplicates_tail())
   236→    return phases
   237→
   238→
   239→def generic_lang(
   240→    name: str,
   241→    extensions: list[str],
   242→    tools: list[dict[str, Any]],
   243→    *,
   244→    options: GenericLangOptions | None = None,
   245→    exclude: list[str] | None = None,
   246→    depth: str = "shallow",
   247→    detect_markers: list[str] | None = None,
   248→    default_src: str = ".",
   249→    treesitter_spec=None,
   250→    zone_rules: list[ZoneRule] | None = None,
   251→    test_coverage_module: Any | None = None,
   252→) -> LangConfig:
   253→    """Build and register a generic language plugin from tool specs.
   254→
   255→    Each entry in `tools` is::
   256→
   257→        {"label": str, "cmd": str, "fmt": str, "id": str, "tier": int,
   258→         "fix_cmd": str | None}
   259→
   260→    When ``treesitter_spec`` is provided and ``tree-sitter-language-pack`` is
   261→    installed, the plugin gains function extraction (enables duplicate
   262→    detection), and optionally import analysis (enables coupling/orphan/cycle
   263→    detection and test-coverage analysis) for no additional configuration.
   264→
   265→    Returns the built LangConfig (also registered in the language registry).
   266→    """
   267→    opts = options or GenericLangOptions(
   268→        exclude=exclude,
   269→        depth=depth,
   270→        detect_markers=detect_markers,
   271→        default_src=default_src,
   272→        treesitter_spec=treesitter_spec,
   273→        zone_rules=zone_rules,
   274→        test_coverage_module=test_coverage_module,
   275→    )
   276→
   277→    from desloppify.languages import register_generic_lang
   278→
   279→    tool_specs = normalize_tool_specs(tools, supported_formats=set(_PARSERS))
   280→    fixers = _register_generic_tool_specs(tool_specs)
   281→    file_finder, extract_fn, dep_graph_fn, has_treesitter, ts_spec = _resolve_generic_extractors(
   282→        path_extensions=extensions,
   283→        opts=opts,
   284→    )
   285→    phases = _build_generic_phases(
   286→        tool_specs=tool_specs,
   287→        ts_spec=ts_spec,
   288→        has_treesitter=has_treesitter,
   289→        extract_fn=extract_fn,
   290→        dep_graph_fn=dep_graph_fn,
   291→    )
   292→
   293→    cfg = LangConfig(
   294→        name=name,
   295→        extensions=extensions,
   296→        exclusions=opts.exclude or [],
   297→        default_src=opts.default_src,
   298→        build_dep_graph=dep_graph_fn,
   299→        entry_patterns=[],
   300→        barrel_names=set(),
   301→        phases=phases,
   302→        fixers=fixers,
   303→        get_area=None,
   304→        detect_commands={
   305→            t["id"]: make_detect_fn(t["cmd"], _PARSERS[t["fmt"]])
   306→            for t in tool_specs
   307→        },
   308→        extract_functions=extract_fn,
   309→        boundaries=[],
   310→        typecheck_cmd="",
   311→        file_finder=file_finder,
   312→        large_threshold=500,
   313→        complexity_threshold=15,
   314→        default_scan_profile="objective",
   315→        detect_markers=opts.detect_markers or [],
   316→        external_test_dirs=["tests", "test"],
   317→        test_file_extensions=extensions,
   318→        zone_rules=opts.zone_rules if opts.zone_rules is not None else generic_zone_rules(extensions),
   319→    )
   320→
   321→    # Set integration depth — upgrade when tree-sitter provides capabilities.
   322→    if has_treesitter and opts.depth in ("shallow", "minimal"):
   323→        cfg.integration_depth = "standard"
   324→    else:
   325→        cfg.integration_depth = opts.depth
   326→
   327→    # Register language-specific test coverage hooks if provided.
   328→    if opts.test_coverage_module is not None:
   329→        from desloppify.engine.hook_registry import register_lang_hooks
   330→
   331→        register_lang_hooks(name, test_coverage=opts.test_coverage_module)
   332→
   333→    register_generic_lang(name, cfg)
   334→    return cfg
   335→
   336→
   337→# ── Structural + coupling phase helpers ──────────────────────
   338→
   339→
   340→def _make_structural_phase(treesitter_spec=None) -> DetectorPhase:
   341→    """Create a structural analysis phase for generic plugins."""
   342→    from desloppify.base.output.terminal import log
   343→    from desloppify.engine.detectors.base import ComplexitySignal
   344→
   345→    signals = [
   346→        ComplexitySignal(
   347→            "TODOs",
   348→            r"(?://|#|--|/\*)\s*(?:TODO|FIXME|HACK|XXX)",
   349→            weight=2,
   350→            threshold=0,
   351→        ),
   352→    ]
   353→
   354→    if treesitter_spec is not None:
   355→        from desloppify.languages._framework.treesitter import is_available
   356→
   357→        if is_available():
   358→            from desloppify.languages._framework.treesitter._complexity import (
   359→                make_callback_depth_compute,
   360→                make_cyclomatic_complexity_compute,
   361→                make_long_functions_compute,
   362→                make_max_params_compute,
   363→                make_nesting_depth_compute,
   364→            )
   365→
   366→            signals.append(ComplexitySignal(
   367→                "nesting_depth", None, weight=3, threshold=4,
   368→                compute=make_nesting_depth_compute(treesitter_spec),
   369→            ))
   370→            signals.append(ComplexitySignal(
   371→                "long_functions", None, weight=3, threshold=80,
   372→                compute=make_long_functions_compute(treesitter_spec),
   373→            ))
   374→            signals.append(ComplexitySignal(
   375→                "cyclomatic_complexity", None, weight=2, threshold=15,
   376→                compute=make_cyclomatic_complexity_compute(treesitter_spec),
   377→            ))
   378→            signals.append(ComplexitySignal(
   379→                "many_params", None, weight=2, threshold=7,
   380→                compute=make_max_params_compute(treesitter_spec),
   381→            ))
   382→            signals.append(ComplexitySignal(
   383→                "callback_depth", None, weight=2, threshold=3,
   384→                compute=make_callback_depth_compute(treesitter_spec),
   385→            ))
   386→
   387→    # God class rules (active when tree-sitter provides class extraction).
   388→    god_rules = None
   389→    has_class_query = treesitter_spec is not None and treesitter_spec.class_query
   390→    if has_class_query:
   391→        from desloppify.engine.detectors.base import GodRule
   392→
   393→        god_rules = [
   394→            GodRule("methods", "methods", lambda c: len(c.methods), 15),
   395→            GodRule("loc", "LOC", lambda c: c.loc, 500),
   396→            GodRule("attributes", "attributes", lambda c: len(c.attributes), 10),
   397→        ]
   398→
   399→    def run(path, lang):
   400→        from desloppify.languages._framework.base.shared_phases import (
   401→            run_structural_phase,
   402→        )
   403→
   404→        god_extractor_fn = None
   405→        if god_rules and has_class_query:
   406→            god_extractor_fn = _make_god_extractor(treesitter_spec, lang.file_finder)
   407→
   408→        return run_structural_phase(
   409→            path, lang,
   410→            complexity_signals=signals,
   411→            log_fn=log,
   412→            min_loc=40,
   413→            god_rules=god_rules,
   414→            god_extractor_fn=god_extractor_fn,
   415→        )
   416→
   417→    return DetectorPhase("Structural analysis", run)
   418→
   419→
   420→def _make_god_extractor(treesitter_spec, file_finder):
   421→    """Create a god-class extractor function bound to the given spec."""
   422→    def extractor(p):
   423→        return _extract_ts_classes(p, treesitter_spec, file_finder)
   424→    return extractor
   425→
   426→
   427→def _extract_ts_classes(path, treesitter_spec, file_finder):
   428→    """Extract classes with methods populated via tree-sitter.
   429→
   430→    Returns [] on any error (graceful degradation).
   431→    """
   432→    try:
   433→        from collections import defaultdict
   434→
   435→        from desloppify.languages._framework.treesitter._extractors import (
   436→            ts_extract_classes,
   437→            ts_extract_functions,
   438→        )
   439→
   440→        file_list = file_finder(path)
   441→        classes = ts_extract_classes(path, treesitter_spec, file_list)
   442→        if not classes:
   443→            return classes
   444→
   445→        functions = ts_extract_functions(path, treesitter_spec, file_list)
   446→        by_file = defaultdict(list)
   447→        for fn in functions:
   448→            by_file[fn.file].append(fn)
   449→        for cls in classes:
   450→            cls_end = cls.line + cls.loc
   451→            for fn in by_file.get(cls.file, []):
   452→                if cls.line <= fn.line <= cls_end:
   453→                    cls.methods.append(fn)
   454→
   455→        return classes
   456→    except _TS_INIT_ERRORS as exc:
   457→        logger.debug("tree-sitter class extraction failed: %s", exc)
   458→        return []
   459→
   460→
   461→def _make_coupling_phase(dep_graph_fn) -> DetectorPhase:
   462→    """Create a coupling phase for generic plugins with a dep graph."""
   463→    from desloppify.base.output.terminal import log
   464→
   465→    def run(path, lang):
   466→        from desloppify.languages._framework.base.shared_phases import (
   467→            run_coupling_phase,
   468→        )
   469→
   470→        return run_coupling_phase(
   471→            path, lang, build_dep_graph_fn=dep_graph_fn, log_fn=log,
   472→        )
   473→
   474→    return DetectorPhase("Coupling + cycles + orphaned", run)
   475→
   476→

   478→    "GenericLangOptions",
   479→    "SHARED_PHASE_LABELS",

    23→def append_full_sweep_batch(
    24→    *,
    25→    batches: list[dict[str, Any]],
    26→    dims: list[str],
    27→    all_files: list[str],
    28→    lang: Any,
    29→    max_files: int | None = None,
    30→) -> None:
    31→    """Append an optional cross-cutting full-codebase batch."""
    32→    if not dims:
    33→        return
    34→    all_rel_files: list[str] = []
    35→    for filepath in all_files:
    36→        if lang.zone_map is not None:
    37→            zone = lang.zone_map.get(filepath)
    38→            if zone.value in ("test", "generated", "vendor"):
    39→                continue
    40→        all_rel_files.append(rel(filepath))
    41→        if isinstance(max_files, int) and max_files > 0 and len(all_rel_files) >= max_files:
    42→            break
    43→    if not all_rel_files:
    44→        return
    45→    batches.append(
    46→        {
    47→            "name": "Full Codebase Sweep",
    48→            "dimensions": list(dims),
    49→            "files_to_read": all_rel_files,
    50→            "why": "thorough default: evaluate cross-cutting quality across all production files",
    51→        }
    52→    )

   286→def _validate_run_dir(run_dir: Path) -> tuple[dict, Path, str]:
   287→    """Validate run directory, load summary, and return (summary, blind_packet_path, immutable_packet_path).
   288→
   289→    Raises CommandError on any validation failure.
   290→    """
   291→    if not run_dir.is_dir():
   292→        raise CommandError(f"run directory not found: {run_dir}", exit_code=1)
   293→
   294→    summary_path = run_dir / "run_summary.json"
   295→    if not summary_path.exists():
   296→        raise CommandError(f"no run_summary.json in {run_dir}", exit_code=1)
   297→    try:
   298→        summary = json.loads(summary_path.read_text())
   299→    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
   300→        raise CommandError(f"Error reading run summary: {exc}", exit_code=1) from exc
   301→
   302→    successful = summary.get("successful_batches", [])
   303→    blind_packet_path = Path(str(summary.get("blind_packet", "")))
   304→    immutable_packet_path = str(summary.get("immutable_packet", ""))
   305→
   306→    if not successful:
   307→        raise CommandError("no successful batches in run summary.", exit_code=1)
   308→    if not blind_packet_path.exists():
   309→        raise PacketValidationError(f"blind packet not found: {blind_packet_path}", exit_code=1)
   310→
   311→    try:
   312→        packet = json.loads(Path(immutable_packet_path).read_text())
   313→    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
   314→        raise PacketValidationError(f"Error reading immutable packet: {exc}", exit_code=1) from exc
   315→
   316→    summary["_packet"] = packet
   317→    return summary, blind_packet_path, immutable_packet_path
   318→
   319→
   320→def do_import_run(
   321→    run_dir_path: str,
   322→    state: dict,
   323→    lang,
   324→    state_file: str,
   325→    *,
   326→    config: dict | None = None,
   327→    allow_partial: bool = False,
   328→    scan_after_import: bool = False,
   329→    scan_path: str = ".",
   330→) -> None:
   331→    """Re-import results from a completed run directory.
   332→
   333→    Replays the merge+provenance+import step that normally runs at the end of
   334→    ``--run-batches``.  Useful when the original pipeline was interrupted (e.g.
   335→    broken pipe from background execution) but all batch results completed.
   336→    """
   337→    run_dir = Path(run_dir_path)
   338→    summary, blind_packet_path, _immutable_path = _validate_run_dir(run_dir)
   339→
   340→    runner = str(summary.get("runner", "codex"))
   341→    stamp = str(summary.get("run_stamp", ""))
   342→    successful = summary.get("successful_batches", [])
   343→    packet = summary.pop("_packet", {})
   344→    allowed_dims = {str(d) for d in packet.get("dimensions", []) if isinstance(d, str)}
   345→
   346→    # -- locate and parse raw batch results --
   347→    results_dir = run_dir / "results"
   348→    selected_indexes = [idx - 1 for idx in successful]  # convert 1-based to 0-based
   349→    output_files = {
   350→        idx: results_dir / f"batch-{idx + 1}.raw.txt"
   351→        for idx in selected_indexes
   352→    }
   353→
   354→    missing = [idx + 1 for idx in selected_indexes if not output_files[idx].exists()]
   355→    if missing:
   356→        raise CommandError(f"missing result files for batches: {missing}", exit_code=1)
   357→
   358→    batch_results, failures = collect_batch_results(
   359→        selected_indexes=selected_indexes,
   360→        failures=[],
   361→        output_files=output_files,
   362→        allowed_dims=allowed_dims,
   363→        extract_payload_fn=lambda raw: batch_core_mod.extract_json_payload(raw, log_fn=log),
   364→        normalize_result_fn=lambda payload, dims: batch_core_mod.normalize_batch_result(
   365→            payload,
   366→            dims,
   367→            max_batch_issues=max_batch_issues_for_dimension_count(len(dims)),
   368→            abstraction_sub_axes=ABSTRACTION_SUB_AXES,
   369→        ),
   370→    )
   371→
   372→    if not batch_results:
   373→        raise CommandError("no valid batch results could be parsed.", exit_code=1)
   374→
   375→    print(colorize(f"  Parsed {len(batch_results)} batch results from {run_dir}", "bold"))
   376→    if failures:
   377→        print(colorize(f"  Warning: {len(failures)} batches failed to parse: {[f + 1 for f in failures]}", "yellow"))
   378→
   379→    # -- merge --
   380→    merged = _merge_batch_results(batch_results)
   381→
   382→    # -- build provenance --
   383→    successful_indexes = [idx for idx in selected_indexes if idx not in set(failures)]
   384→    merged["provenance"] = build_batch_import_provenance(
   385→        runner=runner,
   386→        blind_packet_path=blind_packet_path,
   387→        run_stamp=stamp,
   388→        batch_indexes=successful_indexes,
   389→    )
   390→
   391→    # -- write merged output --
   392→    merged_path = run_dir / "holistic_issues_merged.json"
   393→    safe_write_text(merged_path, json.dumps(merged, indent=2) + "\n")
   394→    print(colorize(f"  Merged output: {merged_path}", "bold"))
   395→
   396→    # -- import with trusted source --
   397→    _do_import(
   398→        str(merged_path),
   399→        state,
   400→        lang,
   401→        state_file,
   402→        config=config,
   403→        allow_partial=allow_partial,
   404→        trusted_assessment_source=True,
   405→        trusted_assessment_label=f"trusted import-run replay from {run_dir.name}",
   406→    )
   407→
   408→    # -- optional follow-up scan --
   409→    if scan_after_import:
   410→        lang_name = getattr(lang, "name", None) or str(getattr(lang, "lang", ""))
   411→        if lang_name:
   412→            run_followup_scan(
   413→                lang_name=lang_name,
   414→                scan_path=scan_path,
   415→                deps=FollowupScanDeps(
   416→                    project_root=_runtime_project_root(),
   417→                    timeout_seconds=FOLLOWUP_SCAN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
   418→                    python_executable=sys.executable,
   419→                    subprocess_run=subprocess.run,
   420→                    timeout_error=subprocess.TimeoutExpired,
   421→                    colorize_fn=colorize,
   422→                ),
   423→            )
   424→

    25→class Zone(str, Enum):

    43→@dataclass
    44→class ZoneRule:
    45→    """A classification rule: zone + list of path patterns.
    46→
    47→    Patterns are matched against relative file paths. First matching rule wins.
    48→    Pattern types (auto-detected from shape):
    49→      - "/dir/"   → substring match on full path (directory marker)
    50→      - ".ext"    → basename ends-with (suffix/extension, e.g. ".d.ts", ".test.")
    51→      - "prefix_" → basename starts-with (trailing underscore)
    52→      - "name.py" → basename exact match (has extension, no /)
    53→      - fallback  → substring on full path
    54→    """
    55→
    56→    zone: Zone
    57→    patterns: list[str]
    58→
    59→
    60→def _match_pattern(rel_path: str, pattern: str) -> bool:
    61→    """Match a zone pattern against a relative file path.
    62→
    63→    See ZoneRule docstring for pattern type conventions.
    64→    """
    65→    basename = os.path.basename(rel_path)
    66→
    67→    # Directory pattern: "/dir/" → substring on padded path
    68→    if pattern.startswith("/") and pattern.endswith("/"):
    69→        return pattern in ("/" + rel_path + "/")
    70→
    71→    # Suffix/extension pattern: starts with "." → contains on basename
    72→    if pattern.startswith("."):
    73→        return pattern in basename
    74→
    75→    # Prefix pattern: ends with "_" → basename starts-with
    76→    if pattern.endswith("_"):
    77→        return basename.startswith(pattern)
    78→
    79→    # Suffix pattern: starts with "_" → basename ends-with (_test.py, _pb2.py)
    80→    if pattern.startswith("_"):
    81→        return basename.endswith(pattern)
    82→
    83→    # Exact basename: has a proper file extension (1-5 chars after last dot),
    84→    # no "/" → exact basename match (config.py, setup.py, conftest.py)
    85→    if "/" not in pattern and "." in pattern:
    86→        ext = pattern.rsplit(".", 1)[-1]
    87→        if ext and len(ext) <= 5 and ext.isalnum():
    88→            return basename == pattern
    89→
    90→    # Fallback: substring on full path (vite.config, tsconfig, eslint, etc.)
    91→    return pattern in rel_path

   104→def classify_file(
   105→    rel_path: str, rules: list[ZoneRule], overrides: dict[str, str] | None = None
   106→) -> Zone:
   107→    """Classify a file by its relative path. Overrides take priority."""
   108→    if overrides:
   109→        override = overrides.get(rel_path)
   110→        if override:
   111→            try:
   112→                return Zone(override)
   113→            except ValueError as exc:
   114→                log_best_effort_failure(
   115→                    logger, f"parse zone override for {rel_path}", exc

   117→    for rule in rules:
   118→        for pattern in rule.patterns:
   119→            if _match_pattern(rel_path, pattern):
   120→                return rule.zone
   121→    return Zone.PRODUCTION

   124→class FileZoneMap:
   125→    """Cached zone classification for a set of files.
   126→
   127→    Built once per scan from file list + zone rules.

   129→
   130→    def __init__(
   131→        self,
   132→        files: list[str],

   134→        rel_fn=None,
   135→        overrides: dict[str, str] | None = None,
   136→    ):
   137→        """Build a zone map from files, ordered rules, and optional overrides."""
   138→        self._map: dict[str, Zone] = {}
   139→        self._overrides = overrides
   140→        for f in files:
   141→            rp = rel_fn(f) if rel_fn else f
   142→            self._map[f] = classify_file(rp, rules, overrides)
   143→
   144→    def get(self, path: str) -> Zone:
   145→        """Get zone for a file path. Returns PRODUCTION if not classified."""
   146→        return self._map.get(path, Zone.PRODUCTION)

   148→    def exclude(self, files: list[str], *zones: Zone) -> list[str]:
   149→        """Return files NOT in the given zones."""
   150→        zone_set = set(zones)
   151→        return [f for f in files if self._map.get(f, Zone.PRODUCTION) not in zone_set]
   152→
   153→    def include_only(self, files: list[str], *zones: Zone) -> list[str]:
   154→        """Return files that ARE in the given zones."""

   158→    def counts(self) -> dict[str, int]:
   159→        """Return file count per zone."""
   160→        counts: dict[str, int] = {}
   161→        for zone in self._map.values():

   163→        return counts

   264→        return val[0] if isinstance(val, list) else val
   265→
   266→    return [
   267→        e for e in entries if not should_skip_issue(zone_map, _get_path(e), detector)
   268→    ]
   269→

1→"""Cache and issue-summary helpers for review file selection."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import logging
     6→from datetime import UTC, datetime
     7→
     8→from desloppify.base.discovery.file_paths import rel
     9→
    10→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    11→
    12→
    13→def get_file_issues(state: dict, filepath: str) -> list[dict]:
    14→    """Get existing open issues for a file (summaries for context)."""
    15→    rpath = rel(filepath)
    16→    issues = state.get("issues", {})
    17→    return [
    18→        {"detector": issue["detector"], "summary": issue["summary"], "id": issue["id"]}
    19→        for issue in issues.values()
    20→        if issue.get("file") == rpath and issue["status"] == "open"
    21→    ]
    22→
    23→
    24→def count_fresh(state: dict, max_age_days: int) -> int:
    25→    """Count files in review cache that are still fresh."""
    26→    cache = state.get("review_cache", {}).get("files", {})
    27→    now = datetime.now(UTC)
    28→    count = 0
    29→    for entry in cache.values():
    30→        reviewed_at = entry.get("reviewed_at", "")
    31→        if reviewed_at:
    32→            try:
    33→                reviewed = datetime.fromisoformat(reviewed_at)
    34→                if (now - reviewed).days <= max_age_days:
    35→                    count += 1
    36→            except (ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
    37→                logger.debug(
    38→                    "Invalid review cache date %r while counting fresh files: %s",
    39→                    reviewed_at,
    40→                    exc,
    41→                )
    42→    return count
    43→
    44→
    45→def count_stale(state: dict, max_age_days: int) -> int:
    46→    """Count files in review cache that are stale."""
    47→    cache = state.get("review_cache", {}).get("files", {})
    48→    total = len(cache)
    49→    return total - count_fresh(state, max_age_days)
    50→
    51→
    52→__all__ = ["count_fresh", "count_stale", "get_file_issues"]
    53→
    54→

    20→DEFAULT_EXCLUSIONS = frozenset(

    45→
    46→def set_exclusions(patterns: list[str]) -> None:
    47→    """Set global exclusion patterns (called once from CLI at startup)."""
    48→    runtime = current_runtime_context()
    49→    runtime.exclusions = tuple(patterns)
    50→    runtime.source_file_cache.clear()
    51→
    52→
    53→def get_exclusions() -> tuple[str, ...]:
    54→    """Return current extra exclusion patterns."""
    55→    return current_runtime_context().exclusions
    56→
    57→
    58→def enable_file_cache() -> None:
    59→    """Enable scan-scoped file content cache."""
    60→    runtime = current_runtime_context()
    61→    runtime.file_text_cache.enable()
    62→    runtime.cache_enabled = True
    63→
    64→
    65→def disable_file_cache() -> None:
    66→    """Disable file content cache and free memory."""
    67→    runtime = current_runtime_context()
    68→    runtime.file_text_cache.disable()
    69→    runtime.cache_enabled = False
    70→
    71→
    72→@contextmanager
    73→def file_cache_scope():
    74→    """Temporarily enable file cache within a context, with nested safety."""
    75→    runtime = current_runtime_context()
    76→    was_enabled = runtime.cache_enabled
    77→    if not was_enabled:
    78→        enable_file_cache()
    79→    try:
    80→        yield
    81→    finally:
    82→        if not was_enabled:
    83→            disable_file_cache()
    84→
    85→
    86→def is_file_cache_enabled() -> bool:
    87→    """Return whether scan-scoped file cache is currently enabled."""
    88→    return current_runtime_context().cache_enabled

    92→    """Read a file as text, with optional caching."""

    94→
    95→
    96→def clear_source_file_cache_for_tests() -> None:
    97→    current_runtime_context().source_file_cache.clear()
    98→
    99→
   100→def collect_exclude_dirs(scan_root: Path) -> list[str]:
   101→    """All exclusion directories as absolute paths, for passing to external tools.
   102→
   103→    Combines DEFAULT_EXCLUSIONS (non-glob entries) + get_exclusions() (runtime/config),
   104→    resolves each against *scan_root*. Filters out glob patterns (``*`` in name)
   105→    since most CLI tools want plain directory paths.
   106→    """
   107→    patterns = set()
   108→    for pat in DEFAULT_EXCLUSIONS:
   109→        if "*" not in pat:
   110→            patterns.add(pat)
   111→    patterns.update(p for p in get_exclusions() if p and "*" not in p)
   112→    return [str(scan_root / p) for p in sorted(patterns) if p]
   113→
   114→
   115→def _is_excluded_dir(name: str, rel_path: str, extra: tuple[str, ...]) -> bool:
   116→    in_default_exclusions = name in DEFAULT_EXCLUSIONS or name.endswith(".egg-info")
   117→    is_virtualenv_dir = name.startswith(".venv") or name.startswith("venv")
   118→    matches_extra_exclusion = bool(
   119→        extra
   120→        and any(
   121→            matches_exclusion(rel_path, exclusion)
   122→            or exclusion == name
   123→            or exclusion == name + "/**"
   124→            or exclusion == name + "/*"
   125→            for exclusion in extra
   126→        )
   127→    )
   128→    return in_default_exclusions or is_virtualenv_dir or matches_extra_exclusion
   129→
   130→
   131→def _find_source_files_cached(
   132→    path: str,
   133→    extensions: tuple[str, ...],
   134→    exclusions: tuple[str, ...] | None = None,
   135→    extra_exclusions: tuple[str, ...] = (),
   136→) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   137→    """Cached file discovery using os.walk with traversal-time pruning."""
   138→    cache_key = (path, extensions, exclusions, extra_exclusions)
   139→    cache = current_runtime_context().source_file_cache
   140→    cached = cache.get(cache_key)
   141→    if cached is not None:
   142→        return cached
   143→
   144→    project_root = get_project_root()
   145→    root = Path(path)
   146→    if not root.is_absolute():
   147→        root = project_root / root
   148→    all_exclusions = (exclusions or ()) + extra_exclusions
   149→    ext_set = set(extensions)
   150→    files: list[str] = []
   151→    for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(root):
   152→        rel_dir = _normalize_path_separators(_safe_relpath(dirpath, project_root))
   153→        dirnames[:] = sorted(
   154→            d
   155→            for d in dirnames
   156→            if not _is_excluded_dir(d, rel_dir + "/" + d, all_exclusions)
   157→        )
   158→        for fname in filenames:
   159→            if any(fname.endswith(ext) for ext in ext_set):
   160→                full = os.path.join(dirpath, fname)
   161→                rel_file = _normalize_path_separators(_safe_relpath(full, project_root))
   162→                if all_exclusions and any(
   163→                    matches_exclusion(rel_file, ex) for ex in all_exclusions
   164→                ):
   165→                    continue
   166→                files.append(rel_file)
   167→    result = tuple(sorted(files))
   168→    cache.put(cache_key, result)
   169→    return result
   170→
   171→
   172→def find_source_files(
   173→    path: str | Path, extensions: list[str], exclusions: list[str] | None = None
   174→) -> list[str]:
   175→    """Find all files with given extensions under a path, excluding patterns."""
   176→    return list(
   177→        _find_source_files_cached(
   178→            str(path),
   179→            tuple(extensions),
   180→            tuple(exclusions) if exclusions else None,
   181→            get_exclusions(),
   182→        )
   183→    )
   184→
   185→
   186→def find_ts_files(path: str | Path) -> list[str]:
   187→    return find_source_files(path, [".ts", ".tsx"])
   188→
   189→
   190→def find_tsx_files(path: str | Path) -> list[str]:
   191→    return find_source_files(path, [".tsx"])
   192→
   193→
   194→def find_py_files(path: str | Path) -> list[str]:
   195→    return find_source_files(path, [".py"])
   196→
   197→
   198→__all__ = [
   199→    "DEFAULT_EXCLUSIONS",
   200→    "collect_exclude_dirs",
   201→    "set_exclusions",

   149→        except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
   150→            logger.debug("Skipping unresolvable file %s: %s", file_path, exc)
   151→            continue
   152→
   153→        parent = str((scan_root / parent_rel).resolve())
   154→        dir_counts[parent] += 1
   155→        parts = parent_rel.parts
   156→        for idx in range(len(parts) - 1):
   157→            ancestor = (scan_root / Path(*parts[: idx + 1])).resolve()
   158→            child = (scan_root / Path(*parts[: idx + 2])).resolve()
   159→            ancestor_key = str(ancestor)
   160→            child_dirs.setdefault(ancestor_key, set()).add(str(child))

    10→def print_user_message(text: str) -> None:
    11→    """Print a plain bordered box to nudge LLM agent behavior.
    12→
    13→    Uses a simple box without JSON framing — experiments showed agents
    14→    engage with the content rather than reflexively dismissing it as
    15→    prompt injection (which JSON-framed variants triggered).
    16→
    17→    Plain text (no color) so it stands out among colored triage output.
    18→    """
    19→    wrapped = textwrap.wrap(text, width=54)
    20→
    21→    print()
    22→    print(f"  ┌{'─' * _BOX_WIDTH}┐")
    23→    print(f"  │{' ' * _BOX_WIDTH}│")
    24→    for line in wrapped:
    25→        print(f"  │  {line.ljust(_BOX_WIDTH - 2)}│")
    26→    print(f"  │{' ' * _BOX_WIDTH}│")
    27→    print(f"  └{'─' * _BOX_WIDTH}┘")
    28→    print()
    29→

    24→def _execute_serial(
    25→    *,
    26→    tasks: dict[int, BatchTask],
    27→    indexes: list[int],
    28→    progress_fn,
    29→    error_log_fn,
    30→    clock_fn,
    31→    contract_cache: dict[int, str],
    32→) -> list[int]:
    33→    """Run tasks one at a time — no threads, no closures."""
    34→    failures: set[int] = set()
    35→    for idx in indexes:
    36→        t0 = float(clock_fn())
    37→        start_error = _emit_progress(
    38→            progress_fn,
    39→            idx,
    40→            "start",
    41→            None,
    42→            details={"max_workers": 1},
    43→            contract_cache=contract_cache,
    44→        )
    45→        if start_error is not None:
    46→            _record_execution_error(
    47→                error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
    48→                failures=failures,
    49→                idx=idx,
    50→                exc=start_error,
    51→            )
    52→        try:
    53→            code = tasks[idx]()
    54→        except _RUNNER_TASK_EXCEPTIONS as exc:
    55→            _record_execution_error(
    56→                error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
    57→                failures=failures,
    58→                idx=idx,
    59→                exc=exc,
    60→            )

   320→
   321→
   322→def do_import(
   323→    import_file,
   324→    state,
   325→    lang,
   326→    state_file,
   327→    *,
   328→    config: dict | None = None,
   329→    allow_partial: bool = False,
   330→    trusted_assessment_source: bool = False,
   331→    trusted_assessment_label: str | None = None,
   332→    attested_external: bool = False,
   333→    manual_override: bool = False,
   334→    manual_attest: str | None = None,
   335→) -> None:
   336→    """Import mode: ingest agent-produced issues."""
   337→    import_config = ReviewImportConfig(
   338→        config=config,
   339→        allow_partial=allow_partial,
   340→        trusted_assessment_source=trusted_assessment_source,
   341→        trusted_assessment_label=trusted_assessment_label,
   342→        attested_external=attested_external,
   343→        manual_override=manual_override,
   344→        manual_attest=manual_attest,
   345→    )
   346→    override_enabled, override_attest = import_helpers_mod.resolve_override_context(
   347→        manual_override=import_config.manual_override,
   348→        manual_attest=import_config.manual_attest,
   349→    )
   350→    try:
   351→        _validate_import_flag_combos(
   352→            attested_external=import_config.attested_external,
   353→            allow_partial=import_config.allow_partial,
   354→            override_enabled=override_enabled,
   355→            override_attest=override_attest,
   356→        )
   357→    except ImportFlagValidationError as exc:
   358→        raise CommandError(str(exc), exit_code=1) from exc
   359→
   360→    try:
   361→        issues_data = import_helpers_mod.load_import_issues_data(
   362→            import_file,
   363→            config=_build_import_load_config(
   364→                lang_name=lang.name,
   365→                import_config=import_config,
   366→                override_enabled=override_enabled,
   367→                override_attest=override_attest,
   368→            ),
   369→        )
   370→    except import_helpers_mod.ImportPayloadLoadError as exc:
   371→        import_helpers_mod.print_import_load_errors(
   372→            exc.errors,
   373→            import_file=str(import_file),
   374→            colorize_fn=colorize,
   375→        )
   376→        raise PacketValidationError("import payload validation failed", exit_code=1) from exc
   377→    assessment_policy: AssessmentImportPolicyModel = (
   378→        import_helpers_mod.assessment_policy_model_from_payload(issues_data)
   379→    )
   380→    import_helpers_mod.print_assessment_mode_banner(
   381→        assessment_policy.to_dict(),
   382→        colorize_fn=colorize,
   383→    )
   384→    import_helpers_mod.print_assessment_policy_notice(
   385→        assessment_policy.to_dict(),
   386→        import_file=str(import_file),
   387→        colorize_fn=colorize,
   388→    )
   389→
   390→    prev = state_mod.score_snapshot(state)
   391→
   392→    # Transactional import: only persist if all post-import guards pass.
   393→    # Rebase on the latest on-disk state when available so long-running review
   394→    # sessions don't clobber newer imports/scans that completed while batches ran.
   395→    state_path = Path(state_file) if state_file is not None else None
   396→    if state_path is not None and state_path.exists():
   397→        working_state = copy.deepcopy(state_mod.load_state(state_path))
   398→    else:
   399→        working_state = copy.deepcopy(state)
   400→    diff = review_mod.import_holistic_issues(issues_data, working_state, lang.name)
   401→    label = "Holistic review"
   402→    imported_assessment_keys = _imported_assessment_keys(issues_data)
   403→    provisional_count = 0
   404→    if assessment_policy.mode == "manual_override":
   405→        provisional_count = _mark_manual_override_assessments_provisional(
   406→            working_state,
   407→            assessment_keys=imported_assessment_keys,
   408→        )
   409→    elif assessment_policy.mode in {"trusted_internal", "attested_external"}:
   410→        _clear_provisional_override_flags(
   411→            working_state,
   412→            assessment_keys=imported_assessment_keys,
   413→        )
   414→
   415→    if diff.get("skipped", 0) > 0 and not import_config.allow_partial:
   416→        details_lines: list[str] = []
   417→        for detail in diff.get("skipped_details", []):
   418→            reasons = "; ".join(detail.get("missing", []))
   419→            details_lines.append(
   420→                f"  #{detail.get('index', '?')} ({detail.get('identifier', '<none>')}): {reasons}"
   421→            )
   422→        msg = "import produced skipped issue(s); refusing partial import."
   423→        if details_lines:
   424→            msg += "\n" + "\n".join(details_lines)
   425→        msg += "\nFix the payload and retry, or pass --allow-partial to override."
   426→        raise CommandError(msg, exit_code=1)
   427→
   428→    if assessment_policy.assessments_present:
   429→        audit = working_state.setdefault("assessment_import_audit", [])
   430→        audit.append(
   431→            {
   432→                "timestamp": state_mod.utc_now(),
   433→                "mode": assessment_policy.mode,
   434→                "trusted": bool(assessment_policy.trusted),
   435→                "reason": assessment_policy.reason,
   436→                "override_used": bool(assessment_policy.mode == "manual_override"),
   437→                "attested_external": bool(assessment_policy.mode == "attested_external"),
   438→                "provisional": bool(assessment_policy.mode == "manual_override"),
   439→                "provisional_count": int(provisional_count),
   440→                "attest": (override_attest or "").strip(),
   441→                "import_file": str(import_file),
   442→            }
   443→        )
   444→    state.clear()
   445→    state.update(working_state)
   446→    state_mod.save_state(state, state_file)
   447→
   448→    # Sync plan: issue sync (if new issues) + workflow items (always).
   449→    _sync_plan_after_import(state, diff, assessment_policy.mode)
   450→
   451→    _print_import_results(
   452→        state=state,
   453→        lang_name=lang.name,
   454→        config=import_config.config,
   455→        diff=diff,
   456→        prev=prev,
   457→        label=label,
   458→        provisional_count=provisional_count,
   459→        assessment_policy=assessment_policy,
   460→    )
   461→
   462→
   463→def _print_import_results(
   464→    *,
   465→    state: dict,
   466→    lang_name: str,
   467→    config: dict | None,
   468→    diff: dict,
   469→    prev: dict,
   470→    label: str,
   471→    provisional_count: int,
   472→    assessment_policy,
   473→) -> None:
   474→    """Print import results, scores, and write query.json."""
   475→    narrative = narrative_mod.compute_narrative(
   476→        state, NarrativeContext(lang=lang_name, command="review")
   477→    )
   478→
   479→    print(colorize(f"\n  {label} imported:", "bold"))
   480→    issue_count = int(diff.get("new", 0) or 0)
   481→    print(
   482→        colorize(
   483→            f"  +{issue_count} new issue{'s' if issue_count != 1 else ''} "
   484→            f"(review issues), "
   485→            f"{diff['auto_resolved']} resolved, "
   486→            f"{diff['reopened']} reopened",
   487→            "dim",
   488→        )
   489→    )
   490→    if provisional_count > 0:
   491→        print(
   492→            colorize(
   493→                "  WARNING: manual override assessments are provisional and will "
   494→                "reset on the next scan unless replaced by "
   495→                "a trusted review path (see skill doc for options).",
   496→                "yellow",
   497→            )
   498→        )
   499→    import_helpers_mod.print_skipped_validation_details(diff, colorize_fn=colorize)
   500→    import_helpers_mod.print_assessments_summary(state, colorize_fn=colorize)
   501→    next_command = import_helpers_mod.print_open_review_summary(
   502→        state, colorize_fn=colorize
   503→    )
   504→    show_score_with_plan_context(state, prev)
   505→    at_target = import_helpers_mod.print_review_import_scores_and_integrity(
   506→        state,
   507→        config or {},
   508→        state_mod=state_mod,
   509→        target_strict_score_from_config_fn=target_strict_score_from_config,
   510→        subjective_at_target_fn=_SCORECARD_SUBJECTIVE_AT_TARGET,
   511→        subjective_rerun_command_fn=reporting_dimensions_mod.subjective_rerun_command,
   512→        colorize_fn=colorize,
   513→    )
   514→
   515→    print(
   516→        colorize(
   517→            f"  Next command to improve subjective scores: `{next_command}`", "dim"
   518→        )
   519→    )
   520→    write_query(
   521→        {
   522→            "command": "review",
   523→            "action": "import",
   524→            "mode": "holistic",
   525→            "diff": diff,
   526→            "next_command": next_command,
   527→            "subjective_at_target": [
   528→                {"dimension": entry["name"], "score": entry["score"]}
   529→                for entry in at_target
   530→            ],
   531→            "assessment_import": {
   532→                "mode": assessment_policy.mode,
   533→                "trusted": bool(assessment_policy.trusted),
   534→                "reason": assessment_policy.reason,
   535→            },
   536→            "narrative": narrative,
   537→        }
   538→    )

   541→def do_validate_import(
   542→    import_file,
   543→    lang,
   544→    *,
   545→    allow_partial: bool = False,
   546→    attested_external: bool = False,
   547→    manual_override: bool = False,
   548→    manual_attest: str | None = None,
   549→) -> None:
   550→    """Validate import payload/policy and print mode without mutating state."""
   551→    import_config = ReviewImportConfig(
   552→        allow_partial=allow_partial,
   553→        attested_external=attested_external,
   554→        manual_override=manual_override,
   555→        manual_attest=manual_attest,
   556→    )
   557→    override_enabled, override_attest = import_helpers_mod.resolve_override_context(
   558→        manual_override=import_config.manual_override,
   559→        manual_attest=import_config.manual_attest,
   560→    )
   561→    try:
   562→        _validate_import_flag_combos(
   563→            attested_external=import_config.attested_external,
   564→            allow_partial=import_config.allow_partial,
   565→            override_enabled=override_enabled,
   566→            override_attest=override_attest,
   567→        )
   568→    except ImportFlagValidationError as exc:
   569→        raise CommandError(str(exc), exit_code=1) from exc
   570→
   571→    try:
   572→        issues_data = import_helpers_mod.load_import_issues_data(
   573→            import_file,
   574→            config=_build_import_load_config(
   575→                lang_name=lang.name,
   576→                import_config=import_config,
   577→                override_enabled=override_enabled,
   578→                override_attest=override_attest,
   579→            ),
   580→        )
   581→    except import_helpers_mod.ImportPayloadLoadError as exc:
   582→        import_helpers_mod.print_import_load_errors(
   583→            exc.errors,
   584→            import_file=str(import_file),
   585→            colorize_fn=colorize,
   586→        )
   587→        raise PacketValidationError("import payload validation failed", exit_code=1) from exc
   588→    assessment_policy = import_helpers_mod.assessment_policy_model_from_payload(
   589→        issues_data
   590→    )
   591→    import_helpers_mod.print_assessment_mode_banner(
   592→        assessment_policy.to_dict(),
   593→        colorize_fn=colorize,
   594→    )
   595→    import_helpers_mod.print_assessment_policy_notice(
   596→        assessment_policy.to_dict(),
   597→        import_file=str(import_file),
   598→        colorize_fn=colorize,
   599→    )
   600→
   601→    issues_count = len(issues_data["issues"])
   602→    print(colorize("\n  Import payload validation passed.", "bold"))
   603→    print(colorize(f"  Issues parsed: {issues_count}", "dim"))
   604→    if assessment_policy.assessments_present:
   605→        count = int(assessment_policy.assessment_count)
   606→        print(colorize(f"  Assessment entries in payload: {count}", "dim"))
   607→    print(colorize("  No state changes were made (--validate-import).", "dim"))
   608→
   609→
   610→__all__ = [

   616→]

    13→def render_deps_cli(args, *, build_dep_graph, resolve_roslyn_cmd) -> None:
    14→    """Show dependency info for a specific C# file or top coupled files."""
    15→    graph = build_dep_graph(Path(args.path), roslyn_cmd=resolve_roslyn_cmd(args))
    16→
    17→    if getattr(args, "file", None):
    18→        coupling = get_coupling_score(args.file, graph)
    19→        if getattr(args, "json", False):
    20→            print(json.dumps({"file": rel(args.file), **coupling}, indent=2))
    21→            return
    22→        print(colorize(f"\nDependency info: {rel(args.file)}\n", "bold"))
    23→        print(f"  Fan-in (importers):  {coupling['fan_in']}")
    24→        print(f"  Fan-out (imports):   {coupling['fan_out']}")
    25→        print(f"  Instability:         {coupling['instability']}")
    26→        return
    27→
    28→    by_importers = sorted(graph.items(), key=lambda kv: (-kv[1].get("importer_count", 0), rel(kv[0])))
    29→    if getattr(args, "json", False):
    30→        top = by_importers[: getattr(args, "top", 20)]
    31→        print(
    32→            json.dumps(
    33→                {
    34→                    "files": len(graph),
    35→                    "entries": [
    36→                        {
    37→                            "file": rel(filepath),
    38→                            "importers": entry.get("importer_count", 0),
    39→                            "imports": entry.get("import_count", 0),
    40→                        }
    41→                        for filepath, entry in top
    42→                    ],
    43→                },
    44→                indent=2,
    45→            )
    46→        )
    47→        return
    48→
    49→    print(colorize(f"\nC# dependency graph: {len(graph)} files\n", "bold"))
    50→    rows = []
    51→    for filepath, entry in by_importers[: getattr(args, "top", 20)]:
    52→        rows.append([rel(filepath), str(entry.get("importer_count", 0)), str(entry.get("import_count", 0))])
    53→    if rows:
    54→        print_table(["File", "Importers", "Imports"], rows, [70, 9, 7])
    55→
    56→
    57→def render_cycles_cli(args, *, build_dep_graph, resolve_roslyn_cmd) -> None:
    58→    """Show import cycles in C# source files."""
    59→    graph = build_dep_graph(Path(args.path), roslyn_cmd=resolve_roslyn_cmd(args))
    60→    cycles, _ = detect_cycles(graph)
    61→
    62→    if getattr(args, "json", False):
    63→        print(
    64→            json.dumps(
    65→                {
    66→                    "count": len(cycles),
    67→                    "cycles": [
    68→                        {"length": cycle["length"], "files": [rel(filepath) for filepath in cycle["files"]]}
    69→                        for cycle in cycles
    70→                    ],
    71→                },
    72→                indent=2,
    73→            )
    74→        )
    75→        return
    76→
    77→    if not cycles:
    78→        print(colorize("No import cycles found.", "green"))
    79→        return
    80→
    81→    print(colorize(f"\nImport cycles: {len(cycles)}\n", "bold"))
    82→    for cycle in cycles[: getattr(args, "top", 20)]:
    83→        files = [rel(filepath) for filepath in cycle["files"]]
    84→        suffix = f" -> +{len(files) - 6}" if len(files) > 6 else ""
    85→        print(f"  [{cycle['length']} files] {' -> '.join(files[:6])}{suffix}")

   140→def _handle_heartbeat(
   141→    *,
   142→    details: dict,
   143→    total_batches: int,
   144→    stall_warning_seconds: float,
   145→    stall_warned_batches: set[int],
   146→    append_run_log,
   147→    colorize_fn,
   148→) -> None:
   149→    """Handle a heartbeat progress event — print status and stall warnings."""
   150→    active = details.get("active_batches")
   151→    queued = details.get("queued_batches", [])
   152→    elapsed = details.get("elapsed_seconds", {})
   153→    if not isinstance(active, list):
   154→        active = []
   155→    if not isinstance(queued, list):
   156→        queued = []
   157→    if not active and not queued:
   158→        return
   159→    segments: list[str] = []
   160→    for idx in active[:6]:
   161→        secs = 0
   162→        if isinstance(elapsed, dict):
   163→            raw_secs = elapsed.get(idx, 0)
   164→            secs = int(raw_secs) if isinstance(raw_secs, int | float) else 0
   165→        segments.append(f"#{idx + 1}:{secs}s")
   166→    if len(active) > 6:
   167→        segments.append(f"+{len(active) - 6} more")
   168→    queued_segment = ""
   169→    if queued:
   170→        queued_segment = f", queued {len(queued)}"
   171→    print(
   172→        colorize_fn(
   173→            "  Batch heartbeat: "
   174→            f"{len(active)}/{total_batches} active{queued_segment} "
   175→            f"({', '.join(segments) if segments else 'running batches pending'})",
   176→            "dim",
   177→        )
   178→    )
   179→    append_run_log(
   180→        "heartbeat "
   181→        f"active={[idx + 1 for idx in active]} queued={[idx + 1 for idx in queued]} "
   182→        f"elapsed={{{', '.join(f'{idx + 1}:{elapsed.get(idx, 0)}' for idx in active)}}}"
   183→    )
   184→    if stall_warning_seconds > 0 and isinstance(elapsed, dict):
   185→        slow_active = [
   186→            idx
   187→            for idx in active
   188→            if isinstance(elapsed.get(idx), int | float)

   191→        newly_warned = [idx for idx in slow_active if idx not in stall_warned_batches]

   207→def _collect_and_reconcile_results(

   212→    output_files: dict,

   215→    batch_status: dict[str, dict[str, object]],
   216→) -> tuple[list[dict], list[int], list[int], set[int]]:
   217→    """Collect batch results and reconcile per-batch status entries.
   218→
   219→    Returns (batch_results, successful_indexes, failures, failure_set).
   220→    """
   221→    allowed_dims = {
   222→        str(dim) for dim in packet.get("dimensions", []) if isinstance(dim, str)
   223→    }
   224→    batch_results, failures = collect_batch_results_fn(

   228→        allowed_dims=allowed_dims,
   229→    )
   230→
   231→    execution_failure_set = set(execution_failures)
   232→    failure_set = set(failures)
   233→    successful_indexes = sorted(idx for idx in selected_indexes if idx not in failure_set)
   234→    for idx in selected_indexes:
   235→        key = str(idx + 1)
   236→        state = batch_status.setdefault(
   237→            key,
   238→            {"position": batch_positions.get(idx, 0), "status": "pending"},

   244→            state["status"] = "failed"

   246→        if not output_files[idx].exists():
   247→            state["status"] = "missing_output"
   248→            continue
   249→        state["status"] = "parse_failed"
   250→
   251→    return batch_results, successful_indexes, failures, failure_set

1→"""Runtime compatibility governance matrix and helper predicates.
     2→
     3→This module is the single source of truth for import-boundary policy:
     4→- public runtime modules (stable entry surfaces),
     5→- deprecated compatibility modules (removal candidates),
     6→- private modules (internal implementation details).
     7→"""
     8→
     9→from __future__ import annotations
    10→
    11→from collections.abc import Iterable
    12→
    13→# Public package roots intended for runtime imports across the codebase.
    14→PUBLIC_RUNTIME_ROOTS: tuple[str, ...] = (
    15→    "desloppify.app",
    16→    "desloppify.base",
    17→    "desloppify.engine",
    18→    "desloppify.intelligence",
    19→    "desloppify.languages",
    20→)
    21→
    22→# Compatibility shims removed from runtime usage; these must not be reintroduced.
    23→SOFT_DEPRECATED_MODULES: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
    24→    {
    25→        "desloppify.utils",
    26→        "desloppify.file_discovery",
    27→        "desloppify.base.output_api",
    28→        "desloppify.base.output_contract",
    29→        "desloppify.base.text.text_api",
    30→        "desloppify.base.discovery.api",
    31→        "desloppify.base.discovery.path_io",
    32→    }
    33→)
    34→
    35→SOFT_DEPRECATED_SHORT_IMPORTS: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
    36→    {
    37→        "utils",
    38→        "file_discovery",
    39→    }
    40→)
    41→
    42→# Private internals: only code under these roots may import them directly.
    43→PRIVATE_MODULE_PREFIXES: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    44→PRIVATE_ALLOWED_IMPORTER_PREFIXES: tuple[str, ...] = ("desloppify.base",)
    45→
    46→
    47→def is_soft_deprecated_module(module: str) -> bool:
    48→    """Return True when module is a soft-deprecated compatibility surface."""
    49→    return module in SOFT_DEPRECATED_MODULES
    50→
    51→
    52→def is_private_module(module: str) -> bool:
    53→    """Return True when module path belongs to a private internal namespace."""
    54→    normalized = module.strip()
    55→    if not normalized:
    56→        return False
    57→    for prefix in PRIVATE_MODULE_PREFIXES:
    58→        if normalized == prefix or normalized.startswith(f"{prefix}."):
    59→            return True
    60→    return False
    61→
    62→
    63→def importer_can_access_private(importer_module: str) -> bool:
    64→    """Return True when importer module is allowed to reference private APIs."""
    65→    normalized = importer_module.strip()
    66→    if not normalized:
    67→        return False
    68→    for prefix in PRIVATE_ALLOWED_IMPORTER_PREFIXES:
    69→        if normalized == prefix or normalized.startswith(f"{prefix}."):
    70→            return True
    71→    return False
    72→
    73→
    74→def iter_soft_deprecated_module_paths() -> Iterable[str]:
    75→    """Yield python-module relative paths for deprecated compatibility modules."""
    76→    for module in sorted(SOFT_DEPRECATED_MODULES):
    77→        parts = module.split(".")
    78→        yield "/".join(parts) + ".py"
    79→
    80→
    81→__all__ = [
    82→    "PRIVATE_ALLOWED_IMPORTER_PREFIXES",
    83→    "PRIVATE_MODULE_PREFIXES",
    84→    "PUBLIC_RUNTIME_ROOTS",
    85→    "SOFT_DEPRECATED_MODULES",
    86→    "SOFT_DEPRECATED_SHORT_IMPORTS",
    87→    "importer_can_access_private",
    88→    "is_private_module",
    89→    "is_soft_deprecated_module",
    90→    "iter_soft_deprecated_module_paths",
    91→]

   684→def _cmd_confirm_stage(
   685→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   686→    *,
   687→    services: TriageServices | None = None,
   688→) -> None:
   689→    """Router for ``--confirm observe/reflect/organize/enrich/sense-check``."""
   690→    resolved_services = services or default_triage_services()
   691→    confirm_stage = getattr(args, "confirm", None)
   692→    attestation = getattr(args, "attestation", None)
   693→    plan = resolved_services.load_plan()
   694→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   695→    stages = meta.get("triage_stages", {})
   696→
   697→    if confirm_stage == "observe":
   698→        _confirm_observe(args, plan, stages, attestation, services=resolved_services)
   699→    elif confirm_stage == "reflect":
   700→        _confirm_reflect(args, plan, stages, attestation, services=resolved_services)
   701→    elif confirm_stage == "organize":
   702→        _confirm_organize(args, plan, stages, attestation, services=resolved_services)
   703→    elif confirm_stage == "enrich":
   704→        _confirm_enrich(args, plan, stages, attestation, services=resolved_services)
   705→    elif confirm_stage == "sense-check":
   706→        _confirm_sense_check(args, plan, stages, attestation, services=resolved_services)
   707→
   708→
   709→MIN_ATTESTATION_LEN = _MIN_ATTESTATION_LEN
   710→validate_attestation = _validate_attestation
   711→
   712→
   713→def cmd_confirm_stage(
   714→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   715→    *,
   716→    services: TriageServices | None = None,
   717→) -> None:
   718→    """Public triage confirmation entrypoint."""
   719→    _cmd_confirm_stage(args, services=services)
