    41→    r"\bfunction\s+(\w+)\s*\([^)]*\)\s*\{\s*return\s+(\w+)\s*\(",
    42→    re.MULTILINE,
    43→)
    44→
    45→_INTERFACE_RE = re.compile(
    46→    r"\binterface\s+([A-Za-z_]\w*)\b|\bclass\s+([A-Za-z_]\w*Protocol)\b"
    47→)
    48→
    49→_IMPLEMENTS_RE = re.compile(r"\bclass\s+\w+\s+implements\s+([^{:\n]+)")
    50→
    51→_INHERITS_RE = re.compile(r"\bclass\s+\w+\s*(?:\(([^)\n]+)\)\s*:|:\s*([^\n{]+))")
    52→
    53→_CHAIN_RE = re.compile(r"\b(?:\w+\.){2,}\w+\b")
    54→
    55→_CONFIG_BAG_RE = re.compile(
    56→    r"\b(?:config|configs|options|opts|params|ctx|context)\b",
    57→    re.IGNORECASE,
    58→)
    59→
    60→
    61→def _compute_sub_axes(
    62→    *,
    63→    wrapper_rate: float,
    64→    util_files: list,
    65→    indirection_hotspots: list,
    66→    wide_param_bags: list,
    67→    one_impl_interfaces: list,
    68→    delegation_classes: list,
    69→    facade_modules: list,
    70→    typed_dict_violation_files: set,
    71→    total_typed_dict_violations: int,
    72→    dict_any_count: int = 0,
    73→    enum_bypass_count: int = 0,
    74→) -> dict[str, float]:
    75→    """Compute all 6 sub-axis scores for the abstractions dimension."""
    76→    abstraction_leverage = _score_clamped(
    77→        100 - (wrapper_rate * 120) - (len(util_files) * 1.5)
    78→    )
    79→    indirection_cost = _score_clamped(
    80→        100
    81→        - (sum(item["max_chain_depth"] for item in indirection_hotspots[:20]) * 2.5)
    82→        - (sum(item["wide_functions"] for item in wide_param_bags[:20]) * 2.0)
    83→    )
    84→    interface_honesty = _score_clamped(100 - (len(one_impl_interfaces) * 8))
    85→
    86→    top10_delegation = delegation_classes[:10]
    87→    avg_delegation_ratio = (
    88→        sum(d["delegation_ratio"] for d in top10_delegation) / len(top10_delegation)
    89→        if top10_delegation
    90→        else 0.0
    91→    )
    92→    delegation_density = _score_clamped(
    93→        100 - (avg_delegation_ratio * 80) - (len(delegation_classes) * 5)
    94→    )
    95→    avg_facade_ratio = (
    96→        sum(f["re_export_ratio"] for f in facade_modules[:10]) / len(facade_modules[:10])
    97→        if facade_modules
    98→        else 0.0
    99→    )
   100→    definition_directness = _score_clamped(
   101→        100 - (len(facade_modules) * 8) - (avg_facade_ratio * 50)
   102→    )
   103→    type_discipline = _score_clamped(
   104→        100
   105→        - (len(typed_dict_violation_files) * 6)
   106→        - (total_typed_dict_violations * 1.5)
   107→        - (dict_any_count * 1.0)
   108→        - (enum_bypass_count * 2.0)
   109→    )
   110→    return {
   111→        "abstraction_leverage": abstraction_leverage,
   112→        "indirection_cost": indirection_cost,
   113→        "interface_honesty": interface_honesty,
   114→        "delegation_density": delegation_density,
   115→        "definition_directness": definition_directness,
   116→        "type_discipline": type_discipline,
   117→    }
   118→
   119→
   120→def _build_abstraction_leverage_context(
   121→    *,
   122→    util_files: list[dict],
   123→    wrappers_by_file: list[dict[str, object]],
   124→) -> dict[str, object]:
   125→    context: dict[str, object] = {}
   126→    if util_files:
   127→        context["util_files"] = sorted(util_files, key=lambda item: -item["loc"])[:20]
   128→    if wrappers_by_file:
   129→        context["pass_through_wrappers"] = wrappers_by_file[:20]
   130→    return context
   131→
   132→
   133→def _build_indirection_cost_context(
   134→    *,
   135→    indirection_hotspots: list[dict[str, object]],
   136→    wide_param_bags: list[dict[str, object]],
   137→) -> dict[str, object]:
   138→    context: dict[str, object] = {}
   139→    if indirection_hotspots:
   140→        context["indirection_hotspots"] = indirection_hotspots[:20]
   141→    if wide_param_bags:
   142→        context["wide_param_bags"] = wide_param_bags[:20]
   143→    return context
   144→
   145→
   146→def _build_interface_honesty_context(
   147→    *,
   148→    one_impl_interfaces: list[dict[str, object]],
   149→) -> dict[str, object]:
   150→    if one_impl_interfaces:
   151→        return {"one_impl_interfaces": one_impl_interfaces[:20]}
   152→    return {}
   153→
   154→
   155→def _build_delegation_density_context(
   156→    *,
   157→    delegation_classes: list[dict],
   158→) -> dict[str, object]:
   159→    if delegation_classes:
   160→        return {"delegation_heavy_classes": delegation_classes}
   161→    return {}
   162→
   163→
   164→def _build_definition_directness_context(
   165→    *,
   166→    facade_modules: list[dict],
   167→) -> dict[str, object]:
   168→    if facade_modules:
   169→        return {"facade_modules": facade_modules}
   170→    return {}
   171→
   172→
   173→def _build_type_discipline_context(
   174→    *,
   175→    typed_dict_violations: list[dict],
   176→    dict_any_annotations: list[dict] | None = None,
   177→    enum_bypass_patterns: list[dict] | None = None,
   178→    type_strategy_census: dict[str, list[dict]] | None = None,
   179→) -> dict[str, object]:
   180→    context: dict[str, object] = {}
   181→    if typed_dict_violations:
   182→        context["typed_dict_violations"] = typed_dict_violations
   183→    if dict_any_annotations:
   184→        context["dict_any_annotations"] = dict_any_annotations
   185→    if enum_bypass_patterns:
   186→        context["enum_bypass_patterns"] = enum_bypass_patterns
   187→    if type_strategy_census:
   188→        context["type_strategy_census"] = {
   189→            strategy: len(items)
   190→            for strategy, items in type_strategy_census.items()
   191→        }
   192→    return context
   193→
   194→
   195→def _assemble_context(
   196→    *,
   197→    util_files: list,
   198→    wrapper_rate: float,
   199→    total_wrappers: int,
   200→    total_function_signatures: int,
   201→    wrappers_by_file: list,
   202→    one_impl_interfaces: list,
   203→    indirection_hotspots: list,
   204→    wide_param_bags: list,
   205→    delegation_classes: list,
   206→    facade_modules: list,
   207→    typed_dict_violations: list,
   208→    total_typed_dict_violations: int,
   209→    sub_axes: dict[str, float],
   210→    dict_any_annotations: list | None = None,
   211→    enum_bypass_patterns: list | None = None,
   212→    type_strategy_census: dict | None = None,
   213→) -> dict:
   214→    """Build the final context dict from collected data and sub-axis scores."""
   215→    util_list = sorted(util_files, key=lambda item: -item["loc"])[:20]
   216→    context: dict[str, object] = {
   217→        "util_files": util_list,
   218→        "summary": {
   219→            "wrapper_rate": round(wrapper_rate, 3),
   220→            "total_wrappers": total_wrappers,
   221→            "total_function_signatures": total_function_signatures,
   222→            "one_impl_interface_count": len(one_impl_interfaces),
   223→            "indirection_hotspot_count": len(indirection_hotspots),
   224→            "wide_param_bag_count": len(wide_param_bags),
   225→            "delegation_heavy_class_count": len(delegation_classes),
   226→            "facade_module_count": len(facade_modules),
   227→            "typed_dict_violation_count": total_typed_dict_violations,
   228→            "dict_any_annotation_count": len(dict_any_annotations or []),
   229→            "enum_bypass_count": len(enum_bypass_patterns or []),
   230→        },
   231→        "sub_axes": sub_axes,
   232→    }
   233→
   234→    context.update(
   235→        _build_abstraction_leverage_context(
   236→            util_files=util_files,
   237→            wrappers_by_file=wrappers_by_file,
   238→        )
   239→    )
   240→    context.update(
   241→        _build_indirection_cost_context(
   242→            indirection_hotspots=indirection_hotspots,
   243→            wide_param_bags=wide_param_bags,
   244→        )
   245→    )
   246→    context.update(
   247→        _build_interface_honesty_context(one_impl_interfaces=one_impl_interfaces)
   248→    )
   249→    context.update(
   250→        _build_delegation_density_context(delegation_classes=delegation_classes)
   251→    )
   252→    context.update(
   253→        _build_definition_directness_context(facade_modules=facade_modules)
   254→    )
   255→    context.update(
   256→        _build_type_discipline_context(
   257→            typed_dict_violations=typed_dict_violations,
   258→            dict_any_annotations=dict_any_annotations,
   259→            enum_bypass_patterns=enum_bypass_patterns,
   260→            type_strategy_census=type_strategy_census,
   261→        )
   262→    )
   263→
   264→    return context
   265→
   266→
   267→@dataclasses.dataclass
   268→class _AbstractionsCollector:
   269→    """Accumulated state for the abstractions scan pass."""
   270→
   271→    util_files: list = dataclasses.field(default_factory=list)
   272→    wrappers_by_file: list[dict[str, object]] = dataclasses.field(default_factory=list)
   273→    interface_declarations: dict[str, set[str]] = dataclasses.field(
   274→        default_factory=lambda: defaultdict(set)
   275→    )
   276→    implementations: dict[str, set[str]] = dataclasses.field(
   277→        default_factory=lambda: defaultdict(set)
   278→    )
   279→    indirection_hotspots: list[dict[str, object]] = dataclasses.field(
   280→        default_factory=list
   281→    )
   282→    wide_param_bags: list[dict[str, object]] = dataclasses.field(default_factory=list)
   283→    delegation_classes: list[dict] = dataclasses.field(default_factory=list)
   284→    facade_modules: list[dict] = dataclasses.field(default_factory=list)
   285→    typed_dict_defs: dict[str, set[str]] = dataclasses.field(default_factory=dict)
   286→    parsed_trees: dict[str, ast.Module] = dataclasses.field(default_factory=dict)
   287→    total_function_signatures: int = 0
   288→    total_wrappers: int = 0
   289→
   290→
   291→def _scan_file(
   292→    col: _AbstractionsCollector, filepath: str, content: str
   293→) -> None:
   294→    """Scan a single file and accumulate results into *col*."""
   295→    rpath = rel(filepath)
   296→    loc = len(content.splitlines())
   297→    basename = Path(rpath).stem.lower()
   298→    if basename in {"utils", "helpers", "util", "helper", "common", "misc"}:
   299→        col.util_files.append(
   300→            {"file": rpath, "loc": loc, "excerpt": file_excerpt(filepath) or ""}
   301→        )
   302→
   303→    signatures = _DEF_SIGNATURE_RE.findall(content)
   304→    col.total_function_signatures += len(signatures)
   305→
   306→    ts_wrappers = [
   307→        (wrapper, target)
   308→        for wrapper, target in _TS_PASSTHROUGH_RE.findall(content)
   309→        if wrapper != target
   310→    ]
   311→
   312→    for match in _INTERFACE_RE.finditer(content):
   313→        iface = match.group(1) or match.group(2)
   314→        if iface:
   315→            col.interface_declarations[iface].add(rpath)
   316→
   317→    for match in _IMPLEMENTS_RE.finditer(content):
   318→        for iface in _extract_type_names(match.group(1)):
   319→            col.implementations[iface].add(rpath)
   320→    for match in _INHERITS_RE.finditer(content):
   321→        blob = match.group(1) or match.group(2) or ""
   322→        for iface in _extract_type_names(blob):
   323→            col.implementations[iface].add(rpath)
   324→
   325→    chain_matches = _CHAIN_RE.findall(content)
   326→    max_chain_depth = max((token.count(".") for token in chain_matches), default=0)
   327→    if max_chain_depth >= 3 or len(chain_matches) >= 6:
   328→        col.indirection_hotspots.append(
   329→            {
   330→                "file": rpath,
   331→                "max_chain_depth": max_chain_depth,
   332→                "chain_count": len(chain_matches),
   333→            }
   334→        )
   335→
   336→    wide_functions = sum(
   337→        1 for params_blob in signatures if _count_signature_params(params_blob) >= 7
   338→    )
   339→    bag_mentions = len(_CONFIG_BAG_RE.findall(content))
   340→    if wide_functions > 0 or bag_mentions >= 10:
   341→        col.wide_param_bags.append(
   342→            {
   343→                "file": rpath,
   344→                "wide_functions": wide_functions,
   345→                "config_bag_mentions": bag_mentions,
   346→            }
   347→        )
   348→
   349→    try:
   350→        tree = ast.parse(content)
   351→    except SyntaxError:
   352→        tree = None
   353→
   354→    if tree is not None:
   355→        col.parsed_trees[filepath] = tree
   356→        py_wrappers = _find_python_passthrough_wrappers(tree)
   357→        for entry in _find_delegation_heavy_classes(tree):
   358→            col.delegation_classes.append({"file": rpath, **entry})
   359→        facade_result = _find_facade_modules(tree, loc=loc)
   360→        if facade_result is not None:
   361→            col.facade_modules.append({"file": rpath, **facade_result})
   362→        _collect_typed_dict_defs(tree, col.typed_dict_defs)
   363→    else:
   364→        py_wrappers = []
   365→
   366→    wrapper_pairs = py_wrappers + ts_wrappers
   367→    if wrapper_pairs:
   368→        col.total_wrappers += len(wrapper_pairs)
   369→        col.wrappers_by_file.append(
   370→            {
   371→                "file": rpath,
   372→                "count": len(wrapper_pairs),
   373→                "samples": [f"{w}->{t}" for w, t in wrapper_pairs[:5]],
   374→            }
   375→        )
   376→
   377→
   378→def _derive_post_scan_results(col: _AbstractionsCollector) -> dict:
   379→    """Compute derived analyses from the completed scan collector."""
   380→    one_impl_interfaces: list[dict[str, object]] = []
   381→    for iface, declared_in in col.interface_declarations.items():
   382→        implemented_in = sorted(col.implementations.get(iface, set()))
   383→        if len(implemented_in) != 1:
   384→            continue
   385→        one_impl_interfaces.append(
   386→            {
   387→                "interface": iface,
   388→                "declared_in": sorted(declared_in),
   389→                "implemented_in": implemented_in,
   390→            }
   391→        )
   392→
   393→    typed_dict_violations = _find_typed_dict_usage_violations(
   394→        col.parsed_trees, col.typed_dict_defs
   395→    )[:20]
   396→    total_typed_dict_violations = sum(
   397→        v.get("count", 1) for v in typed_dict_violations
   398→    )
   399→    typed_dict_violation_files = {v["file"] for v in typed_dict_violations}
   400→
   401→    all_td_names = set(col.typed_dict_defs.keys())
   402→    dict_any_annotations = _find_dict_any_annotations(
   403→        col.parsed_trees, all_td_names
   404→    )[:30]
   405→
   406→    enum_defs = _collect_enum_defs(col.parsed_trees)
   407→    enum_bypass_patterns = _find_enum_bypass(col.parsed_trees, enum_defs)[:30]
   408→
   409→    type_strategy_census = _census_type_strategies(col.parsed_trees)
   410→
   411→    return {
   412→        "one_impl_interfaces": one_impl_interfaces,
   413→        "typed_dict_violations": typed_dict_violations,
   414→        "total_typed_dict_violations": total_typed_dict_violations,
   415→        "typed_dict_violation_files": typed_dict_violation_files,
   416→        "dict_any_annotations": dict_any_annotations,
   417→        "enum_bypass_patterns": enum_bypass_patterns,
   418→        "type_strategy_census": type_strategy_census,
   419→    }
   420→
   421→
   422→def _sort_and_trim(col: _AbstractionsCollector, derived: dict) -> None:
   423→    """Sort and trim collected lists in-place for final output."""
   424→    col.wrappers_by_file.sort(key=lambda item: -int(item["count"]))
   425→    col.indirection_hotspots.sort(
   426→        key=lambda item: (-int(item["max_chain_depth"]), -int(item["chain_count"]))
   427→    )
   428→    col.wide_param_bags.sort(
   429→        key=lambda item: (
   430→            -int(item["wide_functions"]),
   431→            -int(item["config_bag_mentions"]),
   432→        )
   433→    )
   434→    derived["one_impl_interfaces"].sort(key=lambda item: str(item["interface"]))
   435→    col.delegation_classes.sort(key=lambda d: -d["delegation_ratio"])
   436→    col.delegation_classes = col.delegation_classes[:20]
   437→    col.facade_modules.sort(key=lambda d: -d["re_export_ratio"])
   438→    col.facade_modules = col.facade_modules[:20]
   439→
   440→
   441→def _abstractions_context(file_contents: dict[str, str]) -> dict:
   442→    col = _AbstractionsCollector()
   443→
   444→    for filepath, content in file_contents.items():
   445→        _scan_file(col, filepath, content)
   446→
   447→    derived = _derive_post_scan_results(col)
   448→    _sort_and_trim(col, derived)
   449→
   450→    wrapper_rate = col.total_wrappers / max(col.total_function_signatures, 1)
   451→    sub_axes = _compute_sub_axes(
   452→        wrapper_rate=wrapper_rate,
   453→        util_files=col.util_files,
   454→        indirection_hotspots=col.indirection_hotspots,
   455→        wide_param_bags=col.wide_param_bags,
   456→        one_impl_interfaces=derived["one_impl_interfaces"],
   457→        delegation_classes=col.delegation_classes,
   458→        facade_modules=col.facade_modules,
   459→        typed_dict_violation_files=derived["typed_dict_violation_files"],
   460→        total_typed_dict_violations=derived["total_typed_dict_violations"],
   461→        dict_any_count=len(derived["dict_any_annotations"]),
   462→        enum_bypass_count=len(derived["enum_bypass_patterns"]),
   463→    )
   464→
   465→    return _assemble_context(
   466→        util_files=col.util_files,
   467→        wrapper_rate=wrapper_rate,
   468→        total_wrappers=col.total_wrappers,
   469→        total_function_signatures=col.total_function_signatures,
   470→        wrappers_by_file=col.wrappers_by_file,
   471→        one_impl_interfaces=derived["one_impl_interfaces"],
   472→        indirection_hotspots=col.indirection_hotspots,
   473→        wide_param_bags=col.wide_param_bags,
   474→        delegation_classes=col.delegation_classes,
   475→        facade_modules=col.facade_modules,
   476→        typed_dict_violations=derived["typed_dict_violations"],
   477→        total_typed_dict_violations=derived["total_typed_dict_violations"],
   478→        sub_axes=sub_axes,
   479→        dict_any_annotations=derived["dict_any_annotations"],
   480→        enum_bypass_patterns=derived["enum_bypass_patterns"],
   481→        type_strategy_census=derived["type_strategy_census"],
   482→    )
   483→
   484→
   485→__all__ = [
   486→    "_abstractions_context",
   487→    "_assemble_context",
   488→    "_build_abstraction_leverage_context",
   489→    "_build_definition_directness_context",
   490→    "_build_delegation_density_context",
   491→    "_build_indirection_cost_context",
   492→    "_build_interface_honesty_context",
   493→    "_build_type_discipline_context",
   494→    "_compute_sub_axes",
   495→]
   496→

    55→    for pf in production_files:

    57→        module_name = rel_pf.replace("/", ".").replace("\\", ".")
    58→        if "." in module_name:
    59→            module_name = module_name.rsplit(".", 1)[0]
    60→        prod_by_module[module_name] = pf
    61→
    62→        # __init__.py: also map package path (e.g. "foo.bar" -> __init__.py).
    63→        if module_name.endswith(".__init__"):
    64→            prod_by_module[module_name[: -len(".__init__")]] = pf
    65→
    66→        parts = module_name.split(".")
    67→        if parts:
    68→            prod_by_module[parts[-1]] = pf
    69→    return prod_by_module
    70→
    71→
    72→def _graph_tested_imports(
    73→    graph: dict,
    74→    test_files: set[str],
    75→    production_files: set[str],
    76→    prod_by_module: dict[str, str],
    77→    lang_name: str | None,
    78→) -> set[str]:
    79→    """Follow import graph edges from test files to find directly-tested production files."""
    80→    tested: set[str] = set()
    81→    for tf in test_files:
    82→        entry = graph.get(tf)
    83→        graph_mapped: set[str] = set()
    84→        if entry is not None:
    85→            for imp in entry.get("imports", set()):
    86→                if imp in production_files:
    87→                    graph_mapped.add(imp)
    88→            tested |= graph_mapped
    89→
    90→        # Parse source imports as a supplement when graph imports are absent,
    91→        # or always for TypeScript where dynamic import('...') is common in
    92→        # coverage smoke tests and may be missed by static graph building.
    93→        if not graph_mapped or lang_name == "typescript":
    94→            tested |= _parse_test_imports(
    95→                tf, production_files, prod_by_module, lang_name
    96→            )
    97→    return tested
    98→
    99→
   100→def _expand_barrel_targets(
   101→    *,
   102→    tested: set[str],
   103→    barrel_basenames: set[str],
   104→    production_files: set[str],
   105→    lang_name: str | None,
   106→) -> set[str]:
   107→    """Expand barrel/index file imports to the actual modules they re-export."""
   108→    extra: set[str] = set()
   109→    barrel_files = [f for f in tested if os.path.basename(f) in barrel_basenames]
   110→    for bf in barrel_files:
   111→        extra |= _resolve_barrel_reexports(bf, production_files, lang_name)
   112→    return extra
   113→
   114→
   115→def _expand_facade_targets(
   116→    *,
   117→    tested: set[str],
   118→    graph: dict,
   119→    production_files: set[str],
   120→    has_logic,
   121→) -> set[str]:
   122→    """Expand facade imports to their underlying implementation files.
   123→
   124→    If a directly-tested file has no testable logic (pure re-export facade),
   125→    promote its imports to directly tested.  This prevents false
   126→    "transitive_only" issues for internal modules behind facades like
   127→    scoring.py -> _scoring/policy/core.py.
   128→    """
   129→    facade_targets: set[str] = set()
   130→    for f in list(tested):
   131→        entry = graph.get(f)
   132→        if entry is None:
   133→            continue
   134→        read_result = read_coverage_file(
   135→            f, context="coverage_import_mapping_facade_logic"
   136→        )
   137→        if not read_result.ok:
   138→            continue
   139→        content = read_result.content
   140→        if not has_logic(f, content):
   141→            for imp in entry.get("imports", set()):
   142→                if imp in production_files:
   143→                    facade_targets.add(imp)
   144→    return facade_targets
   145→
   146→
   147→def import_based_mapping(
   148→    graph: dict,
   149→    test_files: set[str],
   150→    production_files: set[str],
   151→    lang_name: str | None = None,
   152→) -> set[str]:
   153→    """Map test files to production files via import edges."""
   154→    lang_name = lang_name or _infer_lang_name(test_files, production_files)
   155→    mod = _load_lang_test_coverage_module(lang_name)
   156→
   157→    prod_by_module = _build_prod_module_index(production_files)
   158→    tested = _graph_tested_imports(
   159→        graph, test_files, production_files, prod_by_module, lang_name
   160→    )
   161→
   162→    barrel_basenames = getattr(mod, "BARREL_BASENAMES", set())
   163→    if barrel_basenames:
   164→        tested |= _expand_barrel_targets(
   165→            tested=tested,
   166→            barrel_basenames=barrel_basenames,
   167→            production_files=production_files,
   168→            lang_name=lang_name,
   169→        )
   170→
   171→    has_logic = getattr(mod, "has_testable_logic", None)
   172→    if callable(has_logic):
   173→        tested |= _expand_facade_targets(
   174→            tested=tested,
   175→            graph=graph,
   176→            production_files=production_files,
   177→            has_logic=has_logic,
   178→        )
   179→
   180→    return tested
   181→
   182→
   183→def _resolve_import(
   184→    spec: str,
   185→    test_path: str,
   186→    production_files: set[str],
   187→    lang_name: str | None,
   188→) -> str | None:
   189→    mod = _load_lang_test_coverage_module(lang_name)
   190→    resolver = getattr(mod, "resolve_import_spec", None)
   191→    if callable(resolver):
   192→        return resolver(spec, test_path, production_files)
   193→    return None
   194→
   195→
   196→def _resolve_barrel_reexports(
   197→    filepath: str,
   198→    production_files: set[str],
   199→    lang_name: str | None = None,
   200→) -> set[str]:
   201→    """Resolve one-hop re-exports using language-specific helpers."""
   202→    if lang_name is None:
   203→        lang_name = _infer_lang_name({filepath}, production_files)
   204→    mod = _load_lang_test_coverage_module(lang_name)
   205→    resolver = getattr(mod, "resolve_barrel_reexports", None)
   206→    if callable(resolver):
   207→        return resolver(filepath, production_files)
   208→    return set()
   209→
   210→
   211→def _parse_test_imports(
   212→    test_path: str,
   213→    production_files: set[str],
   214→    prod_by_module: dict[str, str],
   215→    lang_name: str | None = None,
   216→) -> set[str]:
   217→    """Parse import statements from a test file and resolve production files."""
   218→    tested = set()
   219→    read_result = read_coverage_file(test_path, context="coverage_import_mapping_parse")
   220→    if not read_result.ok:
   221→        return tested
   222→    content = read_result.content
   223→
   224→    if lang_name is None:
   225→        lang_name = _infer_lang_name({test_path}, production_files)
   226→
   227→    mod = _load_lang_test_coverage_module(lang_name)
   228→    parse_specs = getattr(mod, "parse_test_import_specs", None)
   229→    if not callable(parse_specs):
   230→        return tested
   231→
   232→    for spec in parse_specs(content):
   233→        if not spec:
   234→            continue
   235→
   236→        resolved = _resolve_import(spec, test_path, production_files, lang_name)
   237→        if resolved:
   238→            tested.add(resolved)
   239→            continue
   240→
   241→        # Fallback: module-name lookup with progressively shorter prefixes.
   242→        cleaned = spec.lstrip("./").replace("/", ".")
   243→        parts = cleaned.split(".")
   244→        for i in range(len(parts), 0, -1):
   245→            candidate = ".".join(parts[:i])
   246→            if candidate in prod_by_module:
   247→                tested.add(prod_by_module[candidate])
   248→                break
   249→
   250→    return tested
   251→
   252→
   253→def _map_test_to_source(
   254→    test_path: str,
   255→    production_set: set[str],
   256→    lang_name: str,
   257→) -> str | None:
   258→    """Match a test file to a production file using language conventions."""
   259→    mod = _load_lang_test_coverage_module(lang_name)
   260→    mapper = getattr(mod, "map_test_to_source", None)
   261→    if callable(mapper):
   262→        return mapper(test_path, production_set)
   263→    return None
   264→
   265→
   266→def naming_based_mapping(
   267→    test_files: set[str],
   268→    production_files: set[str],
   269→    lang_name: str,
   270→) -> set[str]:
   271→    """Map test files to production files by naming conventions."""
   272→    tested = set()
   273→
   274→    prod_by_basename: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
   275→    for p in production_files:
   276→        bn = os.path.basename(p)
   277→        prod_by_basename.setdefault(bn, []).append(p)
   278→
   279→    for tf in test_files:
   280→        matched = _map_test_to_source(tf, production_files, lang_name)
   281→        if matched:
   282→            tested.add(matched)
   283→            continue
   284→
   285→        basename = os.path.basename(tf)
   286→        src_name = _strip_test_markers(basename, lang_name)
   287→        if src_name and src_name in prod_by_basename:
   288→            for p in prod_by_basename[src_name]:
   289→                tested.add(p)
   290→
   291→    return tested
   292→
   293→
   294→def _strip_test_markers(basename: str, lang_name: str) -> str | None:
   295→    """Strip test naming markers from a basename to derive source basename."""
   296→    mod = _load_lang_test_coverage_module(lang_name)
   297→    strip_markers = getattr(mod, "strip_test_markers", None)
   298→    if callable(strip_markers):
   299→        return strip_markers(basename)
   300→    return None
   301→
   302→
   303→def transitive_coverage(
   304→    directly_tested: set[str],
   305→    graph: dict,
   306→    production_files: set[str],
   307→) -> set[str]:
   308→    """BFS from directly-tested files through dep-graph imports."""
   309→    return transitive_coverage_core(directly_tested, graph, production_files)
   310→
   311→
   312→def analyze_test_quality(
   313→    test_files: set[str],
   314→    lang_name: str,
   315→) -> dict[str, dict]:
   316→    """Analyze test quality per file."""
   317→    return analyze_test_quality_core(
   318→        test_files,
   319→        lang_name,
   320→        load_lang_module=_load_lang_test_coverage_module,
   321→        read_coverage_file_fn=read_coverage_file,
   322→        logger=logger,
   323→    )
   324→
   325→
   326→def get_test_files_for_prod(
   327→    prod_file: str,
   328→    test_files: set[str],
   329→    graph: dict,
   330→    lang_name: str,
   331→    parsed_imports_by_test: dict[str, set[str]] | None = None,
   332→) -> list[str]:
   333→    """Find which test files exercise a given production file."""
   334→    return get_test_files_for_prod_core(
   335→        prod_file,
   336→        test_files,
   337→        graph,
   338→        lang_name,
   339→        parsed_imports_by_test,
   340→        parse_test_imports_fn=_parse_test_imports,
   341→        map_test_to_source_fn=_map_test_to_source,
   342→        project_root=str(get_project_root()),
   343→    )
   344→
   345→
   346→def build_test_import_index(
   347→    test_files: set[str],
   348→    production_files: set[str],
   349→    lang_name: str,
   350→) -> dict[str, set[str]]:

     8→

    20→    "/api/",

    29→def is_server_only_path(path: str) -> bool:
    30→    """Best-effort classification for server-only source paths."""
    31→    if not path:
    32→        return False
    33→    normalized = path.replace("\\", "/")
    34→    prefixed = normalized if normalized.startswith("/") else f"/{normalized}"
    35→    return any(hint in prefixed for hint in SERVER_ONLY_PATH_HINTS)

1→"""Cross-platform grep-style helpers."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import os
     6→import re
     7→
     8→from desloppify.base.discovery.source import read_file_text as _read_file_text
     9→from desloppify.base.discovery.paths import get_project_root
    10→
    11→
    12→def grep_files(
    13→    pattern: str, file_list: list[str], *, flags: int = 0
    14→) -> list[tuple[str, int, str]]:
    15→    """Search files for a regex pattern. Returns (filepath, lineno, line_text)."""
    16→    compiled = re.compile(pattern, flags)
    17→    results: list[tuple[str, int, str]] = []
    18→    for filepath in file_list:
    19→        abs_path = filepath if os.path.isabs(filepath) else str(get_project_root() / filepath)
    20→        content = _read_file_text(abs_path)
    21→        if content is None:
    22→            continue
    23→        for lineno, line in enumerate(content.splitlines(), 1):
    24→            if compiled.search(line):
    25→                results.append((filepath, lineno, line))
    26→    return results
    27→
    28→
    29→def grep_files_containing(
    30→    names: set[str], file_list: list[str], *, word_boundary: bool = True
    31→) -> dict[str, set[str]]:
    32→    r"""Find which files contain which names. Returns {name: set(filepaths)}."""
    33→    if not names:
    34→        return {}
    35→    names_by_length = sorted(names, key=len, reverse=True)
    36→    if word_boundary:
    37→        combined = re.compile(
    38→            r"\b(?:" + "|".join(re.escape(n) for n in names_by_length) + r")\b"
    39→        )
    40→    else:
    41→        combined = re.compile("|".join(re.escape(n) for n in names_by_length))
    42→
    43→    name_to_files: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
    44→    for filepath in file_list:
    45→        abs_path = filepath if os.path.isabs(filepath) else str(get_project_root() / filepath)
    46→        content = _read_file_text(abs_path)
    47→        if content is None:
    48→            continue
    49→        found = set(combined.findall(content))
    50→        for name in found & names:
    51→            name_to_files.setdefault(name, set()).add(filepath)
    52→    return name_to_files
    53→
    54→
    55→def grep_count_files(
    56→    name: str, file_list: list[str], *, word_boundary: bool = True
    57→) -> list[str]:
    58→    """Return list of files containing name."""
    59→    if word_boundary:
    60→        pat = re.compile(r"\b" + re.escape(name) + r"\b")
    61→    else:
    62→        pat = re.compile(re.escape(name))
    63→    matching: list[str] = []
    64→    for filepath in file_list:
    65→        abs_path = filepath if os.path.isabs(filepath) else str(get_project_root() / filepath)
    66→        content = _read_file_text(abs_path)
    67→        if content is None:
    68→            continue
    69→        if pat.search(content):
    70→            matching.append(filepath)
    71→    return matching
    72→
    73→
    74→__all__ = [
    75→    "grep_count_files",
    76→    "grep_files",
    77→    "grep_files_containing",
    78→]
    79→

   141→    completed = [s for s in ("observe", "reflect", "organize", "enrich", "sense-check") if s in stages]

   145→            "complete all stages to exit. Run: desloppify plan triage"

1→"""Runtime state model for exclusions and in-memory caches."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from contextlib import contextmanager
     6→from contextvars import ContextVar
     7→from dataclasses import dataclass, field
     8→from pathlib import Path
     9→
    10→
    11→class FileTextCache:
    12→    """Optional read-through file-text cache used by scan/review passes."""
    13→
    14→    def __init__(self) -> None:
    15→        self._enabled = False
    16→        self._values: dict[str, str | None] = {}
    17→
    18→    def enable(self) -> None:
    19→        self._enabled = True
    20→        self._values.clear()
    21→
    22→    def disable(self) -> None:
    23→        self._enabled = False
    24→        self._values.clear()
    25→
    26→    def read(self, filepath: str) -> str | None:
    27→        if self._enabled and filepath in self._values:
    28→            return self._values[filepath]
    29→
    30→        try:
    31→            content = Path(filepath).read_text(errors="replace")
    32→        except OSError:
    33→            content = None
    34→        if self._enabled:
    35→            self._values[filepath] = content
    36→        return content
    37→
    38→
    39→class SourceFileCache:
    40→    """Small FIFO cache for source-file discovery results."""
    41→
    42→    def __init__(self, *, max_entries: int) -> None:
    43→        self.max_entries = max_entries
    44→        self.values: dict[tuple, tuple[str, ...]] = {}
    45→
    46→    def get(self, key: tuple) -> tuple[str, ...] | None:
    47→        return self.values.get(key)
    48→
    49→    def put(self, key: tuple, value: tuple[str, ...]) -> None:
    50→        if len(self.values) >= self.max_entries:
    51→            self.values.pop(next(iter(self.values)))
    52→        self.values[key] = value
    53→
    54→    def clear(self) -> None:
    55→        self.values.clear()
    56→
    57→
    58→@dataclass
    59→class RuntimeContext:
    60→    """Mutable runtime container for exclusion and cache state."""
    61→
    62→    exclusions: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    63→    project_root: Path | None = None
    64→    query_file: Path | None = None
    65→    file_text_cache: FileTextCache = field(default_factory=FileTextCache)
    66→    cache_enabled: bool = False
    67→    source_file_cache: SourceFileCache = field(
    68→        default_factory=lambda: SourceFileCache(max_entries=16)
    69→    )
    70→
    71→
    72→_PROCESS_RUNTIME_CONTEXT = RuntimeContext()
    73→_RUNTIME_CONTEXT: ContextVar[RuntimeContext | None] = ContextVar(
    74→    "desloppify_runtime_context",
    75→    default=None,
    76→)
    77→
    78→
    79→def make_runtime_context(*, source_file_cache_max_entries: int = 16) -> RuntimeContext:
    80→    """Create an isolated runtime context."""
    81→    return RuntimeContext(
    82→        source_file_cache=SourceFileCache(max_entries=source_file_cache_max_entries)
    83→    )
    84→
    85→
    86→def current_runtime_context() -> RuntimeContext:
    87→    """Return the active runtime context (or process fallback)."""
    88→    runtime = _RUNTIME_CONTEXT.get()
    89→    if runtime is not None:
    90→        return runtime
    91→    return _PROCESS_RUNTIME_CONTEXT
    92→
    93→
    94→@contextmanager
    95→def runtime_scope(runtime: RuntimeContext | None = None):
    96→    """Run code with an isolated runtime context."""
    97→    active = runtime or make_runtime_context()
    98→    [REDACTED](active)
    99→    try:
   100→        yield active
   101→    finally:
   102→        _RUNTIME_CONTEXT.reset(token)

1→"""Read helpers for per-issue plan override annotations."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from typing import Any
     6→
     7→
     8→def get_issue_override(plan: dict[str, Any], issue_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
     9→    """Return override payload for an issue ID or an empty mapping."""
    10→    overrides = plan.get("overrides", {})
    11→    if not isinstance(overrides, dict):
    12→        return {}
    13→    payload = overrides.get(issue_id, {})
    14→    if isinstance(payload, dict):
    15→        return payload
    16→    return {}
    17→
    18→
    19→def get_issue_description(plan: dict[str, Any], issue_id: str) -> str | None:
    20→    """Return per-issue plan description if one is set."""
    21→    value = get_issue_override(plan, issue_id).get("description")
    22→    return value if isinstance(value, str) else None
    23→
    24→
    25→def get_issue_note(plan: dict[str, Any], issue_id: str) -> str | None:
    26→    """Return per-issue plan note if one is set."""
    27→    value = get_issue_override(plan, issue_id).get("note")
    28→    return value if isinstance(value, str) else None
    29→
    30→
    31→def annotation_counts(plan: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[int, int]:
    32→    """Return counts of non-empty descriptions and notes in overrides."""
    33→    overrides = plan.get("overrides", {})
    34→    if not isinstance(overrides, dict):
    35→        return 0, 0
    36→    described = 0
    37→    noted = 0
    38→    for payload in overrides.values():
    39→        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
    40→            continue
    41→        if payload.get("description"):
    42→            described += 1
    43→        if payload.get("note"):
    44→            noted += 1
    45→    return described, noted
    46→

    49→    "annotation_counts",
    50→    "get_issue_description",

    52→    "get_issue_override",

1→"""Zone classification system — deterministic file intent classification.
     2→
     3→Classifies files into zones (production, test, config, generated, script, vendor)
     4→based on path patterns. Zone metadata flows through issues, scoring, and the LLM.
     5→"""
     6→
     7→from __future__ import annotations
     8→
     9→import logging
    10→import os
    11→from dataclasses import dataclass, field
    12→from enum import Enum
    13→
    14→from desloppify.base.output.fallbacks import log_best_effort_failure
    15→from desloppify.engine.policy.zones_data import (
    16→    CONFIG_SKIP_DETECTORS,
    17→    SCRIPT_SKIP_DETECTORS,
    18→    SKIP_ALL_DETECTORS,
    19→    TEST_SKIP_DETECTORS,
    20→)
    21→
    22→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    23→
    24→
    25→class Zone(str, Enum):
    26→    """File intent zone — determines scoring and detection policy."""
    27→
    28→    PRODUCTION = "production"
    29→    TEST = "test"
    30→    CONFIG = "config"
    31→    GENERATED = "generated"
    32→    SCRIPT = "script"
    33→    VENDOR = "vendor"
    34→
    35→
    36→# Zones excluded from the health score
    37→EXCLUDED_ZONES = {Zone.TEST, Zone.CONFIG, Zone.GENERATED, Zone.VENDOR}
    38→
    39→# String values for quick lookup in scoring (issues store zone as string)
    40→EXCLUDED_ZONE_VALUES = {z.value for z in EXCLUDED_ZONES}
    41→
    42→
    43→@dataclass
    44→class ZoneRule:
    45→    """A classification rule: zone + list of path patterns.
    46→
    47→    Patterns are matched against relative file paths. First matching rule wins.
    48→    Pattern types (auto-detected from shape):
    49→      - "/dir/"   → substring match on full path (directory marker)
    50→      - ".ext"    → basename ends-with (suffix/extension, e.g. ".d.ts", ".test.")
    51→      - "prefix_" → basename starts-with (trailing underscore)
    52→      - "name.py" → basename exact match (has extension, no /)
    53→      - fallback  → substring on full path
    54→    """
    55→
    56→    zone: Zone
    57→    patterns: list[str]
    58→
    59→
    60→def _match_pattern(rel_path: str, pattern: str) -> bool:
    61→    """Match a zone pattern against a relative file path.
    62→
    63→    See ZoneRule docstring for pattern type conventions.
    64→    """
    65→    basename = os.path.basename(rel_path)
    66→
    67→    # Directory pattern: "/dir/" → substring on padded path
    68→    if pattern.startswith("/") and pattern.endswith("/"):
    69→        return pattern in ("/" + rel_path + "/")
    70→
    71→    # Suffix/extension pattern: starts with "." → contains on basename
    72→    if pattern.startswith("."):
    73→        return pattern in basename
    74→
    75→    # Prefix pattern: ends with "_" → basename starts-with
    76→    if pattern.endswith("_"):
    77→        return basename.startswith(pattern)
    78→
    79→    # Suffix pattern: starts with "_" → basename ends-with (_test.py, _pb2.py)
    80→    if pattern.startswith("_"):
    81→        return basename.endswith(pattern)
    82→
    83→    # Exact basename: has a proper file extension (1-5 chars after last dot),
    84→    # no "/" → exact basename match (config.py, setup.py, conftest.py)
    85→    if "/" not in pattern and "." in pattern:
    86→        ext = pattern.rsplit(".", 1)[-1]
    87→        if ext and len(ext) <= 5 and ext.isalnum():
    88→            return basename == pattern
    89→
    90→    # Fallback: substring on full path (vite.config, tsconfig, eslint, etc.)
    91→    return pattern in rel_path
    92→
    93→
    94→# ── Common zone rules (shared across languages) ──────────
    95→
    96→COMMON_ZONE_RULES = [
    97→    ZoneRule(Zone.VENDOR, ["/vendor/", "/third_party/", "/vendored/"]),
    98→    ZoneRule(Zone.GENERATED, ["/generated/", "/__generated__/"]),
    99→    ZoneRule(Zone.TEST, ["/tests/", "/test/", "/fixtures/"]),
   100→    ZoneRule(Zone.SCRIPT, ["/scripts/", "/bin/"]),
   101→]
   102→
   103→
   104→def classify_file(
   105→    rel_path: str, rules: list[ZoneRule], overrides: dict[str, str] | None = None
   106→) -> Zone:
   107→    """Classify a file by its relative path. Overrides take priority."""
   108→    if overrides:
   109→        override = overrides.get(rel_path)
   110→        if override:
   111→            try:
   112→                return Zone(override)
   113→            except ValueError as exc:
   114→                log_best_effort_failure(
   115→                    logger, f"parse zone override for {rel_path}", exc
   116→                )
   117→    for rule in rules:
   118→        for pattern in rule.patterns:
   119→            if _match_pattern(rel_path, pattern):
   120→                return rule.zone
   121→    return Zone.PRODUCTION
   122→
   123→
   124→class FileZoneMap:
   125→    """Cached zone classification for a set of files.
   126→
   127→    Built once per scan from file list + zone rules.
   128→    """
   129→
   130→    def __init__(
   131→        self,
   132→        files: list[str],
   133→        rules: list[ZoneRule],
   134→        rel_fn=None,
   135→        overrides: dict[str, str] | None = None,
   136→    ):
   137→        """Build a zone map from files, ordered rules, and optional overrides."""
   138→        self._map: dict[str, Zone] = {}
   139→        self._overrides = overrides
   140→        for f in files:
   141→            rp = rel_fn(f) if rel_fn else f
   142→            self._map[f] = classify_file(rp, rules, overrides)
   143→
   144→    def get(self, path: str) -> Zone:
   145→        """Get zone for a file path. Returns PRODUCTION if not classified."""
   146→        return self._map.get(path, Zone.PRODUCTION)
   147→
   148→    def exclude(self, files: list[str], *zones: Zone) -> list[str]:
   149→        """Return files NOT in the given zones."""
   150→        zone_set = set(zones)
   151→        return [f for f in files if self._map.get(f, Zone.PRODUCTION) not in zone_set]
   152→
   153→    def include_only(self, files: list[str], *zones: Zone) -> list[str]:
   154→        """Return files that ARE in the given zones."""
   155→        zone_set = set(zones)
   156→        return [f for f in files if self._map.get(f, Zone.PRODUCTION) in zone_set]
   157→
   158→    def counts(self) -> dict[str, int]:
   159→        """Return file count per zone."""
   160→        counts: dict[str, int] = {}
   161→        for zone in self._map.values():
   162→            counts[zone.value] = counts.get(zone.value, 0) + 1
   163→        return counts
   164→
   165→    def production_count(self) -> int:
   166→        """Count files classified as production."""
   167→        return len(self._map) - self.non_production_count()
   168→
   169→    def non_production_count(self) -> int:
   170→        """Count files in excluded zones (test/config/generated/vendor)."""
   171→        return sum(1 for z in self._map.values() if z in EXCLUDED_ZONES)
   172→
   173→    def all_files(self) -> list[str]:
   174→        """Return all classified file paths."""
   175→        return list(self._map.keys())
   176→
   177→    def items(self) -> list[tuple[str, Zone]]:
   178→        """Return all (path, zone) pairs."""
   179→        return list(self._map.items())
   180→
   181→
   182→# ── Zone detection policies ────────────────────────────────
   183→
   184→
   185→@dataclass
   186→class ZonePolicy:
   187→    """Per-zone detection policy.
   188→
   189→    skip_detectors: detectors to skip entirely for this zone.
   190→    downgrade_detectors: detectors whose confidence is downgraded to "low".
   191→    exclude_from_score: whether issues in this zone are excluded from scoring.
   192→    """
   193→
   194→    skip_detectors: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
   195→    downgrade_detectors: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
   196→    exclude_from_score: bool = False
   197→
   198→
   199→ZONE_POLICIES: dict[Zone, ZonePolicy] = {
   200→    Zone.PRODUCTION: ZonePolicy(),
   201→    Zone.TEST: ZonePolicy(
   202→        skip_detectors=TEST_SKIP_DETECTORS,
   203→        downgrade_detectors={"smells", "structural"},
   204→        exclude_from_score=True,
   205→    ),
   206→    Zone.CONFIG: ZonePolicy(
   207→        skip_detectors=CONFIG_SKIP_DETECTORS,
   208→        exclude_from_score=True,
   209→    ),
   210→    Zone.GENERATED: ZonePolicy(
   211→        skip_detectors=SKIP_ALL_DETECTORS,
   212→        exclude_from_score=True,
   213→    ),
   214→    Zone.VENDOR: ZonePolicy(
   215→        skip_detectors=SKIP_ALL_DETECTORS,
   216→        exclude_from_score=True,
   217→    ),
   218→    Zone.SCRIPT: ZonePolicy(
   219→        skip_detectors=SCRIPT_SKIP_DETECTORS,
   220→        downgrade_detectors={"structural"},
   221→    ),
   222→}
   223→
   224→
   225→# ── Helpers for phase runners ─────────────────────────────
   226→
   227→
   228→def adjust_potential(zone_map, total: int) -> int:
   229→    """Subtract non-production files from a potential count.
   230→
   231→    Uses the zone map's own file list — no need to pass files separately.
   232→    No-op if zone_map is None.
   233→    """
   234→    if zone_map is None:
   235→        return total
   236→    return max(total - zone_map.non_production_count(), 0)
   237→
   238→
   239→def should_skip_issue(zone_map, filepath: str, detector: str) -> bool:
   240→    """Check if a issue should be skipped based on zone policy.
   241→
   242→    Returns True if the file's zone policy says to skip this detector.
   243→    """
   244→    if zone_map is None:
   245→        return False
   246→    zone = zone_map.get(filepath)
   247→    policy = ZONE_POLICIES.get(zone)
   248→    return policy is not None and detector in policy.skip_detectors
   249→
   250→
   251→def filter_entries(
   252→    zone_map, entries: list[dict], detector: str, file_key: str = "file"
   253→) -> list[dict]:
   254→    """Filter detector entries by zone policy. No-op if zone_map is None.
   255→
   256→    If file_key points to a list (e.g. cycle entries with "files"), checks
   257→    the first element.
   258→    """
   259→    if zone_map is None:
   260→        return entries
   261→
   262→    def _get_path(entry):
   263→        val = entry[file_key]
   264→        return val[0] if isinstance(val, list) else val
   265→
   266→    return [
   267→        e for e in entries if not should_skip_issue(zone_map, _get_path(e), detector)
   268→    ]
   269→

   295→def _apply_lifecycle_filter(items: list[WorkQueueItem]) -> list[WorkQueueItem]:
   296→    """Enforce lifecycle visibility rules.
   297→
   298→    The queue enforces a phase order: scan → initial review → triage → objective work.

   301→       The user must complete first-time reviews before working objective items.
   302→    2. **Triage in progress** → only show triage stages and workflow items.
   303→       Cluster work items aren't ready until triage completes (enrich adds
   304→       the detail that makes steps actionable).
   305→    3. **Objective work remains** → show objective items, hide endgame-only
   306→       subjective reassessments (stale re-reviews).

   309→    if _has_initial_reviews(items):

1→"""Stale @deprecated symbol detection."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import json
     6→import logging
     7→import re
     8→from pathlib import Path
     9→from typing import Any
    10→
    11→from desloppify.base.discovery.file_paths import (
    12→
    13→    rel,
    14→
    15→    resolve_path,
    16→
    17→)
    18→
    19→from desloppify.base.discovery.source import find_ts_files
    20→from desloppify.base.output.fallbacks import log_best_effort_failure
    21→from desloppify.base.search.grep import grep_count_files, grep_files
    22→from desloppify.base.output.terminal import colorize, print_table
    23→from desloppify.base.signal_patterns import DEPRECATION_MARKER_RE
    24→from desloppify.languages.typescript.detectors.contracts import DetectorResult
    25→
    26→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    27→def detect_deprecated_result(path: Path) -> DetectorResult[dict[str, Any]]:
    28→    """Find deprecated symbols with explicit population semantics."""
    29→    ts_files = find_ts_files(path)
    30→    hits = grep_files(DEPRECATION_MARKER_RE.pattern, ts_files, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
    31→
    32→    entries = []
    33→    seen_symbols = set()  # Deduplicate by file+symbol
    34→    for filepath, lineno, content in hits:
    35→        symbol, kind = _extract_deprecated_symbol(
    36→            filepath,
    37→            lineno,
    38→            content,
    39→            scan_root=path,
    40→        )
    41→        if not symbol:
    42→            continue
    43→        # Deduplicate (same symbol in same file, e.g., multiple @deprecated on interface props)
    44→        key = (filepath, symbol)
    45→        if key in seen_symbols:
    46→            continue
    47→        seen_symbols.add(key)
    48→        importers = (
    49→            _count_importers(symbol, filepath, ts_files=ts_files, scan_root=path)
    50→            if kind == "top-level"
    51→            else -1
    52→        )
    53→        entries.append(
    54→            {
    55→                "file": filepath,
    56→                "line": lineno,
    57→                "symbol": symbol,
    58→                "kind": kind,
    59→                "importers": importers,
    60→            }
    61→        )
    62→    sorted_entries = sorted(entries, key=lambda e: e["importers"])
    63→    return DetectorResult(
    64→        entries=sorted_entries,
    65→        population_kind="deprecated_symbols",
    66→        population_size=len(sorted_entries),
    67→    )
    68→
    69→
    70→def _extract_deprecated_symbol(
    71→    filepath: str,
    72→    lineno: int,
    73→    content: str,
    74→    *,
    75→    scan_root: Path | None = None,
    76→) -> tuple[str | None, str]:
    77→    """Extract the deprecated symbol name and whether it's a top-level or inline deprecation.
    78→
    79→    Returns (symbol_name, kind) where kind is "top-level" or "property".
    80→    """
    81→    try:
    82→        p = _resolve_source_file(filepath, scan_root=scan_root)
    83→        lines = p.read_text().splitlines()
    84→        content_stripped = content.strip()
    85→
    86→        # Case 1: Inline @deprecated on a property/field
    87→        # e.g., `/** @deprecated Use X instead */ fieldName?: Type;`
    88→        # or `/** @deprecated */ export const oldThing = ...`
    89→        if "/**" in content_stripped and "*/" in content_stripped:
    90→            # This is a single-line JSDoc. Check what follows on the same or next line
    91→            after_jsdoc = content_stripped.split("*/", 1)[1].strip()
    92→            if after_jsdoc:
    93→                # Property on same line: `/** @deprecated */ someField?: string;`
    94→                m = re.match(r"(\w+)\s*[?:=]", after_jsdoc)
    95→                if m:
    96→                    return m.group(1), "property"
    97→                # Declaration on same line: `/** @deprecated */ export const foo`
    98→                m = re.match(
    99→                    r"(?:export\s+)?(?:const|let|var|function|class|type|interface|enum)\s+(\w+)",
   100→                    after_jsdoc,
   101→                )
   102→                if m:
   103→                    return m.group(1), "top-level"
   104→
   105→        # Case 2: @deprecated inside a multi-line JSDoc block — check if it's on a property
   106→        # We need to look ahead to find what this annotates
   107→        for offset in range(1, 8):
   108→            idx = lineno - 1 + offset
   109→            if idx >= len(lines):
   110→                break
   111→            src = lines[idx].strip()
   112→            # Skip empty lines, comment continuations, closing comment
   113→            if not src or src.startswith("*") or src.startswith("//"):
   114→                continue
   115→            # Top-level declaration
   116→            m = re.match(
   117→                r"(?:export\s+)?(?:declare\s+)?(?:const|let|var|function|class|type|interface|enum)\s+(\w+)",
   118→                src,
   119→            )
   120→            if m:
   121→                return m.group(1), "top-level"
   122→            # Property/field: `fieldName?: Type;` or `fieldName: Type;`
   123→            m = re.match(r"(\w+)\s*[?:]", src)
   124→            if m:
   125→                return m.group(1), "property"
   126→            break
   127→
   128→        # Case 3: @deprecated as inline comment on same line
   129→        # e.g., `shotImageEntryId?: string; // @deprecated`
   130→        # Check the current line for a preceding field name
   131→        if "//" in content_stripped or "*" in content_stripped:
   132→            # Look at the same line before the @deprecated
   133→            marker_match = re.search(r"@deprecated", content_stripped, re.IGNORECASE)
   134→            line_before = content_stripped
   135→            if marker_match:
   136→                line_before = content_stripped[: marker_match.start()]
   137→            line_before = line_before.strip().rstrip("/*").rstrip("*").strip()
   138→            m = re.search(r"(\w+)\s*[?:]", line_before)
   139→            if m:
   140→                return m.group(1), "property"
   141→
   142→    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
   143→        log_best_effort_failure(
   144→            logger, f"read deprecated source context {filepath}", exc
   145→        )
   146→    return None, "unknown"
   147→
   148→
   149→def _resolve_source_file(filepath: str, *, scan_root: Path | None) -> Path:
   150→    if Path(filepath).is_absolute():
   151→        return Path(filepath)
   152→    if scan_root is not None:
   153→        candidate = scan_root / filepath
   154→        if candidate.exists():
   155→            return candidate
   156→    return Path(resolve_path(filepath))
   157→
   158→
   159→def _count_importers(
   160→    name: str, declaring_file: str, *, ts_files: list[str], scan_root: Path
   161→) -> int:
   162→    if not name:
   163→        return -1
   164→    matching = grep_count_files(name, ts_files, word_boundary=True)
   165→    declaring_resolved = str(
   166→        _resolve_source_file(declaring_file, scan_root=scan_root).resolve()
   167→    )
   168→    count = 0
   169→    for match_file in matching:
   170→        match_resolved = str(_resolve_source_file(match_file, scan_root=scan_root).resolve())
   171→        if match_resolved != declaring_resolved:
   172→            count += 1
   173→    return count
   174→

1→"""Auto-clustering algorithm — groups issues into task clusters."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from desloppify.base.config import DEFAULT_TARGET_STRICT_SCORE
     6→from desloppify.engine._plan.constants import AUTO_PREFIX
     7→from desloppify.engine._plan.auto_cluster_sync import (
     8→    prune_stale_clusters as _prune_stale_clusters,
     9→    sync_issue_clusters as _sync_issue_clusters,
    10→    sync_subjective_clusters as _sync_subjective_clusters,
    11→)
    12→from desloppify.engine._plan.schema import PlanModel, ensure_plan_defaults
    13→from desloppify.engine._plan.subjective_policy import SubjectiveVisibility
    14→from desloppify.engine._state.schema import StateModel, utc_now
    15→
    16→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    17→# Repair
    18→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    19→
    20→def _repair_ghost_cluster_refs(plan: PlanModel, now: str) -> int:
    21→    """Clear override cluster refs that point to non-existent clusters."""
    22→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
    23→    overrides = plan.get("overrides", {})
    24→    repaired = 0
    25→    for override in overrides.values():
    26→        cluster_name = override.get("cluster")
    27→        if cluster_name and cluster_name not in clusters:
    28→            override["cluster"] = None
    29→            override["updated_at"] = now
    30→            repaired += 1
    31→    return repaired
    32→
    33→
    34→def auto_cluster_issues(
    35→    plan: PlanModel,
    36→    state: StateModel,
    37→    *,
    38→    target_strict: float = DEFAULT_TARGET_STRICT_SCORE,
    39→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility | None = None,
    40→    cycle_just_completed: bool = False,
    41→) -> int:
    42→    """Regenerate auto-clusters from current open issues.
    43→
    44→    Returns count of changes made (clusters created, updated, or deleted).
    45→    """
    46→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
    47→
    48→    issues = state.get("issues", {})
    49→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
    50→
    51→    # Map existing auto-clusters by cluster_key
    52→    existing_by_key: dict[str, str] = {}  # cluster_key → cluster_name
    53→    for name, cluster in list(clusters.items()):
    54→        if cluster.get("auto"):
    55→            ck = cluster.get("cluster_key", "")
    56→            if ck:
    57→                existing_by_key[ck] = name
    58→
    59→    now = utc_now()
    60→    active_auto_keys: set[str] = set()
    61→    changes = 0
    62→
    63→    changes += _sync_issue_clusters(
    64→        plan, issues, clusters, existing_by_key, active_auto_keys, now,
    65→    )
    66→    changes += _sync_subjective_clusters(
    67→        plan, state, issues, clusters, existing_by_key, active_auto_keys, now,
    68→        target_strict=target_strict,
    69→        policy=policy,
    70→        cycle_just_completed=cycle_just_completed,
    71→    )
    72→    changes += _prune_stale_clusters(
    73→        plan, issues, clusters, active_auto_keys, now,
    74→    )
    75→    changes += _repair_ghost_cluster_refs(plan, now)
    76→
    77→    plan["updated"] = now
    78→    return changes
    79→
    80→
    81→__all__ = [
    82→    "AUTO_PREFIX",
    83→    "auto_cluster_issues",
    84→]
    85→

   419→    """Register a detector at runtime (used by generic plugins)."""

   421→    _RUNTIME.detectors[meta.name] = meta
   422→    if meta.name not in _RUNTIME.display_order:
   423→        _RUNTIME.display_order.append(meta.name)
   424→    _RUNTIME.judgment_detectors = frozenset(
   425→        name for name, m in _RUNTIME.detectors.items() if m.needs_judgment
   426→    )
   427→    JUDGMENT_DETECTORS = _RUNTIME.judgment_detectors

   436→    _RUNTIME.detectors.update(_BASE_DETECTORS)
   437→    _RUNTIME.display_order.clear()
   438→    _RUNTIME.display_order.extend(_BASE_DISPLAY_ORDER)
   439→    _RUNTIME.judgment_detectors = _BASE_JUDGMENT_DETECTORS

   461→}

   463→
   464→def dimension_action_type(dim_name: str) -> str:
   465→    """Return a compact action type label for a dimension based on its detectors."""
   466→    best = "manual"
   467→    best_pri = 99
   468→    for d in _RUNTIME.detectors.values():
   469→        if d.dimension == dim_name:
   470→            pri = _ACTION_PRIORITY.get(d.action_type, 99)
   471→            if pri < best_pri:
   472→                best_pri = pri
   473→                best = d.action_type
   474→    return _ACTION_LABELS.get(best, "manual")
   475→

   477→def detector_tools() -> dict[str, dict]:
   478→    """Build detector tool metadata keyed by detector name."""
   479→    result = {}

   482→            "fixers": list(d.fixers),
   483→            "action_type": d.action_type,
   484→        }
   485→        if d.tool:
   486→            entry["tool"] = d.tool
   487→        if d.guidance:
   488→            entry["guidance"] = d.guidance
   489→        result[name] = entry
   490→    return result

    10→from desloppify.engine._work_queue.helpers import (

    14→)
    15→from desloppify.engine._work_queue.plan_order import (
    16→    collapse_clusters,
    17→    enrich_plan_metadata,
    18→    filter_cluster_focus,
    19→    separate_skipped,
    20→    stamp_plan_sort_keys,
    21→    stamp_positions,
    22→)
    23→from desloppify.engine._work_queue.plan_order import (
    24→    new_item_ids as _new_item_ids,
    25→)
    26→from desloppify.engine._work_queue.ranking import (
    27→    build_issue_items,
    28→    enrich_with_impact,
    29→    group_queue_items,
    30→    item_explain,
    31→    item_sort_key,
    32→)
    33→from desloppify.engine._work_queue.synthetic import (
    34→    build_communicate_score_item,
    35→    build_create_plan_item,

    41→from desloppify.engine._work_queue.types import WorkQueueItem
    42→from desloppify.state import StateModel
    43→
    44→# Sentinel: "read scan_path from state" (the safe default).
    45→# Callers that want to override can pass an explicit str or None.
    46→_SCAN_PATH_FROM_STATE = object()
    47→
    48→
    49→@dataclass(frozen=True)
    50→class QueueBuildOptions:
    51→    """Configuration for queue construction.
    52→
    53→    ``scan_path`` defaults to reading from ``state["scan_path"]`` so callers
    54→    don't need to thread it manually.  Pass an explicit ``str`` or ``None``
    55→    to override (``None`` disables scope filtering).
    56→    """
    57→
    58→    # Output control
    59→    count: int | None = 1
    60→    explain: bool = False
    61→
    62→    # Scope filtering
    63→    scan_path: str | None | object = _SCAN_PATH_FROM_STATE
    64→    scope: str | None = None
    65→    status: str = "open"
    66→    chronic: bool = False
    67→
    68→    # Subjective gating
    69→    include_subjective: bool = True
    70→    subjective_threshold: float = 100.0
    71→
    72→    # Plan integration
    73→    plan: dict | None = None
    74→    include_skipped: bool = False
    75→    cluster: str | None = None
    76→
    77→    # Pre-computed context (overrides plan)
    78→    context: QueueContext | None = None
    79→
    80→
    81→class WorkQueueResult(TypedDict):
    82→    """Typed shape of the dict returned by :func:`build_work_queue`."""
    83→
    84→    items: list[WorkQueueItem]
    85→    total: int
    86→    grouped: dict[str, list[WorkQueueItem]]
    87→    new_ids: set[str]
    88→
    89→
    90→def build_work_queue(
    91→    state: StateModel,
    92→    *,
    93→    options: QueueBuildOptions | None = None,
    94→) -> WorkQueueResult:
    95→    """Build a ranked work queue from state issues.
    96→
    97→    Pipeline:
    98→    1. Gather    — issue items, subjective dimensions, workflow stages
    99→    2. Score     — estimate impact from dimension headroom
   100→    3. Presort   — stamp plan positions, separate skipped items
   101→    4. Lifecycle — filter endgame-only items when objective work remains
   102→    5. Sort      — rank by impact/confidence, apply plan order
   103→    6. Limit     — truncate to count, optionally add explain metadata
   104→    """
   105→    opts = options or QueueBuildOptions()
   106→    plan, scan_path, status, threshold = _resolve_inputs(opts, state)
   107→
   108→    # 1. Gather
   109→    items = build_issue_items(
   110→        state, scan_path=scan_path, status_filter=status,
   111→        scope=opts.scope, chronic=opts.chronic,
   112→    )
   113→    items += _gather_subjective_items(state, opts, threshold)
   114→    items += _gather_workflow_items(state, plan, status)
   115→
   116→    # 2. Score
   117→    enrich_with_impact(items, state.get("dimension_scores", {}))
   118→
   119→    # 3. Plan-aware ordering (part 1: separate skipped items)
   120→    new_ids, skipped = _plan_presort(items, state, plan)
   121→
   122→    # 4. Lifecycle filter — endgame-only items filtered when objective work remains
   123→    items = _apply_lifecycle_filter(items)
   124→
   125→    # 5. Sort & plan post-processing
   126→    items.sort(key=item_sort_key)
   127→    _plan_postsort(items, skipped, plan, opts)
   128→
   129→    # 6. Finalize
   130→    if not items:
   131→        items += _empty_queue_fallback(plan)
   132→    total = len(items)
   133→    if opts.count is not None and opts.count > 0:
   134→        items = items[:opts.count]
   135→    if opts.explain:
   136→        for item in items:
   137→            item["explain"] = item_explain(item)
   138→
   139→    return {
   140→        "items": items,
   141→        "total": total,
   142→        "grouped": group_queue_items(items, "item"),
   143→        "new_ids": new_ids,
   144→    }
   145→
   146→
   147→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   148→# Pipeline helpers (private to this module)
   149→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   150→
   151→
   152→def _resolve_inputs(
   153→    opts: QueueBuildOptions, state: StateModel,
   154→) -> tuple[dict | None, str | None, str, float]:
   155→    """Resolve plan, scan_path, status, and subjective threshold from options."""
   156→    ctx = opts.context
   157→    plan = ctx.plan if ctx is not None else opts.plan
   158→
   159→    scan_path: str | None = (
   160→        state.get("scan_path")
   161→        if opts.scan_path is _SCAN_PATH_FROM_STATE
   162→        else opts.scan_path  # type: ignore[assignment]
   163→    )
   164→
   165→    status = opts.status
   166→    if status not in ALL_STATUSES:
   167→        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported status filter: {status}")
   168→
   169→    try:
   170→        threshold = float(opts.subjective_threshold)
   171→    except (TypeError, ValueError):
   172→        threshold = 100.0
   173→    threshold = max(0.0, min(100.0, threshold))
   174→
   175→    return plan, scan_path, status, threshold
   176→
   177→
   178→def _gather_subjective_items(
   179→    state: StateModel,
   180→    opts: QueueBuildOptions,
   181→    threshold: float,
   182→) -> list[WorkQueueItem]:
   183→    """Build subjective dimension candidates.
   184→
   185→    Lifecycle filtering (endgame gating) happens in _apply_lifecycle_filter,
   186→    not here. This function only handles configuration and scope.
   187→    """
   188→    if not opts.include_subjective:
   189→        return []
   190→    if opts.status not in {"open", "all"}:
   191→        return []
   192→    if opts.chronic:
   193→        return []
   194→
   195→    candidates = build_subjective_items(
   196→        state, state.get("issues", {}), threshold=threshold,
   197→    )
   198→    return [item for item in candidates if scope_matches(item, opts.scope)]
   199→
   200→
   201→def _gather_workflow_items(
   202→    state: StateModel, plan: dict | None, status: str,
   203→) -> list[WorkQueueItem]:
   204→    """Inject triage stages, checkpoints, and create-plan when plan is active."""
   205→    if not plan or status not in {"open", "all"}:
   206→        return []
   207→
   208→    items: list[WorkQueueItem] = list(build_triage_stage_items(plan, state))
   209→    for builder in (
   210→        build_score_checkpoint_item,
   211→        build_import_scores_item,
   212→        build_communicate_score_item,
   213→    ):
   214→        item = builder(plan, state)
   215→        if item is not None:
   216→            items.append(item)
   217→    plan_item = build_create_plan_item(plan)
   218→    if plan_item is not None:
   219→        items.append(plan_item)
   220→    return items
   221→
   222→
   223→
   224→def _plan_presort(
   225→    items: list[WorkQueueItem], state: StateModel, plan: dict | None,
   226→) -> tuple[set[str], list[WorkQueueItem]]:
   227→    """Enrich plan metadata and stamp sort keys before sorting.
   228→
   229→    Returns ``(new_ids, skipped)`` — skipped items are removed from
   230→    ``items`` in place and returned separately for post-sort re-append.
   231→    """
   232→    if not plan:
   233→        return set(), []
   234→
   235→    new_ids = _new_item_ids(state)
   236→    enrich_plan_metadata(items, plan)
   237→    stamp_plan_sort_keys(items, plan, new_ids)
   238→    remaining, skipped = separate_skipped(items, plan)
   239→    items[:] = remaining
   240→    return new_ids, skipped
   241→
   242→
   243→def _plan_postsort(
   244→    items: list[WorkQueueItem],
   245→    skipped: list[WorkQueueItem],
   246→    plan: dict | None,
   247→    opts: QueueBuildOptions,
   248→) -> None:
   249→    """Re-append skipped items, stamp positions, filter to cluster focus."""
   250→    if not plan:
   251→        return
   252→
   253→    if opts.include_skipped:
   254→        items.extend(skipped)
   255→    stamp_positions(items, plan)
   256→    focused = filter_cluster_focus(items, plan, opts.cluster)
   257→    items[:] = focused
   258→
   259→
   260→def _has_objective_items(items: list[WorkQueueItem]) -> bool:
   261→    """True if any objective mechanical work items remain in the queue."""
   262→    return any(
   263→        i.get("kind") == "issue"
   264→        and i.get("detector", "") not in NON_OBJECTIVE_DETECTORS
   265→        for i in items
   266→    )
   267→
   268→
   269→def _has_initial_reviews(items: list[WorkQueueItem]) -> bool:
   270→    """True if any unassessed subjective dimensions need initial review."""
   271→    return any(
   272→        i.get("kind") == "subjective_dimension"
   273→        and i.get("initial_review")
   274→        for i in items
   275→    )
   276→
   277→
   278→def _is_endgame_only(item: WorkQueueItem) -> bool:
   279→    """True if this item should only appear when the objective queue is drained."""
   280→    return (
   281→        item.get("kind") == "subjective_dimension"
   282→        and not item.get("initial_review")
   283→    )
   284→
   285→
   286→def _has_triage_stages(items: list[WorkQueueItem]) -> bool:
   287→    """True if any pending triage stage items are in the queue."""
   288→    return any(
   289→        i.get("kind") == "workflow_stage"
   290→        and str(i.get("id", "")).startswith("triage::")
   291→        for i in items
   292→    )
   293→
   294→
   295→def _apply_lifecycle_filter(items: list[WorkQueueItem]) -> list[WorkQueueItem]:
   296→    """Enforce lifecycle visibility rules.
   297→
   298→    The queue enforces a phase order: scan → initial review → triage → objective work.
   299→
   300→    1. **Initial reviews pending** → only show initial-review subjective items.
   301→       The user must complete first-time reviews before working objective items.
   302→    2. **Triage in progress** → only show triage stages and workflow items.
   303→       Cluster work items aren't ready until triage completes (enrich adds
   304→       the detail that makes steps actionable).
   305→    3. **Objective work remains** → show objective items, hide endgame-only
   306→       subjective reassessments (stale re-reviews).
   307→    4. **Objective drained** → everything visible (endgame).
   308→    """
   309→    if _has_initial_reviews(items):
   310→        # Phase 1: only initial reviews visible — triage and workflow
   311→        # items stay hidden until initial reviews are complete.
   312→        return [
   313→            i for i in items
   314→            if i.get("kind") == "subjective_dimension" and i.get("initial_review")
   315→        ]
   316→    if _has_triage_stages(items):
   317→        # Phase 2: triage in progress — only triage stages and workflow items visible.
   318→        # Cluster work items aren't ready until enrich completes.
   319→        return [
   320→            i for i in items
   321→            if i.get("kind") in ("workflow_stage", "workflow_action")
   322→        ]
   323→    if not _has_objective_items(items):
   324→        return items  # endgame: everything visible
   325→    return [i for i in items if not _is_endgame_only(i)]
   326→
   327→
   328→def _empty_queue_fallback(plan: dict | None) -> list[WorkQueueItem]:
   329→    """Return a 'run scan' nudge when an active plan cycle has cleared."""
   330→    if not plan:
   331→        return []
   332→    plan_scores = plan.get("plan_start_scores", {})
   333→    if plan_scores.get("strict") is None:
   334→        return []
   335→    return [{
   336→        "id": "workflow::run-scan",
   337→        "kind": "workflow_action",
   338→        "summary": "Queue cleared \u2014 run scan to finalize and reveal your updated score.",
   339→        "primary_command": "desloppify scan",
   340→        "file": "",
   341→        "detector": "workflow",
   342→        "confidence": "high",
   343→    }]
   344→
   345→
   346→__all__ = [
   347→    "ATTEST_EXAMPLE",
   348→    "QueueBuildOptions",
   349→    "QueueContext",
   350→    "WorkQueueResult",
   351→    "build_work_queue",
   352→    "collapse_clusters",
   353→    "group_queue_items",
   354→]
   355→
