   246→) -> None:
   247→    """Configure metadata providers for subjective-dimension lookups."""
   248→    state = _PROVIDER_STATE
   249→
   250→    changed = False
   251→    if (
   252→        available_languages_provider is not None
   253→        and available_languages_provider is not state.available_languages_provider
   254→    ):
   255→        state.available_languages_provider = available_languages_provider
   256→        changed = True
   257→    if (
   258→        load_dimensions_payload_provider is not None
   259→        and load_dimensions_payload_provider
   260→        is not state.load_dimensions_payload_provider
   261→    ):
   262→        state.load_dimensions_payload_provider = load_dimensions_payload_provider
   263→        changed = True
   264→    if (
   265→        load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider is not None
   266→        and load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider
   267→        is not state.load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider
   268→    ):
   269→        state.load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider = (
   270→            load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider
   271→        )
   272→        changed = True
   273→
   274→    if changed:
   275→        _clear_subjective_dimension_caches()
   276→
   277→
   278→def reset_subjective_dimension_providers() -> None:
   279→    """Reset metadata providers to built-in defaults."""
   280→    configure_subjective_dimension_providers(
   281→        available_languages_provider=_default_available_languages,
   282→        load_dimensions_payload_provider=_default_load_dimensions_payload,
   283→        load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider=_default_load_dimensions_payload_for_lang,
   284→    )
   285→
   286→
   287→def _normalize_dimension_list(values: list[str]) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   288→    normalized: list[str] = []
   289→    for raw in values:
   290→        if not isinstance(raw, str):
   291→            continue
   292→        dim = _normalize_dimension_name(raw)
   293→        if not dim or dim in normalized:
   294→            continue
   295→        normalized.append(dim)
   296→    return tuple(normalized)
   297→
   298→
   299→@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
   300→def default_dimension_keys() -> tuple[str, ...]:
   301→    """Return canonical default subjective dimension keys."""
   302→    try:
   303→        dims, _, _ = _load_dimensions_payload()
   304→    except (ImportError, ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
   305→        logger.debug("Failed to load default subjective dimensions: %s", exc)
   306→        return tuple(_LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES.keys())
   307→    return _normalize_dimension_list(dims)
   308→
   309→
   310→@lru_cache(maxsize=16)
   311→def default_dimension_keys_for_lang(lang_name: str | None) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   312→    """Return default subjective dimension keys for a specific language."""
   313→    normalized = _normalize_lang_name(lang_name)
   314→    if normalized is None:
   315→        return default_dimension_keys()
   316→    try:
   317→        dims, _, _ = _load_dimensions_payload_for_lang(normalized)
   318→    except (ImportError, ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
   319→        logger.debug(
   320→            "Failed to load subjective dimensions for lang %s: %s",
   321→            normalized,
   322→            exc,
   323→        )
   324→        return default_dimension_keys()
   325→    return _normalize_dimension_list(dims)
   326→
   327→
   328→def _build_subjective_dimension_metadata(
   329→    *,
   330→    lang_name: str | None,
   331→) -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
   332→    out: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
   333→
   334→    try:
   335→        shared_defaults, shared_prompts, _ = _load_dimensions_payload()
   336→    except (ImportError, ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
   337→        logger.debug("Failed to load shared subjective dimension payload: %s", exc)
   338→        shared_defaults, shared_prompts = [], {}
   339→    _merge_dimension_meta(out, dimensions=shared_defaults, prompts=shared_prompts)
   340→
   341→    langs = (
   342→        [lang_name]
   343→        if isinstance(lang_name, str) and lang_name.strip()
   344→        else _available_languages()
   345→    )
   346→    for name in langs:
   347→        try:
   348→            lang_defaults, lang_prompts, _ = _load_dimensions_payload_for_lang(name)
   349→            _merge_dimension_meta(
   350→                out,
   351→                dimensions=lang_defaults,
   352→                prompts=lang_prompts,
   353→                override_existing=bool(lang_name),
   354→            )
   355→        except (ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
   356→            logger.debug("Failed to load dimensions for lang %s: %s", name, exc)
   357→            continue
   358→
   359→    for dim, payload in out.items():
   360→        payload.setdefault(
   361→            "display_name",
   362→            _LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES.get(dim, _title_display_name(dim)),
   363→        )
   364→        payload.setdefault("weight", _LEGACY_WEIGHT_BY_DIMENSION.get(dim, 1.0))
   365→        payload.setdefault("enabled_by_default", False)
   366→        if dim in _LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES:
   367→            payload.setdefault("reset_on_scan", dim in _LEGACY_RESET_ON_SCAN_DIMENSIONS)
   368→        else:
   369→            payload.setdefault("reset_on_scan", True)
   370→
   371→    # Preserve legacy dimensions even if a payload temporarily drops one.
   372→    for dim, display in _LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES.items():
   373→        payload = out.setdefault(dim, {})
   374→        payload.setdefault("display_name", display)
   375→        payload.setdefault("weight", _LEGACY_WEIGHT_BY_DIMENSION.get(dim, 1.0))
   376→        payload.setdefault("enabled_by_default", True)
   377→        payload.setdefault("reset_on_scan", dim in _LEGACY_RESET_ON_SCAN_DIMENSIONS)
   378→
   379→    return out
   380→
   381→
   382→@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
   383→def load_subjective_dimension_metadata() -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
   384→    """Return merged metadata across all known dimensions/languages."""
   385→    return _build_subjective_dimension_metadata(lang_name=None)
   386→
   387→
   388→@lru_cache(maxsize=16)
   389→def load_subjective_dimension_metadata_for_lang(
   390→    lang_name: str | None,
   391→) -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
   392→    """Return merged metadata for one language (with language overrides)."""
   393→    normalized = _normalize_lang_name(lang_name)
   394→    return _build_subjective_dimension_metadata(lang_name=normalized)
   395→
   396→
   397→def _metadata_registry(lang_name: str | None) -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
   398→    normalized = _normalize_lang_name(lang_name)
   399→    if normalized is None:
   400→        return load_subjective_dimension_metadata()
   401→    return load_subjective_dimension_metadata_for_lang(normalized)
   402→
   403→
   404→def get_dimension_metadata(
   405→    dimension_name: str, *, lang_name: str | None = None
   406→) -> dict[str, object]:
   407→    """Return metadata for one dimension key (with sane defaults)."""
   408→    dim = _normalize_dimension_name(dimension_name)
   409→    all_meta = _metadata_registry(lang_name)
   410→    payload = dict(all_meta.get(dim, {}))
   411→
   412→    payload.setdefault("display_name", _title_display_name(dim))
   413→    payload.setdefault("weight", 1.0)
   414→    payload.setdefault("enabled_by_default", False)
   415→    payload.setdefault("reset_on_scan", True)
   416→    return payload
   417→
   418→
   419→def dimension_display_name(dimension_name: str, *, lang_name: str | None = None) -> str:
   420→    meta = get_dimension_metadata(dimension_name, lang_name=lang_name)
   421→    return str(meta.get("display_name", _title_display_name(dimension_name)))
   422→
   423→
   424→def dimension_weight(dimension_name: str, *, lang_name: str | None = None) -> float:
   425→    meta = get_dimension_metadata(dimension_name, lang_name=lang_name)
   426→    raw = meta.get("weight", 1.0)
   427→    if is_numeric(raw):
   428→        return max(0.0, float(raw))
   429→    return 1.0
   430→
   431→
   432→def default_display_names_map(*, lang_name: str | None = None) -> dict[str, str]:
   433→    """Display-name map for default subjective dimensions."""
   434→    out: dict[str, str] = {}
   435→    for dim, payload in _metadata_registry(lang_name).items():
   436→        if not bool(payload.get("enabled_by_default", False)):
   437→            continue
   438→        out[dim] = str(payload.get("display_name", _title_display_name(dim)))
   439→    return out
   440→
   441→
   442→def resettable_default_dimensions(*, lang_name: str | None = None) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   443→    """Default subjective dimensions that should be reset by scan reset."""
   444→    out = []
   445→    for dim, payload in _metadata_registry(lang_name).items():
   446→        if not bool(payload.get("enabled_by_default", False)):
   447→            continue
   448→        if not bool(payload.get("reset_on_scan", True)):
   449→            continue
   450→        out.append(dim)
   451→    return tuple(sorted(set(out)))
   452→
   453→
   454→__all__ = [
   455→    "DISPLAY_NAMES",
   456→    "configure_subjective_dimension_providers",
   457→    "default_dimension_keys",
   458→    "default_dimension_keys_for_lang",
   459→    "default_display_names_map",
   460→    "dimension_display_name",
   461→    "dimension_weight",
   462→    "get_dimension_metadata",
   463→    "load_subjective_dimension_metadata",
   464→    "load_subjective_dimension_metadata_for_lang",
   465→    "reset_subjective_dimension_providers",
   466→    "resettable_default_dimensions",
   467→]
   468→

1→"""Zone classification system — deterministic file intent classification.
     2→
     3→Classifies files into zones (production, test, config, generated, script, vendor)
     4→based on path patterns. Zone metadata flows through issues, scoring, and the LLM.
     5→"""
     6→
     7→from __future__ import annotations
     8→
     9→import logging
    10→import os
    11→from dataclasses import dataclass, field
    12→from enum import Enum
    13→
    14→from desloppify.base.output.fallbacks import log_best_effort_failure
    15→from desloppify.engine.policy.zones_data import (
    16→    CONFIG_SKIP_DETECTORS,
    17→    SCRIPT_SKIP_DETECTORS,
    18→    SKIP_ALL_DETECTORS,
    19→    TEST_SKIP_DETECTORS,
    20→)
    21→
    22→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    23→
    24→
    25→class Zone(str, Enum):
    26→    """File intent zone — determines scoring and detection policy."""
    27→
    28→    PRODUCTION = "production"
    29→    TEST = "test"
    30→    CONFIG = "config"
    31→    GENERATED = "generated"
    32→    SCRIPT = "script"
    33→    VENDOR = "vendor"
    34→
    35→
    36→# Zones excluded from the health score
    37→EXCLUDED_ZONES = {Zone.TEST, Zone.CONFIG, Zone.GENERATED, Zone.VENDOR}
    38→
    39→# String values for quick lookup in scoring (issues store zone as string)
    40→EXCLUDED_ZONE_VALUES = {z.value for z in EXCLUDED_ZONES}
    41→
    42→
    43→@dataclass
    44→class ZoneRule:
    45→    """A classification rule: zone + list of path patterns.
    46→
    47→    Patterns are matched against relative file paths. First matching rule wins.
    48→    Pattern types (auto-detected from shape):
    49→      - "/dir/"   → substring match on full path (directory marker)
    50→      - ".ext"    → basename ends-with (suffix/extension, e.g. ".d.ts", ".test.")
    51→      - "prefix_" → basename starts-with (trailing underscore)
    52→      - "name.py" → basename exact match (has extension, no /)
    53→      - fallback  → substring on full path
    54→    """
    55→
    56→    zone: Zone
    57→    patterns: list[str]
    58→
    59→
    60→def _match_pattern(rel_path: str, pattern: str) -> bool:
    61→    """Match a zone pattern against a relative file path.
    62→
    63→    See ZoneRule docstring for pattern type conventions.
    64→    """
    65→    basename = os.path.basename(rel_path)
    66→
    67→    # Directory pattern: "/dir/" → substring on padded path
    68→    if pattern.startswith("/") and pattern.endswith("/"):
    69→        return pattern in ("/" + rel_path + "/")
    70→
    71→    # Suffix/extension pattern: starts with "." → contains on basename
    72→    if pattern.startswith("."):
    73→        return pattern in basename
    74→
    75→    # Prefix pattern: ends with "_" → basename starts-with
    76→    if pattern.endswith("_"):
    77→        return basename.startswith(pattern)
    78→
    79→    # Suffix pattern: starts with "_" → basename ends-with (_test.py, _pb2.py)
    80→    if pattern.startswith("_"):
    81→        return basename.endswith(pattern)
    82→
    83→    # Exact basename: has a proper file extension (1-5 chars after last dot),
    84→    # no "/" → exact basename match (config.py, setup.py, conftest.py)
    85→    if "/" not in pattern and "." in pattern:
    86→        ext = pattern.rsplit(".", 1)[-1]
    87→        if ext and len(ext) <= 5 and ext.isalnum():
    88→            return basename == pattern
    89→
    90→    # Fallback: substring on full path (vite.config, tsconfig, eslint, etc.)
    91→    return pattern in rel_path
    92→
    93→
    94→# ── Common zone rules (shared across languages) ──────────
    95→
    96→COMMON_ZONE_RULES = [
    97→    ZoneRule(Zone.VENDOR, ["/vendor/", "/third_party/", "/vendored/"]),
    98→    ZoneRule(Zone.GENERATED, ["/generated/", "/__generated__/"]),
    99→    ZoneRule(Zone.TEST, ["/tests/", "/test/", "/fixtures/"]),
   100→    ZoneRule(Zone.SCRIPT, ["/scripts/", "/bin/"]),
   101→]
   102→
   103→
   104→def classify_file(
   105→    rel_path: str, rules: list[ZoneRule], overrides: dict[str, str] | None = None
   106→) -> Zone:
   107→    """Classify a file by its relative path. Overrides take priority."""
   108→    if overrides:
   109→        override = overrides.get(rel_path)
   110→        if override:
   111→            try:
   112→                return Zone(override)
   113→            except ValueError as exc:
   114→                log_best_effort_failure(
   115→                    logger, f"parse zone override for {rel_path}", exc
   116→                )
   117→    for rule in rules:
   118→        for pattern in rule.patterns:
   119→            if _match_pattern(rel_path, pattern):
   120→                return rule.zone
   121→    return Zone.PRODUCTION
   122→
   123→
   124→class FileZoneMap:
   125→    """Cached zone classification for a set of files.
   126→
   127→    Built once per scan from file list + zone rules.
   128→    """
   129→
   130→    def __init__(
   131→        self,
   132→        files: list[str],
   133→        rules: list[ZoneRule],
   134→        rel_fn=None,
   135→        overrides: dict[str, str] | None = None,
   136→    ):
   137→        """Build a zone map from files, ordered rules, and optional overrides."""
   138→        self._map: dict[str, Zone] = {}
   139→        self._overrides = overrides
   140→        for f in files:
   141→            rp = rel_fn(f) if rel_fn else f
   142→            self._map[f] = classify_file(rp, rules, overrides)
   143→
   144→    def get(self, path: str) -> Zone:
   145→        """Get zone for a file path. Returns PRODUCTION if not classified."""
   146→        return self._map.get(path, Zone.PRODUCTION)
   147→
   148→    def exclude(self, files: list[str], *zones: Zone) -> list[str]:
   149→        """Return files NOT in the given zones."""
   150→        zone_set = set(zones)
   151→        return [f for f in files if self._map.get(f, Zone.PRODUCTION) not in zone_set]
   152→
   153→    def include_only(self, files: list[str], *zones: Zone) -> list[str]:
   154→        """Return files that ARE in the given zones."""
   155→        zone_set = set(zones)
   156→        return [f for f in files if self._map.get(f, Zone.PRODUCTION) in zone_set]
   157→
   158→    def counts(self) -> dict[str, int]:
   159→        """Return file count per zone."""
   160→        counts: dict[str, int] = {}
   161→        for zone in self._map.values():
   162→            counts[zone.value] = counts.get(zone.value, 0) + 1
   163→        return counts
   164→
   165→    def production_count(self) -> int:
   166→        """Count files classified as production."""
   167→        return len(self._map) - self.non_production_count()
   168→
   169→    def non_production_count(self) -> int:
   170→        """Count files in excluded zones (test/config/generated/vendor)."""
   171→        return sum(1 for z in self._map.values() if z in EXCLUDED_ZONES)
   172→
   173→    def all_files(self) -> list[str]:
   174→        """Return all classified file paths."""
   175→        return list(self._map.keys())
   176→
   177→    def items(self) -> list[tuple[str, Zone]]:
   178→        """Return all (path, zone) pairs."""
   179→        return list(self._map.items())
   180→
   181→
   182→# ── Zone detection policies ────────────────────────────────
   183→
   184→
   185→@dataclass
   186→class ZonePolicy:
   187→    """Per-zone detection policy.
   188→
   189→    skip_detectors: detectors to skip entirely for this zone.
   190→    downgrade_detectors: detectors whose confidence is downgraded to "low".
   191→    exclude_from_score: whether issues in this zone are excluded from scoring.
   192→    """
   193→
   194→    skip_detectors: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
   195→    downgrade_detectors: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
   196→    exclude_from_score: bool = False
   197→
   198→
   199→ZONE_POLICIES: dict[Zone, ZonePolicy] = {
   200→    Zone.PRODUCTION: ZonePolicy(),
   201→    Zone.TEST: ZonePolicy(
   202→        skip_detectors=TEST_SKIP_DETECTORS,
   203→        downgrade_detectors={"smells", "structural"},
   204→        exclude_from_score=True,
   205→    ),
   206→    Zone.CONFIG: ZonePolicy(
   207→        skip_detectors=CONFIG_SKIP_DETECTORS,
   208→        exclude_from_score=True,
   209→    ),
   210→    Zone.GENERATED: ZonePolicy(
   211→        skip_detectors=SKIP_ALL_DETECTORS,
   212→        exclude_from_score=True,
   213→    ),
   214→    Zone.VENDOR: ZonePolicy(
   215→        skip_detectors=SKIP_ALL_DETECTORS,
   216→        exclude_from_score=True,
   217→    ),
   218→    Zone.SCRIPT: ZonePolicy(
   219→        skip_detectors=SCRIPT_SKIP_DETECTORS,
   220→        downgrade_detectors={"structural"},
   221→    ),
   222→}
   223→
   224→
   225→# ── Helpers for phase runners ─────────────────────────────
   226→
   227→
   228→def adjust_potential(zone_map, total: int) -> int:
   229→    """Subtract non-production files from a potential count.
   230→
   231→    Uses the zone map's own file list — no need to pass files separately.
   232→    No-op if zone_map is None.
   233→    """
   234→    if zone_map is None:
   235→        return total
   236→    return max(total - zone_map.non_production_count(), 0)
   237→
   238→
   239→def should_skip_issue(zone_map, filepath: str, detector: str) -> bool:
   240→    """Check if a issue should be skipped based on zone policy.
   241→
   242→    Returns True if the file's zone policy says to skip this detector.
   243→    """
   244→    if zone_map is None:
   245→        return False
   246→    zone = zone_map.get(filepath)
   247→    policy = ZONE_POLICIES.get(zone)
   248→    return policy is not None and detector in policy.skip_detectors
   249→
   250→
   251→def filter_entries(
   252→    zone_map, entries: list[dict], detector: str, file_key: str = "file"
   253→) -> list[dict]:
   254→    """Filter detector entries by zone policy. No-op if zone_map is None.
   255→
   256→    If file_key points to a list (e.g. cycle entries with "files"), checks
   257→    the first element.
   258→    """
   259→    if zone_map is None:
   260→        return entries
   261→
   262→    def _get_path(entry):
   263→        val = entry[file_key]
   264→        return val[0] if isinstance(val, list) else val
   265→
   266→    return [
   267→        e for e in entries if not should_skip_issue(zone_map, _get_path(e), detector)
   268→    ]
   269→

   489→        result[name] = entry
   490→    return result

   317→def utc_now() -> str:
   318→    """Return current UTC timestamp with second-level precision."""
   319→    return datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds")
   320→
   321→
   322→def empty_state() -> StateModel:
   323→    """Return a new empty state payload."""
   324→    return {
   325→        "version": CURRENT_VERSION,
   326→        "created": utc_now(),
   327→        "last_scan": None,
   328→        "scan_count": 0,
   329→        "overall_score": 0,
   330→        "objective_score": 0,
   331→        "strict_score": 0,
   332→        "verified_strict_score": 0,
   333→        "stats": {},
   334→        "issues": {},
   335→        "scan_coverage": {},
   336→        "score_confidence": {},
   337→        "subjective_integrity": {},
   338→        "subjective_assessments": {},
   339→    }

   341→
   342→def _as_non_negative_int(value: Any, default: int = 0) -> int:
   343→    try:
   344→        parsed = int(value)
   345→    except (TypeError, ValueError):
   346→        return default
   347→    return parsed if parsed >= 0 else 0
   348→
   349→
   350→def _rename_key(d: dict, old: str, new: str) -> bool:
   351→    if old not in d:
   352→        return False
   353→    d.setdefault(new, d.pop(old))
   354→    return True
   355→
   356→
   357→def migrate_state_keys(state: StateModel | dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   358→    """Migrate legacy key names in-place.
   359→
   360→    - ``"findings"`` → ``"issues"``
   361→    - ``dimension_scores[dim]["issues"]`` → ``"failing"``
   362→    """
   363→    state_dict = cast(dict[str, Any], state)
   364→    _rename_key(state_dict, "findings", "issues")
   365→
   366→    for ds in state_dict.get("dimension_scores", {}).values():
   367→        if isinstance(ds, dict):
   368→            _rename_key(ds, "issues", "failing")
   369→
   370→    for entry in state_dict.get("scan_history", []):
   371→        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
   372→            continue
   373→        _rename_key(entry, "raw_findings", "raw_issues")
   374→        for ds in (entry.get("dimension_scores") or {}).values():
   375→            if isinstance(ds, dict):
   376→                _rename_key(ds, "issues", "failing")
   377→
   378→
   379→def ensure_state_defaults(state: StateModel | dict) -> None:
   380→    """Normalize loose/legacy state payloads to a valid base shape in-place."""
   381→    migrate_state_keys(state)
   382→
   383→    mutable_state = cast(dict[str, Any], state)
   384→    for key, value in empty_state().items():
   385→        mutable_state.setdefault(key, value)
   386→
   387→    if not isinstance(state.get("issues"), dict):
   388→        state["issues"] = {}
   389→    if not isinstance(state.get("stats"), dict):
   390→        state["stats"] = {}
   391→    if not isinstance(state.get("scan_history"), list):
   392→        state["scan_history"] = []
   393→    if not isinstance(state.get("scan_coverage"), dict):
   394→        state["scan_coverage"] = {}
   395→    if not isinstance(state.get("score_confidence"), dict):
   396→        state["score_confidence"] = {}
   397→    if not isinstance(state.get("subjective_integrity"), dict):
   398→        state["subjective_integrity"] = {}
   399→
   400→    all_issues = state["issues"]
   401→    to_remove: list[str] = []
   402→    for issue_id, issue in all_issues.items():
   403→        if not isinstance(issue, dict):
   404→            to_remove.append(issue_id)
   405→            continue
   406→
   407→        issue.setdefault("id", issue_id)
   408→        issue.setdefault("detector", "unknown")
   409→        issue.setdefault("file", "")
   410→        issue.setdefault("tier", 3)
   411→        issue.setdefault("confidence", "low")
   412→        issue.setdefault("summary", "")
   413→        issue.setdefault("detail", {})
   414→        issue.setdefault("status", "open")
   415→        issue["status"] = canonical_issue_status(
   416→            issue.get("status"),
   417→            default="open",
   418→        )
   419→        issue.setdefault("note", None)
   420→        issue.setdefault("first_seen", state.get("created") or utc_now())
   421→        issue.setdefault("last_seen", issue["first_seen"])
   422→        issue.setdefault("resolved_at", None)
   423→        issue["reopen_count"] = _as_non_negative_int(
   424→            issue.get("reopen_count", 0), default=0
   425→        )
   426→        issue.setdefault("suppressed", False)
   427→        issue.setdefault("suppressed_at", None)
   428→        issue.setdefault("suppression_pattern", None)
   429→
   430→    for issue_id in to_remove:
   431→        all_issues.pop(issue_id, None)
   432→
   433→    for entry in state["scan_history"]:
   434→        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
   435→            continue
   436→        integrity = entry.get("subjective_integrity")
   437→        if integrity is not None and not isinstance(integrity, dict):
   438→            entry["subjective_integrity"] = None
   439→
   440→    state["scan_count"] = _as_non_negative_int(state.get("scan_count", 0), default=0)
   441→    return None
   442→
   443→
   444→def validate_state_invariants(state: StateModel) -> None:
   445→    """Raise ValueError when core state invariants are violated."""
   446→    if not isinstance(state.get("issues"), dict):
   447→        raise ValueError("state.issues must be a dict")
   448→    if not isinstance(state.get("stats"), dict):
   449→        raise ValueError("state.stats must be a dict")
   450→
   451→    all_issues = state["issues"]
   452→    for issue_id, issue in all_issues.items():
   453→        if not isinstance(issue, dict):
   454→            raise ValueError(f"issue {issue_id!r} must be a dict")
   455→        if issue.get("id") != issue_id:
   456→            raise ValueError(f"issue id mismatch for {issue_id!r}")
   457→        if issue.get("status") not in _ALLOWED_ISSUE_STATUSES:
   458→            raise ValueError(
   459→                f"issue {issue_id!r} has invalid status {issue.get('status')!r}"
   460→            )
   461→
   462→        tier = issue.get("tier")
   463→        if not isinstance(tier, int) or tier < 1 or tier > 4:
   464→            raise ValueError(f"issue {issue_id!r} has invalid tier {tier!r}")
   465→
   466→        reopen_count = issue.get("reopen_count")
   467→        if not isinstance(reopen_count, int) or reopen_count < 0:
   468→            raise ValueError(
   469→                f"issue {issue_id!r} has invalid reopen_count {reopen_count!r}"
   470→            )
   471→

   140→def _handle_heartbeat(
   141→    *,
   142→    details: dict,
   143→    total_batches: int,
   144→    stall_warning_seconds: float,
   145→    stall_warned_batches: set[int],
   146→    append_run_log,
   147→    colorize_fn,
   148→) -> None:
   149→    """Handle a heartbeat progress event — print status and stall warnings."""
   150→    active = details.get("active_batches")
   151→    queued = details.get("queued_batches", [])
   152→    elapsed = details.get("elapsed_seconds", {})
   153→    if not isinstance(active, list):
   154→        active = []
   155→    if not isinstance(queued, list):
   156→        queued = []
   157→    if not active and not queued:
   158→        return
   159→    segments: list[str] = []
   160→    for idx in active[:6]:
   161→        secs = 0
   162→        if isinstance(elapsed, dict):
   163→            raw_secs = elapsed.get(idx, 0)
   164→            secs = int(raw_secs) if isinstance(raw_secs, int | float) else 0
   165→        segments.append(f"#{idx + 1}:{secs}s")
   166→    if len(active) > 6:
   167→        segments.append(f"+{len(active) - 6} more")
   168→    queued_segment = ""
   169→    if queued:
   170→        queued_segment = f", queued {len(queued)}"
   171→    print(
   172→        colorize_fn(
   173→            "  Batch heartbeat: "
   174→            f"{len(active)}/{total_batches} active{queued_segment} "
   175→            f"({', '.join(segments) if segments else 'running batches pending'})",
   176→            "dim",
   177→        )
   178→    )
   179→    append_run_log(
   180→        "heartbeat "
   181→        f"active={[idx + 1 for idx in active]} queued={[idx + 1 for idx in queued]} "
   182→        f"elapsed={{{', '.join(f'{idx + 1}:{elapsed.get(idx, 0)}' for idx in active)}}}"
   183→    )
   184→    if stall_warning_seconds > 0 and isinstance(elapsed, dict):
   185→        slow_active = [
   186→            idx
   187→            for idx in active
   188→            if isinstance(elapsed.get(idx), int | float)
   189→            and int(elapsed.get(idx) or 0) >= stall_warning_seconds
   190→        ]
   191→        newly_warned = [idx for idx in slow_active if idx not in stall_warned_batches]
   192→        if newly_warned:
   193→            stall_warned_batches.update(newly_warned)
   194→            warning_message = (
   195→                "  Stall warning: batches "
   196→                f"{[idx + 1 for idx in sorted(newly_warned)]} exceeded "
   197→                f"{stall_warning_seconds}s elapsed. "
   198→                "This may be normal for long runs; review run.log and batch logs."
   199→            )
   200→            print(colorize_fn(warning_message, "yellow"))
   201→            append_run_log(
   202→                "stall-warning "
   203→                f"threshold={stall_warning_seconds}s batches={[idx + 1 for idx in sorted(newly_warned)]}"
   204→            )
   205→

   207→def _collect_and_reconcile_results(
   208→    *,
   209→    collect_batch_results_fn,
   210→    selected_indexes: list[int],
   211→    execution_failures: list[int],
   212→    output_files: dict,
   213→    packet: dict,
   214→    batch_positions: dict[int, int],
   215→    batch_status: dict[str, dict[str, object]],
   216→) -> tuple[list[dict], list[int], list[int], set[int]]:
   217→    """Collect batch results and reconcile per-batch status entries.
   218→
   219→    Returns (batch_results, successful_indexes, failures, failure_set).
   220→    """
   221→    allowed_dims = {
   222→        str(dim) for dim in packet.get("dimensions", []) if isinstance(dim, str)
   223→    }
   224→    batch_results, failures = collect_batch_results_fn(
   225→        selected_indexes=selected_indexes,
   226→        failures=execution_failures,
   227→        output_files=output_files,
   228→        allowed_dims=allowed_dims,
   229→    )
   230→
   231→    execution_failure_set = set(execution_failures)
   232→    failure_set = set(failures)
   233→    successful_indexes = sorted(idx for idx in selected_indexes if idx not in failure_set)
   234→    for idx in selected_indexes:
   235→        key = str(idx + 1)
   236→        state = batch_status.setdefault(
   237→            key,
   238→            {"position": batch_positions.get(idx, 0), "status": "pending"},
   239→        )
   240→        if idx not in failure_set:
   241→            state["status"] = "succeeded"
   242→            continue
   243→        if idx in execution_failure_set:
   244→            state["status"] = "failed"
   245→            continue
   246→        if not output_files[idx].exists():
   247→            state["status"] = "missing_output"
   248→            continue
   249→        state["status"] = "parse_failed"
   250→
   251→    return batch_results, successful_indexes, failures, failure_set
   252→

   255→    *,

   257→    build_import_provenance_fn,

   101→    4. Lifecycle — filter endgame-only items when objective work remains

   152→def _resolve_inputs(

   155→    """Resolve plan, scan_path, status, and subjective threshold from options."""
   156→    ctx = opts.context
   157→    plan = ctx.plan if ctx is not None else opts.plan

   160→        state.get("scan_path")

   165→    status = opts.status
   166→    if status not in ALL_STATUSES:

   168→
   169→    try:
   170→        threshold = float(opts.subjective_threshold)
   171→    except (TypeError, ValueError):
   172→        threshold = 100.0
   173→    threshold = max(0.0, min(100.0, threshold))

   175→    return plan, scan_path, status, threshold

   243→def _plan_postsort(
   244→    items: list[WorkQueueItem],
   245→    skipped: list[WorkQueueItem],
   246→    plan: dict | None,
   247→    opts: QueueBuildOptions,
   248→) -> None:
   249→    """Re-append skipped items, stamp positions, filter to cluster focus."""
   250→    if not plan:

   253→    if opts.include_skipped:
   254→        items.extend(skipped)

   260→def _has_objective_items(items: list[WorkQueueItem]) -> bool:
   261→    """True if any objective mechanical work items remain in the queue."""
   262→    return any(

   264→        and i.get("detector", "") not in NON_OBJECTIVE_DETECTORS
   265→        for i in items
   266→    )
   267→
   268→

   270→    """True if any unassessed subjective dimensions need initial review."""
   271→    return any(

   273→        and i.get("initial_review")
   274→        for i in items
   275→    )
   276→
   277→

   279→    """True if this item should only appear when the objective queue is drained."""
   280→    return (
   281→        item.get("kind") == "subjective_dimension"
   282→        and not item.get("initial_review")
   283→    )
   284→
   285→
   286→def _has_triage_stages(items: list[WorkQueueItem]) -> bool:
   287→    """True if any pending triage stage items are in the queue."""
   288→    return any(
   289→        i.get("kind") == "workflow_stage"
   290→        and str(i.get("id", "")).startswith("triage::")
   291→        for i in items
   292→    )
   293→
   294→
   295→def _apply_lifecycle_filter(items: list[WorkQueueItem]) -> list[WorkQueueItem]:
   296→    """Enforce lifecycle visibility rules.
   297→
   298→    The queue enforces a phase order: scan → initial review → triage → objective work.
   299→
   300→    1. **Initial reviews pending** → only show initial-review subjective items.
   301→       The user must complete first-time reviews before working objective items.
   302→    2. **Triage in progress** → only show triage stages and workflow items.
   303→       Cluster work items aren't ready until triage completes (enrich adds
   304→       the detail that makes steps actionable).
   305→    3. **Objective work remains** → show objective items, hide endgame-only
   306→       subjective reassessments (stale re-reviews).
   307→    4. **Objective drained** → everything visible (endgame).
   308→    """
   309→    if _has_initial_reviews(items):
   310→        # Phase 1: only initial reviews visible — triage and workflow
   311→        # items stay hidden until initial reviews are complete.
   312→        return [
   313→            i for i in items
   314→            if i.get("kind") == "subjective_dimension" and i.get("initial_review")
   315→        ]
   316→    if _has_triage_stages(items):
   317→        # Phase 2: triage in progress — only triage stages and workflow items visible.
   318→        # Cluster work items aren't ready until enrich completes.
   319→        return [
   320→            i for i in items
   321→            if i.get("kind") in ("workflow_stage", "workflow_action")
   322→        ]
   323→    if not _has_objective_items(items):
   324→        return items  # endgame: everything visible
   325→    return [i for i in items if not _is_endgame_only(i)]

   339→        "primary_command": "desloppify scan",

   130→        for f in state.get("issues", {}).values()
   131→    )
   132→
   133→
   134→def _prune_subjective_ids(
   135→    order: list[str],
   136→    *,
   137→    keep_ids: set[str],
   138→    pruned: list[str],
   139→) -> None:
   140→    """Remove subjective IDs from *order* that are not in *keep_ids*, appending removed to *pruned*."""
   141→    to_remove = [
   142→        fid for fid in order
   143→        if fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX)
   144→        and fid not in keep_ids
   145→    ]
   146→    for fid in to_remove:
   147→        order.remove(fid)
   148→        pruned.append(fid)
   149→
   150→
   151→def _inject_subjective_ids(
   152→    order: list[str],
   153→    plan: PlanModel,
   154→    *,
   155→    inject_ids: set[str],
   156→    to_front: bool,
   157→    injected: list[str],
   158→) -> None:
   159→    """Inject subjective IDs into *order* if not already present.
   160→
   161→    When *to_front* is True, inserts after promoted items (front of queue).
   162→    Otherwise appends to the back.
   163→    """
   164→    existing = set(order)
   165→    if to_front:
   166→        insert_at = promoted_insertion_index(order, plan)
   167→        for sid in reversed(sorted(inject_ids)):
   168→            if sid not in existing:
   169→                order.insert(insert_at, sid)
   170→                injected.append(sid)
   171→    else:
   172→        for sid in sorted(inject_ids):
   173→            if sid not in existing:
   174→                order.append(sid)
   175→                injected.append(sid)
   176→
   177→
   178→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   179→# Helpers for sync_triage_needed
   180→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   181→
   182→def _open_review_issue_ids(state: StateModel) -> set[str]:
   183→    """Return set of open issue IDs whose detector is 'review' or 'concerns'."""
   184→    issues = state.get("issues", {})
   185→    return {
   186→        fid for fid, f in issues.items()
   187→        if f.get("status") == "open"
   188→        and f.get("detector") in ("review", "concerns")
   189→    }
   190→
   191→
   192→def _new_review_ids_since_triage(
   193→    state: StateModel,
   194→    meta: dict,
   195→) -> set[str]:
   196→    """Return review issue IDs that are new since the last triage."""
   197→    current_review_ids = _open_review_issue_ids(state)
   198→    triaged_ids = set(meta.get("triaged_ids", []))
   199→    return current_review_ids - triaged_ids
   200→
   201→
   202→def _prune_all_triage_stages(order: list[str]) -> None:
   203→    """Remove all ``triage::*`` stage IDs from *order*."""
   204→    for sid in TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS:
   205→        while sid in order:
   206→            order.remove(sid)
   207→
   208→
   209→def _inject_pending_triage_stages(
   210→    order: list[str],
   211→    plan: PlanModel,
   212→    confirmed: set[str],
   213→) -> bool:
   214→    """Inject triage stages for pending (unconfirmed) items.
   215→
   216→    Returns True if any stages were injected.
   217→    """
   218→    insert_at = promoted_insertion_index(order, plan)
   219→    stage_names = ("observe", "reflect", "organize", "enrich", "sense-check", "commit")
   220→    existing = set(order)
   221→    injected_count = 0
   222→    for sid, name in zip(TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS, stage_names, strict=False):
   223→        if name not in confirmed and sid not in existing:
   224→            order.insert(insert_at + injected_count, sid)
   225→            injected_count += 1
   226→    return injected_count > 0
   227→
   228→
   229→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   230→# Unscored dimension sync (front of queue, unconditional)
   231→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   232→
   233→def sync_unscored_dimensions(
   234→    plan: PlanModel,
   235→    state: StateModel,
   236→) -> UnscoredDimensionSyncResult:
   237→    """Keep the plan queue in sync with unscored (placeholder) subjective dimensions.
   238→
   239→    1. **Prune** — remove ``subjective::*`` IDs from ``queue_order`` that are
   240→       no longer unscored AND not stale (avoids pruning stale IDs — that is
   241→       ``sync_stale_dimensions``' responsibility).
   242→    2. **Inject** — unconditionally prepend currently-unscored IDs to the
   243→       *front* of ``queue_order`` so initial reviews are the first priority.
   244→    """
   245→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   246→    result = UnscoredDimensionSyncResult()
   247→
   248→    # Mid-cycle: don't inject unscored dimensions — they'll surface at cycle end.
   249→    if plan.get("plan_start_scores"):
   250→        return result
   251→
   252→    unscored_ids = current_unscored_ids(state)
   253→    stale_ids = _current_stale_ids(state)
   254→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   255→
   256→    # --- Cleanup: prune subjective IDs that are no longer unscored --------
   257→    # Only prune IDs that are neither unscored nor stale (stale sync owns those).
   258→    _prune_subjective_ids(order, keep_ids=unscored_ids | stale_ids, pruned=result.pruned)
   259→
   260→    # --- Inject: prepend unscored IDs after any promoted items -------------
   261→    _inject_subjective_ids(order, plan, inject_ids=unscored_ids, to_front=True, injected=result.injected)
   262→
   263→    return result
   264→
   265→
   266→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   267→# Stale dimension sync (back of queue, conditional)
   268→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   269→
   270→def sync_stale_dimensions(
   271→    plan: PlanModel,
   272→    state: StateModel,
   273→    *,
   274→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility | None = None,
   275→    cycle_just_completed: bool = False,
   276→) -> StaleDimensionSyncResult:
   277→    """Keep the plan queue in sync with stale and under-target subjective dimensions.
   278→
   279→    1. Remove any ``subjective::*`` IDs from ``queue_order`` that are no
   280→       longer stale/under-target and not unscored (avoids pruning IDs owned
   281→       by ``sync_unscored_dimensions``).
   282→    2. Inject stale and under-target dimension IDs when either:
   283→       a. No objective items remain (mid-cycle: append to back), OR
   284→       b. A cycle just completed (post-cycle: insert at front so subjective
   285→          review takes priority over new objective issues).
   286→    """
   287→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   288→    result = StaleDimensionSyncResult()
   289→    stale_ids = _current_stale_ids(state)
   290→    under_target_ids = current_under_target_ids(state)
   291→    injectable_ids = stale_ids | under_target_ids
   292→    unscored_ids = current_unscored_ids(state)
   293→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   294→
   295→    # --- Cleanup: prune resolved subjective IDs --------------------------
   296→    # Only prune IDs that are no longer injectable and not unscored.
   297→    _prune_subjective_ids(order, keep_ids=injectable_ids | unscored_ids, pruned=result.pruned)
   298→
   299→    # --- Inject or evict stale + under-target dimensions -----------------
   300→    has_real_items = _has_objective_backlog(state, policy)
   301→    should_inject = not has_real_items or cycle_just_completed
   302→
   303→    if not should_inject:
   304→        # Mid-cycle with objective backlog: evict any stale/under-target IDs
   305→        # that are present in the queue.  They may have been grandfathered from
   306→        # the unscored phase and should not be visible until the objective
   307→        # backlog clears or a cycle completes.
   308→        to_evict = [
   309→            fid for fid in order
   310→            if fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX)
   311→            and fid in injectable_ids
   312→        ]
   313→        for fid in to_evict:
   314→            order.remove(fid)
   315→            result.pruned.append(fid)
   316→
   317→    if should_inject and injectable_ids:
   318→        to_front = cycle_just_completed and has_real_items
   319→        _inject_subjective_ids(order, plan, inject_ids=injectable_ids, to_front=to_front, injected=result.injected)
   320→
   321→    return result
   322→
   323→
   324→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   325→# Triage snapshot hash + sync
   326→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   327→
   328→def review_issue_snapshot_hash(state: StateModel) -> str:
   329→    """Hash open review issue IDs to detect changes.
   330→
   331→    Returns empty string when there are no open review issues.
   332→    """
   333→    return stale_policy_mod.review_issue_snapshot_hash(state)
   334→
   335→
   336→@dataclass
   337→class TriageSyncResult:
   338→    """What changed during a triage sync."""
   339→
   340→    injected: bool = False
   341→    pruned: bool = False
   342→
   343→    @property
   344→    def changes(self) -> int:
   345→        return int(self.injected) + int(self.pruned)
   346→
   347→
   348→def sync_triage_needed(
   349→    plan: PlanModel,
   350→    state: StateModel,
   351→) -> TriageSyncResult:
   352→    """Inject 4 triage stage IDs at front of queue when review issues change.
   353→
   354→    Only injects stages not already confirmed in ``epic_triage_meta``.
   355→
   356→    When stages are already present but all new issues have been resolved
   357→    since injection, auto-prunes the stale stages and updates the hash.
   358→
   359→    When issues are *resolved* (current IDs are a subset of previously
   360→    triaged IDs), the snapshot hash is updated silently — no re-triage
   361→    is needed since the user is working through the plan.
   362→    """
   363→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   364→    result = TriageSyncResult()
   365→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   366→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   367→    confirmed = set(meta.get("triage_stages", {}).keys())
   368→
   369→    # Check if any triage stage is already in queue
   370→    already_present = any(sid in order for sid in TRIAGE_IDS)
   371→
   372→    current_hash = review_issue_snapshot_hash(state)
   373→    last_hash = meta.get("issue_snapshot_hash", "")
   374→
   375→    if already_present:
   376→        # Stages present — check if the reason for injection still applies.
   377→        # Only auto-prune when triage was completed before (hash exists),
   378→        # all new issues have been resolved, and no triage work is in
   379→        # progress.  This avoids pruning the initial triage or a
   380→        # user-started triage session.
   381→        if last_hash and not confirmed:
   382→            new_since_triage = _new_review_ids_since_triage(state, meta)
   383→
   384→            if not new_since_triage:
   385→                # No new issues remain — prune stale stages
   386→                _prune_all_triage_stages(order)
   387→                if current_hash:
   388→                    meta["issue_snapshot_hash"] = current_hash
   389→                    plan["epic_triage_meta"] = meta
   390→                result.pruned = True
   391→        return result
   392→
   393→    if current_hash and current_hash != last_hash:
   394→        # Distinguish "new issues appeared" from "issues were resolved".
   395→        # Only re-triage when genuinely new issues exist.
   396→        new_since_triage = _new_review_ids_since_triage(state, meta)
   397→
   398→        if new_since_triage:
   399→            # New review issues appeared — re-triage needed
   400→            result.injected = _inject_pending_triage_stages(order, plan, confirmed)
   401→        else:
   402→            # Only resolved issues changed the hash — update silently
   403→            meta["issue_snapshot_hash"] = current_hash
   404→            plan["epic_triage_meta"] = meta
   405→
   406→    return result
   407→
   408→
   409→@dataclass
   410→class ScoreCheckpointSyncResult:
   411→    """What changed during a score-checkpoint sync."""
   412→
   413→    injected: bool = False
   414→
   415→    @property
   416→    def changes(self) -> int:
   417→        return int(self.injected)
   418→
   419→
   420→def sync_score_checkpoint_needed(
   421→    plan: PlanModel,
   422→    state: StateModel,
   423→    *,
   424→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility | None = None,
   425→) -> ScoreCheckpointSyncResult:
   426→    """Inject ``workflow::score-checkpoint`` when all initial reviews complete.
   427→
   428→    Injects when:
   429→    - No unscored (placeholder) subjective dimensions remain
   430→    - ``workflow::score-checkpoint`` is not already in the queue
   431→
   432→    Positioned after subjective items but before triage/create-plan
   433→    so the user sees their updated strict score right after reviews finish.
   434→    """
   435→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   436→    result = ScoreCheckpointSyncResult()
   437→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   438→
   439→    if WORKFLOW_SCORE_CHECKPOINT_ID in order:
   440→        return result
   441→
   442→    # Check that no unscored dimensions remain
   443→    if policy is not None:
   444→        if policy.unscored_ids:
   445→            return result
   446→    else:
   447→        unscored = current_unscored_ids(state)
   448→        if unscored:
   449→            return result
   450→
   451→    # Insert after any subjective items, before triage/workflow/issues
   452→    insert_at = 0
   453→    for i, fid in enumerate(order):
   454→        if fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX):
   455→            insert_at = i + 1
   456→    order.insert(insert_at, WORKFLOW_SCORE_CHECKPOINT_ID)
   457→    result.injected = True
   458→    return result

   461→@dataclass
   462→class CreatePlanSyncResult:
   463→    """What changed during a create-plan sync."""
   464→
   465→    injected: bool = False
   466→
   467→    @property
   468→    def changes(self) -> int:
   469→        return int(self.injected)
   470→
   471→
   472→def sync_create_plan_needed(
   473→    plan: PlanModel,
   474→    state: StateModel,
   475→    *,
   476→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility | None = None,
   477→) -> CreatePlanSyncResult:
   478→    """Inject ``workflow::create-plan`` when reviews complete + objective backlog exists.
   479→
   480→    Only injects when:
   481→    - No unscored (placeholder) subjective dimensions remain
   482→    - At least one objective issue exists
   483→    - ``workflow::create-plan`` is not already in the queue
   484→    - No triage stages are pending
   485→    """
   486→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   487→    result = CreatePlanSyncResult()
   488→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   489→
   490→    if WORKFLOW_CREATE_PLAN_ID in order:
   491→        return result
   492→
   493→    # Don't inject if triage stages are pending
   494→    if any(sid in order for sid in TRIAGE_IDS):
   495→        return result
   496→
   497→    # Check that no unscored dimensions remain
   498→    if policy is not None:
   499→        if policy.unscored_ids:
   500→            return result
   501→        has_objective = policy.has_objective_backlog
   502→    else:
   503→        unscored = current_unscored_ids(state)
   504→        if unscored:
   505→            return result
   506→        issues = state.get("issues", {})
   507→        has_objective = any(
   508→            f.get("status") == "open"
   509→            and f.get("detector") not in _NON_OBJECTIVE_DETECTORS
   510→            for f in issues.values()
   511→        )
   512→    if not has_objective:
   513→        return result
   514→
   515→    # Insert after any subjective/workflow items, at the end of the
   516→    # synthetic block (so create-plan comes after score-checkpoint).
   517→    insert_at = 0
   518→    for i, fid in enumerate(order):
   519→        if fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX) or fid.startswith(TRIAGE_PREFIX) or fid.startswith(WORKFLOW_PREFIX):
   520→            insert_at = i + 1
   521→    order.insert(insert_at, WORKFLOW_CREATE_PLAN_ID)
   522→    result.injected = True
   523→    return result

   534→def is_triage_stale(plan: PlanModel, state: StateModel) -> bool:
   535→    """Side-effect-free check: is triage needed?
   536→
   537→    Returns True when genuinely *new* review issues appeared since the
   538→    last triage.  Triage stage IDs being in the queue alone is not
   539→    sufficient — the new issues that triggered injection may have been
   540→    resolved since then.
   541→
   542→    When issues are merely resolved (current IDs are a subset of
   543→    previously triaged IDs), triage is NOT stale — the user is working
   544→    through the plan.
   545→    """
   546→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   547→    return stale_policy_mod.is_triage_stale(plan, state, triage_ids=TRIAGE_IDS)

   568→
   569→    Only injects when:
   570→    - Assessment mode was ``issues_only`` (scores were skipped)
   571→    - ``workflow::import-scores`` is not already in the queue
   572→    - There are assessments in the payload that could be imported
   573→
   574→    Positioned after score-checkpoint, before create-plan.
   575→    """

   580→    if WORKFLOW_IMPORT_SCORES_ID in order:
   581→        return result
   582→
   583→    # Only inject when scores were skipped (issues-only mode)
   584→    if assessment_mode != "issues_only":
   585→        return result
   586→
   587→    # Insert after any subjective/workflow items
   588→    insert_at = 0
   589→    for i, fid in enumerate(order):
   590→        if fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX) or fid.startswith(WORKFLOW_PREFIX):
   591→            insert_at = i + 1
   592→    order.insert(insert_at, WORKFLOW_IMPORT_SCORES_ID)

   597→@dataclass
   598→class CommunicateScoreSyncResult:

   601→    injected: bool = False
   602→
   603→    @property
   604→    def changes(self) -> int:

   606→
   607→
   608→def sync_communicate_score_needed(
   609→    plan: PlanModel,
   610→    state: StateModel,
   611→    *,
   612→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility | None = None,
   613→    scores_just_imported: bool = False,
   614→) -> CommunicateScoreSyncResult:
   615→    """Inject ``workflow::communicate-score`` when scores should be shown.
   616→
   617→    Injects when either:
   618→    - All initial subjective reviews are complete (no unscored dimensions), OR
   619→    - Scores were just imported (trusted/attested/override)
   620→
   621→    And ``workflow::communicate-score`` is not already in the queue.
   622→    Positioned after subjective items but before triage/create-plan.
   623→    """
   624→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   625→    result = CommunicateScoreSyncResult()
   626→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   627→
   628→    # Also treat legacy score-checkpoint as already-present
   629→    if WORKFLOW_COMMUNICATE_SCORE_ID in order or WORKFLOW_SCORE_CHECKPOINT_ID in order:
   630→        return result
   631→
   632→    # Trigger 1: scores just imported
   633→    should_inject = scores_just_imported
   634→
   635→    # Trigger 2: all initial reviews complete (no unscored dimensions)
   636→    if not should_inject:
   637→        if policy is not None:
   638→            should_inject = not policy.unscored_ids
   639→        else:
   640→            should_inject = not current_unscored_ids(state)
   641→
   642→    if not should_inject:
   643→        return result
   644→
   645→    # Insert after any subjective items, before triage/workflow/issues
   646→    insert_at = 0
   647→    for i, fid in enumerate(order):
   648→        if fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX):
   649→            insert_at = i + 1
   650→    order.insert(insert_at, WORKFLOW_COMMUNICATE_SCORE_ID)
   651→    result.injected = True
   652→    return result

    10→    SUBJECTIVE_DIMENSION_WEIGHTS,
    11→    SUBJECTIVE_WEIGHT_FRACTION,
    12→)
    13→
    14→
    15→def _normalize_dimension_name(name: str) -> str:
    16→    return " ".join(str(name).strip().lower().split())
    17→
    18→
    19→def _mechanical_dimension_weight(name: str) -> float:
    20→    return float(
    21→        MECHANICAL_DIMENSION_WEIGHTS.get(
    22→            _normalize_dimension_name(name),
    23→            1.0,
    24→        )
    25→    )
    26→
    27→
    28→def _subjective_dimension_weight(name: str, data: dict) -> float:
    29→    subjective_meta = (
    30→        data.get("detectors", {}).get("subjective_assessment", {})
    31→        if isinstance(data, dict)
    32→        else {}
    33→    )
    34→    configured = (
    35→        subjective_meta.get("configured_weight")
    36→        if isinstance(subjective_meta, dict)
    37→        else None
    38→    )
    39→    if is_numeric(configured):
    40→        return max(0.0, float(configured))
    41→
    42→    return float(
    43→        SUBJECTIVE_DIMENSION_WEIGHTS.get(
    44→            _normalize_dimension_name(name),
    45→            1.0,
    46→        )
    47→    )
    48→
    49→
    50→def compute_health_breakdown(
    51→    dimension_scores: dict,
    52→    *,
    53→    score_key: str = "score",
    54→) -> dict[str, object]:
    55→    """Return pool averages and weighted contribution breakdown for score transparency."""
    56→    if not dimension_scores:
    57→        return {
    58→            "overall_score": 100.0,
    59→            "mechanical_fraction": 1.0,
    60→            "subjective_fraction": 0.0,
    61→            "mechanical_avg": 100.0,
    62→            "subjective_avg": None,
    63→            "entries": [],
    64→        }
    65→
    66→    mech_sum = 0.0
    67→    mech_weight = 0.0
    68→    subj_sum = 0.0
    69→    subj_weight = 0.0
    70→    mechanical_rows: list[dict[str, float | str]] = []
    71→    subjective_rows: list[dict[str, float | str]] = []
    72→
    73→    for name, data in dimension_scores.items():
    74→        score = float(data.get(score_key, data.get("score", 0.0)))
    75→        is_subjective = "subjective_assessment" in data.get("detectors", {})
    76→        if is_subjective:
    77→            configured = max(0.0, _subjective_dimension_weight(name, data))
    78→            effective = configured
    79→            subj_sum += score * effective
    80→            subj_weight += effective
    81→            subjective_rows.append(
    82→                {
    83→                    "name": str(name),
    84→                    "score": score,
    85→                    "configured_weight": configured,
    86→                    "effective_weight": effective,
    87→                }
    88→            )
    89→            continue
    90→
    91→        checks = float(data.get("checks", 0) or 0)
    92→        sample_factor = min(1.0, checks / MIN_SAMPLE) if checks > 0 else 0.0
    93→        configured = max(0.0, _mechanical_dimension_weight(name))
    94→        effective = configured * sample_factor
    95→        mech_sum += score * effective
    96→        mech_weight += effective
    97→        mechanical_rows.append(
    98→            {
    99→                "name": str(name),
   100→                "score": score,
   101→                "checks": checks,
   102→                "sample_factor": sample_factor,
   103→                "configured_weight": configured,
   104→                "effective_weight": effective,
   105→            }
   106→        )
   107→
   108→    mech_avg = (mech_sum / mech_weight) if mech_weight > 0 else 100.0
   109→    subj_avg = (subj_sum / subj_weight) if subj_weight > 0 else None
   110→
   111→    if subj_avg is None:
   112→        mechanical_fraction = 1.0
   113→        subjective_fraction = 0.0
   114→        overall_score = round(mech_avg, 1)
   115→    elif mech_weight == 0:
   116→        mechanical_fraction = 0.0
   117→        subjective_fraction = 1.0
   118→        overall_score = round(subj_avg, 1)
   119→    else:
   120→        mechanical_fraction = MECHANICAL_WEIGHT_FRACTION
   121→        subjective_fraction = SUBJECTIVE_WEIGHT_FRACTION
   122→        overall_score = round(
   123→            mech_avg * mechanical_fraction + subj_avg * subjective_fraction,
   124→            1,
   125→        )
   126→
   127→    entries: list[dict[str, float | str]] = []
   128→    for row in mechanical_rows:
   129→        pool_share = (
   130→            float(row["effective_weight"]) / mech_weight if mech_weight > 0 else 0.0
   131→        )
   132→        per_point = mechanical_fraction * pool_share
   133→        score = float(row["score"])
   134→        entries.append(
   135→            {
   136→                "name": str(row["name"]),
   137→                "pool": "mechanical",
   138→                "score": score,
   139→                "checks": float(row["checks"]),
   140→                "sample_factor": float(row["sample_factor"]),
   141→                "configured_weight": float(row["configured_weight"]),
   142→                "effective_weight": float(row["effective_weight"]),
   143→                "pool_share": pool_share,
   144→                "overall_per_point": per_point,
   145→                "overall_contribution": per_point * score,
   146→                "overall_drag": per_point * (100.0 - score),
   147→            }
   148→        )
   149→
   150→    for row in subjective_rows:
   151→        pool_share = (
   152→            float(row["effective_weight"]) / subj_weight if subj_weight > 0 else 0.0
   153→        )
   154→        per_point = subjective_fraction * pool_share
   155→        score = float(row["score"])
   156→        entries.append(
   157→            {
   158→                "name": str(row["name"]),
   159→                "pool": "subjective",
   160→                "score": score,
   161→                "checks": 0.0,
   162→                "sample_factor": 1.0,
   163→                "configured_weight": float(row["configured_weight"]),
   164→                "effective_weight": float(row["effective_weight"]),
   165→                "pool_share": pool_share,
   166→                "overall_per_point": per_point,
   167→                "overall_contribution": per_point * score,
   168→                "overall_drag": per_point * (100.0 - score),
   169→            }
   170→        )
   171→
   172→    return {
   173→        "overall_score": overall_score,
   174→        "mechanical_fraction": mechanical_fraction,
   175→        "subjective_fraction": subjective_fraction,
   176→        "mechanical_avg": mech_avg,
   177→        "subjective_avg": subj_avg,
   178→        "entries": entries,
   179→    }
   180→
   181→
   182→def compute_health_score(
   183→    dimension_scores: dict,
   184→    *,
   185→    score_key: str = "score",
   186→) -> float:
   187→    """Budget-weighted blend of mechanical and subjective dimension scores."""
   188→    return float(
   189→        compute_health_breakdown(dimension_scores, score_key=score_key)[
   190→            "overall_score"
   191→        ]
   192→    )
   193→
   194→
   195→__all__ = ["compute_health_breakdown", "compute_health_score"]
   196→
   197→

    75→def _apply_persisted_exclusions(args, config: dict):

    77→    cli_exclusions = getattr(args, "exclude", None) or []
    78→    persisted = config.get("exclude", [])

   106→    runtime_root = get_project_root()
   107→    if getattr(args, "command", None) == "review":
   108→        try:

   110→            if state_file:
   111→                saved = load_state(state_file)
   112→                saved_path = saved.get("scan_path")
   113→                if saved_path:
   114→                    args.path = str((runtime_root / saved_path).resolve())
   115→                    return
   116→        except (OSError, KeyError, ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError) as exc:
   117→            log_best_effort_failure(logger, "resolve default review path from saved state", exc)
   118→    lang = resolve_lang(args)
   119→    if lang:

   130→    state = load_state(state_file)
   131→    _apply_persisted_exclusions(args, config)

   151→    for stream in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr):

   154→                stream.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
   155→            except (AttributeError, OSError):

    13→def _is_test_file(filepath: str) -> bool:

    15→    normalized = filepath.replace("\\", "/")

    18→
    19→def _detect_monster_functions(filepath: str, node: ast.AST) -> list[dict]:
    20→    """Flag functions longer than 150 LOC."""
    21→    if not (hasattr(node, "end_lineno") and node.end_lineno):
    22→        return []
    23→    loc = node.end_lineno - node.lineno + 1
    24→    if loc > 150:
    25→        return [
    26→            {
    27→                "file": filepath,
    28→                "line": node.lineno,
    29→                "content": f"{node.name}() — {loc} LOC",
    30→            }
    31→        ]
    32→    return []
    33→
    34→
    35→def _detect_dead_functions(filepath: str, node: ast.AST) -> list[dict]:
    36→    """Flag functions whose body is only pass, return, or return None."""
    37→    if node.decorator_list:

    39→    body = node.body
    40→    if len(body) == 1:
    41→        stmt = body[0]
    42→        if isinstance(stmt, ast.Pass) or _is_return_none(stmt):
    43→            return [
    44→                {
    45→                    "file": filepath,
    46→                    "line": node.lineno,
    47→                    "content": f"{node.name}() — body is only {ast.dump(stmt)[:40]}",
    48→                }
    49→            ]
    50→    elif len(body) == 2:
    51→        first, second = body
    52→        if not _is_docstring(first):
    53→            return []
    54→        if isinstance(second, ast.Pass):
    55→            desc = "docstring + pass"
    56→        elif _is_return_none(second):
    57→            desc = "docstring + return None"
    58→        else:
    59→            return []
    60→        return [
    61→            {
    62→                "file": filepath,
    63→                "line": node.lineno,
    64→                "content": f"{node.name}() — {desc}",
    65→            }
    66→        ]
    67→    return []
    68→
    69→
    70→def _detect_deferred_imports(filepath: str, node: ast.AST) -> list[dict]:
    71→    """Flag function-level imports (possible circular import workarounds)."""
    72→    if _is_test_file(filepath):
    73→        return []
    74→    _SKIP_MODULES = ("typing", "typing_extensions", "__future__")
    75→    for child in ast.walk(node):
    76→        if (
    77→            not isinstance(child, ast.Import | ast.ImportFrom)
    78→            or child.lineno <= node.lineno
    79→        ):
    80→            continue
    81→        module = getattr(child, "module", None) or ""
    82→        if module in _SKIP_MODULES:
    83→            continue
    84→        names = ", ".join(a.name for a in child.names[:3])
    85→        if len(child.names) > 3:
    86→            names += f", +{len(child.names) - 3}"
    87→        return [
    88→            {
    89→                "file": filepath,
    90→                "line": child.lineno,
    91→                "content": f"import {module or names} inside {node.name}()",
    92→            }
    93→        ]
    94→    return []
    95→
    96→
    97→def _detect_inline_classes(filepath: str, node: ast.AST) -> list[dict]:
    98→    """Flag classes defined inside functions."""
    99→    results: list[dict] = []
   100→    for child in node.body:
   101→        if isinstance(child, ast.ClassDef):
   102→            results.append(
   103→                {
   104→                    "file": filepath,
   105→                    "line": child.lineno,
   106→                    "content": f"class {child.name} defined inside {node.name}()",
   107→                }
   108→            )
   109→    return results
   110→
   111→
   112→_FUNC_TYPES = (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef, ast.Lambda)
   113→_BLOCK_ATTRS = ("body", "handlers", "orelse", "finalbody")
   114→
   115→
   116→def _walk_inner_defs(
   117→    body: list[ast.AST], depth: int, inner_defs: list[ast.AST],
   118→) -> int:
   119→    """Recursively collect inner function/lambda defs and return max nesting depth."""
   120→    max_depth = 0
   121→    for child in body:
   122→        if isinstance(child, _FUNC_TYPES):
   123→            inner_defs.append(child)
   124→            current_depth = depth + 1
   125→            max_depth = max(max_depth, current_depth)
   126→            child_body = getattr(child, "body", None)
   127→            if isinstance(child_body, list):
   128→                max_depth = max(
   129→                    max_depth,
   130→                    _walk_inner_defs(child_body, current_depth, inner_defs),
   131→                )
   132→            elif isinstance(child, ast.Lambda):
   133→                max_depth = max(
   134→                    max_depth,
   135→                    _collect_nested_lambdas(child, current_depth, inner_defs),
   136→                )
   137→        else:
   138→            for attr in _BLOCK_ATTRS:
   139→                sub_body = getattr(child, attr, None)
   140→                if isinstance(sub_body, list):
   141→                    max_depth = max(
   142→                        max_depth, _walk_inner_defs(sub_body, depth, inner_defs),
   143→                    )
   144→    return max_depth
   145→
   146→
   147→def _collect_nested_lambdas(
   148→    parent: ast.Lambda, depth: int, inner_defs: list[ast.AST],
   149→) -> int:
   150→    """Walk a lambda's expression body for nested lambdas."""
   151→    max_depth = depth
   152→    for sub in ast.walk(parent.body):
   153→        if isinstance(sub, ast.Lambda) and sub is not parent:
   154→            inner_defs.append(sub)
   155→            max_depth = max(max_depth, depth + 1)
   156→    return max_depth
   157→
   158→
   159→def _format_inner_def_names(inner_defs: list[ast.AST]) -> str:
   160→    """Format inner def names for the issue content string."""
   161→    names = [
   162→        getattr(d, "name", "<lambda>")
   163→        for d in inner_defs[:5]
   164→        if isinstance(d, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef)
   165→    ]
   166→    names_str = ", ".join(names) if names else "<lambdas>"
   167→    if len(inner_defs) > 5:
   168→        names_str += ", ..."
   169→    return names_str
   170→
   171→
   172→def _detect_nested_closures(filepath: str, node: ast.AST) -> list[dict]:
   173→    """Flag functions with deeply nested inner defs or too many inner defs total."""
   174→    inner_defs: list[ast.AST] = []
   175→    max_depth = _walk_inner_defs(node.body, 0, inner_defs)
   176→
   177→    if max_depth < 2 and len(inner_defs) < 3:
   178→        return []
   179→    return [
   180→        {
   181→            "file": filepath,
   182→            "line": node.lineno,
   183→            "content": (
   184→                f"{node.name}() — {len(inner_defs)} inner defs"
   185→                f" (depth {max_depth}): {_format_inner_def_names(inner_defs)}"
   186→            ),
   187→        }
   188→    ]
   189→
   190→
   191→def _collect_single_list_assignments(body: list[ast.AST]) -> dict[str, int]:
   192→    """Return {name: lineno} for `x = [single_value]` assignments."""
   193→    result: dict[str, int] = {}
   194→    for stmt in body:
   195→        if not isinstance(stmt, ast.Assign) or len(stmt.targets) != 1:
   196→            continue
   197→        target = stmt.targets[0]
   198→        if (
   199→            isinstance(target, ast.Name)
   200→            and isinstance(stmt.value, ast.List)
   201→            and len(stmt.value.elts) == 1
   202→        ):
   203→            result[target.id] = stmt.lineno
   204→    return result
   205→
   206→
   207→def _find_subscript_zero_refs(
   208→    node: ast.AST, candidate_names: set[str],
   209→) -> set[str]:
   210→    """Find names from candidate_names accessed as x[0] inside nested functions."""
   211→    used: set[str] = set()
   212→    for child in ast.walk(node):
   213→        if child is node or not isinstance(child, _FUNC_TYPES):
   214→            continue
   215→        for sub in ast.walk(child):
   216→            if not isinstance(sub, ast.Subscript):
   217→                continue
   218→            if not isinstance(sub.value, ast.Name):
   219→                continue
   220→            if sub.value.id not in candidate_names:
   221→                continue
   222→            if isinstance(sub.slice, ast.Constant) and sub.slice.value == 0:
   223→                used.add(sub.value.id)
   224→    return used
   225→
   226→
   227→def _detect_mutable_ref_hack(filepath: str, node: ast.AST) -> list[dict]:
   228→    """Flag mutable-list-as-ref hacks: x = [value] then x[0] inside a nested function."""
   229→    single_list_names = _collect_single_list_assignments(node.body)
   230→    if not single_list_names:
   231→        return []
   232→
   233→    used_names = _find_subscript_zero_refs(node, set(single_list_names))
   234→    return [
   235→        {
   236→            "file": filepath,
   237→            "line": single_list_names[name],
   238→            "content": (
   239→                f"{name} = [v] in {node.name}()"
   240→                " — mutable-list ref hack (use nonlocal or a dataclass)"
   241→            ),
   242→        }
   243→        for name in sorted(used_names)
   244→    ]
   245→
   246→
   247→# Node types that contribute to cyclomatic complexity.
   248→_DECISION_TYPES = (
   249→    ast.If, ast.IfExp, ast.For, ast.AsyncFor, ast.While,
   250→    ast.ExceptHandler, ast.With, ast.AsyncWith, ast.Assert,
   251→)
   252→
   253→
   254→def _compute_cyclomatic_complexity(node: ast.AST) -> int:
   255→    """Compute cyclomatic complexity for a function AST node."""
   256→    complexity = 1
   257→    for child in ast.walk(node):
   258→        if isinstance(child, _DECISION_TYPES):
   259→            complexity += 1
   260→        elif isinstance(child, ast.BoolOp):
   261→            complexity += len(child.values) - 1
   262→    return complexity
   263→
   264→
   265→def _detect_high_cyclomatic_complexity(filepath: str, node: ast.AST) -> list[dict]:
   266→    """Flag functions with cyclomatic complexity > 12."""
   267→    complexity = _compute_cyclomatic_complexity(node)
   268→    if complexity > 12:
   269→        return [
   270→            {
   271→                "file": filepath,
   272→                "line": node.lineno,
   273→                "content": f"{node.name}() — cyclomatic complexity {complexity}",
   274→            }
   275→        ]
   276→    return []
   277→
   278→
   279→def _detect_lru_cache_mutable(
   280→    filepath: str,
   281→    node: ast.AST,
   282→    tree: ast.Module,
   283→) -> list[dict]:
   284→    """Flag @lru_cache/@cache functions that reference module-level mutable variables.
   285→
   286→    Finds globals referenced in the function body that aren't in the parameter list,
   287→    checking if those names are assigned to mutable values at module level.
   288→    """
   289→    # Check if this function has @lru_cache or @cache decorator
   290→    has_cache = False
   291→    for dec in node.decorator_list:
   292→        if isinstance(dec, ast.Name) and dec.id in ("lru_cache", "cache"):
   293→            has_cache = True
   294→        elif isinstance(dec, ast.Call) and isinstance(dec.func, ast.Name):
   295→            if dec.func.id in ("lru_cache", "cache"):
   296→                has_cache = True
   297→        elif isinstance(dec, ast.Attribute) and dec.attr in ("lru_cache", "cache"):
   298→            has_cache = True
   299→    if not has_cache:
   300→        return []
   301→
   302→    # Get parameter names
   303→    param_names = set()
   304→    for arg in node.args.args + node.args.posonlyargs + node.args.kwonlyargs:
   305→        param_names.add(arg.arg)
   306→    if node.args.vararg:
   307→        param_names.add(node.args.vararg.arg)
   308→    if node.args.kwarg:
   309→        param_names.add(node.args.kwarg.arg)
   310→
   311→    # Collect module-level mutable assignments
   312→    module_mutables = set()
   313→    for stmt in tree.body:
   314→        if isinstance(stmt, ast.Assign):
   315→            for target in stmt.targets:
   316→                if isinstance(target, ast.Name) and isinstance(
   317→                    stmt.value, ast.List | ast.Dict | ast.Set | ast.Call
   318→                ):
   319→                    module_mutables.add(target.id)
   320→        elif (
   321→            isinstance(stmt, ast.AnnAssign)
   322→            and stmt.target
   323→            and isinstance(stmt.target, ast.Name)
   324→        ):
   325→            if stmt.value and isinstance(
   326→                stmt.value, ast.List | ast.Dict | ast.Set | ast.Call
   327→            ):
   328→                module_mutables.add(stmt.target.id)
   329→
   330→    # Find Name references in function body that point to module-level mutables
   331→    for child in ast.walk(node):
   332→        if (
   333→            isinstance(child, ast.Name)
   334→            and child.id in module_mutables
   335→            and child.id not in param_names
   336→        ):
   337→            return [
   338→                {
   339→                    "file": filepath,
   340→                    "line": node.lineno,
   341→                    "content": f"@lru_cache on {node.name}() reads mutable global '{child.id}'",
   342→                }
   343→            ]
   344→    return []
   345→
