   609→def _cmd_cluster_update(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   610→    """Update cluster description, steps, and/or priority."""
   611→    cluster_name: str = getattr(args, "cluster_name", "")
   612→    description: str | None = getattr(args, "description", None)
   613→    steps: list[str] | None = getattr(args, "steps", None)
   614→    steps_file: str | None = getattr(args, "steps_file", None)
   615→    add_step: str | None = getattr(args, "add_step", None)
   616→    detail: str | None = getattr(args, "detail", None)
   617→    update_step: int | None = getattr(args, "update_step", None)
   618→    remove_step: int | None = getattr(args, "remove_step", None)
   619→    done_step: int | None = getattr(args, "done_step", None)
   620→    undone_step: int | None = getattr(args, "undone_step", None)
   621→    priority: int | None = getattr(args, "priority", None)
   622→    effort: str | None = getattr(args, "effort", None)
   623→    depends_on: list[str] | None = getattr(args, "depends_on", None)
   624→    issue_refs: list[str] | None = getattr(args, "issue_refs", None)
   625→
   626→    has_update = any(x is not None for x in [
   627→        description, steps, steps_file, add_step, update_step,
   628→        remove_step, done_step, undone_step, priority, effort,
   629→        depends_on, issue_refs,
   630→    ])
   631→    if not has_update:
   632→        print(colorize("  Nothing to update. Use --description, --steps, --steps-file, --add-step, --priority, etc.", "yellow"))
   633→        return
   634→
   635→    with plan_lock():
   636→        _cmd_cluster_update_locked(args, cluster_name=cluster_name,
   637→            description=description, steps=steps, steps_file=steps_file,
   638→            add_step=add_step, detail=detail, update_step=update_step,
   639→            remove_step=remove_step, done_step=done_step,
   640→            undone_step=undone_step, priority=priority, effort=effort,
   641→            depends_on=depends_on, issue_refs=issue_refs)
   642→
   643→
   644→def _cmd_cluster_update_locked(
   645→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   646→    *,
   647→    cluster_name: str,
   648→    description: str | None,
   649→    steps: list[str] | None,
   650→    steps_file: str | None,
   651→    add_step: str | None,
   652→    detail: str | None,
   653→    update_step: int | None,
   654→    remove_step: int | None,
   655→    done_step: int | None,
   656→    undone_step: int | None,
   657→    priority: int | None,
   658→    effort: str | None,
   659→    depends_on: list[str] | None,
   660→    issue_refs: list[str] | None,
   661→) -> None:
   662→    """Inner body of cluster update, called under plan_lock."""
   663→    plan = load_plan()
   664→    cluster = plan.get("clusters", {}).get(cluster_name)
   665→    if cluster is None:
   666→        print(colorize(f"  Cluster {cluster_name!r} does not exist.", "red"))
   667→        return
   668→
   669→    if description is not None:
   670→        cluster["description"] = description
   671→
   672→    if priority is not None:
   673→        cluster["priority"] = priority
   674→        print(colorize(f"  Priority set to {priority}.", "dim"))
   675→
   676→    if depends_on is not None:
   677→        all_clusters = set(plan.get("clusters", {}).keys())
   678→        bad = [n for n in depends_on if n not in all_clusters]
   679→        if bad:
   680→            print(colorize(f"  Unknown cluster(s): {', '.join(bad)}", "red"))
   681→            return
   682→        cluster["depends_on_clusters"] = depends_on
   683→        print(colorize(f"  Dependencies set: {', '.join(depends_on)}", "dim"))
   684→
   685→    # Steps replacement: --steps-file takes precedence over --steps
   686→    if steps_file is not None:
   687→        path = Path(steps_file)
   688→        if not path.is_file():
   689→            print(colorize(f"  Steps file not found: {steps_file}", "red"))
   690→            return
   691→        parsed = parse_steps_file(path.read_text())
   692→        cluster["action_steps"] = parsed
   693→        print(colorize(f"  Loaded {len(parsed)} step(s) from {steps_file}.", "dim"))
   694→    elif steps is not None:
   695→        # Legacy flat strings → wrap as ActionStep dicts
   696→        cluster["action_steps"] = [normalize_step(s) for s in steps]
   697→        print(colorize(f"  Stored {len(steps)} action step(s).", "dim"))
   698→
   699→    # Incremental step operations
   700→    current_steps: list = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
   701→
   702→    MAX_STEP_TITLE = 150
   703→
   704→    if add_step is not None:
   705→        new_step: dict = {"title": add_step}
   706→        if detail is not None:
   707→            new_step["detail"] = detail
   708→        if effort is not None:
   709→            new_step["effort"] = effort
   710→        if issue_refs is not None:
   711→            new_step["issue_refs"] = issue_refs
   712→        if len(add_step) > MAX_STEP_TITLE:
   713→            print(colorize(
   714→                f"  Warning: step title is {len(add_step)} chars (recommended max {MAX_STEP_TITLE}).",
   715→                "yellow",
   716→            ))
   717→            print(colorize("  Move implementation detail to --detail instead.", "dim"))
   718→        current_steps.append(new_step)
   719→        cluster["action_steps"] = current_steps
   720→        print(colorize(f"  Added step {len(current_steps)}: {add_step}", "dim"))
   721→
   722→    if update_step is not None:
   723→        idx = update_step - 1
   724→        if idx < 0 or idx >= len(current_steps):
   725→            print(colorize(f"  Step {update_step} out of range (1-{len(current_steps)}).", "red"))
   726→            return
   727→        old = current_steps[idx]
   728→        if isinstance(old, str):
   729→            old = {"title": old}
   730→        if add_step is None:
   731→            # When --update-step is used without --add-step, keep title, update detail only
   732→            if detail is not None:
   733→                old["detail"] = detail
   734→        else:
   735→            old["title"] = add_step
   736→            if detail is not None:
   737→                old["detail"] = detail
   738→            if len(add_step) > MAX_STEP_TITLE:
   739→                print(colorize(
   740→                    f"  Warning: step title is {len(add_step)} chars (recommended max {MAX_STEP_TITLE}).",
   741→                    "yellow",
   742→                ))
   743→                print(colorize("  Move implementation detail to --detail instead.", "dim"))
   744→        if effort is not None:
   745→            old["effort"] = effort
   746→        if issue_refs is not None:
   747→            old["issue_refs"] = issue_refs
   748→        current_steps[idx] = old
   749→        cluster["action_steps"] = current_steps
   750→        print(colorize(f"  Updated step {update_step}.", "dim"))
   751→
   752→    if remove_step is not None:
   753→        idx = remove_step - 1
   754→        if idx < 0 or idx >= len(current_steps):
   755→            print(colorize(f"  Step {remove_step} out of range (1-{len(current_steps)}).", "red"))
   756→            return
   757→        removed = current_steps.pop(idx)
   758→        cluster["action_steps"] = current_steps
   759→        title = step_summary(removed)
   760→        print(colorize(f"  Removed step {remove_step}: {title}", "dim"))
   761→
   762→    if done_step is not None:
   763→        idx = done_step - 1
   764→        if idx < 0 or idx >= len(current_steps):
   765→            print(colorize(f"  Step {done_step} out of range (1-{len(current_steps)}).", "red"))
   766→            return
   767→        step = current_steps[idx]
   768→        if isinstance(step, str):
   769→            step = {"title": step}
   770→            current_steps[idx] = step
   771→        step["done"] = True
   772→        cluster["action_steps"] = current_steps
   773→        print(colorize(f"  Marked step {done_step} as done: {step.get('title', '')}", "dim"))
   774→
   775→    if undone_step is not None:
   776→        idx = undone_step - 1
   777→        if idx < 0 or idx >= len(current_steps):
   778→            print(colorize(f"  Step {undone_step} out of range (1-{len(current_steps)}).", "red"))
   779→            return
   780→        step = current_steps[idx]
   781→        if isinstance(step, str):
   782→            step = {"title": step}
   783→            current_steps[idx] = step
   784→        step["done"] = False
   785→        cluster["action_steps"] = current_steps
   786→        print(colorize(f"  Marked step {undone_step} as not done: {step.get('title', '')}", "dim"))
   787→
   788→    # Show resulting steps after any mutation
   789→    final_steps = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
   790→    if final_steps and any(x is not None for x in [steps, steps_file, add_step, update_step, remove_step, done_step, undone_step]):
   791→        print()
   792→        print(colorize(f"  Current steps ({len(final_steps)}):", "dim"))
   793→        for i, s in enumerate(final_steps, 1):
   794→            _print_step(i, s)
   795→
   796→    cluster["user_modified"] = True
   797→    cluster["updated_at"] = utc_now()
   798→    append_log_entry(
   799→        plan, "cluster_update", cluster_name=cluster_name, actor="user",
   800→        detail={"description": description},
   801→    )
   802→    save_plan(plan)
   803→    print(colorize(f"  Updated cluster: {cluster_name}", "green"))
   804→
   805→
   806→def _cmd_cluster_export(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   807→    """Export cluster steps to stdout in text or YAML format."""
   808→    cluster_name: str = getattr(args, "cluster_name", "")
   809→    export_format: str = getattr(args, "export_format", "text")
   810→
   811→    plan = load_plan()
   812→    cluster = plan.get("clusters", {}).get(cluster_name)
   813→    if cluster is None:
   814→        print(colorize(f"  Cluster {cluster_name!r} does not exist.", "red"))
   815→        return
   816→
   817→    steps = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
   818→    if not steps:
   819→        print(colorize("  No steps to export.", "yellow"))
   820→        return
   821→
   822→    if export_format == "yaml":
   823→        import yaml  # noqa: PLC0415
   824→        data = {
   825→            "clusters": [{
   826→                "name": cluster_name,
   827→                "description": cluster.get("description") or "",
   828→                **({"priority": cluster["priority"]} if "priority" in cluster else {}),
   829→                "steps": [
   830→                    normalize_step(s) for s in steps
   831→                ],
   832→            }]
   833→        }
   834→        print(yaml.dump(data, default_flow_style=False, sort_keys=False))
   835→    else:
   836→        print(format_steps(steps))
   837→
   838→
   839→def _cmd_cluster_import(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   840→    """Bulk create/update clusters from a YAML file."""
   841→    file_path: str = getattr(args, "file", "")
   842→    dry_run: bool = getattr(args, "dry_run", False)
   843→
   844→    path = Path(file_path)
   845→    if not path.is_file():
   846→        print(colorize(f"  File not found: {file_path}", "red"))
   847→        return
   848→
   849→    import yaml  # noqa: PLC0415
   850→    data = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text())
   851→    if not isinstance(data, dict) or "clusters" not in data:
   852→        print(colorize("  Invalid YAML: expected top-level 'clusters' key.", "red"))
   853→        return
   854→
   855→    entries = data["clusters"]
   856→    if not isinstance(entries, list):
   857→        print(colorize("  Invalid YAML: 'clusters' must be a list.", "red"))
   858→        return
   859→
   860→    plan = load_plan()
   861→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   862→    created = 0
   863→    updated = 0
   864→
   865→    for entry in entries:
   866→        if not isinstance(entry, dict) or "name" not in entry:
   867→            print(colorize(f"  Skipping entry without 'name': {entry!r}", "yellow"))
   868→            continue
   869→        name = entry["name"]
   870→        is_new = name not in clusters
   871→
   872→        if dry_run:
   873→            action = "CREATE" if is_new else "UPDATE"
   874→            step_count = len(entry.get("steps", []))
   875→            print(colorize(f"  [{action}] {name}: {step_count} step(s)", "cyan"))
   876→            continue
   877→
   878→        if is_new:
   879→            try:
   880→                cluster = create_cluster(plan, name, entry.get("description"))
   881→            except ValueError as ex:
   882→                print(colorize(f"  {ex}", "red"))
   883→                continue
   884→            created += 1
   885→        else:
   886→            cluster = clusters[name]
   887→            updated += 1
   888→
   889→        if "description" in entry:
   890→            cluster["description"] = entry["description"]
   891→        if "priority" in entry:
   892→            cluster["priority"] = entry["priority"]
   893→        if "steps" in entry:
   894→            imported_steps = []
   895→            for s in entry["steps"]:
   896→                if isinstance(s, str):
   897→                    imported_steps.append({"title": s})
   898→                elif isinstance(s, dict):
   899→                    step: dict = {"title": s.get("title", "")}
   900→                    if "detail" in s:
   901→                        step["detail"] = s["detail"]
   902→                    if "refs" in s:
   903→                        step["issue_refs"] = s["refs"]
   904→                    elif "issue_refs" in s:
   905→                        step["issue_refs"] = s["issue_refs"]
   906→                    imported_steps.append(step)
   907→            cluster["action_steps"] = imported_steps
   908→        cluster["user_modified"] = True
   909→        cluster["updated_at"] = utc_now()
   910→
   911→    if dry_run:
   912→        print(colorize("  (dry run — no changes saved)", "dim"))
   913→        return
   914→
   915→    save_plan(plan)
   916→    print(colorize(f"  Import complete: {created} created, {updated} updated.", "green"))
   917→
   918→
   919→def _cmd_cluster_merge(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   920→    """Merge source cluster into target cluster."""
   921→    source: str = getattr(args, "source", "")
   922→    target: str = getattr(args, "target", "")
   923→
   924→    plan = load_plan()
   925→    try:
   926→        added, source_ids = merge_clusters(plan, source, target)
   927→    except ValueError as ex:
   928→        print(colorize(f"  {ex}", "red"))
   929→        return
   930→
   931→    append_log_entry(
   932→        plan, "cluster_merge", issue_ids=source_ids,
   933→        cluster_name=target, actor="user",
   934→        detail={"source": source, "added": added},
   935→    )
   936→    save_plan(plan)
   937→    print(colorize(
   938→        f"  Merged cluster {source!r} into {target!r}: "
   939→        f"{added} issue(s) added, {len(source_ids)} total moved. Source deleted.",
   940→        "green",
   941→    ))
   942→
   943→
   944→def cmd_cluster_dispatch(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   945→    """Route cluster subcommands."""
   946→    cluster_action = getattr(args, "cluster_action", None)
   947→    dispatch = {
   948→        "create": _cmd_cluster_create,
   949→        "add": _cmd_cluster_add,
   950→        "remove": _cmd_cluster_remove,
   951→        "delete": _cmd_cluster_delete,
   952→        "reorder": _cmd_cluster_reorder,
   953→        "show": _cmd_cluster_show,
   954→        "list": _cmd_cluster_list,
   955→        "update": _cmd_cluster_update,
   956→        "merge": _cmd_cluster_merge,
   957→        "export": _cmd_cluster_export,
   958→        "import": _cmd_cluster_import,
   959→    }
   960→    handler = dispatch.get(cluster_action)
   961→    if handler is None:
   962→        _cmd_cluster_list(args)
   963→        return
   964→    handler(args)
   965→
   966→
   967→__all__ = ["cmd_cluster_dispatch"]

   138→def _build_dir_stats(
   139→    scan_root: Path,
   140→    files: list[str],
   141→) -> tuple[Counter[str], dict[str, set[str]]]:
   142→    dir_counts: Counter[str] = Counter()
   143→    child_dirs: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
   144→    for file_path in files:
   145→        try:
   146→            resolved_file = resolve_scan_file(file_path, scan_root=scan_root).resolve()
   147→            parent_path = resolved_file.parent
   148→            parent_rel = parent_path.relative_to(scan_root)
   149→        except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
   150→            logger.debug("Skipping unresolvable file %s: %s", file_path, exc)
   151→            continue
   152→
   153→        parent = str((scan_root / parent_rel).resolve())
   154→        dir_counts[parent] += 1
   155→        parts = parent_rel.parts
   156→        for idx in range(len(parts) - 1):
   157→            ancestor = (scan_root / Path(*parts[: idx + 1])).resolve()
   158→            child = (scan_root / Path(*parts[: idx + 2])).resolve()
   159→            ancestor_key = str(ancestor)
   160→            child_dirs.setdefault(ancestor_key, set()).add(str(child))
   161→    return dir_counts, child_dirs
   162→
   163→
   164→def _all_tracked_dirs(
   165→    dir_counts: Counter[str],
   166→    child_dirs: dict[str, set[str]],
   167→) -> set[str]:
   168→    all_dirs: set[str] = set(dir_counts.keys())
   169→    all_dirs.update(child_dirs.keys())
   170→    for children in child_dirs.values():
   171→        all_dirs.update(children)
   172→    return all_dirs
   173→
   174→
   175→def _is_overloaded(
   176→    *,
   177→    file_count: int,
   178→    direct_child_count: int,
   179→    combined_score: int,
   180→    settings: FlatDirDetectionConfig,
   181→) -> bool:
   182→    return (
   183→        file_count >= settings.threshold
   184→        or direct_child_count >= settings.child_dir_threshold
   185→        or combined_score >= settings.combined_threshold
   186→    )
   187→
   188→
   189→def _fragmentation_entry(
   190→    *,
   191→    dir_path: str,
   192→    file_count: int,
   193→    direct_children: set[str],
   194→    direct_child_count: int,
   195→    combined_score: int,
   196→    settings: FlatDirDetectionConfig,
   197→    dir_counts: Counter[str],
   198→    child_dirs: dict[str, set[str]],
   199→) -> dict | None:
   200→    sparse_child_count = 0
   201→    for child in direct_children:
   202→        child_file_count = int(dir_counts.get(child, 0))
   203→        child_child_count = len(child_dirs.get(child, set()))
   204→        if (
   205→            child_file_count <= settings.sparse_child_file_threshold
   206→            and child_child_count == 0
   207→        ):
   208→            sparse_child_count += 1
   209→    sparse_child_ratio = (
   210→        float(sparse_child_count) / float(direct_child_count)
   211→        if direct_child_count
   212→        else 0.0
   213→    )
   214→    fragmented = (
   215→        direct_child_count >= settings.sparse_parent_child_threshold
   216→        and sparse_child_count >= settings.sparse_child_count_threshold
   217→        and sparse_child_ratio >= settings.sparse_child_ratio_threshold
   218→    )
   219→    if not fragmented:
   220→        return None
   221→    return {
   222→        "directory": dir_path,
   223→        "file_count": file_count,
   224→        "child_dir_count": direct_child_count,
   225→        "combined_score": combined_score,
   226→        "kind": "fragmented",
   227→        "sparse_child_count": sparse_child_count,
   228→        "sparse_child_ratio": sparse_child_ratio,
   229→        "sparse_child_file_threshold": settings.sparse_child_file_threshold,
   230→    }
   231→
   232→
   233→def _thin_wrapper_entry(
   234→    *,
   235→    dir_path: str,
   236→    thin_names: set[str],
   237→    file_count: int,
   238→    direct_child_count: int,
   239→    combined_score: int,
   240→    settings: FlatDirDetectionConfig,
   241→    child_dirs: dict[str, set[str]],
   242→) -> dict | None:
   243→    dir_name = Path(dir_path).name.lower()
   244→    parent_key = str(Path(dir_path).parent)
   245→    parent_sibling_count = len(child_dirs.get(parent_key, set()))
   246→    wrapper_item_count = file_count + direct_child_count
   247→    thin_wrapper = (
   248→        dir_name in thin_names
   249→        and wrapper_item_count == 1
   250→        and file_count <= settings.thin_wrapper_max_file_count
   251→        and direct_child_count <= settings.thin_wrapper_max_child_dir_count
   252→        and parent_sibling_count >= settings.thin_wrapper_parent_sibling_threshold
   253→    )
   254→    if not thin_wrapper:
   255→        return None
   256→    return {
   257→        "directory": dir_path,
   258→        "file_count": file_count,
   259→        "child_dir_count": direct_child_count,
   260→        "combined_score": combined_score,
   261→        "kind": "thin_wrapper",
   262→        "parent_sibling_count": parent_sibling_count,
   263→        "wrapper_item_count": wrapper_item_count,
   264→    }

   267→def _sort_entries(entries: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
   268→    return sorted(
   269→        entries,
   270→        key=lambda entry: (
   271→            -int(entry["combined_score"]),
   272→            -int(entry.get("parent_sibling_count", 0)),

   280→def detect_flat_dirs(

   294→    thin_wrapper_max_file_count: int = 1,

   312→    """Find overloaded/fragmented directories using count and fan-out heuristics."""

   317→        child_dir_weight=child_dir_weight,

   336→
   337→    entries: list[dict] = []
   338→    for dir_path in sorted(all_dirs):
   339→        file_count = int(dir_counts.get(dir_path, 0))
   340→        direct_children = child_dirs.get(dir_path, set())
   341→        direct_child_count = len(direct_children)
   342→        combined_score = file_count + (settings.child_dir_weight * direct_child_count)
   343→        has_local_files = dir_path in dir_counts
   344→
   345→        if has_local_files:
   346→            if _is_overloaded(
   347→                file_count=file_count,
   348→                direct_child_count=direct_child_count,
   349→                combined_score=combined_score,
   350→                settings=settings,
   351→            ):
   352→                entries.append(
   353→                    {
   354→                        "directory": dir_path,
   355→                        "file_count": file_count,
   356→                        "child_dir_count": direct_child_count,
   357→                        "combined_score": combined_score,
   358→                        "kind": "overload",
   359→                    }
   360→                )
   361→                continue
   362→            fragmented_entry = _fragmentation_entry(
   363→                dir_path=dir_path,
   364→                file_count=file_count,
   365→                direct_children=direct_children,
   366→                direct_child_count=direct_child_count,
   367→                combined_score=combined_score,
   368→                settings=settings,
   369→                dir_counts=dir_counts,
   370→                child_dirs=child_dirs,
   371→            )
   372→            if fragmented_entry is not None:
   373→                entries.append(fragmented_entry)
   374→                continue
   375→
   376→        thin_wrapper = _thin_wrapper_entry(
   377→            dir_path=dir_path,
   378→            thin_names=thin_names,
   379→            file_count=file_count,
   380→            direct_child_count=direct_child_count,
   381→            combined_score=combined_score,
   382→            settings=settings,
   383→            child_dirs=child_dirs,
   384→        )
   385→        if thin_wrapper is not None:
   386→            entries.append(thin_wrapper)
   387→    return _sort_entries(entries), len(all_dirs)
   388→

    20→_STAGE_ORDER = ["observe", "reflect", "organize", "enrich", "sense-check"]

    22→
    23→def has_triage_in_queue(plan: dict) -> bool:
    24→    """Check if any triage stage ID is in the queue."""
    25→    order = set(plan.get("queue_order", []))
    26→    return bool(order & TRIAGE_IDS)
    27→
    28→def inject_triage_stages(plan: dict) -> None:
    29→    """Inject all 4 triage stage IDs into the queue (fresh start)."""
    30→    order: list[str] = plan.setdefault("queue_order", [])
    31→    existing = set(order)
    32→    for sid in TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS:
    33→        if sid not in existing:
    34→            order.insert(0 if sid == TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS[0] else len(order), sid)
    35→    # Re-insert in correct order at front
    36→    for sid in reversed(TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS):
    37→        if sid in order:
    38→            order.remove(sid)
    39→    insert_at = 0
    40→    for sid in TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS:
    41→        order.insert(insert_at, sid)
    42→        insert_at += 1
    43→
    44→def purge_triage_stage(plan: dict, stage_name: str) -> None:
    45→    """Purge a single triage stage ID from the queue."""
    46→    sid = f"triage::{stage_name}"
    47→    purge_ids(plan, [sid])
    48→
    49→def cascade_clear_later_confirmations(stages: dict, from_stage: str) -> list[str]:
    50→    """Clear confirmed_at/confirmed_text on stages AFTER *from_stage*. Returns cleared names."""
    51→    try:
    52→        idx = _STAGE_ORDER.index(from_stage)
    53→    except ValueError:
    54→        return []
    55→    cleared: list[str] = []
    56→    for later in _STAGE_ORDER[idx + 1:]:
    57→        if later in stages and stages[later].get("confirmed_at"):
    58→            stages[later].pop("confirmed_at", None)
    59→            stages[later].pop("confirmed_text", None)
    60→            cleared.append(later)
    61→    return cleared
    62→
    63→def print_cascade_clear_feedback(cleared: list[str], stages: dict) -> None:
    64→    """Print yellow cascade-clear message with next-step guidance."""
    65→    if not cleared:
    66→        return
    67→    print(colorize(f"  Cleared confirmations on: {', '.join(cleared)}", "yellow"))
    68→    next_unconfirmed = next(
    69→        (s for s in _STAGE_ORDER if s in stages and not stages[s].get("confirmed_at")),
    70→        None,
    71→    )
    72→    if next_unconfirmed:
    73→        print(colorize(
    74→            f"  Re-confirm with: desloppify plan triage --confirm {next_unconfirmed}",
    75→            "dim",
    76→        ))
    77→
    78→def observe_dimension_breakdown(si) -> tuple[dict[str, int], list[str]]:
    79→    """Count issues per dimension from a TriageInput. Returns (by_dim, sorted_dim_names)."""
    80→    by_dim: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)
    81→    for _fid, f in si.open_issues.items():
    82→        detail = f.get("detail", {}) if isinstance(f.get("detail"), dict) else {}
    83→        dim = detail.get("dimension", "unknown")
    84→        by_dim[dim] += 1
    85→    dim_names = sorted(by_dim, key=lambda d: (-by_dim[d], d))
    86→    return dict(by_dim), dim_names
    87→
    88→def group_issues_into_observe_batches(
    89→    si,
    90→    max_batches: int = 5,
    91→) -> list[tuple[list[str], dict[str, dict]]]:
    92→    """Group issues by dimension into batches for parallel observe.
    93→
    94→    Returns list of (dimension_names, issues_subset) tuples.
    95→    Single batch if only one dimension exists.
    96→    """
    97→    by_dim, dim_names = observe_dimension_breakdown(si)
    98→
    99→    if len(dim_names) <= 1:
   100→        return [(dim_names, dict(si.open_issues))]
   101→
   102→    # Distribute dimensions into balanced batches by issue count
   103→    num_batches = min(max_batches, len(dim_names))
   104→    batch_dims: list[list[str]] = [[] for _ in range(num_batches)]
   105→    batch_counts: list[int] = [0] * num_batches
   106→
   107→    # Greedy: assign each dimension (largest first) to the lightest batch
   108→    for dim in dim_names:
   109→        lightest = min(range(num_batches), key=lambda i: batch_counts[i])
   110→        batch_dims[lightest].append(dim)
   111→        batch_counts[lightest] += by_dim[dim]
   112→
   113→    # Build issue subsets per batch
   114→    # Pre-index issues by dimension
   115→    dim_to_issues: dict[str, dict[str, dict]] = defaultdict(dict)
   116→    for fid, f in si.open_issues.items():
   117→        detail = f.get("detail", {}) if isinstance(f.get("detail"), dict) else {}
   118→        dim = detail.get("dimension", "unknown")
   119→        dim_to_issues[dim][fid] = f
   120→
   121→    result: list[tuple[list[str], dict[str, dict]]] = []
   122→    for dims in batch_dims:
   123→        if not dims:
   124→            continue
   125→        subset: dict[str, dict] = {}
   126→        for dim in dims:
   127→            subset.update(dim_to_issues.get(dim, {}))
   128→        if subset:
   129→            result.append((dims, subset))
   130→
   131→    return result
   132→
   133→
   134→def open_review_ids_from_state(state: dict) -> set[str]:
   135→    """Return IDs of all open review/concerns issues in state."""
   136→    return {
   137→        fid for fid, f in state.get("issues", {}).items()
   138→        if f.get("status") == "open" and f.get("detector") in _REVIEW_DETECTORS
   139→    }
   140→
   141→def triage_coverage(
   142→    plan: dict,
   143→    open_review_ids: set[str] | None = None,
   144→) -> tuple[int, int, dict]:
   145→    """Return (organized, total, clusters) for review issues in triage.
   146→
   147→    When *open_review_ids* is provided, use it as the full set of review
   148→    issues (from state) instead of falling back to queue_order.
   149→    """
   150→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   151→    all_cluster_ids: set[str] = set()
   152→    for c in clusters.values():
   153→        all_cluster_ids.update(c.get("issue_ids", []))
   154→    if open_review_ids is not None:
   155→        review_ids = list(open_review_ids)
   156→    else:
   157→        review_ids = [
   158→            fid for fid in plan.get("queue_order", [])
   159→            if not fid.startswith("triage::") and not fid.startswith("workflow::") and (fid.startswith("review::") or fid.startswith("concerns::"))
   160→        ]
   161→    organized = sum(1 for fid in review_ids if fid in all_cluster_ids)
   162→    return organized, len(review_ids), clusters
   163→
   164→def manual_clusters_with_issues(plan: dict) -> list[str]:
   165→    """Return names of non-auto clusters that have issues."""
   166→    return [
   167→        name for name, c in plan.get("clusters", {}).items()
   168→        if c.get("issue_ids") and not c.get("auto")
   169→    ]
   170→
   171→def apply_completion(
   172→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   173→    plan: dict,
   174→    strategy: str,
   175→    *,
   176→    services: TriageServices | None = None,
   177→) -> None:
   178→    """Shared completion logic: update meta, remove triage::pending, save."""
   179→    resolved_services = services or default_triage_services()
   180→    runtime = resolved_services.command_runtime(args)
   181→    state = runtime.state
   182→
   183→    organized, total, clusters = triage_coverage(
   184→        plan, open_review_ids=open_review_ids_from_state(state),
   185→    )
   186→
   187→    # Purge all triage stage IDs.
   188→    purge_ids(plan, list(TRIAGE_IDS))
   189→
   190→    current_hash = review_issue_snapshot_hash(state)
   191→
   192→    meta = plan.setdefault("epic_triage_meta", {})
   193→    meta["issue_snapshot_hash"] = current_hash
   194→    open_ids = sorted(
   195→        fid for fid, f in state.get("issues", {}).items()
   196→        if f.get("status") == "open" and f.get("detector") in _REVIEW_DETECTORS
   197→    )
   198→    meta["triaged_ids"] = open_ids
   199→    if strategy.strip().lower() != "same":
   200→        meta["strategy_summary"] = strategy
   201→    meta["trigger"] = "manual_triage"
   202→    meta["last_completed_at"] = utc_now()
   203→    # Archive stages before clearing so previous analysis is preserved
   204→    stages = meta.get("triage_stages", {})
   205→    if stages:
   206→        meta["last_triage"] = {
   207→            "completed_at": utc_now(),
   208→            "stages": {k: dict(v) for k, v in stages.items()},
   209→            "strategy": strategy if strategy.strip().lower() != "same" else meta.get("strategy_summary", ""),
   210→        }
   211→    meta["triage_stages"] = {}  # clear stages on completion
   212→    meta.pop("stage_refresh_required", None)
   213→    meta.pop("stage_snapshot_hash", None)
   214→
   215→    resolved_services.save_plan(plan)
   216→
   217→    cluster_count = len([c for c in clusters.values() if c.get("issue_ids")])
   218→    print(colorize(f"  Triage complete: {organized}/{total} issues in {cluster_count} cluster(s).", "green"))
   219→    effective_strategy = strategy if strategy.strip().lower() != "same" else meta.get("strategy_summary", "")
   220→    if effective_strategy:
   221→        print(colorize(f"  Strategy: {effective_strategy}", "cyan"))
   222→    print(colorize("  Run `desloppify next` to start implementation.", "green"))
   223→
   224→def find_cluster_for(fid: str, clusters: dict) -> str | None:
   225→    """Return the cluster name containing *fid*, or None."""
   226→    for name, c in clusters.items():
   227→        if fid in c.get("issue_ids", []):
   228→            return name
   229→    return None

   231→def count_log_activity_since(plan: dict, since: str) -> dict[str, int]:
   232→    """Count execution log entries by action since *since* timestamp."""
   233→    counts: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)
   234→    for entry in plan.get("execution_log", []):
   235→        if entry.get("timestamp", "") >= since:

   237→    return dict(counts)

    58→    unclustered = _collect_unclustered_issues(clusters, open_issues)
    59→    _print_unclustered_issues(plan, open_issues, unclustered)
    60→
    61→
    62→def _print_active_clusters(clusters: dict[str, dict]) -> None:
    63→    """Print current clusters that contain issues."""
    64→    active_clusters = {name: cluster for name, cluster in clusters.items() if cluster.get("issue_ids")}
    65→    if not active_clusters:
    66→        return
    67→    print(colorize("\n  Current clusters:", "cyan"))
    68→    for name, cluster in active_clusters.items():
    69→        count = len(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
    70→        desc = cluster.get("description") or ""
    71→        tag_str = _cluster_tag_summary(cluster)
    72→        desc_str = f" \u2014 {desc}" if desc else ""
    73→        print(f"    {name}: {count} items{tag_str}{desc_str}")
    74→
    75→
    76→def _cluster_tag_summary(cluster: dict) -> str:
    77→    """Build compact tag summary for one cluster row."""
    78→    steps = cluster.get("action_steps", [])
    79→    auto = cluster.get("auto", False)
    80→    tags: list[str] = []
    81→    tags.append("auto" if auto else "manual")
    82→    tags.append("desc" if cluster.get("description") else "no desc")
    83→    if steps:
    84→        tags.append(f"{len(steps)} steps")
    85→    elif not auto:
    86→        tags.append("no steps")
    87→    return f" [{', '.join(tags)}]"
    88→
    89→
    90→def _collect_unclustered_issues(clusters: dict[str, dict], open_issues: dict) -> list[str]:
    91→    """Return issue IDs that are not attached to any cluster."""
    92→    all_clustered: set[str] = set()
    93→    for cluster in clusters.values():
    94→        all_clustered.update(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
    95→    return [issue_id for issue_id in open_issues if issue_id not in all_clustered]
    96→
    97→
    98→def _print_unclustered_issues(
    99→    plan: dict,
   100→    open_issues: dict,
   101→    unclustered: list[str],
   102→) -> None:
   103→    """Print unclustered issues summary or all-clustered confirmation."""
   104→    if unclustered:
   105→        print(colorize(f"\n  {len(unclustered)} issues not yet in a cluster:", "yellow"))
   106→        for issue_id in unclustered[:10]:
   107→            issue = open_issues[issue_id]
   108→            dim = (
   109→                (issue.get("detail", {}) or {}).get("dimension", "")
   110→                if isinstance(issue.get("detail"), dict)
   111→                else ""
   112→            )
   113→            short = short_issue_id(issue_id)
   114→            print(f"    [{short}] [{dim}] {issue.get('summary', '')}")
   115→        if len(unclustered) > 10:
   116→            print(colorize(f"    ... and {len(unclustered) - 10} more", "dim"))
   117→        return
   118→    if open_issues:
   119→        organized, total, _ = _triage_coverage(plan)
   120→        print(colorize(f"\n  All {organized}/{total} issues are in clusters.", "green"))
   121→

    24→    detail = item.get("detail")

    32→def is_subjective_issue(item: WorkQueueItem | dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    33→    detector = item.get("detector")
    34→    if detector in {"subjective_assessment"}:
    35→        return True
    36→    if detector == "holistic_review":

    46→    """True for subjective work items, including collapsed subjective clusters."""
    47→    if item.get("kind") == "subjective_dimension":
    48→        return True
    49→    if item.get("kind") == "cluster":
    50→        members = item.get("members", [])
    51→        return bool(members) and all(

    53→        )
    54→    return False

    57→def review_issue_weight(item: WorkQueueItem | dict[str, Any]) -> float:
    58→    """Return review issue weight aligned with issues list ordering."""
    59→    confidence = str(item.get("confidence", "low")).lower()
    60→    weight_by_confidence = {
    61→        "high": 1.0,
    62→        "medium": 0.7,
    63→        "low": 0.3,
    64→    }
    65→    weight = weight_by_confidence.get(confidence, 0.3)
    66→    if detail_dict(item).get("holistic"):

    71→def scope_matches(item: WorkQueueItem | dict[str, Any], scope: str | None) -> bool:
    72→    """Apply show-style pattern matching against a queue item."""
    73→    if not scope:

    75→
    76→    item_id = item.get("id", "")
    77→    detector = item.get("detector", "")

    83→    if "*" in scope:

   118→    if stage_name:

   120→
   121→    item_id = str(item.get("id", "")).strip()
   122→    if item_id.startswith("triage::"):

   132→    state: StateModel, item: WorkQueueItem
   133→) -> set[str] | None:
   134→    """Return supported fixers for an item's language when known."""
   135→    lang = str(item.get("lang", "") or "").strip()
   136→    if not lang:
   137→        return None
   138→
   139→    caps_obj = state.get("lang_capabilities")
   140→    if not isinstance(caps_obj, dict):
   141→        return None
   142→    lang_caps_obj = caps_obj.get(lang)
   143→    if not isinstance(lang_caps_obj, dict):
   144→        return None
   145→
   146→    fixers = lang_caps_obj.get("fixers")
   147→    if not isinstance(fixers, list):
   148→        return None
   149→    return {fixer for fixer in fixers if isinstance(fixer, str)}

   153→    item: WorkQueueItem, *, supported_fixers: set[str] | None = None
   154→) -> str:
   155→    detector = item.get("detector", "")
   156→    meta = DETECTORS.get(detector)
   157→    if meta and meta.action_type == "auto_fix" and meta.fixers:
   158→        available_fixers = [
   159→            fixer
   160→            for fixer in meta.fixers
   161→            if supported_fixers is not None and fixer in supported_fixers
   162→        ]
   163→        if available_fixers:
   164→            return f"desloppify autofix {available_fixers[0]} --dry-run"
   165→    if detector == "subjective_review":
   166→        from desloppify.intelligence.integrity import (
   167→            is_holistic_subjective_issue,  # cycle-break: helpers.py ↔ integrity.py
   168→        )
   169→
   170→        if is_holistic_subjective_issue(item):
   171→            return "desloppify review --prepare"
   172→        return "desloppify show subjective"
   173→    return f'desloppify plan resolve "{item.get("id", "")}" --note "<what you did>" --confirm'

1→"""Holistic review preparation workflow helpers."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations

    10→from desloppify.base.discovery.file_paths import rel
    11→from desloppify.intelligence.review._context.models import HolisticContext
    12→from desloppify.intelligence.review._prepare.helpers import HOLISTIC_WORKFLOW
    13→from desloppify.intelligence.review._prepare.issue_history import (
    14→    ReviewHistoryOptions,

    19→_NON_PRODUCTION_ZONES = frozenset({"test", "config", "generated", "vendor"})
    20→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

    22→
    23→def collect_allowed_review_files(
    24→    files: list[str],
    25→    lang: object,
    26→    *,
    27→    base_path: Path | None = None,
    28→) -> set[str]:
    29→    """Return relative production-file paths allowed for holistic review batches."""
    30→    allowed: set[str] = set()
    31→    zone_map = getattr(lang, "zone_map", None)
    32→    resolved_base = base_path.resolve() if isinstance(base_path, Path) else None
    33→    for filepath in files:
    34→        if not isinstance(filepath, str):
    35→            continue
    36→        normalized = filepath.strip().replace("\\", "/")
    37→        if not normalized:
    38→            continue
    39→        if zone_map is not None:
    40→            zone_get = getattr(zone_map, "get", None)
    41→            zone = zone_get(filepath) if callable(zone_get) else None
    42→            zone_value = getattr(zone, "value", zone)
    43→            if zone_value is None:
    44→                zone_value = "production"
    45→            if not isinstance(zone_value, str):
    46→                zone_value = str(zone_value)
    47→            if zone_value in _NON_PRODUCTION_ZONES:
    48→                continue
    49→        allowed.add(normalized)
    50→        allowed.add(rel(filepath))
    51→        if resolved_base is not None:
    52→            try:
    53→                resolved_path = Path(filepath).resolve()
    54→            except OSError as exc:
    55→                logger.debug("Skipping invalid review file path %s: %s", filepath, exc)
    56→                continue
    57→            if resolved_path.is_relative_to(resolved_base):
    58→                allowed.add(resolved_path.relative_to(resolved_base).as_posix())
    59→    return allowed
    60→
    61→
    62→def file_in_allowed_scope(filepath: object, allowed_files: set[str]) -> bool:
    63→    """True when *filepath* resolves to a currently in-scope review file."""
    64→    if not isinstance(filepath, str):
    65→        return False
    66→    normalized = filepath.strip().replace("\\", "/")
    67→    if not normalized:
    68→        return False
    69→    if normalized in allowed_files:
    70→        return True
    71→    return rel(filepath) in allowed_files
    72→
    73→
    74→def filter_issue_focus_to_scope(
    75→    issue_focus: object,
    76→    allowed_files: set[str],
    77→) -> dict[str, object] | None:
    78→    """Drop out-of-scope related_files from historical issue focus payload."""
    79→    if not isinstance(issue_focus, dict):
    80→        return None
    81→    issues_raw = issue_focus.get("issues", [])
    82→    issues: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    83→    if isinstance(issues_raw, list):
    84→        for raw_issue in issues_raw:
    85→            if not isinstance(raw_issue, dict):
    86→                continue
    87→            issue = dict(raw_issue)
    88→            related_raw = issue.get("related_files", [])
    89→            if isinstance(related_raw, list):
    90→                issue["related_files"] = [
    91→                    path for path in related_raw if file_in_allowed_scope(path, allowed_files)
    92→                ]
    93→            issues.append(issue)
    94→    scoped = dict(issue_focus)
    95→    scoped["issues"] = issues
    96→    scoped["selected_count"] = len(issues)
    97→    return scoped
    98→
    99→
   100→def filter_batches_to_file_scope(
   101→    batches: list[dict[str, Any]],
   102→    *,
   103→    allowed_files: set[str],
   104→) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   105→    """Strip out-of-scope files/signals from review batches."""
   106→    if not allowed_files:
   107→        return []
   108→
   109→    scoped_batches: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
   110→    for raw_batch in batches:
   111→        if not isinstance(raw_batch, dict):
   112→            continue
   113→        batch = dict(raw_batch)
   114→        files_to_read = batch.get("files_to_read", [])
   115→        if isinstance(files_to_read, list):
   116→            scoped_files = [
   117→                filepath
   118→                for filepath in files_to_read
   119→                if file_in_allowed_scope(filepath, allowed_files)
   120→            ]
   121→        else:
   122→            scoped_files = []
   123→        batch["files_to_read"] = scoped_files
   124→
   125→        concern_signals = batch.get("concern_signals", [])
   126→        if isinstance(concern_signals, list):
   127→            batch["concern_signals"] = [
   128→                signal
   129→                for signal in concern_signals
   130→                if isinstance(signal, dict)
   131→                and file_in_allowed_scope(signal.get("file", ""), allowed_files)
   132→            ]
   133→            if "concern_signal_count" in batch:
   134→                batch["concern_signal_count"] = len(batch["concern_signals"])
   135→
   136→        issue_focus = filter_issue_focus_to_scope(
   137→            batch.get("historical_issue_focus"),
   138→            allowed_files,
   139→        )
   140→        if issue_focus is not None:
   141→            batch["historical_issue_focus"] = issue_focus
   142→
   143→        has_seed_files = bool(batch["files_to_read"])
   144→        has_signals = bool(batch.get("concern_signals"))
   145→        if has_seed_files or has_signals:
   146→            scoped_batches.append(batch)

   176→    is_file_cache_enabled_fn,

   242→def _append_concerns_batch(
   243→    batches: list[dict[str, Any]],
   244→    state: dict,
   245→    dims: list[str],
   246→    allowed_review_files: set[str],
   247→    max_files_per_batch: int,
   248→    *,
   249→    batch_concerns_fn,
   250→    log_best_effort_failure_fn,
   251→    log: object,
   252→) -> None:
   253→    """Generate concern signals and append as a batch (best-effort)."""
   254→    try:
   255→        from desloppify.engine.concerns import generate_concerns
   256→
   257→        concerns = generate_concerns(state)
   258→        concerns = [
   259→            concern
   260→            for concern in concerns
   261→            if file_in_allowed_scope(getattr(concern, "file", ""), allowed_review_files)
   262→        ]
   263→        concerns_batch = batch_concerns_fn(
   264→            concerns,

   270→            # rather than creating a duplicate batch.
   271→            concern_dim = concerns_batch["dimensions"][0]
   272→            merged = False
   273→            for existing in batches:
   274→                if existing.get("dimensions") == [concern_dim]:
   275→                    # Merge seed files and concern signals
   276→                    existing_files = set(existing.get("files_to_read", []))
   277→                    for f in concerns_batch.get("files_to_read", []):
   278→                        if f not in existing_files:
   279→                            existing["files_to_read"].append(f)
   280→                            existing_files.add(f)
   281→                    existing["concern_signals"] = concerns_batch.get("concern_signals", [])
   282→                    existing["concern_signal_count"] = concerns_batch.get("concern_signal_count", 0)
   283→                    merged = True
   284→                    break
   285→            if not merged:
   286→                batches.append(concerns_batch)

   308→def _attach_issue_history_context(

   321→            max_issues=options.issue_history_max_issues,
   322→        ),
   323→    )
   324→    payload["historical_review_issues"] = history_payload
   325→    for batch in batches:
   326→        if not isinstance(batch, dict):
   327→            continue
   328→        batch_dims = batch.get("dimensions", [])
   329→        batch["historical_issue_focus"] = build_batch_issue_focus(
   330→            history_payload,

1→"""Payload parsing helpers for review import workflows."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from dataclasses import dataclass
     6→from typing import Any
     7→
     8→from desloppify.intelligence.review.importing.contracts_types import (
     9→    ReviewImportPayload,
    10→    ReviewIssuePayload,
    11→)
    12→
    13→LEGACY_FINDINGS_ALIAS_SUNSET_DATE = "2026-12-31"
    14→ALLOW_LEGACY_FINDINGS_ALIAS = True
    15→
    16→
    17→@dataclass(frozen=True)
    18→class ReviewImportEnvelope:
    19→    """Validated shared payload shape for review imports."""
    20→
    21→    issues: list[ReviewIssuePayload]
    22→    assessments: dict[str, Any] | None
    23→    reviewed_files: list[str]
    24→
    25→
    26→def normalize_legacy_findings_alias(
    27→    payload: dict[str, Any],
    28→    *,
    29→    missing_issues_error: str,
    30→    allow_legacy_findings: bool = ALLOW_LEGACY_FINDINGS_ALIAS,
    31→) -> str | None:
    32→    """Normalize legacy ``findings`` into canonical ``issues`` in one place.
    33→
    34→    ``allow_legacy_findings`` is the compatibility cutoff flag; once flipped to
    35→    ``False`` only canonical ``issues`` payloads are accepted.
    36→    """
    37→    if "issues" in payload:
    38→        return None
    39→    if "findings" not in payload:
    40→        return missing_issues_error
    41→    if not allow_legacy_findings:
    42→        return (
    43→            "legacy key 'findings' is no longer accepted; use 'issues' "
    44→            f"(support sunset: {LEGACY_FINDINGS_ALIAS_SUNSET_DATE})"
    45→        )
    46→    payload["issues"] = payload.pop("findings")
    47→    return None
    48→
    49→
    50→def extract_reviewed_files(data: list[dict] | dict) -> list[str]:
    51→    """Parse optional reviewed-file list from import payload."""
    52→    if not isinstance(data, dict):
    53→        return []
    54→    raw = data.get("reviewed_files")
    55→    if not isinstance(raw, list):
    56→        return []
    57→
    58→    reviewed: list[str] = []
    59→    seen: set[str] = set()
    60→    for item in raw:
    61→        if not isinstance(item, str):
    62→            continue
    63→        path = item.strip()
    64→        if not path or path in seen:
    65→            continue
    66→        seen.add(path)
    67→        reviewed.append(path)
    68→    return reviewed
    69→
    70→
    71→def parse_review_import_payload(
    72→    data: ReviewImportPayload | dict[str, Any],
    73→    *,
    74→    mode_name: str,
    75→) -> ReviewImportEnvelope:
    76→    """Parse shared review import payload shape for per-file/holistic flows."""
    77→    if not isinstance(data, dict):
    78→        raise ValueError(f"{mode_name} review import payload must be a JSON object")
    79→
    80→    missing_issues_error = f"{mode_name} review import payload must contain 'issues'"
    81→    key_error = normalize_legacy_findings_alias(
    82→        data,
    83→        missing_issues_error=missing_issues_error,
    84→    )
    85→    if key_error is not None:
    86→        raise ValueError(key_error)
    87→
    88→    issues_list = data.get("issues")
    89→    if not isinstance(issues_list, list):
    90→        raise ValueError(f"{mode_name} review import payload 'issues' must be a list")
    91→    for idx, entry in enumerate(issues_list):
    92→        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
    93→            raise ValueError(
    94→                f"{mode_name} review import payload 'issues[{idx}]' must be an object"
    95→            )
    96→
    97→    assessments = data.get("assessments")
    98→    if assessments is not None and not isinstance(assessments, dict):
    99→        raise ValueError(
   100→            f"{mode_name} review import payload 'assessments' must be an object"
   101→        )
   102→    return ReviewImportEnvelope(
   103→        issues=issues_list,
   104→        assessments=assessments,
   105→        reviewed_files=extract_reviewed_files(data),
   106→    )
   107→
   108→
   109→def normalize_review_confidence(value: object) -> str:
   110→    """Normalize review confidence labels to high/medium/low."""
   111→    confidence = str(value).strip().lower()
   112→    return confidence if confidence in {"high", "medium", "low"} else "low"
   113→
   114→
   115→def review_tier(confidence: str, *, holistic: bool) -> int:
   116→    """Derive natural tier from review confidence and scope."""
   117→    if confidence == "high":
   118→        return 1 if holistic else 3
   119→    if confidence == "medium":
   120→        return 2 if holistic else 3
   121→    return 3
   122→

1→"""Bridge between state persistence and scoring computation.

     3→This module owns the score-recomputation step that runs before state is written.

    30→def _resolve_lang_from_state(state: StateModel) -> str | None:
    31→    """Best-effort language detection from state (scan_history > lang_capabilities)."""
    32→    history = state.get("scan_history")
    33→    if isinstance(history, list):
    34→        for entry in reversed(history):
    35→            if isinstance(entry, dict):
    36→                lang = entry.get("lang")
    37→                if isinstance(lang, str) and lang.strip():
    38→                    return lang.strip().lower()
    39→    capabilities = state.get("lang_capabilities")
    40→    if isinstance(capabilities, dict) and len(capabilities) == 1:
    41→        only_lang = next(iter(capabilities.keys()))
    42→        if isinstance(only_lang, str) and only_lang.strip():
    43→            return only_lang.strip().lower()
    44→    return None

    47→def _count_issues(issues: dict) -> tuple[dict[str, int], dict[int, dict[str, int]]]:
    48→    """Tally per-status counters and per-tier breakdowns."""
    49→    counters = dict.fromkeys(_EMPTY_COUNTERS, 0)
    50→    tier_stats: dict[int, dict[str, int]] = {}
    51→
    52→    for issue in issues.values():
    53→        if issue.get("suppressed"):
    54→            continue
    55→        status = issue["status"]
    56→        tier = issue.get("tier", 3)
    57→        counters[status] = counters.get(status, 0) + 1
    58→        tier_counter = tier_stats.setdefault(tier, dict.fromkeys(_EMPTY_COUNTERS, 0))
    59→        tier_counter[status] = tier_counter.get(status, 0) + 1
    60→
    61→    return counters, tier_stats

    66→    raw = value.get("score", 0) if isinstance(value, dict) else value

    74→def _subjective_target_matches(

    96→
    97→def _apply_subjective_integrity_policy(
    98→    subjective_assessments: dict,

   102→    """Apply anti-gaming penalties for subjective scores clustered on the target."""
   103→    normalized_target = max(0.0, min(100.0, float(target)))

   113→        meta["status"] = "warn" if matched_dimensions else "pass"

   116→    adjusted = deepcopy(subjective_assessments)

   243→       *front* of ``queue_order`` so initial reviews are the first priority.

   245→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   246→    result = UnscoredDimensionSyncResult()

   249→    if plan.get("plan_start_scores"):

   253→    stale_ids = _current_stale_ids(state)

   257→    # Only prune IDs that are neither unscored nor stale (stale sync owns those).
   258→    _prune_subjective_ids(order, keep_ids=unscored_ids | stale_ids, pruned=result.pruned)
   259→
   260→    # --- Inject: prepend unscored IDs after any promoted items -------------
   261→    _inject_subjective_ids(order, plan, inject_ids=unscored_ids, to_front=True, injected=result.injected)
   262→

   269→
   270→def sync_stale_dimensions(
   271→    plan: PlanModel,
   272→    state: StateModel,
   273→    *,

   275→    cycle_just_completed: bool = False,
   276→) -> StaleDimensionSyncResult:

   278→

   280→       longer stale/under-target and not unscored (avoids pruning IDs owned
   281→       by ``sync_unscored_dimensions``).
   282→    2. Inject stale and under-target dimension IDs when either:
   283→       a. No objective items remain (mid-cycle: append to back), OR
   284→       b. A cycle just completed (post-cycle: insert at front so subjective
   285→          review takes priority over new objective issues).
   286→    """
   287→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   288→    result = StaleDimensionSyncResult()
   289→    stale_ids = _current_stale_ids(state)
   290→    under_target_ids = current_under_target_ids(state)
   291→    injectable_ids = stale_ids | under_target_ids
   292→    unscored_ids = current_unscored_ids(state)
   293→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   294→
   295→    # --- Cleanup: prune resolved subjective IDs --------------------------
   296→    # Only prune IDs that are no longer injectable and not unscored.
   297→    _prune_subjective_ids(order, keep_ids=injectable_ids | unscored_ids, pruned=result.pruned)
   298→
   299→    # --- Inject or evict stale + under-target dimensions -----------------
   300→    has_real_items = _has_objective_backlog(state, policy)
   301→    should_inject = not has_real_items or cycle_just_completed
   302→
   303→    if not should_inject:

   305→        # that are present in the queue.  They may have been grandfathered from
   306→        # the unscored phase and should not be visible until the objective
   307→        # backlog clears or a cycle completes.
   308→        to_evict = [
   309→            fid for fid in order
   310→            if fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX)
   311→            and fid in injectable_ids
   312→        ]
   313→        for fid in to_evict:
   314→            order.remove(fid)
   315→            result.pruned.append(fid)
   316→
   317→    if should_inject and injectable_ids:
   318→        to_front = cycle_just_completed and has_real_items
   319→        _inject_subjective_ids(order, plan, inject_ids=injectable_ids, to_front=to_front, injected=result.injected)
   320→

   348→def sync_triage_needed(
   349→    plan: PlanModel,
   350→    state: StateModel,
   351→) -> TriageSyncResult:
   352→    """Inject 4 triage stage IDs at front of queue when review issues change.
   353→
   354→    Only injects stages not already confirmed in ``epic_triage_meta``.
   355→
   356→    When stages are already present but all new issues have been resolved
   357→    since injection, auto-prunes the stale stages and updates the hash.
   358→
   359→    When issues are *resolved* (current IDs are a subset of previously
   360→    triaged IDs), the snapshot hash is updated silently — no re-triage
   361→    is needed since the user is working through the plan.
   362→    """
   363→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   364→    result = TriageSyncResult()
   365→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   366→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   367→    confirmed = set(meta.get("triage_stages", {}).keys())
   368→
   369→    # Check if any triage stage is already in queue
   370→    already_present = any(sid in order for sid in TRIAGE_IDS)
   371→
   372→    current_hash = review_issue_snapshot_hash(state)
   373→    last_hash = meta.get("issue_snapshot_hash", "")
   374→
   375→    if already_present:
   376→        # Stages present — check if the reason for injection still applies.
   377→        # Only auto-prune when triage was completed before (hash exists),
   378→        # all new issues have been resolved, and no triage work is in
   379→        # progress.  This avoids pruning the initial triage or a
   380→        # user-started triage session.
   381→        if last_hash and not confirmed:
   382→            new_since_triage = _new_review_ids_since_triage(state, meta)
   383→
   384→            if not new_since_triage:
   385→                # No new issues remain — prune stale stages
   386→                _prune_all_triage_stages(order)
   387→                if current_hash:
   388→                    meta["issue_snapshot_hash"] = current_hash
   389→                    plan["epic_triage_meta"] = meta
   390→                result.pruned = True
   391→        return result
   392→
   393→    if current_hash and current_hash != last_hash:
   394→        # Distinguish "new issues appeared" from "issues were resolved".
   395→        # Only re-triage when genuinely new issues exist.
   396→        new_since_triage = _new_review_ids_since_triage(state, meta)
   397→
   398→        if new_since_triage:
   399→            # New review issues appeared — re-triage needed
   400→            result.injected = _inject_pending_triage_stages(order, plan, confirmed)
   401→        else:
   402→            # Only resolved issues changed the hash — update silently
   403→            meta["issue_snapshot_hash"] = current_hash
   404→            plan["epic_triage_meta"] = meta
   405→
   406→    return result

   569→    Only injects when:
   570→    - Assessment mode was ``issues_only`` (scores were skipped)
   571→    - ``workflow::import-scores`` is not already in the queue
   572→    - There are assessments in the payload that could be imported
   573→
   574→    Positioned after score-checkpoint, before create-plan.
   575→    """
   576→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   577→    result = ImportScoresSyncResult()
   578→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   579→
   580→    if WORKFLOW_IMPORT_SCORES_ID in order:
   581→        return result
   582→
   583→    # Only inject when scores were skipped (issues-only mode)
   584→    if assessment_mode != "issues_only":
   585→        return result
   586→
   587→    # Insert after any subjective/workflow items
   588→    insert_at = 0
   589→    for i, fid in enumerate(order):
   590→        if fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX) or fid.startswith(WORKFLOW_PREFIX):
   591→            insert_at = i + 1
   592→    order.insert(insert_at, WORKFLOW_IMPORT_SCORES_ID)
   593→    result.injected = True
   594→    return result
   595→
   596→
   597→@dataclass
   598→class CommunicateScoreSyncResult:
   599→    """What changed during a communicate-score sync."""
   600→
   601→    injected: bool = False
   602→
   603→    @property
   604→    def changes(self) -> int:
   605→        return int(self.injected)
   606→
   607→
   608→def sync_communicate_score_needed(
   609→    plan: PlanModel,
   610→    state: StateModel,
   611→    *,
   612→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility | None = None,
   613→    scores_just_imported: bool = False,
   614→) -> CommunicateScoreSyncResult:
   615→    """Inject ``workflow::communicate-score`` when scores should be shown.
   616→
   617→    Injects when either:
   618→    - All initial subjective reviews are complete (no unscored dimensions), OR
   619→    - Scores were just imported (trusted/attested/override)
   620→
   621→    And ``workflow::communicate-score`` is not already in the queue.
   622→    Positioned after subjective items but before triage/create-plan.
   623→    """
   624→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   625→    result = CommunicateScoreSyncResult()
   626→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   627→
   628→    # Also treat legacy score-checkpoint as already-present
   629→    if WORKFLOW_COMMUNICATE_SCORE_ID in order or WORKFLOW_SCORE_CHECKPOINT_ID in order:
   630→        return result
   631→
   632→    # Trigger 1: scores just imported
   633→    should_inject = scores_just_imported
   634→
   635→    # Trigger 2: all initial reviews complete (no unscored dimensions)
   636→    if not should_inject:
   637→        if policy is not None:
   638→            should_inject = not policy.unscored_ids
   639→        else:
   640→            should_inject = not current_unscored_ids(state)
   641→
   642→    if not should_inject:
   643→        return result
   644→
   645→    # Insert after any subjective items, before triage/workflow/issues
   646→    insert_at = 0
   647→    for i, fid in enumerate(order):
   648→        if fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX):
   649→            insert_at = i + 1
   650→    order.insert(insert_at, WORKFLOW_COMMUNICATE_SCORE_ID)
   651→    result.injected = True
   652→    return result
   653→
   654→
   655→__all__ = [
   656→    "SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX",

    30→def _detect_subprocess_no_timeout(
    31→    filepath: str,
    32→    tree: ast.Module,
    33→    *,
    34→    all_nodes: tuple[ast.AST, ...] | None = None,
    35→) -> list[dict]:
    36→    """Flag subprocess.run/Popen/call/check_call/check_output without timeout=."""
    37→    _SUBPROCESS_FUNCS = {"run", "Popen", "call", "check_call", "check_output"}
    38→    results: list[dict] = []
    39→    for node in _iter_nodes(tree, all_nodes, ast.Call):
    40→        # Match subprocess.run(...) or subprocess.call(...) etc.
    41→        func = node.func
    42→        if isinstance(func, ast.Attribute) and func.attr in _SUBPROCESS_FUNCS:
    43→            # Check if the receiver is 'subprocess'
    44→            if isinstance(func.value, ast.Name) and func.value.id == "subprocess":
    45→                has_timeout = any(kw.arg == "timeout" for kw in node.keywords)
    46→                if not has_timeout:
    47→                    results.append(
    48→                        {
    49→                            "file": filepath,
    50→                            "line": node.lineno,
    51→                            "content": f"subprocess.{func.attr}() without timeout",
    52→                        }
    53→                    )
    54→    return results
    55→
    56→
    57→def _detect_unsafe_file_write(
    58→    filepath: str,
    59→    tree: ast.Module,
    60→    *,
    61→    all_nodes: tuple[ast.AST, ...] | None = None,
    62→) -> list[dict]:
    63→    """Flag Path.write_text/write_bytes and open(..., 'w') without atomic pattern.
    64→
    65→    Looks for .write_text() or .write_bytes() calls that aren't preceded by
    66→    a nearby os.replace() or os.rename() call in the same function.
    67→    Also flags open(file, 'w') without evidence of temp+rename.
    68→    """
    69→    results: list[dict] = []
    70→    for node in _iter_nodes(tree, all_nodes, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
    71→        # Collect all method calls and check for atomic patterns in this function
    72→        has_atomic_pattern = False
    73→        write_calls: list[ast.Call] = []
    74→
    75→        for child in ast.walk(node):
    76→            if not isinstance(child, ast.Call):
    77→                continue
    78→            func = child.func
    79→
    80→            # Check for os.replace or os.rename (indicates atomic write pattern)
    81→            if isinstance(func, ast.Attribute) and func.attr in ("replace", "rename"):
    82→                if isinstance(func.value, ast.Name) and func.value.id == "os":
    83→                    has_atomic_pattern = True
    84→
    85→            # Check for shutil.move (also indicates careful file handling)
    86→            if isinstance(func, ast.Attribute) and func.attr == "move":
    87→                if isinstance(func.value, ast.Name) and func.value.id == "shutil":
    88→                    has_atomic_pattern = True
    89→
    90→            # Collect .write_text() and .write_bytes() calls
    91→            if isinstance(func, ast.Attribute) and func.attr in (
    92→                "write_text",
    93→                "write_bytes",
    94→            ):
    95→                write_calls.append(child)
    96→
    97→        # Only flag if no atomic pattern exists in the same function
    98→        if not has_atomic_pattern:
    99→            for call in write_calls:
   100→                results.append(
   101→                    {
   102→                        "file": filepath,
   103→                        "line": call.lineno,
   104→                        "content": f".{call.func.attr}() in {node.name}() without atomic write pattern",
   105→                    }
   106→                )
   107→    return results
   108→
   109→
   110→def _detect_regex_backtrack(
   111→    filepath: str,
   112→    tree: ast.Module,
   113→    *,
   114→    all_nodes: tuple[ast.AST, ...] | None = None,
   115→) -> list[dict]:
   116→    """Flag regex patterns vulnerable to catastrophic backtracking (ReDoS).
   117→
   118→    Detects nested quantifiers like (a+)+, (a*)*b, ([^)]*|.)*,
   119→    and overlapping alternation inside quantifiers.
   120→    """
   121→    _RE_FUNCS = {
   122→        "compile",
   123→        "search",
   124→        "match",
   125→        "fullmatch",
   126→        "findall",
   127→        "finditer",
   128→        "sub",
   129→        "subn",
   130→        "split",
   131→    }
   132→    # Nested quantifier: group with inner +/* quantifier, outer +/* quantifier.
   133→    # Only + and * are dangerous — ? (zero-or-one) can never cause ReDoS.
   134→    _NESTED_QUANT = re.compile(
   135→        r"\([^)]*[+*][^)]*\)[+*]"  # (stuff+stuff)+ or (stuff*stuff)*
   136→        r"|"
   137→        r"\(\?:[^)]*[+*][^)]*\)[+*]"  # (?:stuff+stuff)+
   138→    )
   139→
   140→    results: list[dict] = []
   141→    for node in _iter_nodes(tree, all_nodes, ast.Call):
   142→        # Match re.X(...) or compiled.X(...)
   143→        func = node.func
   144→        if isinstance(func, ast.Attribute) and func.attr in _RE_FUNCS:
   145→            if isinstance(func.value, ast.Name) and func.value.id == "re":
   146→                pass  # re.compile(...) etc.
   147→            else:
   148→                continue
   149→        elif isinstance(func, ast.Name) and func.id in _RE_FUNCS:
   150→            pass  # Bare compile(...) etc. (rare)
   151→        else:
   152→            continue
   153→
   154→        # Extract pattern string from first arg
   155→        if not node.args:
   156→            continue
   157→        pat_node = node.args[0]
   158→        if not isinstance(pat_node, ast.Constant) or not isinstance(
   159→            pat_node.value, str
   160→        ):
   161→            continue
   162→        pattern = pat_node.value
   163→
   164→        # Check for nested quantifiers
   165→        m_bt = _NESTED_QUANT.search(pattern)
   166→        if not m_bt:
   167→            continue
   168→
   169→        # Extract the flagged fragment for safety checks
   170→        frag = m_bt.group(0)
   171→
   172→        # Safe: negated character classes [^X]+ can't overlap with adjacent chars
   173→        if re.search(r"\[\^[^\]]+\][+*]", frag):
   174→            continue
   175→
   176→        # Safe: inner quantifier is on a literal-anchored subpattern like \.\w+
   177→        # The required literal prevents ambiguous backtracking
   178→        if re.search(r"\\.\w*[+*]", frag):
   179→            continue
   180→
   181→        results.append(
   182→            {
   183→                "file": filepath,
   184→                "line": node.lineno,
   185→                "content": f"pattern: {pattern[:80]}",
   186→            }
   187→        )
   188→    return results
   189→
   190→
   191→def _detect_naive_comment_strip(
   192→    filepath: str,
   193→    tree: ast.Module,
   194→    *,
   195→    all_nodes: tuple[ast.AST, ...] | None = None,
   196→) -> list[dict]:
   197→    """Flag re.sub() calls that strip comments without string awareness.
   198→
   199→    Detects patterns like re.sub(r"//[^\\n]*", "") or re.sub(r"/\\*.*?\\*/", "")
   200→    which corrupt URLs and other legitimate // or /* sequences inside strings.
   201→    """
   202→    _COMMENT_PATTERNS = (
   203→        r"//",  # Line comment stripping
   204→        r"/\*",  # Block comment stripping
   205→        r"#[^\n]",  # Python comment stripping (when applied to non-Python content)
   206→    )
   207→
   208→    results: list[dict] = []
   209→    for node in _iter_nodes(tree, all_nodes, ast.Call):
   210→        func = node.func
   211→        # Match re.sub(...)
   212→        if not (
   213→            isinstance(func, ast.Attribute)
   214→            and func.attr == "sub"
   215→            and isinstance(func.value, ast.Name)
   216→            and func.value.id == "re"
   217→        ):
   218→            continue
   219→
   220→        if len(node.args) < 2:
   221→            continue
   222→        pat_node = node.args[0]
   223→        if not isinstance(pat_node, ast.Constant) or not isinstance(
   224→            pat_node.value, str
   225→        ):
   226→            continue
   227→        pattern = pat_node.value
   228→
   229→        # Check if this is a comment-stripping pattern
   230→        for comment_sig in _COMMENT_PATTERNS:
   231→            if comment_sig in pattern:
   232→                # Check replacement is empty or whitespace
   233→                repl_node = node.args[1]
   234→                if isinstance(repl_node, ast.Constant) and isinstance(
   235→                    repl_node.value, str
   236→                ):
   237→                    if repl_node.value.strip() == "":
   238→                        results.append(
   239→                            {
   240→                                "file": filepath,
   241→                                "line": node.lineno,
   242→                                "content": f're.sub(r"{pattern[:60]}", "") — not string-aware',
   243→                            }
   244→                        )
   245→                        break
   246→    return results

    10→    "Read .desloppify/query.json for context, excerpts, and investigation batches",
    11→    "For each batch: start from listed seed files, then explore likely hotspots/unreviewed neighbors; evaluate the batch's dimensions (batches are independent — parallelize)",
    12→    "Cross-reference issues with the sibling_behavior and convention data",
    13→    "IMPORTANT: issues must be defects only — never positive observations. High scores capture quality; issues capture problems.",
    14→    "Write ALL issues to issues.json — do NOT fix code before importing. Import creates tracked state entries that let desloppify correlate fixes to issues.",
    15→    "Codex: desloppify review --run-batches --runner codex --parallel --scan-after-import",
    16→    "Claude / other agent: desloppify review --run-batches --dry-run → launch one subagent per prompt file (all in parallel) → desloppify review --import-run <run-dir> --scan-after-import",
    17→    "Cloud/external: run `desloppify review --external-start --external-runner claude`, follow the session template, then run the printed `--external-submit` command",
    18→    "Fallback path: `desloppify review --import issues.json` (issues only). Use manual override only for emergency/provisional imports.",

    22→
    23→def append_full_sweep_batch(
    24→    *,
    25→    batches: list[dict[str, Any]],
    26→    dims: list[str],
    27→    all_files: list[str],
    28→    lang: Any,
    29→    max_files: int | None = None,
    30→) -> None:
    31→    """Append an optional cross-cutting full-codebase batch."""
    32→    if not dims:
    33→        return
    34→    all_rel_files: list[str] = []
    35→    for filepath in all_files:
    36→        if lang.zone_map is not None:
    37→            zone = lang.zone_map.get(filepath)
    38→            if zone.value in ("test", "generated", "vendor"):
    39→                continue
    40→        all_rel_files.append(rel(filepath))
    41→        if isinstance(max_files, int) and max_files > 0 and len(all_rel_files) >= max_files:
    42→            break
    43→    if not all_rel_files:
    44→        return
    45→    batches.append(
    46→        {
    47→            "name": "Full Codebase Sweep",
    48→            "dimensions": list(dims),
    49→            "files_to_read": all_rel_files,
    50→            "why": "thorough default: evaluate cross-cutting quality across all production files",
    51→        }
    52→    )
