   105→    print("    5. Proceed to the next stage.\n")
   106→    print("  After all 5 stages:")
   107→    print('    desloppify plan triage --complete --strategy "..." --attestation "..."\n')
   108→    print(colorize("  Key rules:", "yellow"))
   109→    print("    - ONE subagent per stage. Don't combine stages.")
   110→    print("    - Check the dashboard between stages.")
   111→    print("    - Observe subagent should use sub-subagents (one per dimension group).")
   112→    print("    - Enrich subagent should use sub-subagents (one per cluster).")
   113→    print("    - Sense-check launches TWO parallel subagents (content + structure).")
   114→    print("    - If a stage fails validation, fix and re-record.")

   117→def _merge_observe_outputs(
   118→    batch_outputs: list[tuple[list[str], Path]],
   119→) -> str:
   120→    """Concatenate batch outputs with dimension headers into single observe report."""
   121→    parts: list[str] = []
   122→    for dims, output_file in batch_outputs:
   123→        header = f"## Dimensions: {', '.join(dims)}"
   124→        content = ""
   125→        if output_file.exists():
   126→            try:
   127→                content = output_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").strip()
   128→            except OSError:
   129→                content = "(batch output missing)"
   130→        if not content:
   131→            content = "(batch produced no output)"
   132→        parts.append(f"{header}\n\n{content}")
   133→    return "\n\n---\n\n".join(parts)
   134→
   135→
   136→def _run_observe(
   137→    *,
   138→    si,
   139→    repo_root: Path,
   140→    prompts_dir: Path,
   141→    output_dir: Path,
   142→    logs_dir: Path,
   143→    timeout_seconds: int,
   144→    dry_run: bool = False,
   145→    append_run_log=None,
   146→) -> tuple[bool, str]:
   147→    """Run observe stage via codex subprocess batches.
   148→
   149→    Returns (ok, merged_report) where ok is True on success, False on failure.
   150→    """
   151→    from functools import partial
   152→
   153→    from desloppify.app.commands.review._runner_parallel_types import BatchProgressEvent
   154→
   155→    from .codex_runner import _output_file_has_text, run_triage_stage
   156→
   157→    _log = append_run_log or (lambda _msg: None)
   158→
   159→    batches = group_issues_into_observe_batches(si)
   160→    total = len(batches)
   161→    print(colorize(f"\n  Observe: splitting into {total} parallel batches.", "bold"))
   162→    _log(f"observe-parallel batches={total}")
   163→
   164→    # Build prompts and tasks
   165→    tasks: dict[int, object] = {}
   166→    batch_meta: list[tuple[list[str], Path]] = []
   167→
   168→    for i, (dims, issues_subset) in enumerate(batches):
   169→        prompt = build_observe_batch_prompt(
   170→            batch_index=i + 1,
   171→            total_batches=total,
   172→            dimension_group=dims,
   173→            issues_subset=issues_subset,
   174→            repo_root=repo_root,
   175→        )
   176→        prompt_file = prompts_dir / f"observe_batch_{i}.md"
   177→        safe_write_text(prompt_file, prompt)
   178→
   179→        output_file = output_dir / f"observe_batch_{i}.raw.txt"
   180→        log_file = logs_dir / f"observe_batch_{i}.log"
   181→        batch_meta.append((dims, output_file))
   182→
   183→        if not dry_run:
   184→            tasks[i] = partial(
   185→                run_triage_stage,
   186→                prompt=prompt,
   187→                repo_root=repo_root,
   188→                output_file=output_file,
   189→                log_file=log_file,
   190→                timeout_seconds=timeout_seconds,
   191→                validate_output_fn=_output_file_has_text,
   192→            )
   193→
   194→        dim_list = ", ".join(dims)
   195→        print(colorize(f"    Batch {i + 1}: {len(issues_subset)} issues ({dim_list})", "dim"))
   196→        _log(f"observe-batch batch={i + 1} issues={len(issues_subset)} dims={dim_list}")
   197→
   198→    if dry_run:
   199→        print(colorize("  [dry-run] Would execute parallel observe batches.", "dim"))
   200→        return True, ""
   201→
   202→    # Progress callback — same pattern as review batch execution
   203→    def _progress(event: BatchProgressEvent) -> None:
   204→        idx = event.batch_index
   205→        if event.event == "start":
   206→            print(colorize(f"    Observe batch {idx + 1}/{total} started", "dim"))
   207→            _log(f"observe-batch-start batch={idx + 1}")
   208→        elif event.event == "done":
   209→            elapsed = event.details.get("elapsed_seconds", 0) if event.details else 0
   210→            status = "done" if event.code == 0 else f"failed ({event.code})"
   211→            tone = "dim" if event.code == 0 else "yellow"
   212→            print(colorize(f"    Observe batch {idx + 1}/{total} {status} in {int(elapsed)}s", tone))
   213→            _log(f"observe-batch-done batch={idx + 1} code={event.code} elapsed={int(elapsed)}s")
   214→        elif event.event == "heartbeat":
   215→            details = event.details or {}
   216→            active = details.get("active_batches", [])
   217→            elapsed_map = details.get("elapsed_seconds", {})
   218→            if active:
   219→                parts = [f"#{i + 1}:{int(elapsed_map.get(i, 0))}s" for i in active[:6]]
   220→                print(colorize(f"    Observe heartbeat: {len(active)}/{total} active ({', '.join(parts)})", "dim"))
   221→
   222→    def _error_log(batch_index: int, exc: Exception) -> None:
   223→        _log(f"observe-batch-error batch={batch_index + 1} error={exc}")
   224→
   225→    # Execute in parallel
   226→    failures = execute_batches(
   227→        tasks=tasks,
   228→        options=BatchExecutionOptions(run_parallel=True, heartbeat_seconds=15.0),
   229→        progress_fn=_progress,
   230→        error_log_fn=_error_log,
   231→    )
   232→
   233→    if failures:
   234→        print(colorize(
   235→            f"  Observe: {len(failures)} batch(es) failed: {failures}",
   236→            "red",
   237→        ))
   238→        for idx in failures:
   239→            log_file = logs_dir / f"observe_batch_{idx}.log"
   240→            print(colorize(f"    Check log: {log_file}", "dim"))
   241→        _log(f"observe-parallel-failed failures={failures}")
   242→        return False, ""
   243→
   244→    merged = _merge_observe_outputs(batch_meta)
   245→    print(colorize(f"  Observe: merged {total} batch outputs ({len(merged)} chars).", "green"))
   246→    _log(f"observe-parallel-done merged_chars={len(merged)}")
   247→    return True, merged
   248→
   249→
   250→def _run_codex_pipeline(
   251→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   252→    *,
   253→    services: TriageServices | None = None,
   254→) -> None:
   255→    """Run triage stages via Codex subprocesses (automated pipeline)."""
   256→    from .codex_runner import run_triage_stage
   257→
   258→    resolved_services = services or default_triage_services()
   259→    timeout_seconds = int(getattr(args, "stage_timeout_seconds", 1800) or 1800)
   260→    dry_run = bool(getattr(args, "dry_run", False))
   261→
   262→    try:
   263→        stages_to_run = _parse_only_stages(getattr(args, "only_stages", None))
   264→    except ValueError as exc:
   265→        print(colorize(f"  {exc}", "red"))
   266→        return
   267→
   268→    repo_root = get_project_root()
   269→    plan = resolved_services.load_plan()
   270→    _ensure_triage_started(plan, resolved_services)
   271→
   272→    # Create run directory
   273→    stamp = _run_stamp()
   274→    desloppify_dir = repo_root / ".desloppify"
   275→    run_dir = desloppify_dir / "triage_runs" / stamp
   276→    prompts_dir = run_dir / "prompts"
   277→    output_dir = run_dir / "output"
   278→    logs_dir = run_dir / "logs"
   279→    for d in (prompts_dir, output_dir, logs_dir):
   280→        d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   281→
   282→    # Run log — same pattern as review batch execution
   283→    run_log_path = run_dir / "run.log"
   284→    append_run_log = make_run_log_writer(run_log_path)
   285→    append_run_log(
   286→        f"run-start runner=codex stages={','.join(stages_to_run)} "
   287→        f"timeout={timeout_seconds}s dry_run={dry_run}"
   288→    )
   289→
   290→    print(colorize(f"  Run artifacts: {run_dir}", "dim"))
   291→    print(colorize(f"  Live run log:  {run_log_path}", "dim"))
   292→
   293→    # Collect triage input
   294→    runtime = resolved_services.command_runtime(args)
   295→    state = runtime.state
   296→
   297→    prior_reports: dict[str, str] = {}
   298→    stage_results: dict[str, dict] = {}
   299→    pipeline_start = time.monotonic()
   300→
   301→    for stage in stages_to_run:
   302→        plan = resolved_services.load_plan()
   303→        meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   304→        stages = meta.get("triage_stages", {})
   305→
   306→        # Skip if already confirmed (resume support)
   307→        if stage in stages and stages[stage].get("confirmed_at"):
   308→            print(colorize(f"  Stage {stage}: already confirmed, skipping.", "green"))
   309→            append_run_log(f"stage-skip stage={stage} reason=already_confirmed")
   310→            stage_results[stage] = {"status": "skipped"}
   311→            report = stages[stage].get("report", "")
   312→            if report:
   313→                prior_reports[stage] = report
   314→            continue
   315→
   316→        stage_start = time.monotonic()
   317→        append_run_log(f"stage-start stage={stage}")
   318→
   319→        # Collect fresh triage input each stage
   320→        si = resolved_services.collect_triage_input(plan, state)
   321→
   322→        # Parallel observe path
   323→        used_parallel = False
   324→        if stage == "observe":
   325→            parallel_ok, merged_report = _run_observe(
   326→                si=si,
   327→                repo_root=repo_root,
   328→                prompts_dir=prompts_dir,
   329→                output_dir=output_dir,
   330→                logs_dir=logs_dir,
   331→                timeout_seconds=timeout_seconds,
   332→                dry_run=dry_run,
   333→                append_run_log=append_run_log,
   334→            )
   335→            if parallel_ok is True and dry_run:
   336→                stage_results[stage] = {"status": "dry_run"}
   337→                continue
   338→            if parallel_ok is True and merged_report:
   339→                # Record observe via the stage command with merged report
   340→                from ..stage_flow_commands import cmd_stage_observe
   341→                record_args = argparse.Namespace(
   342→                    stage="observe",
   343→                    report=merged_report,
   344→                    state=getattr(args, "state", None),
   345→                )
   346→                cmd_stage_observe(record_args, services=resolved_services)
   347→                used_parallel = True
   348→            elif parallel_ok is False:
   349→                # Parallel execution failed — abort pipeline
   350→                elapsed = int(time.monotonic() - stage_start)
   351→                print(colorize("  Observe: parallel execution failed. Aborting.", "red"))
   352→                append_run_log(f"stage-failed stage=observe elapsed={elapsed}s reason=parallel_execution_failed")
   353→                stage_results[stage] = {"status": "failed", "elapsed_seconds": elapsed}
   354→                _write_triage_run_summary(run_dir, stamp, stages_to_run, stage_results, append_run_log)
   355→                return
   356→            # parallel_ok is None → not applicable, fall through to single path
   357→
   358→        # Parallel sense-check path
   359→        if stage == "sense-check":
   360→            parallel_ok, merged_report = _run_sense_check(
   361→                plan=plan,
   362→                repo_root=repo_root,
   363→                prompts_dir=prompts_dir,
   364→                output_dir=output_dir,
   365→                logs_dir=logs_dir,
   366→                timeout_seconds=timeout_seconds,
   367→                dry_run=dry_run,
   368→                append_run_log=append_run_log,
   369→            )
   370→            if parallel_ok is True and dry_run:
   371→                stage_results[stage] = {"status": "dry_run"}
   372→                continue
   373→            if parallel_ok is True and merged_report:
   374→                # Subagents mutated plan via CLI; reload and record stage
   375→                plan = resolved_services.load_plan()
   376→                from ..stage_flow_commands import cmd_stage_sense_check
   377→                record_args = argparse.Namespace(
   378→                    stage="sense-check",
   379→                    report=merged_report,
   380→                    state=getattr(args, "state", None),
   381→                )
   382→                cmd_stage_sense_check(record_args, services=resolved_services)
   383→                used_parallel = True
   384→            elif parallel_ok is False:
   385→                elapsed = int(time.monotonic() - stage_start)
   386→                print(colorize("  Sense-check: parallel execution failed. Aborting.", "red"))
   387→                append_run_log(f"stage-failed stage=sense-check elapsed={elapsed}s reason=parallel_execution_failed")
   388→                stage_results[stage] = {"status": "failed", "elapsed_seconds": elapsed}
   389→                _write_triage_run_summary(run_dir, stamp, stages_to_run, stage_results, append_run_log)
   390→                return
   391→
   392→        # Single-subprocess path (non-observe/sense-check stages, or observe with too few issues)
   393→        if not used_parallel:
   394→            prompt = build_stage_prompt(
   395→                stage, si, prior_reports, repo_root=repo_root,
   396→            )
   397→
   398→            prompt_file = prompts_dir / f"{stage}.md"
   399→            safe_write_text(prompt_file, prompt)
   400→
   401→            if dry_run:
   402→                print(colorize(f"  Stage {stage}: prompt written to {prompt_file}", "cyan"))
   403→                print(colorize("  [dry-run] Would execute codex subprocess.", "dim"))
   404→                stage_results[stage] = {"status": "dry_run"}
   405→                continue
   406→
   407→            print(colorize(f"\n  Stage {stage}: launching codex subprocess...", "bold"))
   408→            append_run_log(f"stage-subprocess-start stage={stage}")
   409→
   410→            output_file = output_dir / f"{stage}.raw.txt"
   411→            log_file = logs_dir / f"{stage}.log"
   412→
   413→            exit_code = run_triage_stage(
   414→                prompt=prompt,
   415→                repo_root=repo_root,
   416→                output_file=output_file,
   417→                log_file=log_file,
   418→                timeout_seconds=timeout_seconds,
   419→            )
   420→
   421→            elapsed = int(time.monotonic() - stage_start)
   422→            append_run_log(f"stage-subprocess-done stage={stage} code={exit_code} elapsed={elapsed}s")
   423→
   424→            if exit_code != 0:
   425→                print(colorize(f"  Stage {stage}: codex subprocess failed (exit {exit_code}).", "red"))
   426→                print(colorize(f"  Check log: {log_file}", "dim"))
   427→                print(colorize("  Re-run to resume (confirmed stages are skipped).", "dim"))
   428→                append_run_log(f"stage-failed stage={stage} elapsed={elapsed}s code={exit_code}")
   429→                stage_results[stage] = {"status": "failed", "exit_code": exit_code, "elapsed_seconds": elapsed}
   430→                _write_triage_run_summary(run_dir, stamp, stages_to_run, stage_results, append_run_log)
   431→                return
   432→
   433→        # Common path: reload for validation
   434→        plan = resolved_services.load_plan()
   435→        meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   436→        stages_data = meta.get("triage_stages", {})
   437→
   438→        # Validate stage
   439→        ok, error_msg = validate_stage(stage, plan, state, repo_root, triage_input=si)
   440→        if not ok:
   441→            elapsed = int(time.monotonic() - stage_start)
   442→            print(colorize(f"  Stage {stage}: validation failed: {error_msg}", "red"))
   443→            print(colorize("  Re-run to resume.", "dim"))
   444→            append_run_log(f"stage-validation-failed stage={stage} elapsed={elapsed}s error={error_msg}")
   445→            stage_results[stage] = {"status": "validation_failed", "elapsed_seconds": elapsed, "error": error_msg}
   446→            _write_triage_run_summary(run_dir, stamp, stages_to_run, stage_results, append_run_log)
   447→            return
   448→
   449→        # Auto-confirm via confirmation functions with generated attestation
   450→        attestation = build_auto_attestation(stage, plan, si)
   451→
   452→        # Build a synthetic args namespace for confirm functions
   453→        confirm_args = argparse.Namespace(
   454→            confirm=stage,
   455→            attestation=attestation,
   456→            state=getattr(args, "state", None),
   457→        )
   458→
   459→        from ..confirmations import _cmd_confirm_stage
   460→        _cmd_confirm_stage(confirm_args, services=resolved_services)
   461→
   462→        # Re-load and check confirmation took effect
   463→        plan = resolved_services.load_plan()
   464→        meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   465→        stages_data = meta.get("triage_stages", {})
   466→        elapsed = int(time.monotonic() - stage_start)
   467→        if stage in stages_data and stages_data[stage].get("confirmed_at"):
   468→            print(colorize(f"  Stage {stage}: confirmed ({elapsed}s).", "green"))
   469→            append_run_log(f"stage-confirmed stage={stage} elapsed={elapsed}s")
   470→            stage_results[stage] = {"status": "confirmed", "elapsed_seconds": elapsed}
   471→        else:
   472→            print(colorize(f"  Stage {stage}: auto-confirmation did not take effect.", "red"))
   473→            print(colorize("  Re-run to resume.", "dim"))
   474→            append_run_log(f"stage-confirm-failed stage={stage} elapsed={elapsed}s")
   475→            stage_results[stage] = {"status": "confirm_failed", "elapsed_seconds": elapsed}
   476→            _write_triage_run_summary(run_dir, stamp, stages_to_run, stage_results, append_run_log)
   477→            return
   478→
   479→        # Accumulate report for next stage's prompt
   480→        report = stages_data.get(stage, {}).get("report", "")
   481→        if report:
   482→            prior_reports[stage] = report
   483→
   484→    if dry_run:
   485→        print(colorize("\n  [dry-run] All prompts generated. No stages executed.", "cyan"))
   486→        _write_triage_run_summary(run_dir, stamp, stages_to_run, stage_results, append_run_log)
   487→        return
   488→
   489→    # Auto-complete triage
   490→    plan = resolved_services.load_plan()
   491→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   492→    stages_data = meta.get("triage_stages", {})
   493→
   494→    # Derive strategy from all stage reports
   495→    strategy_parts: list[str] = []
   496→    for s in _STAGES:
   497→        report = stages_data.get(s, {}).get("report", "")
   498→        if report:
   499→            strategy_parts.append(f"[{s}] {report[:200]}")
   500→    strategy = " ".join(strategy_parts)
   501→    if len(strategy) < 200:
   502→        strategy = strategy + " " + "Automated triage via codex subagent pipeline. " * 3
   503→
   504→    print(colorize("\n  Completing triage...", "bold"))
   505→
   506→    # Build attestation for completion
   507→    attestation = build_auto_attestation("sense-check", plan, si)
   508→    complete_args = argparse.Namespace(
   509→        complete=True,
   510→        strategy=strategy[:2000],
   511→        attestation=attestation,
   512→        state=getattr(args, "state", None),
   513→    )
   514→
   515→    from ..stage_completion_commands import _cmd_triage_complete
   516→    _cmd_triage_complete(complete_args, services=resolved_services)
   517→
   518→    total_elapsed = int(time.monotonic() - pipeline_start)
   519→    print(colorize(f"\n  Triage pipeline complete ({total_elapsed}s).", "green"))
   520→    append_run_log(f"run-finished elapsed={total_elapsed}s")
   521→    _write_triage_run_summary(run_dir, stamp, stages_to_run, stage_results, append_run_log)
   522→
   523→
   524→def _run_sense_check(
   525→    *,
   526→    plan: dict,
   527→    repo_root: Path,
   528→    prompts_dir: Path,
   529→    output_dir: Path,
   530→    logs_dir: Path,
   531→    timeout_seconds: int,
   532→    dry_run: bool = False,
   533→    append_run_log=None,
   534→) -> tuple[bool, str]:
   535→    """Run sense-check via two parallel codex subprocess batches.
   536→
   537→    Returns (ok, merged_report) where ok is True on success.
   538→    Launches content batches (one per cluster) and one structure batch
   539→    in parallel.
   540→    """
   541→    from functools import partial
   542→
   543→    from desloppify.app.commands.review._runner_parallel_types import BatchProgressEvent
   544→
   545→    from .codex_runner import _output_file_has_text, run_triage_stage
   546→
   547→    _log = append_run_log or (lambda _msg: None)
   548→
   549→    clusters = manual_clusters_with_issues(plan)
   550→    total_content = len(clusters)
   551→    total = total_content + 1  # +1 for structure
   552→    print(colorize(f"\n  Sense-check: {total_content} content batches + 1 structure batch.", "bold"))
   553→    _log(f"sense-check-parallel content_batches={total_content}")
   554→
   555→    tasks: dict[int, object] = {}
   556→    batch_meta: list[tuple[str, Path]] = []  # (label, output_file)
   557→
   558→    # Content batches — one per cluster
   559→    for i, cluster_name in enumerate(clusters):
   560→        prompt = build_sense_check_content_prompt(
   561→            cluster_name=cluster_name,
   562→            plan=plan,
   563→            repo_root=repo_root,
   564→        )
   565→        prompt_file = prompts_dir / f"sense_check_content_{i}.md"
   566→        safe_write_text(prompt_file, prompt)
   567→
   568→        output_file = output_dir / f"sense_check_content_{i}.raw.txt"
   569→        log_file = logs_dir / f"sense_check_content_{i}.log"
   570→        batch_meta.append((f"content:{cluster_name}", output_file))
   571→
   572→        if not dry_run:
   573→            tasks[i] = partial(
   574→                run_triage_stage,
   575→                prompt=prompt,
   576→                repo_root=repo_root,
   577→                output_file=output_file,
   578→                log_file=log_file,
   579→                timeout_seconds=timeout_seconds,
   580→                validate_output_fn=_output_file_has_text,
   581→            )
   582→        print(colorize(f"    Content batch {i + 1}: {cluster_name}", "dim"))
   583→        _log(f"sense-check-content batch={i + 1} cluster={cluster_name}")
   584→
   585→    # Structure batch — single global
   586→    structure_idx = total_content
   587→    structure_prompt = build_sense_check_structure_prompt(
   588→        plan=plan,
   589→        repo_root=repo_root,
   590→    )
   591→    prompt_file = prompts_dir / "sense_check_structure.md"
   592→    safe_write_text(prompt_file, structure_prompt)
   593→
   594→    structure_output = output_dir / "sense_check_structure.raw.txt"
   595→    structure_log = logs_dir / "sense_check_structure.log"
   596→    batch_meta.append(("structure", structure_output))
   597→
   598→    if not dry_run:
   599→        tasks[structure_idx] = partial(
   600→            run_triage_stage,
   601→            prompt=structure_prompt,
   602→            repo_root=repo_root,
   603→            output_file=structure_output,
   604→            log_file=structure_log,
   605→            timeout_seconds=timeout_seconds,
   606→            validate_output_fn=_output_file_has_text,
   607→        )
   608→    print(colorize("    Structure batch: global dependency check", "dim"))
   609→    _log("sense-check-structure batch=global")
   610→
   611→    if dry_run:
   612→        print(colorize("  [dry-run] Would execute parallel sense-check batches.", "dim"))
   613→        return True, ""
   614→
   615→    def _progress(event: BatchProgressEvent) -> None:
   616→        idx = event.batch_index
   617→        label = batch_meta[idx][0] if idx < len(batch_meta) else f"batch-{idx}"
   618→        if event.event == "start":
   619→            print(colorize(f"    Sense-check {label} started", "dim"))
   620→            _log(f"sense-check-batch-start {label}")
   621→        elif event.event == "done":
   622→            elapsed = event.details.get("elapsed_seconds", 0) if event.details else 0
   623→            status = "done" if event.code == 0 else f"failed ({event.code})"
   624→            tone = "dim" if event.code == 0 else "yellow"
   625→            print(colorize(f"    Sense-check {label} {status} in {int(elapsed)}s", tone))
   626→            _log(f"sense-check-batch-done {label} code={event.code} elapsed={int(elapsed)}s")
   627→
   628→    def _error_log(batch_index: int, exc: Exception) -> None:
   629→        _log(f"sense-check-batch-error batch={batch_index} error={exc}")
   630→
   631→    failures = execute_batches(
   632→        tasks=tasks,
   633→        options=BatchExecutionOptions(run_parallel=True, heartbeat_seconds=15.0),
   634→        progress_fn=_progress,
   635→        error_log_fn=_error_log,
   636→    )
   637→
   638→    if failures:
   639→        print(colorize(
   640→            f"  Sense-check: {len(failures)} batch(es) failed: {failures}",
   641→            "red",
   642→        ))
   643→        _log(f"sense-check-parallel-failed failures={failures}")
   644→        return False, ""
   645→
   646→    # Merge outputs
   647→    parts: list[str] = []
   648→    for label, output_file in batch_meta:
   649→        content = ""
   650→        if output_file.exists():
   651→            try:
   652→                content = output_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").strip()
   653→            except OSError:
   654→                content = "(output missing)"
   655→        if not content:
   656→            content = "(no output)"
   657→        parts.append(f"## {label}\n\n{content}")
   658→
   659→    merged = "\n\n---\n\n".join(parts)
   660→    print(colorize(f"  Sense-check: merged {total} batch outputs ({len(merged)} chars).", "green"))
   661→    _log(f"sense-check-parallel-done merged_chars={len(merged)}")
   662→    return True, merged
   663→
   664→
   665→def _write_triage_run_summary(
   666→    run_dir: Path,
   667→    stamp: str,
   668→    stages: list[str],
   669→    stage_results: dict[str, dict],
   670→    append_run_log,
   671→) -> None:
   672→    """Write a run_summary.json with per-stage results."""
   673→    summary = {
   674→        "created_at": datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
   675→        "run_stamp": stamp,
   676→        "runner": "codex",
   677→        "stages_requested": stages,
   678→        "stage_results": stage_results,
   679→        "run_dir": str(run_dir),
   680→    }
   681→    summary_path = run_dir / "run_summary.json"
   682→    safe_write_text(summary_path, json.dumps(summary, indent=2) + "\n")
   683→    print(colorize(f"  Run summary: {summary_path}", "dim"))
   684→    append_run_log(f"run-summary {summary_path}")
   685→
   686→
   687→__all__ = ["do_run_triage_stages"]
   688→

1→"""Queue-order enforcement helpers for resolve command flows."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations

     5→import logging
     6→
     7→from desloppify.base.exception_sets import PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS
     8→from desloppify.base.output.terminal import colorize
     9→from desloppify.engine._work_queue.context import queue_context
    10→from desloppify.engine._work_queue.core import (
    11→    QueueBuildOptions,
    12→    build_work_queue,
    13→)
    14→from desloppify.engine._work_queue.plan_order import collapse_clusters
    15→from desloppify.engine.plan import has_living_plan, load_plan

    17→_logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

    20→def _front_item_ids(front_item: dict) -> tuple[str, set[str]]:
    21→    front_id = front_item["id"]
    22→    front_ids = {front_id}
    23→    if front_item.get("kind") != "cluster":
    24→        return front_id, front_ids
    25→    for member in front_item.get("members", []):
    26→        front_ids.add(member["id"])
    27→    return front_id, front_ids
    28→
    29→
    30→def _resolve_target_ids(patterns: list[str], clusters: dict) -> set[str]:
    31→    resolved_ids: set[str] = set()
    32→    for pattern in patterns:
    33→        if pattern in clusters:
    34→            resolved_ids.update(clusters[pattern].get("issue_ids", []))
    35→            resolved_ids.add(pattern)
    36→            continue
    37→        resolved_ids.add(pattern)
    38→    return resolved_ids
    39→
    40→
    41→def _filter_open_or_cluster_targets(
    42→    resolved_ids: set[str],
    43→    *,
    44→    clusters: dict,
    45→    issues: dict,
    46→) -> set[str]:
    47→    return {
    48→        issue_id
    49→        for issue_id in resolved_ids
    50→        if issue_id in clusters
    51→        or (issue_id in issues and issues[issue_id].get("status") == "open")
    52→    }
    53→
    54→
    55→def _prune_front_covered_clusters(
    56→    out_of_order: set[str],
    57→    *,
    58→    clusters: dict,
    59→    issues: dict,
    60→    front_ids: set[str],
    61→) -> None:
    62→    for cluster_id in list(out_of_order):
    63→        if cluster_id not in clusters:
    64→            continue
    65→        alive_members = {
    66→            issue_id
    67→            for issue_id in clusters[cluster_id].get("issue_ids", [])
    68→            if issue_id in issues and issues[issue_id].get("status") == "open"
    69→        }
    70→        if alive_members and alive_members <= front_ids:
    71→            out_of_order.discard(cluster_id)
    72→
    73→
    74→def _print_queue_order_violation(front_id: str, out_of_order: set[str]) -> None:
    75→    print(colorize("\n  Queue order violation: these items are not next in the plan queue:\n", "yellow"))
    76→    for issue_id in sorted(out_of_order):
    77→        print(f"    {issue_id}")
    78→    print(colorize(f"\n  The current next item is: {front_id}", "dim"))
    79→    print(colorize("  Items must be resolved in plan order. If you need to reprioritize:", "dim"))
    80→    print(colorize("    desloppify plan reorder <pattern> top            # move to front", "dim"))
    81→    print(colorize("    desloppify plan skip <pattern> --reason '...'    # skip for now", "dim"))
    82→    print(colorize("    desloppify next                                  # see what's next\n", "dim"))
    83→
    84→
    85→def _check_queue_order_guard(
    86→    state: dict,
    87→    patterns: list[str],
    88→    status: str,
    89→) -> bool:
    90→    """Warn and block if resolving items not at the front of the plan queue."""
    91→    if status != "fixed":
    92→        return False
    93→    try:
    94→        if not has_living_plan():
    95→            return False
    96→        plan = load_plan()
    97→        queue_order = plan.get("queue_order", [])
    98→        if not queue_order:
    99→            return False
   100→
   101→        ctx = queue_context(state, plan=plan)
   102→        result = build_work_queue(
   103→            state,
   104→            options=QueueBuildOptions(
   105→                count=None,
   106→                include_subjective=True,
   107→                context=ctx,
   108→            ),
   109→        )
   110→        items = result["items"]
   111→        if not plan.get("active_cluster"):
   112→            items = collapse_clusters(items, plan)
   113→        if not items:
   114→            return False
   115→
   116→        clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   117→        issues = state.get("issues", {})
   118→        resolved_ids = _resolve_target_ids(patterns, clusters)
   119→        resolved_ids = _filter_open_or_cluster_targets(
   120→            resolved_ids,
   121→            clusters=clusters,
   122→            issues=issues,
   123→        )
   124→        if not resolved_ids:
   125→            return False
   126→
   127→        # Collect IDs from the first N queue positions where N is the
   128→        # number of items being resolved.  This allows batch-resolving
   129→        # a contiguous prefix (e.g. the first 9 items in one command).
   130→        prefix_depth = max(len(resolved_ids), 1)
   131→        front_ids: set[str] = set()
   132→        front_id = items[0]["id"]
   133→        for item in items[:prefix_depth]:
   134→            _, item_ids = _front_item_ids(item)
   135→            front_ids.update(item_ids)
   136→
   137→        out_of_order = resolved_ids - front_ids
   138→        _prune_front_covered_clusters(
   139→            out_of_order,
   140→            clusters=clusters,
   141→            issues=issues,
   142→            front_ids=front_ids,
   143→        )
   144→        if not out_of_order:
   145→            return False
   146→
   147→        _print_queue_order_violation(front_id, out_of_order)
   148→        return True
   149→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS:
   150→        _logger.debug("queue order guard skipped", exc_info=True)
   151→        return False
   152→
   153→
   154→__all__ = ["_check_queue_order_guard"]

    40→def _validate_resolve_inputs(args: argparse.Namespace, attestation: str | None) -> None:

    61→def _preview_resolve_count(state: dict, patterns: list[str]) -> int:
    62→    """Count unique open issues matching the provided patterns."""
    63→    matched_ids: set[str] = set()
    64→    for pattern in patterns:
    65→        for issue in state_mod.match_issues(state, pattern, status_filter="open"):
    66→            issue_id = issue.get("id")
    67→            if issue_id:

    73→    state: dict,
    74→    args: argparse.Namespace,
    75→    *,
    76→    attestation: str | None,
    77→    resolve_all_patterns_fn,
    78→) -> float:

    80→    before = state_mod.score_snapshot(state).strict
    81→    if before is None:
    82→        return 0.0
    83→
    84→    preview_state = copy.deepcopy(state)
    85→    resolve_all_patterns_fn(preview_state, args, attestation=attestation)
    86→    after = state_mod.score_snapshot(preview_state).strict
    87→    if after is None:
    88→        return 0.0
    89→    return max(0.0, before - after)
    90→

   114→    _emit_warning(f"Large wontfix batch detected ({preview_count} issues).")
   115→    if strict_delta > 0:

    24→            return None
    25→        plan = load_plan()
    26→        cluster = plan.get("clusters", {}).get(pattern)
    27→        if cluster and cluster.get("issue_ids"):
    28→            return list(cluster["issue_ids"])
    29→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS:
    30→        _logger.debug("cluster expansion skipped for %r", pattern, exc_info=True)
    31→    return None
    32→
    33→
    34→def _resolve_all_patterns(
    35→    state: dict,

    38→    attestation: str | None,

    24→def _execute_serial(

    37→        start_error = _emit_progress(

    41→            None,
    42→            details={"max_workers": 1},
    43→            contract_cache=contract_cache,

    45→        if start_error is not None:
    46→            _record_execution_error(

    52→        try:

    61→            code = 1

   313→        action = "desloppify review --prepare --dimensions " + ",".join(cli_keys)
   314→        changes += _sync_auto_cluster(

   381→
   382→def prune_stale_clusters(
   383→    plan: dict,
   384→    issues: dict,
   385→    clusters: dict,
   386→    active_auto_keys: set[str],
   387→    now: str,
   388→) -> int:
   389→    """Delete auto-clusters that no longer have matching groups."""
   390→    changes = 0
   391→    for name in list(clusters.keys()):
   392→        cluster = clusters[name]
   393→        if not cluster.get("auto"):
   394→            continue
   395→        ck = cluster.get("cluster_key", "")
   396→        if ck in active_auto_keys:
   397→            continue
   398→        if cluster.get("user_modified"):
   399→            alive = [
   400→                fid for fid in cluster.get("issue_ids", [])
   401→                if fid in issues and issues[fid].get("status") == "open"
   402→            ]
   403→            if alive:
   404→                if len(alive) != len(cluster.get("issue_ids", [])):
   405→                    cluster["issue_ids"] = alive
   406→                    cluster["updated_at"] = now
   407→                    changes += 1
   408→                continue
   409→        del clusters[name]
   410→        for fid in cluster.get("issue_ids", []):
   411→            override = plan.get("overrides", {}).get(fid)
   412→            if override and override.get("cluster") == name:
   413→                override["cluster"] = None
   414→                override["updated_at"] = now
   415→        if plan.get("active_cluster") == name:
   416→            plan["active_cluster"] = None
   417→        changes += 1
   418→    return changes
   419→
   420→
   421→__all__ = ["prune_stale_clusters", "sync_issue_clusters", "sync_subjective_clusters"]
   422→

    43→        if not lang_name:

    45→        counts[lang_name] = counts.get(lang_name, 0) + 1

    53→    prod_by_module: dict[str, str] = {}

    55→    for pf in production_files:

     6→from typing import Any

     8→from desloppify.intelligence.review.importing.contracts_types import (
     9→    ReviewImportPayload,
    10→    ReviewIssuePayload,
    11→)
    12→
    13→LEGACY_FINDINGS_ALIAS_SUNSET_DATE = "2026-12-31"
    14→ALLOW_LEGACY_FINDINGS_ALIAS = True
    15→
    16→
    17→@dataclass(frozen=True)
    18→class ReviewImportEnvelope:
    19→    """Validated shared payload shape for review imports."""
    20→
    21→    issues: list[ReviewIssuePayload]
    22→    assessments: dict[str, Any] | None
    23→    reviewed_files: list[str]
    24→
    25→
    26→def normalize_legacy_findings_alias(
    27→    payload: dict[str, Any],
    28→    *,
    29→    missing_issues_error: str,
    30→    allow_legacy_findings: bool = ALLOW_LEGACY_FINDINGS_ALIAS,
    31→) -> str | None:
    32→    """Normalize legacy ``findings`` into canonical ``issues`` in one place.
    33→
    34→    ``allow_legacy_findings`` is the compatibility cutoff flag; once flipped to
    35→    ``False`` only canonical ``issues`` payloads are accepted.
    36→    """
    37→    if "issues" in payload:
    38→        return None
    39→    if "findings" not in payload:
    40→        return missing_issues_error
    41→    if not allow_legacy_findings:
    42→        return (
    43→            "legacy key 'findings' is no longer accepted; use 'issues' "
    44→            f"(support sunset: {LEGACY_FINDINGS_ALIAS_SUNSET_DATE})"
    45→        )
    46→    payload["issues"] = payload.pop("findings")
    47→    return None
    48→
    49→
    50→def extract_reviewed_files(data: list[dict] | dict) -> list[str]:
    51→    """Parse optional reviewed-file list from import payload."""
    52→    if not isinstance(data, dict):
    53→        return []
    54→    raw = data.get("reviewed_files")
    55→    if not isinstance(raw, list):
    56→        return []
    57→
    58→    reviewed: list[str] = []
    59→    seen: set[str] = set()
    60→    for item in raw:
    61→        if not isinstance(item, str):
    62→            continue
    63→        path = item.strip()
    64→        if not path or path in seen:
    65→            continue
    66→        seen.add(path)
    67→        reviewed.append(path)
    68→    return reviewed
    69→
    70→
    71→def parse_review_import_payload(
    72→    data: ReviewImportPayload | dict[str, Any],
    73→    *,
    74→    mode_name: str,
    75→) -> ReviewImportEnvelope:
    76→    """Parse shared review import payload shape for per-file/holistic flows."""
    77→    if not isinstance(data, dict):
    78→        raise ValueError(f"{mode_name} review import payload must be a JSON object")
    79→
    80→    missing_issues_error = f"{mode_name} review import payload must contain 'issues'"
    81→    key_error = normalize_legacy_findings_alias(
    82→        data,
    83→        missing_issues_error=missing_issues_error,
    84→    )
    85→    if key_error is not None:
    86→        raise ValueError(key_error)
    87→
    88→    issues_list = data.get("issues")
    89→    if not isinstance(issues_list, list):
    90→        raise ValueError(f"{mode_name} review import payload 'issues' must be a list")
    91→    for idx, entry in enumerate(issues_list):
    92→        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
    93→            raise ValueError(
    94→                f"{mode_name} review import payload 'issues[{idx}]' must be an object"
    95→            )
    96→
    97→    assessments = data.get("assessments")
    98→    if assessments is not None and not isinstance(assessments, dict):
    99→        raise ValueError(
   100→            f"{mode_name} review import payload 'assessments' must be an object"
   101→        )
   102→    return ReviewImportEnvelope(
   103→        issues=issues_list,
   104→        assessments=assessments,
   105→        reviewed_files=extract_reviewed_files(data),
   106→    )
   107→
   108→
   109→def normalize_review_confidence(value: object) -> str:
   110→    """Normalize review confidence labels to high/medium/low."""
   111→    confidence = str(value).strip().lower()
   112→    return confidence if confidence in {"high", "medium", "low"} else "low"
   113→
   114→
   115→def review_tier(confidence: str, *, holistic: bool) -> int:
   116→    """Derive natural tier from review confidence and scope."""
   117→    if confidence == "high":
   118→        return 1 if holistic else 3
   119→    if confidence == "medium":
   120→        return 2 if holistic else 3
   121→    return 3
   122→

   225→    return _PROVIDER_STATE.load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider(lang_name)
   226→
   227→
   228→def _clear_subjective_dimension_caches() -> None:
   229→    default_dimension_keys.cache_clear()
   230→    default_dimension_keys_for_lang.cache_clear()
   231→    load_subjective_dimension_metadata.cache_clear()
   232→    load_subjective_dimension_metadata_for_lang.cache_clear()
   233→
   234→
   235→def configure_subjective_dimension_providers(
   236→    *,
   237→    available_languages_provider: Callable[[], list[str]] | None = None,
   238→    load_dimensions_payload_provider: Callable[
   239→        [], tuple[list[str], dict[str, dict[str, object]], str]
   240→    ]
   241→    | None = None,
   242→    load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider: Callable[
   243→        [str], tuple[list[str], dict[str, dict[str, object]], str]
   244→    ]
   245→    | None = None,
   246→) -> None:
   247→    """Configure metadata providers for subjective-dimension lookups."""
   248→    state = _PROVIDER_STATE
   249→
   250→    changed = False
   251→    if (
   252→        available_languages_provider is not None
   253→        and available_languages_provider is not state.available_languages_provider
   254→    ):
   255→        state.available_languages_provider = available_languages_provider
   256→        changed = True
   257→    if (
   258→        load_dimensions_payload_provider is not None
   259→        and load_dimensions_payload_provider
   260→        is not state.load_dimensions_payload_provider
   261→    ):
   262→        state.load_dimensions_payload_provider = load_dimensions_payload_provider
   263→        changed = True
   264→    if (
   265→        load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider is not None
   266→        and load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider
   267→        is not state.load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider
   268→    ):
   269→        state.load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider = (
   270→            load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider
   271→        )
   272→        changed = True
   273→
   274→    if changed:
   275→        _clear_subjective_dimension_caches()
   276→
   277→
   278→def reset_subjective_dimension_providers() -> None:
   279→    """Reset metadata providers to built-in defaults."""
   280→    configure_subjective_dimension_providers(
   281→        available_languages_provider=_default_available_languages,
   282→        load_dimensions_payload_provider=_default_load_dimensions_payload,
   283→        load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider=_default_load_dimensions_payload_for_lang,
   284→    )
   285→
   286→
   287→def _normalize_dimension_list(values: list[str]) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   288→    normalized: list[str] = []
   289→    for raw in values:
   290→        if not isinstance(raw, str):
   291→            continue
   292→        dim = _normalize_dimension_name(raw)
   293→        if not dim or dim in normalized:
   294→            continue
   295→        normalized.append(dim)
   296→    return tuple(normalized)
   297→
   298→
   299→@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
   300→def default_dimension_keys() -> tuple[str, ...]:
   301→    """Return canonical default subjective dimension keys."""
   302→    try:
   303→        dims, _, _ = _load_dimensions_payload()
   304→    except (ImportError, ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
   305→        logger.debug("Failed to load default subjective dimensions: %s", exc)
   306→        return tuple(_LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES.keys())
   307→    return _normalize_dimension_list(dims)
   308→
   309→
   310→@lru_cache(maxsize=16)
   311→def default_dimension_keys_for_lang(lang_name: str | None) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   312→    """Return default subjective dimension keys for a specific language."""
   313→    normalized = _normalize_lang_name(lang_name)
   314→    if normalized is None:
   315→        return default_dimension_keys()
   316→    try:
   317→        dims, _, _ = _load_dimensions_payload_for_lang(normalized)
   318→    except (ImportError, ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
   319→        logger.debug(
   320→            "Failed to load subjective dimensions for lang %s: %s",
   321→            normalized,
   322→            exc,
   323→        )
   324→        return default_dimension_keys()
   325→    return _normalize_dimension_list(dims)
   326→
   327→
   328→def _build_subjective_dimension_metadata(
   329→    *,
   330→    lang_name: str | None,
   331→) -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
   332→    out: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
   333→
   334→    try:
   335→        shared_defaults, shared_prompts, _ = _load_dimensions_payload()
   336→    except (ImportError, ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
   337→        logger.debug("Failed to load shared subjective dimension payload: %s", exc)
   338→        shared_defaults, shared_prompts = [], {}
   339→    _merge_dimension_meta(out, dimensions=shared_defaults, prompts=shared_prompts)
   340→
   341→    langs = (
   342→        [lang_name]
   343→        if isinstance(lang_name, str) and lang_name.strip()
   344→        else _available_languages()
   345→    )
   346→    for name in langs:
   347→        try:
   348→            lang_defaults, lang_prompts, _ = _load_dimensions_payload_for_lang(name)
   349→            _merge_dimension_meta(
   350→                out,
   351→                dimensions=lang_defaults,
   352→                prompts=lang_prompts,
   353→                override_existing=bool(lang_name),
   354→            )
   355→        except (ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
   356→            logger.debug("Failed to load dimensions for lang %s: %s", name, exc)
   357→            continue
   358→
   359→    for dim, payload in out.items():
   360→        payload.setdefault(
   361→            "display_name",
   362→            _LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES.get(dim, _title_display_name(dim)),
   363→        )
   364→        payload.setdefault("weight", _LEGACY_WEIGHT_BY_DIMENSION.get(dim, 1.0))
   365→        payload.setdefault("enabled_by_default", False)
   366→        if dim in _LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES:
   367→            payload.setdefault("reset_on_scan", dim in _LEGACY_RESET_ON_SCAN_DIMENSIONS)
   368→        else:
   369→            payload.setdefault("reset_on_scan", True)
   370→
   371→    # Preserve legacy dimensions even if a payload temporarily drops one.
   372→    for dim, display in _LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES.items():
   373→        payload = out.setdefault(dim, {})
   374→        payload.setdefault("display_name", display)
   375→        payload.setdefault("weight", _LEGACY_WEIGHT_BY_DIMENSION.get(dim, 1.0))
   376→        payload.setdefault("enabled_by_default", True)
   377→        payload.setdefault("reset_on_scan", dim in _LEGACY_RESET_ON_SCAN_DIMENSIONS)
   378→
   379→    return out
   380→
   381→
   382→@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
   383→def load_subjective_dimension_metadata() -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
   384→    """Return merged metadata across all known dimensions/languages."""
   385→    return _build_subjective_dimension_metadata(lang_name=None)
   386→
   387→
   388→@lru_cache(maxsize=16)
   389→def load_subjective_dimension_metadata_for_lang(
   390→    lang_name: str | None,
   391→) -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
   392→    """Return merged metadata for one language (with language overrides)."""
   393→    normalized = _normalize_lang_name(lang_name)
   394→    return _build_subjective_dimension_metadata(lang_name=normalized)
   395→
   396→
   397→def _metadata_registry(lang_name: str | None) -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
   398→    normalized = _normalize_lang_name(lang_name)
   399→    if normalized is None:
   400→        return load_subjective_dimension_metadata()
   401→    return load_subjective_dimension_metadata_for_lang(normalized)
   402→
   403→
   404→def get_dimension_metadata(
   405→    dimension_name: str, *, lang_name: str | None = None
   406→) -> dict[str, object]:
   407→    """Return metadata for one dimension key (with sane defaults)."""
   408→    dim = _normalize_dimension_name(dimension_name)
   409→    all_meta = _metadata_registry(lang_name)
   410→    payload = dict(all_meta.get(dim, {}))
   411→
   412→    payload.setdefault("display_name", _title_display_name(dim))
   413→    payload.setdefault("weight", 1.0)
   414→    payload.setdefault("enabled_by_default", False)
   415→    payload.setdefault("reset_on_scan", True)
   416→    return payload
   417→
   418→
   419→def dimension_display_name(dimension_name: str, *, lang_name: str | None = None) -> str:
   420→    meta = get_dimension_metadata(dimension_name, lang_name=lang_name)
   421→    return str(meta.get("display_name", _title_display_name(dimension_name)))
   422→
   423→
   424→def dimension_weight(dimension_name: str, *, lang_name: str | None = None) -> float:
   425→    meta = get_dimension_metadata(dimension_name, lang_name=lang_name)
   426→    raw = meta.get("weight", 1.0)
   427→    if is_numeric(raw):
   428→        return max(0.0, float(raw))
   429→    return 1.0
   430→
   431→
   432→def default_display_names_map(*, lang_name: str | None = None) -> dict[str, str]:
   433→    """Display-name map for default subjective dimensions."""
   434→    out: dict[str, str] = {}
   435→    for dim, payload in _metadata_registry(lang_name).items():
   436→        if not bool(payload.get("enabled_by_default", False)):
   437→            continue
   438→        out[dim] = str(payload.get("display_name", _title_display_name(dim)))
   439→    return out
   440→
   441→
   442→def resettable_default_dimensions(*, lang_name: str | None = None) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   443→    """Default subjective dimensions that should be reset by scan reset."""
   444→    out = []
   445→    for dim, payload in _metadata_registry(lang_name).items():
   446→        if not bool(payload.get("enabled_by_default", False)):
   447→            continue
   448→        if not bool(payload.get("reset_on_scan", True)):
   449→            continue
   450→        out.append(dim)
   451→    return tuple(sorted(set(out)))
   452→
   453→
   454→__all__ = [
   455→    "DISPLAY_NAMES",
   456→    "configure_subjective_dimension_providers",
   457→    "default_dimension_keys",
   458→    "default_dimension_keys_for_lang",
   459→    "default_display_names_map",
   460→    "dimension_display_name",
   461→    "dimension_weight",
   462→    "get_dimension_metadata",
   463→    "load_subjective_dimension_metadata",
   464→    "load_subjective_dimension_metadata_for_lang",
   465→    "reset_subjective_dimension_providers",
   466→    "resettable_default_dimensions",
   467→]

    10→def _resolve_reusable_report(
    11→    report: str | None,
    12→    existing_stage: dict | None,
    13→) -> tuple[str | None, bool]:
    14→    if report:
    15→        return report, False
    16→    if existing_stage and existing_stage.get("report"):
    17→        return existing_stage["report"], True
    18→    return None, False
    19→
    20→
    21→def _record_observe_stage(
    22→    stages: dict,
    23→    *,
    24→    report: str,
    25→    issue_count: int,
    26→    cited_ids: list[str],
    27→    existing_stage: dict | None,
    28→    is_reuse: bool,
    29→) -> list[str]:
    30→    stages["observe"] = {
    31→        "stage": "observe",
    32→        "report": report,
    33→        "cited_ids": cited_ids,
    34→        "timestamp": utc_now(),
    35→        "issue_count": issue_count,

    37→    if is_reuse and existing_stage and existing_stage.get("confirmed_at"):
    38→        stages["observe"]["confirmed_at"] = existing_stage["confirmed_at"]
    39→        stages["observe"]["confirmed_text"] = existing_stage.get("confirmed_text", "")
    40→    cleared = cascade_clear_later_confirmations(stages, "observe")
    41→    if not is_reuse:
    42→        stages["observe"].pop("confirmed_at", None)

    54→})

    58→    """Extract parameter names from a function node's parameter list."""

    62→            _walk_params(child, params)

Now I have a comprehensive view. Let me write the assessment.

The codebase has a well-designed, layered error handling strategy:

1. **Clear top-level boundary**: `CommandError` caught by `cli.main()`, clean user-facing message
2. **Consistent I/O wrapping**: `save_state_or_exit`, `safe_write_text` patterns
3. **Deliberate degradation**: `PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS` used consistently across 22 files for plan-optional operations
4. **Best-effort helpers**: `log_best_effort_failure`, `warn_best_effort` in `fallbacks.py`
5. **Validation as return-value**: `validate_review_issue_payload` returns `(result, errors)` tuple

Key issues to investigate:
- `LangResolutionError(SystemExit)` — inheriting from SystemExit rather than CommandError
- `_RECOVERABLE_LANG_RESOLUTION_ERRORS` defined locally in `visualize.py` overlaps with `PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS`
- `count_lines` silently returns 0 on error
- Some `except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS` blocks that silently swallow without logging

    10→def print_user_message(text: str) -> None:
    11→    """Print a plain bordered box to nudge LLM agent behavior.

    24→    for line in wrapped:

   300→def default_dimension_keys() -> tuple[str, ...]:
   301→    """Return canonical default subjective dimension keys."""
   302→    try:
   303→        dims, _, _ = _load_dimensions_payload()
   304→    except (ImportError, ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
   305→        logger.debug("Failed to load default subjective dimensions: %s", exc)
   306→        return tuple(_LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES.keys())
   307→    return _normalize_dimension_list(dims)

   312→    """Return default subjective dimension keys for a specific language."""
   313→    normalized = _normalize_lang_name(lang_name)
   314→    if normalized is None:
   315→        return default_dimension_keys()
   316→    try:
   317→        dims, _, _ = _load_dimensions_payload_for_lang(normalized)
   318→    except (ImportError, ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
   319→        logger.debug(
   320→            "Failed to load subjective dimensions for lang %s: %s",
   321→            normalized,
   322→            exc,
   323→        )
   324→        return default_dimension_keys()
   325→    return _normalize_dimension_list(dims)

   327→
   328→def _build_subjective_dimension_metadata(
   329→    *,
   330→    lang_name: str | None,
   331→) -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
   332→    out: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
   333→
   334→    try:
   335→        shared_defaults, shared_prompts, _ = _load_dimensions_payload()
   336→    except (ImportError, ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
   337→        logger.debug("Failed to load shared subjective dimension payload: %s", exc)
   338→        shared_defaults, shared_prompts = [], {}
   339→    _merge_dimension_meta(out, dimensions=shared_defaults, prompts=shared_prompts)
   340→
   341→    langs = (
   342→        [lang_name]
   343→        if isinstance(lang_name, str) and lang_name.strip()
   344→        else _available_languages()
   345→    )
   346→    for name in langs:
   347→        try:
   348→            lang_defaults, lang_prompts, _ = _load_dimensions_payload_for_lang(name)
   349→            _merge_dimension_meta(
   350→                out,
   351→                dimensions=lang_defaults,
   352→                prompts=lang_prompts,
   353→                override_existing=bool(lang_name),
   354→            )
   355→        except (ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
   356→            logger.debug("Failed to load dimensions for lang %s: %s", name, exc)
   357→            continue
   358→

   361→            "display_name",

   376→        payload.setdefault("enabled_by_default", True)

    10→from desloppify.base.config import config_for_query, load_config

    17→QUERY_PAYLOAD_MAX_BYTES = 2_000_000
    18→QUERY_ITEMS_SOFT_LIMIT = 200
    19→QUERY_CLUSTER_MEMBER_LIMIT = 10
    20→QUERY_TEXT_LIMIT = 400

    22→
    23→def _payload_size_bytes(payload: dict) -> int:
    24→    """Return UTF-8 byte size for a JSON-serializable payload."""
    25→    return len(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, default=json_default).encode("utf-8"))
    26→
    27→
    28→def _truncate_text(value: object, *, limit: int | None = None) -> object:
    29→    """Return text truncated to a fixed character budget."""
    30→    if not isinstance(value, str):
    31→        return value
    32→    limit_value = QUERY_TEXT_LIMIT if limit is None else limit
    33→    if len(value) <= limit_value:
    34→        return value
    35→    return value[: limit_value - 1] + "…"
    36→
    37→
    38→def _lightweight_item(item: object) -> object:
    39→    """Return a lighter-weight queue item safe for query payload persistence."""
    40→    if not isinstance(item, dict):
    41→        return item
    42→
    43→    light = dict(item)
    44→    light["summary"] = _truncate_text(light.get("summary"))
    45→
    46→    detail = light.get("detail")
    47→    if isinstance(detail, dict):
    48→        compact_detail: dict = {}
    49→        for key, value in detail.items():
    50→            if isinstance(value, str):
    51→                compact_detail[key] = _truncate_text(value, limit=200)
    52→            elif isinstance(value, list):
    53→                compact_detail[key] = value[:20]
    54→            elif isinstance(value, dict):
    55→                compact_detail[key] = {"truncated": True, "keys": len(value)}
    56→            else:
    57→                compact_detail[key] = value
    58→        light["detail"] = compact_detail
    59→
    60→    if item.get("kind") == "cluster":
    61→        members = light.get("members")
    62→        if isinstance(members, list) and len(members) > QUERY_CLUSTER_MEMBER_LIMIT:
    63→            light["members"] = members[:QUERY_CLUSTER_MEMBER_LIMIT]
    64→            light["members_truncated"] = True
    65→            light["members_sample_limit"] = QUERY_CLUSTER_MEMBER_LIMIT
    66→
    67→    return light
    68→
    69→
    70→def _minimal_payload(payload: dict, *, max_bytes: int) -> dict:
    71→    """Build a minimal fallback payload when budget cannot be met."""
    72→    minimal: dict = {
    73→        "command": payload.get("command"),
    74→        "queue": payload.get("queue", {}),
    75→        "overall_score": payload.get("overall_score"),
    76→        "objective_score": payload.get("objective_score"),
    77→        "strict_score": payload.get("strict_score"),
    78→    }
    79→
    80→    sample_items: list[dict] = []
    81→    items = payload.get("items")
    82→    if isinstance(items, list):
    83→        for item in items[:20]:
    84→            if not isinstance(item, dict):
    85→                continue
    86→            sample_items.append(
    87→                {
    88→                    "id": item.get("id"),
    89→                    "kind": item.get("kind"),
    90→                    "detector": item.get("detector"),
    91→                    "file": item.get("file"),
    92→                    "summary": _truncate_text(item.get("summary"), limit=200),
    93→                }
    94→            )
    95→    minimal["items"] = sample_items
    96→
    97→    if "config" in payload:
    98→        minimal["config"] = payload["config"]
    99→    if "config_error" in payload:
   100→        minimal["config_error"] = payload["config_error"]
   101→
   102→    minimal["query_truncated"] = {
   103→        "mode": "minimal",
   104→        "max_bytes": max_bytes,
   105→        "items_sample": len(sample_items),
   106→    }
   107→    return _fit_payload_to_budget(minimal, max_bytes=max_bytes)
   108→
   109→
   110→def _fit_payload_to_budget(payload: dict, *, max_bytes: int) -> dict:
   111→    """Shrink payload further until it fits max_bytes."""
   112→    trimmed = dict(payload)
   113→
   114→    items = trimmed.get("items")
   115→    if isinstance(items, list):
   116→        keep = len(items)
   117→        while keep > 0 and _payload_size_bytes(trimmed) > max_bytes:
   118→            keep = max(0, keep // 2)
   119→            trimmed["items"] = items[:keep]
   120→
   121→    if _payload_size_bytes(trimmed) > max_bytes and "config" in payload:
   122→        trimmed = {key: value for key, value in trimmed.items() if key != "config"}
   123→        trimmed["config_truncated"] = True
   124→
   125→    if _payload_size_bytes(trimmed) > max_bytes and "queue" in trimmed:
   126→        trimmed["queue"] = {}
   127→
   128→    if _payload_size_bytes(trimmed) > max_bytes:
   129→        return {
   130→            "command": payload.get("command"),
   131→            "query_truncated": {
   132→                "mode": "minimal",
   133→                "max_bytes": max_bytes,
   134→                "overflow": True,
   135→            },
   136→        }
   137→
   138→    query_meta = payload.get("query_truncated")
   139→    if isinstance(query_meta, dict) and isinstance(trimmed.get("items"), list):
   140→        updated_query_meta = dict(query_meta)
   141→        updated_query_meta["items_sample"] = len(trimmed["items"])
   142→        trimmed["query_truncated"] = updated_query_meta
   143→    return trimmed
   144→
   145→
   146→def _enforce_payload_budget(
   147→    payload: dict,
   148→    *,
   149→    max_bytes: int | None = None,
   150→) -> tuple[dict, list[str]]:
   151→    """Bound payload size with deterministic truncation steps."""
   152→    budget = QUERY_PAYLOAD_MAX_BYTES if max_bytes is None else max_bytes
   153→    if _payload_size_bytes(payload) <= budget:
   154→        return payload, []
   155→
   156→    notes: list[str] = []
   157→    trimmed = dict(payload)
   158→
   159→    items = trimmed.get("items")
   160→    if isinstance(items, list):
   161→        original_count = len(items)
   162→        limited_items = items[:QUERY_ITEMS_SOFT_LIMIT]
   163→        if len(limited_items) < original_count:
   164→            notes.append(f"items:{original_count}->{len(limited_items)}")
   165→        trimmed["items"] = [_lightweight_item(item) for item in limited_items]
   166→
   167→    if _payload_size_bytes(trimmed) > budget and isinstance(trimmed.get("narrative"), dict):
   168→        trimmed["narrative"] = {"truncated": True}
   169→        notes.append("narrative")
   170→
   171→    plan = trimmed.get("plan")
   172→    if _payload_size_bytes(trimmed) > budget and isinstance(plan, dict):
   173→        clusters = plan.get("clusters")
   174→        if isinstance(clusters, list) and len(clusters) > 100:
   175→            compact_plan = dict(plan)
   176→            compact_plan["clusters"] = clusters[:100]
   177→            compact_plan["clusters_truncated"] = True
   178→            trimmed["plan"] = compact_plan
   179→            notes.append("plan.clusters")
   180→
   181→    if _payload_size_bytes(trimmed) > budget:
   182→        trimmed = _minimal_payload(trimmed, max_bytes=budget)
   183→        notes.append("minimal")
   184→
   185→    if notes:
   186→        meta = trimmed.get("query_truncated")
   187→        if not isinstance(meta, dict):
   188→            meta = {}
   189→        meta["max_bytes"] = budget
   190→        meta["actual_bytes"] = _payload_size_bytes(trimmed)
   191→        meta["applied"] = notes
   192→        trimmed["query_truncated"] = meta
   193→
   194→    return trimmed, notes
   195→
   196→
   197→def write_query(data: dict, *, query_file: Path) -> OutputResult:
   198→    """Write structured query payloads with config context and graceful fallback."""
   199→    payload = dict(data)
   200→    if "config" not in payload:
   201→        try:
   202→            payload["config"] = config_for_query(load_config())
   203→        except (OSError, ValueError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
   204→            payload["config_error"] = str(exc)
   205→            logger.debug("Skipping config injection into query payload: %s", exc)
   206→
   207→    payload, truncation_notes = _enforce_payload_budget(payload)
   208→    try:
   209→        safe_write_text(query_file, json.dumps(payload, indent=2, default=json_default) + "\n")
   210→        print("  → query.json updated", file=sys.stderr)
   211→        if truncation_notes:
   212→            print(
   213→                "  ⚠ query.json payload exceeded budget; wrote truncated artifact.",
   214→                file=sys.stderr,
   215→            )
   216→        return OutputResult(
   217→            ok=True,
   218→            status="written",
   219→            message=f"query payload written to {query_file}",
   220→        )
   221→    except OSError as exc:
   222→        payload["query_write_error"] = str(exc)
   223→        print(f"  ⚠ Could not write query.json: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
   224→        return OutputResult(
   225→            ok=False,
   226→            status="error",
   227→            message=str(exc),
   228→            error_kind="query_write_error",
   229→        )
   230→
   231→
   232→__all__ = ["write_query"]

    56→def get_area(filepath: str, *, min_depth: int = 2) -> str:

    61→    parts = Path(text).parts
    62→    if not parts:
    63→        return "(unknown)"
    64→    return "/".join(parts[:2]) if len(parts) >= min_depth else parts[0]

    10→def _require_triage_pending(plan: dict, *, action: str) -> bool:
    11→    """Require at least one triage stage ID to be present in queue for an action."""
    12→    order = set(plan.get("queue_order", []))
    13→    if order & TRIAGE_IDS:
    14→        return True
    15→    print(colorize(f"  No triage stage in the queue — nothing to {action}.", "yellow"))

    19→def _validate_stage_report(
    20→    report: str | None,
    21→    *,
    22→    stage: str,
    23→    min_chars: int,
    24→    missing_guidance: list[str] | None = None,
    25→    short_guidance: list[str] | None = None,
    26→) -> str | None:
    27→    """Validate staged report presence/length and print consistent guidance."""
    28→    if not report:
    29→        print(colorize(f"  --report is required for --stage {stage}.", "red"))
    30→        for line in missing_guidance or []:
    31→            print(colorize(f"  {line}", "dim"))
    32→        return None
    33→    cleaned = report.strip()
    34→    if len(cleaned) < min_chars:
    35→        print(
    36→            colorize(
    37→                f"  Report too short: {len(cleaned)} chars (minimum {min_chars}).",
    38→                "red",
    39→            )
    40→        )
    41→        for line in short_guidance or []:
    42→            print(colorize(f"  {line}", "dim"))
    43→        return None
    44→    return cleaned
    45→
    46→
    47→def _triage_coverage(plan: dict) -> tuple[int, int, dict]:
    48→    """Return (organized, total, clusters) for triage progress."""
    49→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
    50→    all_cluster_ids: set[str] = set()
    51→    for cluster in clusters.values():
    52→        all_cluster_ids.update(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
    53→    queue_ids = [issue_id for issue_id in plan.get("queue_order", []) if issue_id not in TRIAGE_IDS]
    54→    organized = sum(1 for issue_id in queue_ids if issue_id in all_cluster_ids)
    55→    return organized, len(queue_ids), clusters
    56→
    57→
    58→def _unenriched_clusters(plan: dict) -> list[tuple[str, list[str]]]:
    59→    """Return clusters with issues that are missing required enrichment.
    60→
    61→    Requirements:
    62→    - Every cluster needs a description and at least one action_step.
    63→    - Small clusters (< 5 issues) need at least 1 action step per issue,
    64→      so each item has a concrete plan. Large clusters (>= 5) just need
    65→      steps overall (cluster-level plan is sufficient).
    66→    """
    67→    gaps: list[tuple[str, list[str]]] = []
    68→    for name, cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items():
    69→        if not cluster.get("issue_ids"):
    70→            continue
    71→        if cluster.get("auto"):
    72→            continue
    73→        missing: list[str] = []
    74→        if not cluster.get("description"):
    75→            missing.append("description")
    76→        steps = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
    77→        issue_count = len(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
    78→        if not steps:
    79→            missing.append("action_steps")
    80→        elif issue_count < 5 and len(steps) < issue_count:
    81→            missing.append(
    82→                f"action_steps (have {len(steps)}, need >= {issue_count} for small cluster)"
    83→            )
    84→        if missing:
    85→            gaps.append((name, missing))
    86→    return gaps

    98→    for cluster in clusters.values():

   100→            clustered_ids.update(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   101→
   102→    if state is not None:
   103→        review_ids = [
   104→            fid for fid, f in state.get("issues", {}).items()
   105→            if f.get("status") == "open" and f.get("detector") in _REVIEW_DETECTORS
   106→        ]
   107→    else:

   110→            if not fid.startswith("triage::") and not fid.startswith("workflow::")

   112→        ]
   113→
   114→    return [fid for fid in review_ids if fid not in clustered_ids]

I have enough data to form my assessment. Let me now compile all findings:

**Key observations for cross_module_architecture:**

1. **`state.py` god-module facade**: 94 importers, re-exporting from 6 engine._state submodules. This is an intentional facade with clear `__all__`, so per the dimension skip rules, intentional facades with clear API purpose are excluded.

2. **`base/` imports from `intelligence/`**: `base/subjective_dimensions.py` imports directly from `intelligence.review.dimensions.data` and `intelligence.review.dimensions.metadata`, violating the documented architecture rule that `base/` imports nothing from `engine/app/intelligence`.

3. **`engine/` imports from `app/` and `intelligence/`**: Multiple boundary violations:
   - `engine/_work_queue/synthetic.py` imports from `app.commands.plan.triage_playbook`
   - `engine/planning/dimension_rows.py` imports from `app.output.scorecard_parts.dimensions` (deferred)
   - `engine/_scoring/subjective/core.py` imports from `intelligence.review.dimensions.holistic` (top-level) and `intelligence.review.dimensions.metadata` (deferred)
   - `engine/_work_queue/helpers.py` imports from `intelligence.integrity` (deferred)
   - `engine/_scoring/state_integration.py` imports from `intelligence.review.dimensions.data` (deferred)

4. **DISPLAY_NAMES duplicated across layers**: The same `DISPLAY_NAMES` dict is defined in both `base/subjective_dimensions.py` and `engine/_scoring/subjective/core.py`, indicating a missing shared boundary.

5. **Deferred imports as cycle pressure signal**: The `# cycle-break` comments in multiple engine files show that the architectural boundaries are under tension, with deferred imports used as a workaround rather than fixing the dependency direction.

6. **`engine/planning/scan.py` imports from `languages/`**: While the memory says "Languages -> engine/detectors (never reverse)", `engine/planning/scan.py` imports `auto_detect_lang`, `available_langs`, `get_lang` from `desloppify.languages` and types from `_framework`. This is a different kind of violation — the planning/orchestration layer needs to discover languages, which could be argued as legitimate orchestration.

    12→from desloppify.base.config import DEFAULT_TARGET_STRICT_SCORE
    13→from desloppify.base.registry import DETECTORS

    18→# Detectors whose issues are NOT objective mechanical work.
    19→NON_OBJECTIVE_DETECTORS: frozenset[str] = frozenset({
    20→    "review", "concerns", "subjective_review", "subjective_assessment",
    21→})
    22→
    23→
    24→@dataclass(frozen=True)
    25→class SubjectiveVisibility:
    26→    """Immutable snapshot of the subjective-vs-objective balance."""
    27→
    28→    has_objective_backlog: bool  # any open non-subjective issues?
    29→    objective_count: int  # how many
    30→    unscored_ids: frozenset[str]  # subjective::* IDs needing initial review
    31→    stale_ids: frozenset[str]  # subjective::* IDs needing re-review
    32→    under_target_ids: frozenset[str]  # below target, not stale/unscored
    33→
    34→    def should_inject_to_plan(self, fid: str) -> bool:
    35→        """Should this subjective ID be injected into plan queue_order?"""
    36→        if fid in self.unscored_ids:
    37→            return True  # unconditional
    38→        if fid in self.stale_ids:
    39→            return not self.has_objective_backlog
    40→        if fid in self.under_target_ids:
    41→            return not self.has_objective_backlog
    42→        return False
    43→
    44→    def should_evict_from_plan(self, fid: str) -> bool:
    45→        """Should this subjective ID be removed from plan queue_order?"""
    46→        if fid in self.unscored_ids:
    47→            return False  # never evict unscored
    48→        if fid in self.stale_ids or fid in self.under_target_ids:
    49→            return self.has_objective_backlog
    50→        return False
    51→
    52→    @property
    53→    def backlog_blocks_rerun(self) -> bool:
    54→        """Preflight: should reruns be blocked?"""
    55→        return self.has_objective_backlog
    56→
    57→
    58→def _is_evidence_only(issue: dict) -> bool:
    59→    """Return True if the issue is below its detector's standalone threshold."""
    60→    detector = issue.get("detector", "")
    61→    meta = DETECTORS.get(detector)
    62→    if meta and meta.standalone_threshold:
    63→        threshold_rank = CONFIDENCE_ORDER.get(meta.standalone_threshold, 9)
    64→        issue_rank = CONFIDENCE_ORDER.get(issue.get("confidence", "low"), 9)
    65→        if issue_rank > threshold_rank:
    66→            return True
    67→    return False
    68→
    69→
    70→_SCAN_PATH_FROM_STATE_POLICY = object()
    71→
    72→
    73→def compute_subjective_visibility(
    74→    state: StateModel,
    75→    *,
    76→    target_strict: float = DEFAULT_TARGET_STRICT_SCORE,
    77→    scan_path: str | None | object = _SCAN_PATH_FROM_STATE_POLICY,
    78→    plan: dict | None = None,
    79→) -> SubjectiveVisibility:
    80→    """Build the policy snapshot from current state.
    81→
    82→    *scan_path* defaults to ``state["scan_path"]`` so callers don't need to
    83→    thread it manually.  Pass an explicit ``str`` to override, or ``None``
    84→    to disable scope filtering.  When *plan* is set, issues whose IDs
    85→    appear in ``plan["skipped"]`` are excluded.
    86→
    87→    Imports policy helpers from ``stale_policy`` so this module remains
    88→    side-effect free and cycle-safe.
    89→    """
    90→    from desloppify.engine._plan.stale_policy import (
    91→        current_stale_ids,
    92→        current_under_target_ids,
    93→        current_unscored_ids,
    94→    )
    95→
    96→    resolved_scan_path: str | None = (
    97→        state.get("scan_path")
    98→        if scan_path is _SCAN_PATH_FROM_STATE_POLICY
    99→        else scan_path  # type: ignore[assignment]
   100→    )
   101→
   102→    issues = state.get("issues", {})
   103→    skipped_ids = set((plan or {}).get("skipped", {}).keys())
   104→
   105→    # Count open, non-suppressed, objective issues.
   106→    # Evidence-only issues (below standalone confidence threshold) are
   107→    # excluded — they still affect scores but are not actionable queue items.
   108→    # Issues outside scan_path and plan-skipped issues are also excluded
   109→    # so the policy matches what the user actually sees in the queue.
   110→    objective_count = sum(
   111→        1
   112→        for fid, f in issues.items()
   113→        if f.get("status") == "open"
   114→        and f.get("detector") not in NON_OBJECTIVE_DETECTORS
   115→        and not f.get("suppressed")
   116→        and not _is_evidence_only(f)
   117→        and issue_in_scan_scope(str(f.get("file", "")), resolved_scan_path)
   118→        and fid not in skipped_ids
   119→    )
   120→

    34→    REAL_MODES = {"holistic", "per_file", "trusted_internal", "attested_external"}

    40→                if ts:
    41→                    return str(ts)
    42→    holistic = (state.get("review_cache") or {}).get("holistic")
    43→    if isinstance(holistic, dict):
    44→        return holistic.get("reviewed_at")
    45→    return None

    53→    Returns ``{dimension: {"open": [ids], "resolved": [ids]}}``.
    54→    A dimension with both resolved and open issues signals a potential
    55→    loop — similar issues recur after previous fixes.

    57→    def _dimension(f: dict) -> str:
    58→        detail = f.get("detail", {})
    59→        if isinstance(detail, dict):
    60→            return detail.get("dimension", "")
